ranking.title: [1] Phone instrument: per-object / per-clip identification of (mu, e at a stated impact speed, CoM-by-build) through the validated plane-contact tape, validated by invariants and held-out trial type — MERGED from P10 'A phone is a physics instrument' + P6 'Phone-to-twin per-object' (same idea, same capture, same fitter)
ranking.why: Highest total, but note what that total is: 4.7/10. Every proposal in the set was refuted on novelty, so the ranking compares surviving forms. This one survives best because its feasibility is the strongest in the set (two independent skeptics RAN the day-1 gate instead of arguing it: d(apex)/d(alpha) tape vs central FD = 0.998/1.002/1.053 at BOUNCE_RIG, 0.999–1.17 at the tilt rig incl. edge landings, mass-null exact, 0.3 s per clip) and because what it measures — restitution across materials x surfaces x speeds, CoM where an object topples, friction on the user's own surfaces — is the column no catalogue, benchmark or pipeline carries; gap scout 1's Jul–Oct 2026 sweep confirms no multi-material household restitution set, no CoM-from-video work, and no (mu, e, CoM) table from consumer video with held-out validation. Method novelty is nil (SMASH 2016 did restitution and mass ratio from iPhone 240 fps; Hofherr WACV 2023 did friction from one ordinary video; DiffSDFSim fitted restitution of a real tennis ball through a differentiable sim; Delta-ynamics 2026 did 235 iPhone clips). What survives is a measurement-and-validation contribution: n >= 40 objects with weighed masses, invariant gates, held-out-trial-type prediction (fit drops, predict slides), per-clip Fisher identifiability used prescriptively, and e(v) with the Hunt-Crossley form tested rather than assumed. Impact is capped by consumer facts gap scout 2 verified from primary docs: MuJoCo has no restitution coefficient, Isaac Lab's RigidBodyMaterialCfg defaults restitution to 0.0 and PhysX takes a scalar e, no schema carries a velocity law or a provenance field, and SIMPLER's 8x mass x 8x friction sweep leaves closed-loop policy evaluation unchanged (r 0.957–0.990, MMRV 0.031 in every cell) — so value must be shown on open-loop / outcome-class tasks (BayesSim Fetch Slide, DROPO puck, stays/slides/topples), which the recommendation now does. Gap scout 3 adds that the project's e ~ 1 - alpha v IS Hunt-Crossley 1975, that the literature offers no single velocity exponent to adopt (Kuwabara-Kono's (1-e) ∝ v^1/5 is for a different kernel; a linear spring-dashpot gives constant e; Mueller-Heckel PRL 2013 show oscillations), and that DEM practice calibrates damping from a drop test at the impact speed of use — so the two-height invariant must be stated on the fitted law at a reference speed, not on a constant e (the proposals' own kill criteria were misdesigned here; p8: 0.70 -> 0.54 at alpha 0.4). MIT Push's measured surface drift (friction -11 to -22% after 100 pushes, per-surface sd 0.016–0.064) sets a per-session floor that a re-measured reference pair must track. Differentiable physics is genuinely used for multi-parameter per-clip inversion and joint shared-parameter fits, but FD at 6–10 parameters costs seconds, so on the plane path it is convenience plus identifiability bookkeeping, not capability. P1's scene-level batching and P6's robot partnership are dropped from the merged form.
refuted_by: SMASH, Monszpart et al., SIGGRAPH Asia 2016 (arXiv 1603.08984): restitution + mass ratio from consumer 120/240 fps iPhone collision video, no markers
Hofherr et al., WACV 2023 (arXiv 2204.14030): friction of a real sliding block from a single ordinary-camera video by gradient fit, validated against ruler measurements
DiffSDFSim, Strecke & Stueckler, 3DV 2021 (arXiv 2111.15318): restitution + friction + shape of a real bouncing tennis ball through a differentiable LCP simulator (RealSense, n = 1)
Vid2Param, RA-L 2020 (arXiv 1907.06422): restitution and drag of real balls from video via a sim-trained estimator
Delta-ynamics (arXiv 2605.20576, CVPR 2026): 235 real rigid-body videos, 155 at iPhone 210–240 fps, mass/friction/damping inferred for MuJoCo (human-annotated truth, no restitution)
EKFPhys (arXiv 2309.15703): differentiable LCP engine in an EKF, friction of 4 YCB objects with mocap-tilt truth (median 0.025); characterised accurately
PhysVid (arXiv 2510.02311): real elasticity split over many ball materials (annotated apex heights, oracle Pearson 0.87) — contradicts 'no public dataset holds restitution beyond three materials'
Galileo (NeurIPS 2015) / Physics 101 (BMVC 2016): video-to-physics-engine fits on ramp footage with held-out-object evaluation; restitution already a stated target
Exciting Contact Modes (arXiv 2411.10935) and Heiden et al. ICRA 2022 (arXiv 2109.08815): Fisher information and posteriors from differentiable simulators — 'J^T J as identifiability' is established

Gap scout 2 (primary docs): MuJoCo has no restitution coefficient; Isaac Lab RigidBodyMaterialCfg restitution 0.0 default; UsdPhysicsMaterialAPI/PhysX scalar e with combine modes; no provenance field anywhere; SIMPLER Table X r 0.957–0.990 across an 8x mass x 8x friction sweep

Gap scout 3: Hunt-Crossley family is velocity-dependent by construction; no single exponent in the literature (Kuwabara-Kono v^1/5; PFC linear dashpot constant e; Mueller-Heckel oscillations); the cross-height invariant tests the law, not the camera; docs/results/p8_alpha.json e 0.64–0.70 at 0.99 m/s vs 0.50–0.54 at 1.98 m/s
MIT Push (arXiv 1604.04038): per-surface friction sd 0.016–0.064 and -11 to -22% break-in drift after 100 pushes — the floor any per-object friction claim must beat
Repo: no monocular 6-DoF pose path, no meshes for irregular objects, src/track/balls.py tuned to rendered balls; Hunyuan3D-2 licence excludes South Korea (TripoSR/TRELLIS or photogrammetry instead)

ranking.title: [2] ContactAtlas-240: multi-object tagged tilt-board + drop-station atlas (object x surface) fitted through the differentiable plane contact — P3 (kept separate for its multi-object capture design and atlas output; otherwise the same instrument as [1])
ranking.why: Same instrument as [1] with a throughput lever (10–20 objects per clip on an AprilTag-bordered board) and an atlas rather than a twin as the product. Not refuted on feasibility (the impact adjoint passed at <1% on 60/120/240 substeps), but the skeptic found the forward rotational response to a corner impact is NOT converged in substeps (angular velocity -4.29/-3.98/-3.81 rad/s; its cd-gradient flips sign), and gap scout 3 confirms from the DEM literature (LIGGGHTS, Itasca PFC) that no published convergence criterion exists for corner/edge impacts of polyhedra under penalty contact — every timestep rule is for spheres — so the headline 6-DoF alpha fit of irregular bodies would fit an unconverged model and rule 2 fails before any data. Breadth claims were overstated ('~100x' is ~30x the largest pad-measured set, NeRF2Physics' 15 x 6 iOLab matrix; GAUGE's calibrated trajectories are on Hugging Face — gated per gap scout 1, public per the P3 verdict, to be verified). Gap scout 2 makes the consumer collapse precise: UsdPhysicsMaterialAPI/PhysX ingest per-material scalars combined by average/min/multiply/max (precedence max of the enum), MuJoCo uses element-wise max or explicit <pair>, Genesis is undocumented, and none is a geometric mean — so a 150 x 15 pair table must be re-authored as sqrt(mu) per material under 'multiply' or expanded to explicit pairs, i.e. ~20 numbers at the consumer; the handbook-pair baseline was never run; the phone floor (+/-0.02–0.03 in mu) equals the separation it must resolve and MIT Push shows surfaces drift 11–22% with wear, giving the atlas a shelf life. Scale score is the highest among feasible entries because object x surface pairs on outdoor surface sheets is the only breadth axis actually reachable. Its multi-object board and tag-based scale/angle readout are absorbed into the recommendation as an optional week-5+ throughput step; its 'first contact table validated on motion of objects it never saw' headline is dropped (Physics 101 did split-by-object in 2016; e1 already did the trajectory version).
refuted_by: GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948): measured mu (inclined plane) and e (air-bearing rail) for wood/plastic/metal/rubber, ~1,560 mocap trials, 20 repeats, uncertainty annotated; dataset on Hugging Face (gating status conflicting between scouts)

NeRF2Physics (arXiv 2404.04242): measured kinetic friction for 15 household objects on 6 surfaces (iOLab pads, 10 trials) — ~90 pairs, larger than the 30 PhysVid pairs the proposal credited as the maximum
Physics 101 (BMVC 2016): split-by-object real-outcome prediction incl. bounce height on 5 drop surfaces; the project's own e1 is already the trajectory-level version
ContactNets (arXiv 2009.11193): AprilTag-tracked 148 Hz contact sysid of a cube, 570 tosses — tagged boards are not new
Gap scout 2: PhysX combine modes average/min/multiply/max; MuJoCo element-wise max or <pair>; no engine combines by geometric mean; Isaac Lab DR samples num_buckets materials (PhysX limit 64,000)

Gap scout 3: no convergence criterion for corner/edge impacts of polyhedra under penalty contact anywhere (LIGGGHTS, PFC, 2509.07461 are sphere-only); DiffMJX reports corner-impact chaos on real cube tosses

Feasibility: rotational response of corner impacts not converged in substeps; no AprilTag/ArUco or photogrammetry code in the repo; 150 watertight scanned meshes + ~3,300 clips in days 31–60 is ~2x one researcher's capacity

Impact: consumers ingest per-material scalars; no downstream task shown; the handbook-pair baseline missing from e1 (verified: routes are oracle/material/pipeline/LLM-direct only); MIT Push wear drift

ranking.title: [3] Measured material table + assignment benchmark/audit on Physics 101 (e1-bench scorer, LLM-name resolver, library audit, one-slide surface anchor) — MERGED from P7 'HELD-OUT' + P5 'PhysMat' + P9 'Material Ledger' (same table, same e1 harness, same audit, different emphasis)
ranking.why: The best-defended novelty claim in the set (the P7 skeptic's 4.5 was the highest awarded) and now doubly confirmed: gap scout 1 (Jul–Oct 2026 scoop sweep) found no assignment-route benchmark scored against held-out real motion, and gap scout 2 found no published outcome-flip number for per-object physics, no provenance field in any physics-material schema, and no DR-range ablation in any asset suite — every paper that varies friction/mass either reports the downstream metric as robust (SIMPLER), finds no adaptation signal (2606.20712) or changes everything at once (Kaedim 2610.00731, by its authors' own confound statement). Impact is raised from 3.5 to 4 on that evidence: the outcome-flip audit is the one number a maintainer could act on and it is unreported. Everything else in the cluster exists: Physics 101 itself ran split-by-object and Galileo ran the 10-from-20-degree stays/slides transfer on the same footage; Kaedim's YAM harness already deploys a per-class friction table and reports policy-level sim-to-real correlation 0.51 -> 0.90; LLM-names-material -> table/interval is NeRF2Physics/PUGS/Asset2Sim/UniPhysGen; the one-slide product-rule anchor is the k = 1 case of arXiv 2604.24188's proxy-embedding factorisation, which finds pair friction needs >= 2 proxies. A new caveat from gap scout 2: Acosta, Yang & Posa (RA-L 2022) identified the SAME acrylic cube at mu 0.10 (Drake), 0.22 (MuJoCo) and 0.36 (Bullet) — measured values are effective parameters of a contact law, so the exported table must state the law/engine it was fitted under and be checked by two routes per engine, or it is one more unvalidated number. Feasibility is real (first experiment runs in days; e1 routes exist, data on disk) but the P7 skeptic measured that the 20-degree benchmark is exactly flat above mu = 0.364 (identical 87.8 mm for every generic route), so it cannot rank generators or LLMs that emit ~0.4 until a steeper ramp is captured — it needs [1]'s instrument; the pre-registered rule-1 kill test fails as written (28–39/70 vs 40 required); the 8-object sign test needs 8/8; and the ledger's rows are pair values against MIT's board the user cannot bridge without a self-measured reference board (p1's own 0.28 -> 0.21 cardboard size dependence). Effect size: material 2.55 mm vs dataset median 4.40 mm vs oracle 1.77 mm (dmu 0.017 vs 0.031 vs 0.010), inside any DR band. Zero differentiable physics by its own admission. Ranked below [1]/[2] because it is the scorer and the on-disk control of the recommended direction, not a direction on its own; it is the runner-up.
refuted_by: Physics 101, Wu et al., BMVC 2016: 'Split by object' protocol with held-out-object outcome prediction (moving distance rho 0.33, bounce 0.23) and cross-scenario transfer on this exact footage — the proposals' 'no held-out-object test' claim is false
Galileo, NeurIPS 2015: 10-degree stays/slides prediction from 20-degree videos over 50 Physics 101 objects with a Bullet engine

Kaedim, arXiv 2610.00731 (Oct 2026): VLM-assigned material class -> per-class friction table in a deployed real-to-sim harness, policy-level validation r 0.51 -> 0.90, confounded by the authors' own statement
NeRF2Physics (2404.04242), PUGS (2502.12231), GaussianProperty (2412.11258), Asset2Sim (2605.19136), UniPhysGen (2607.13586): LLM/VLM names material -> property table or interval

Wang & Wang, arXiv 2604.24188: 50+-material tribometer library with proxy-embedding pair-friction factorisation, leave-one-material-out R^2 ~ 1, >= 2 proxies needed — contradicts the one-slide k = 1 product rule

Acosta, Yang & Posa, RA-L 2022 (arXiv 2110.00541): one cube, three engines, three frictions (0.10/0.22/0.36); 'extensive identification of the contact parameters is not necessary' in the inelastic regime
GAUGE (2608.05948), MIT Push (1604.04038), Omnipush (1910.00618), PhysVid (2510.02311): measured friction/restitution tables with trial variability already exist
DROPO (2201.08434) / BayesSim: DR distributions from real trajectories; Scalable Real2Sim (2503.00370): robot-measured mass/CoM/inertia for sim-ready assets (uncited)

Feasibility (measured by the P7 skeptic): held-out RMS vs assigned mu is 87.8 mm identically for mu 0.37–0.60; kill test 2 passes on 28–39/70 objects vs 40 required; only 4/70 resolve +/-0.02; PhysX-Anything/UniPhysGen environments are 3–4 weeks of CUDA-extension installs; Physics 101 has no licence for clip redistribution

Impact: effect size 2.55 vs 4.40 mm (dmu 0.014) is inside the 0.3–1.5 friction DR band every consumer applies; SIMPLER <= 15% and arXiv 2606.20712 leave the 'does it matter' question open; gap scout 2: no schema has a provenance field and no consumer ingests e(v)

ranking.title: [4] IMPACT ATLAS: restitution-only from 240 fps drops with an audio second route and a Newton/Warp contact-law card — P8 (a strict subset of [1], kept separate for its audio route and law-vs-parameter claim)
ranking.why: Feasible (the skeptic ran the impact adjoint: tape/FD 0.999–1.17 at 420 substeps, sign flip at 100 substeps and dead cd) and cheap, but it is the restitution column of [1] sold as a programme, and the gap scouts make its two headline claims weaker still. Two uncited primary results cut its design: Heckel et al., Phys. Rev. E 93, 032901 (2016) show the sound-timing route is valid only for near-perfect spheres (so audio e_t for blocks and assets is dead on arrival), and Mueller et al., PRL 2013, show e(v) is non-monotone with oscillations. Gap scout 3 settles the 'fit a velocity exponent' idea as model selection between damping kernels rather than a measurement: Hunt-Crossley's chi = 3(1-e)/2 is derived assuming e ~ 1 - alpha v near e = 1, Kuwabara-Kono/Brilliantov give (1-e) ∝ v^1/5 only for the delta^1/2 delta-dot kernel, PFC's linear dashpot gives constant e by construction, and DEM sidesteps the question by calibrating damping from a drop test at the impact speed of use (PFC accepts <3% error on e) — which is what the recommendation adopts (e reported at a stated reference speed). The law-vs-parameter diagnosis was done on 550 real cube tosses across Drake/MuJoCo/Bullet by Acosta, Yang & Posa (RA-L 2022), uncited. Impact is lowered to 2.5 on gap scout 2's consumer audit: no consumer ingests e(v); its single consumer is the project's own kernel (HC = 1.0 in src/sim/mesh_contact.py, alpha read only in src/sim/rigs.py); Newton's shipped solvers take no alpha, MuJoCo has no restitution, PhysX/Isaac Lab default it to 0 and users randomise over handbook e. Survives as a 2–3-week instrument gate inside [1] (spheres only for the audio route; a hard reference plate so steel bearings do not dent the board; a camera-calibration day the plan omits).
refuted_by: Kuwabara & Kono 1987; Labous et al. 1997; Cross, Am. J. Phys. 67:222 (1999); Mueller, Heckel, Sack, Poeschel, PRL 2013 (non-monotone e(v) with oscillations): sphere e(v) by high-speed drop video is a mature measurement literature
Bernstein 1977 (AJP) and Heckel et al., Phys. Rev. E 93, 032901 (2016): the sound-timing restitution route exists and is valid only for near-perfect spheres
Yurata et al., Adv. Powder Technol. 2021; Itasca PFC docs; LIGGGHTS: drop-test calibration of damping/restitution across materials and speeds is routine in DEM, with sphere-only timestep criteria

Gap scout 3: Hunt-Crossley / Lankarani-Nikravesh / Flores damping factors are all velocity-dependent once chi is fixed; HC and LN deviate 25–45% from the others at e = 0.2; 'fitting p' is kernel selection, not a material law

Acosta, Yang, Posa, 'Validating Robotics Simulators on Real-World Impacts', RA-L 2022 (arXiv 2110.00541): 550 real cube tosses, per-simulator stiffness/damping/friction identified, engines under-produce restitution — the proposal's engine-fidelity claim, uncited
DiffSDFSim (2111.15318), PIN-WM (2504.16693), ContactNets/Dojo/DiffMJX: gradient-based restitution identification from real video or tosses already exists
GAUGE (2608.05948) has four rigid materials with 20 trials, not three

Impact (gap scout 2): MuJoCo has no restitution coefficient; Isaac Lab defaults restitution 0.0; Genesis coup_restitution 0.0 'could lead to instability'; no consumer ingests e(v); restitution is a pair property dominated by the surface (Bounce and Learn)

ranking.title: [5] Phone-to-Twin (batched, scene-level): identify every movable object in a filmed space on one Warp tape, persistent world API, four pokes incl. a reference-ball strike — P1 (world-bridge; its per-object core is absorbed into [1], its scene claims are what is ranked here, and its strike/stack probes become the validation vehicle of the recommendation's engine track)
ranking.why: The most ambitious design and the one whose pre-registered gate already fails on the project's own measurements: scripts/g0d_grad_free.py gives the body-body cd gradient 1.66x off head-on and 2x off at a 5 cm glancing offset against a 10% gate, so the reference-ball strike (mass ratio, object-ball restitution) reverts to sweeps on day 1 and the 'four parameters in one batched gradient pass' headline cannot stand. The two-height invariant is stated on e, which the project's own Hunt-Crossley calibration makes speed-dependent. No monocular 6-DoF pose path exists; weeks 7–9 ask one researcher to capture 1,600 clips, photogrammetry 150–250 objects, track, identify and ship a deterministic world API at a contact setting measured as nondeterministic (1.5 mm atomic-add). Outdoor floors are unvalidated for an engine with no static friction. Batching 'at 200 objects nobody will sweep' is arithmetically false (FD Jacobians ~11 A6000-hours). What the gap scouts add is a reason to keep its body-body ambition alive in a different form: gap scout 3 establishes that no shipped engine gives FD-validated gradients through sustained frictional mesh–mesh contact, that the project's pair adjoint sits exactly in that hole, and that P1's strikes, stacks and pushes are the probes that would exercise a fixed adjoint — so they re-enter the recommendation as the gated engine track's validation, not as a scene. The surviving pilot (10–30 primitive objects, 2–3 floors, mu and CoM by tape, alpha and mass by analytic/sweep) is [1].
refuted_by: gradSim (ICLR 2021), DiffSDFSim (3DV 2021), EKFPhys (3DV 2024): differentiable-simulation identification of rigid friction/mass from video exists

Galileo (NeurIPS 2015): mass from a collision with another object, fitted to Physics 101 with Bullet — the proposal's claim that Physics 101 'gives neither restitution nor mass from motion' is unfair on mass
PhysTwin (2503.17973), Spring-Gaus (2403.09434): held-out-interaction validation of an identified twin (deformable)
GAUGE (2608.05948): the variability-normalised real-vs-sim metric
ASID (2404.12308), DROPO (2201.08434): Fisher-information identifiability and DR ranges from real data

DiffSDFSim, Ostrich (2609.08800), DiffMJX (2506.14186), Warp SolverSemiImplicit: 'no shipped engine gives gradients through mesh contact' is an overclaim as stated — gap scout 3's precise form is 'none through sustained frictional MESH–MESH narrow phase with FD validation', which holds

Feasibility (run today): g0d body-body/strike gradients 1.66x–2x off a 10% gate; pos0 assignment breaks the tape for s0/v0; CoM and mass are numpy at construction; no PnP/6-DoF pose; the sweep gate (|mu_tape - mu_sweep| <= 0.005) is set at the sweep's own grid half-step and cannot fail

Impact (gap scout 2): pair friction against the filmed floor is not what manipulation consumes (gripper/object, object/object contact); 'interactable worlds at scale' redefined as object count; consumers take USD, not a bespoke state API

ranking.title: [6] M2P: motion-supervised photo -> (mu, e, build) model trained end-to-end through the simulator on real tracked motion, no parameter labels — P4
ranking.why: Refuted at the thesis level by the dataset it would train on: Physics 101 (Wu et al., BMVC 2016) already built exactly this — LeNet on tracked image patches -> material/volume -> physics-interpreter layers (friction, density, restitution, mass) -> hand-coded differentiable physical laws -> MSE against velocities/distances tracked from the real videos, 'no labels for physical properties', with split-by-object evaluation. Galileo (NeurIPS 2015) is the proposal's 'two-stage baseline' on the same footage. PhysVid's real-motion-adapted V-JEPA-2 reaches 0.73 Pearson on held-out objects AND surfaces, which the proposal omitted in favour of the unadapted 0.21–0.28. Feasible (gradient gate passes, warp+torch co-import works, 64-body batch at 4.6 s / 6.8 GiB) but its decisive number is predetermined: the kill bar (>= 4.4 mm / <= 80%) is cleared 2x by the no-model material table (2.55 mm / 94%), the slides are closed-form, 'stays' are parameter-space bounds a Tobit loss handles without a simulator, and the headroom 2.55 -> 1.77 mm is mostly per-object finish noise (p1 Spearman -0.80 with cube size; MIT Push's 11–22% wear drift) a photo cannot carry. What survives — a general exact-mesh simulator in place of analytic laws, shown to beat the analytic/grid surrogate on non-slide clips — is a sub-experiment of [1], not a direction. Gap scouts add nothing that rescues it.
refuted_by: Physics 101, Wu et al., BMVC 2016 (phys101.csail.mit.edu/papers/phys101_bmvc.pdf): image network -> physical properties -> differentiable physics laws -> loss on tracked motion, unlabeled, split-by-object; the same architecture on the same dataset
Galileo, NeurIPS 2015: MCMC fit of mass/friction to tracked ramp videos, then LeNet regression to unseen objects — the two-stage baseline, called 'self-supervised' by its authors
PhysVid (2510.02311) Table 1 / App. B.2: V-JEPA-2 fine-tuned on real motion with disjoint objects and surfaces reaches 0.73 Pearson on real friction
Kandukuri et al., GCPR 2020 (2009.08292); Heiden et al., IROS 2022 (2203.10488); DensePhysNet, RSS 2019 (1906.03853); ETH terrain, RA-L 2024 (2408.16567)

Feasibility: bodies that leave the plane return exactly zero gradient (3/3 off-plane cases); Physics 101 ships no meshes for the 24 rolling clips; SSv2 is 19.4 GB behind registration, not 2 GB; the surface corpus does not exist
Impact: kill bar below the existing no-model baseline; per-object finish effects bound the learnable headroom; consumers would adopt the table + namer, not the model

ranking.title: [7] PhysReady: measured material layer + a 200–1,000-object Newton street scene as persistent, deterministic state with a WRBench look-away protocol — P2 (world-bridge; its table/benchmark half is absorbed into [3], its world half is what is ranked here)
ranking.why: The only proposal that tried to honour 'interactable worlds beyond rooms', and the evidence is unambiguous that this project cannot build it in 90 days: src/sim/mesh_scene.py:365 launches pair_contact_mesh over nV x N threads with no broadphase (verified), so a 1,000-body world is ~1e13 BVH queries per simulated second; 'seeded deterministic replays' contradict the project's own 1.5 mm atomic-add nondeterminism at the validated contact setting; capture is undercounted 2.4x (2,400 clips); there is no controllable real excitation for shove or topple without a rig; the week-2 kill test runs over 11 slidable materials whose mu spans only 0.16–0.33. On novelty, UrbanVerse already ships a dynamic street scene with GPT-assigned mass/friction in Isaac Sim, the 6/163 state-feedback gap is already quantified by survey 2608.23070, GAUGE already scores i2v world models on measured trajectories, and passing a persistence protocol 'by construction' is not a contribution. Gap scout 2 adds that its PhysX export is lossy twice over — restitution collapses HC e(v) to a scalar, and the geometric-mean pair rule has no slot among PhysX's average/min/multiply/max combine modes. The highest scale score in the set, and the least reachable.
refuted_by: UrbanVerse (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.15018): 'assign annotated physical parameters (e.g., mass, friction) and enable rigid-body dynamics, producing stable, interactive scenes' in Isaac Sim; mass validated at 19.58% MAPE vs specs; friction unchecked; no ground-material friction table found (gap scout 2)
Survey arXiv 2608.23070: 6 of 163 world-model implementations expose runtime state — the persistence gap is already published
GAUGE (2608.05948): already scores six image-to-video world models against measured real trajectories
NeRF2Physics / PUGS / GaussianProperty: LLM material naming -> property lookup validated on measured masses and grasps
MIT Push (1604.04038), Omnipush (1910.00618), Physics 101: measured object x surface tables

Feasibility (verified): all-pairs nV x N contact kernel with no broadphase; per-substep state storage; stiff-setting nondeterminism (1.5 mm); p9 topple needs a 40–46 degree rubber-grip ramp, not a hand push; restitution IQR from 6 clips per cell is not an IQR

Impact: numbers 2–3x wrong but outcomes rarely change (its own biggest-risk paragraph; SIMPLER <= 15%); UrbanVerse's 288 ground materials need the same unvalidated naming on the floor side; gap scout 2: no consumer ingests e(v) and no combine mode is a geometric mean

recommendation.title: The instrument, the benchmark and one engine claim: phone-measured (mu, e at a stated impact speed, CoM-by-build) of everyday objects on everyday surfaces through the exact-mesh simulator, scored on held-out real motion as OUTCOME FLIPS for every assignment route the field ships, with the mesh–mesh contact adjoint as the single, gated differentiable-physics contribution — merging the surviving forms of [1] (instrument), [3] (benchmark/audit/library), [2] (multi-object capture), [4] (restitution column) and the body-body probes of [5]
recommendation.thesis: The physical parameters of simulation assets have to be measured, not asked for: every external model this project tested (Cosmos judge, V-JEPA surprise, FPT, MYRIAD, Wan, LLM numbers) returns a generic prior, and the 2026 literature says the same (PhysVid, PokeWorld, ACWM-Phys, WRBench, GAUGE, WorldBench). The cheapest validated instrument is a 240 fps phone plus this project's exact-mesh plane-contact simulator, which reproduces real slides to 0.4–1.0 mm and whose plane-contact adjoint matches finite differences for friction (g0) and, as of this week's reviewer checks, for damping through an impact. Three claims, each with its own pre-registered kill test. (i) Measurement: a material x surface x impact-speed table of friction, restitution and build-aware density/CoM, measured by phone from ~40 everyday objects on three built-environment surfaces with repeat-trial uncertainty and assigned by an LLM that only names material and build, predicts the real motion of objects and surfaces it never fitted within ~1.5x the per-object oracle. (ii) Benchmark: the same held-out real motion scores every other assignment route the field uses — released generators, LLM numbers, handbook tables, shipped library values — in the one unit a maintainer acts on and nobody has reported (gap scout 2 verified across SIMPLER, Kaedim, Acosta, UrbanVerse, BEHAVIOR-1K, RoboCasa, RoboVerse: no published P(outcome flips | parameter error)): the fraction of open-loop stays/slides/topples/bounces outcomes that change, measured where parameters demonstrably set the result (BayesSim Fetch Slide, DROPO puck, ASID) rather than in closed-loop policy evaluation where SIMPLER shows insensitivity. (iii) Engine: the only differentiable-physics claim worth making is the one no shipped engine makes — gap scout 3 read Newton 1.4's source (narrow phase and normals frozen, tests on sphere/box only, marked experimental), Nimble (mesh normals frozen, no friction gradient), DiffMJX (mesh–mesh 'not modified'), Dojo (no meshes), Ostrich (body-vs-terrain, e = 0, code unreleased), Jade (code unreleased), MJX (convex-only), Genesis (zero/undefined on some paths) — FD-validated gradients through sustained frictional mesh–mesh contact. This project's pair kernel is already symmetric in form (mu_eff = sqrt(mu_i mu_j), src/sim/mesh_contact.py:151) with a measured, localisable defect (g0c: FD d(x_A)/d(mu_B) = -0.385, tape -0.032, the total right), so the hole is one diagnosed adjoint away, not a new engine away. If the defect is fixed under a 3-week gate, identification extends from object-on-plane to object–object contact (strikes, stacks, pushes) — the contact manipulation actually consumes, which no floor-pair table reaches; if not, the FD regime map (gradient error vs contact duration and approach angle, which gap scout 3 found nobody reports) is published as a finding and 'differentiable' stays off the title.
recommendation.one_paragraph: Build one thing with four faces. (a) The instrument: a capture protocol (phone on a tripod, 240 fps, inclinometer angle, the object's own measured edge for scale, a reference board + laminate + concrete paver, a hard reference plate for bearings, kitchen-scale mass, a reference pair re-slid every session because MIT Push shows surfaces drift 11–22% with wear) and a fitter that turns CoTracker3 tracks into (mu_pair, alpha at a stated impact speed, CoM offset where the object topples) through DiffMeshScene with per-clip nuisances (release time, offset, initial pose/velocity), tape gradients where they pass a per-class FD gate, FD/CEM where they do not, and a per-clip Fisher matrix that states what the clip identifies. Slides and sphere rebounds are closed-form and are read as such; the tape is used only for the non-closed-form classes (post-impact tumble of blocks, topple-with-slide, the rolling clips p2 discarded) and for joint fits with shared per-session/per-material parameters. (b) The library and its delivery path, now specified from the consumers' own schemas (gap scout 2): rows with n, IQR and provenance (measured / inferred / default) written through src/simready/usd_physics.py as UsdPhysicsMaterialAPI density/staticFriction/dynamicFriction/restitution plus custom provenance attributes (no schema has one); friction authored as sqrt(mu_material) under PhysX 'multiply' or as explicit MuJoCo <pair> elements, because no engine combines by geometric mean; restitution as the scalar e at a stated reference impact speed, because no consumer ingests e(v); and, because Acosta et al. identified one cube at mu 0.10/0.22/0.36 in Drake/MuJoCo/Bullet, every exported value is checked by re-simulating the measured drop and slide in Newton-MuJoCo (pip mujoco) and PhysX where reachable, with the per-engine disagreement reported — two routes to one quantity, rule 2. (c) The benchmark: the e1 harness generalised to a scorer that takes any f(image, mesh) -> (mu, rho, e) and reports re-simulated trajectory error, outcome accuracy and outcome-flip rate on held-out real objects AND held-out surfaces, with routes = own-trials oracle, measured table, LLM-name + table, LLM direct number, handbook table by material pair (never run; one afternoon), VLM-range midpoint in UrbanVerse/EmbodiedGen prompt formats, PhysX-Anything density -> mass, PhysX-Anything -> UniPhysGen friction, BEHAVIOR-1K lookup, Isaac Lab/SimReady defaults (0.5/0.5/0.0), plus PhysVid's 5 x 6 dynamometer matrix and GAUGE's slope-slider trials (if its Hugging Face data is reachable) as external instrument checks. (d) The engine track, gated: week 1 produces the FD regime map of the pair adjoint (sustained push, glancing 3/5 cm, head-on strike, stacked settle, at both rigs, as a function of contact duration and approach angle) plus the rule-6 diagnosis of the split defect (per-launch comparison of the pair kernel's d(force)/d(mu_j) against FD; the symmetric-pair invariant that two identical bodies with equal mu must give d/dmu_A = d/dmu_B); weeks 2–4 attempt the fix with DiffMJX's contacts-from-distance and Ostrich's IFT adjoint as the published templates and Suh et al.'s bundled gradients as the fallback; only if sustained-contact gradients pass FD within 10–20% do strike/stack/push clips with a weighed reference ball (P1's protocol) enter the capture. The pre-registered kill tests are the anti-reinvention device: if a handbook table or a released generator already matches the measured table on held-out motion, that is the result, published, and the capture stops.
recommendation.why_now: (1) The video-model route is closed, by this project's controlled negatives and by independent 2026 results (PhysVid: V-JEPA-2 friction r 0.21–0.28; PokeWorld: mass R^2 0.21–0.25; WRBench: 0/23 models persist state; GAUGE/WorldBench: right law form, wrong accelerations) — so parameters must be measured, and the question is only which instrument. (2) The instrument now exists and is validated: Newton with the project's exact-mesh contact reproduces real Physics 101 slides to 0.4–1.0 mm (p4), seating and CoM/inertia defects were fixed and checked against textbook values within 1%, restitution is parameterised mass-independently (p8), and two reviewers ran the plane-impact adjoint this week (tape/FD 0.998–1.05 flat, <= 1.17 edge) — but none of these gradient results is recorded in docs/results (verified: the g0_*.json files there are judge-era), which the first week must fix. (3) The gap is freshly documented from every side: 2025–26 sim-ready pipelines (PhysX-Anything/Omni, UniPhysGen, EmbodiedGen V2, ManiTwin, UrbanVerse, MolmoSpaces) ship VLM mass/friction at 10^4–10^5 assets validated only against VLM/human labels, spec sheets or policy rankings; GAUGE (Aug 2026) built the measured-trajectory benchmark without an assignment step and reports stock Newton under-predicting slope-slider acceleration (wood 2.06 vs 2.58 m/s^2) and failing the bouncing ball at 22.7x the repeat error — numbers this project's p4/p7/p8 already improve on but have never been compared against; Kaedim (Oct 2026) deployed a per-class table without measuring it; gap scout 2 found no provenance field, no e(v), no outcome-flip number and no DR-range ablation anywhere. (4) The engine hole is open and contested right now: DiffMJX (ICLR 2026) lists mesh–mesh as future work, Ostrich (Sep 2026) and Jade promise code that is not released, Newton's own 'differentiable contacts' are experimental with the narrow phase frozen — several groups are converging on it, which is both the opportunity and the scoop risk, and this project's pair kernel is already symmetric in form with a characterised defect and an FD oracle. (5) 240 fps phones make restitution readable where p3 at 30 fps failed (2.7x g spread), and Newton GA inside Isaac Lab plus the SimReady USD schema give a measured, provenance-tagged physics material a delivery path once it is authored in the engines' own combine conventions.
recommendation.how_it_uses_our_assets: Simulator: MeshProbeScene exact vertex-plane contact on a tilted plane (gn/gt/gp), seat_on_plane with zero clearance, build-aware mass_points (shell/solid/areal) for CoM and inertia, set_restitution_alpha and src/sim/rigs.py (TILT_RIG/BOUNCE_RIG validated jointly), DiffMeshScene from scripts/g0_grad_check.py as the tape path, src/optimize/lm.py (projected-iterate trust-region LM from o8; FD-Jacobian today — the tape-Jacobian variant is new code). Engine track: src/sim/mesh_contact.py pair_contact_mesh (wp.mesh_query_point_sign_normal in the other body's local frame, each wp.Mesh built once, mu_eff = sqrt(mu_i mu_j) at line 151, cd_eff at line 150), Warp 1.15's native adj_mesh_query_point_sign_normal, and the defect record in scripts/g0b_grad_pair.py / g0c_grad_diag.py / g0d_grad_free.py (test A isolates the mesh-query adjoint, test C the pair path, test E a plane-free head-on impact) — the diagnosis starts from those three tests, per rule 6. Real-footage pipeline: scripts/p1/p2 (CoTracker3 at the 19 px grid, slide/roll/stay classification, two-angle and camera-scale invariants — p2's hard-coded SCALE = 1661 px/m and filename angle must become per-clip inputs), p4 (release-aligned Newton replay), p3's two-route restitution design and g-from-parabola scale check, p5's build-aware mass transfer and product-rule test, p9's time-to-topple CoM probe (read off the simulator at 2 ms) and its rule-1 matrix, o7's sensitivity discipline now computed as a per-clip Fisher matrix. Validation: scripts/e1_heldout.py (held-out protocol, LLM naming cache, routes) and docs/results/e1_heldout.json as the ladder (oracle 1.77 / material 2.55 / pipeline 2.72 / global 4.40 / LLM 7.53 mm; outcome 94/92/85/80/62%; mass build-aware 69% within 25%); Physics 101 on disk as the control corpus (not redistributed: no licence). Export: src/simready/usd_physics.py with provenance attributes (its invented static = 1.2 x dynamic must be tagged 'default'; friction re-authored as sqrt(mu) for PhysX 'multiply' or explicit MuJoCo pairs). Baselines: scripts/f14_llm_outcomes.py and the gateway (Claude/GPT/Gemini) for the VLM routes in the pipelines' own prompt formats; scripts/f13_wan.py as the neural world-model row. Scene: blender_city.py + GSO/PolyHaven props and the 13 project assets for the outcome-flip audit (one object active at a time, so the all-pairs kernel needs no broadphase). src/gpu.py to hold one card only while computing.
recommendation.differentiable_physics_role: Stated per clip class and per contact type, never in the title unless it earns it. TIER 1, certified today: the tape through one body on a plane for mu (d(slide)/d(mu) -0.5448 vs FD -0.5453) and for damping through a plane impact (d(apex)/d(alpha) tape/FD 0.998–1.053 flat, 0.97–1.17 edge landings at >= 420 substeps; sign flips at 100 substeps and dead cd, so coarse substeps are forbidden). Load-bearing uses on this path: per-clip inversion of non-closed-form observables with 6–10 unknowns including nuisances (post-impact tumble of blocks, topple-with-slide, rolling clips), joint fits with shared parameters over hundreds of clips (per-session ramp angle and camera scale, per-material alpha, per-surface stiffness), and the Fisher matrix J^T J per clip that turns rule 1 from a manual sweep per probe into a reported quantity with a prescription for the next clip. Honest caveat: FD at 6–10 parameters costs seconds per clip, so here the tape is minutes-not-hours convenience plus bookkeeping; the Fisher idea is textbook (ASID, 2411.10935, 2109.08815). TIER 2, the engine claim, gated: gradients through sustained frictional mesh–mesh contact. Gap scout 3's primary-source read establishes that no shipped engine has them with FD validation (Newton 1.4: narrow phase and normals frozen, tested on sphere/box only; Nimble: dn/dq = 0 for meshes, no friction gradient, FD used only as a timing baseline; DiffMJX: five primitive pairs, mesh–mesh 'not relevant'; Dojo: point/sphere/capsule vs flat; Ostrich: body-vs-terrain, e = 0, FD-in-CI numbers 0.02–1.6% but code unreleased; Jade: mesh–mesh CCD with 'rounding approximation', code unreleased; MJX convex-only; Genesis undefined on some paths), that nobody validates the glancing vs sustained regimes separately, and that nobody exposes gradients through the contact assignment (which face/edge is in contact). This project's measured defect — g0c: FD d(x_A)/d(mu_B) = -0.385 vs tape -0.032 with the total right, and one adjoint component exploding at the stiff setting — sits in exactly that hole, and the kernel's mu_eff is symmetric in form, so the asymmetric split is a lost or attenuated adjoint term on the pair path (the ground route survives), which is localisable by launching the pair kernel alone on a frozen configuration and comparing d(force)/d(mu_j) per launch against FD, and by the symmetric-pair invariant (two identical bodies, equal mu, no plane: d/dmu_A must equal d/dmu_B). The published templates are DiffMJX's contacts-from-distance (straight-through pre-contact gradients in the backward pass only) and Ostrich's IFT adjoint with O(1) memory; Suh et al.'s bundled gradients (N ~ 100 rollouts) are the fallback where the contact-assignment non-differentiability (the tape picks one face at a corner where FD averages three) is fundamental rather than a bug. Gate: sustained-contact pair gradients within 10–20% of central FD and passing the symmetric-pair invariant within three weeks of diagnosis; pass -> strike/stack/push probes enter the capture and the engine result is a headline contribution in a documented hole; fail -> the regime map (gradient error vs contact duration and approach angle, at both rigs) is reported as a finding, every observable stays one object against a plane, and the word 'differentiable' is dropped from the title. TIER 3, where gradients never buy anything, said plainly: a sliding block (closed form; p4's sweep is exact to 0.005 in mu), a sphere's rebound (two closed-form routes), mass (a scale). Further caveats carried into the write-up: the forward rotational response to corner impacts is not converged in substeps (P3 skeptic) and no convergence criterion for polyhedral corner impacts exists anywhere (gap scout 3: LIGGGHTS/PFC rules are sphere-only), so 6-DoF fits are restricted to clip classes whose forward model is shown to converge first (rule 2); the velocity exponent p in e = 1 - alpha v^p is NOT in the kernel (p = 1 at src/sim/mesh_contact.py) and the literature offers no single exponent to adopt (Hunt-Crossley linear near e = 1, Kuwabara-Kono v^1/5 for a different kernel, PFC constant), so restitution is reported at a stated reference impact speed as DEM practice does, and any kernel change triggers rule-5 revalidation of e(alpha, v). Every exported fit carries its tape-vs-FD agreement on its own clip class.
recommendation.scale_path: Scale here is materials x surfaces x impact speeds, catalogue coverage, and — if the engine gate passes — contact TYPE (object-on-plane to object–object), not square metres; the path is stated without the city. Milestone 1 (weeks 1–3): on-disk week (gradient records, handbook route, pair-adjoint regime map and diagnosis), then 10 objects on the user's own reference board — the instrument gate. Milestone 2 (weeks 4–8): ~40 weighed objects (spheres, blocks, cans, cups, mugs, bricks, a cone, a bin; two sizes of several materials for the mass-independence invariant; two known-CoM-offset test objects) on 3 surfaces (board, laminate, concrete paver), slides at 2 tilts x 5, drops at 2–3 heights x 5–10, topple nudges on a high-grip mat where the object can topple; ~1,000 clips; optionally 10 objects per clip on an AprilTag-bordered board once a tag readout exists (P3's lever, ~1 day of OpenCV); a reference pair re-slid each session to track wear drift (MIT Push: -11 to -22% after 100 pushes); if the engine gate passed, +~150 clips of reference-ball strikes, two-block stacks and tracked-pusher shoves on the same objects. Milestone 3 (weeks 9–10): the library — rows with IQR; factorisation tested as the k = 1 product rule vs the k = 2 proxy scheme of arXiv 2604.24188; bridge to the Physics 101 rows via overlapping materials only if their ratios agree within the trial IQR (p1's cardboard size dependence says they may not); USD/MJCF export authored in each engine's combine convention; engine-portability check of the exported drops/slides in Newton-MuJoCo and PhysX, reported per engine as Acosta's three-frictions result requires. Milestone 4 (weeks 11–13): the benchmark and audit; catalogue coverage = fraction of PhysXNet / UniPhys-40K / RoboCasa material strings with a measured row; the outcome-flip audit over 50–200 GSO/PolyHaven props in blender_city with open-loop push/drop/topple primitives, one object at a time. What 'beyond rooms' honestly means at day 90: the concrete/asphalt/paver rows that street-scale simulators (UrbanVerse, URBAN-SIM, Vid2Sim) fill by VLM or texture label now have measured counterparts with uncertainty, and the same rows serve a 100k-asset library at zero marginal cost through USD. What it never becomes without new work: a 1,000-body interactive street in Newton (needs a broadphase and ordered reductions; the kernel is all-pairs nV x N and nondeterministic at the stiff setting), a reconstructed city (someone else's problem: UrbanVerse/Vid2Sim/HUGSIM), or a robot result (needs a partner lab). If the engine gate passes, the longer-horizon scale axis is multi-body identification from video (stacks, strikes, pushes — gripper/object contact once a tracked pusher stands in for a finger), with an upstream contribution of the validated pair adjoint to Newton as the delivery path.
first_90_days: Week 1 (on disk, zero capture — the first experiment): record the gradient checks that exist only in reviewers' scratchpads as scripts/g1_impact_grad.py + docs/results/g1_*.json (d(apex)/d(alpha) tape vs FD at both rigs, flat and edge landings, substep convergence of the rotational response); add the never-run handbook-friction-table route and a leave-one-MATERIAL-out route to e1_heldout.py and report them on the existing ladder with a paired sign test over 70 objects; build the pair-adjoint regime map (sustained push, glancing 3/5 cm, head-on strike, stacked settle; d(x_A)/d(mu_A), d/d(mu_B), d/d(cd), d/d(x_B0); both rigs; vs contact duration and approach angle) from g0b/g0c/g0d, run the symmetric-pair invariant, and launch the pair kernel alone on frozen configurations to locate the lost adjoint term (rule 6); make p2's camera scale and ramp angle per-clip inputs; write a real-video ball/blob tracker (src/track/balls.py is tuned to rendered balls); buy/borrow a 240 fps phone (verify true 240 fps and exposure), tripod, inclinometer app, kitchen scale, callipers, a plywood board and a hard reference plate; run a targeted search for any 2025–26 phone-video (mu, e, CoM) table the scouts' exhausted budgets may have missed.

Weeks 2–3 (first capture): instrument gate on 10 objects on the own reference board: 5 spheres/near-spheres x 3 heights x 10 drops (two routes, g-scale check), 8 block-like objects of 4 materials at 2 tilts x 5 slides (two-angle invariant); the bridge number to the Physics 101 rows; kill decision on the instrument at day 21. In parallel (weeks 2–4): the pair-adjoint fix attempt under the 3-week engine gate, with DiffMJX's contacts-from-distance and Ostrich's IFT adjoint as templates and bundled gradients as the fallback; decision at day 28.

Weeks 3–4: contact-law check: alpha vs drop height and vs object size (two sizes per material) on spheres and flat-landing blocks; decide between a velocity exponent in the kernel (rule-5 revalidation) and e reported per reference impact speed (DEM practice); per-class tape-vs-FD gate and forward-convergence check decide tape vs FD/CEM for each clip class; write the Fisher/Laplace reporting; verify GAUGE's Hugging Face access and PhysVid's release and run both as external instrument checks.

Weeks 5–8: capture at scale: ~40 weighed objects x 3 surfaces (board, laminate, concrete paver), ~1,000 clips; a reference pair re-slid each session; topple nudges on a high-grip mat for objects that can topple plus two known-offset CoM test objects; irregular objects get direct-route e per impact class only; optional multi-object tagged board after a 1-day ArUco readout; LLM names material and build per object (cached); if the engine gate passed, add ~150 clips of weighed-reference-ball strikes, two-block stacks and tracked-pusher shoves; in parallel start the PhysX-Anything and UniPhysGen environments (3–4 weeks of installs, <= 2 shared A6000s).

Weeks 9–10: library v1 with IQR and provenance; held-out-object and held-out-surface tests (own objects) and the held-out-trial-type test (fit on drops, predict the post-bounce slide; fit on slides, predict stay/slide at the second tilt; if the engine gate passed, fit on slides+drops, predict the strike and the stack); factorisation test (k = 1 vs k = 2 proxies); bridge test to the Physics 101 rows; USD/MJCF export authored as sqrt(mu) under PhysX 'multiply' or explicit MuJoCo pairs, e at a stated reference speed, provenance as custom attributes; reproduce the measured drops and slides from the exported files in Newton-MuJoCo (and PhysX if Isaac Sim is reachable) and report the per-engine disagreement.

Weeks 11–12: the benchmark: scorer for f(image, mesh) -> (mu, rho, e) on held-out real motion in trajectory RMS, outcome accuracy and outcome-flip rate; routes: oracle, measured table, LLM-name + table, LLM number, handbook table, VLM-range midpoint (UrbanVerse/EmbodiedGen prompt formats), PhysX-Anything density -> mass, PhysX-Anything -> UniPhysGen friction, BEHAVIOR-1K lookup, Isaac Lab/SimReady defaults; the outcome-flip audit over 50–200 props with OPEN-LOOP push/drop/topple primitives at the table's own IQR bounds (closed-loop policy evaluation is insensitive by SIMPLER's Table X and is not the test).

Week 13: write-up with every kill-test number stated whichever way it fell and every plot carrying its noise floor; the engine result reported as a headline if it passed and as a regime-map finding if it did not; release tracks, splits, scorer, table, USD/MJCF writer and a Physics 101 download script (not the clips); ask the Physics 101 authors about derived-data terms; if the pair adjoint passed, prepare the upstream contribution to Newton.
recommendation.first_experiment: Week 1, on disk, zero capture, one A6000 for a few hours, two decisive numbers plus a map. (A) Does measuring beat looking up? Add a handbook-friction-table route (material pair named by the LLM's existing e1 material labels, values from a standard engineering friction table) to scripts/e1_heldout.py and score it exactly as e1 does on the 70 held-out objects / 359 trials: held-out median trajectory RMS against the measured table's 2.55 mm and the dataset median's 4.40 mm, and a paired sign test over the 70 objects (handbook vs measured). If p > 0.05 and the medians are within 0.5 mm, the friction half of the capture is cancelled before a single clip is shot. (B) Where does the pair adjoint fail, and is it a bug? From scripts/g0b/g0c/g0d, build the regime map: tape vs central FD for d(x_A)/d(mu_A), d(x_A)/d(mu_B), d(x_A)/d(cd_B) and d(x_A)/d(x_B,0) in four configurations (sustained push 0.6 s, glancing strike at 3 and 5 cm offset, head-on strike, two-block stack settling) at both rigs, tabulated against contact duration and approach angle; then the rule-6 isolation — launch pair_contact_mesh alone on a frozen two-body configuration and compare d(force on A)/d(mu_B) per launch against FD, and the symmetric-pair invariant (two identical cubes, equal mu, no plane: d/dmu_A must equal d/dmu_B by symmetry). The numbers it yields: today's known point is FD -0.385 vs tape -0.032 for d(x_A)/d(mu_B) with the total right; the experiment returns the per-launch ratio that localises the lost term, the symmetric-pair asymmetry (must be 1.00), and the full ratio table by regime — a map gap scout 3 found no engine paper reports. (C) Side output: scripts/g1_impact_grad.py recording the plane-impact adjoint numbers the reviewers measured (0.998/1.002/1.053 flat; 0.97–1.17 edge; sign flip at 100 substeps) into docs/results, which currently holds no gradient result at all. The first CAPTURE experiment follows in weeks 2–3 (the 10-object instrument gate: sphere e repeat-IQR <= 0.05, two-route agreement <= 0.03, free-fall g spread <= 5%, e span >= 0.3 across materials, two-angle mu agreement <= 0.03, the Physics-101 bridge ratios).
recommendation.kill_test: Pre-registered now, six parts, each ending a specific claim. (0) Engine: if within three weeks of the week-1 diagnosis the pair adjoint under sustained frictional contact cannot be brought within 10–20% of central FD AND pass the symmetric-pair invariant, or if the diagnosis shows the lost term is the contact-assignment non-differentiability rather than a bug, the engine claim is dropped, the regime map is published as a finding, every observable stays one object against a plane, and 'differentiable' leaves the title. (1) Instrument: if on spheres the repeat IQR of e exceeds 0.10, or the two routes disagree by more than 0.05 in median, or free-fall g spreads more than +/-10% within a session, a phone at 240 fps is not a restitution instrument; no further capture happens, the restitution and CoM columns are dropped, and the direction collapses to the runner-up (on-disk benchmark/audit). (2) Value of measuring over looking up: if the handbook-friction-table route assigned by LLM-named material pair matches the measured table on held-out Physics 101 motion (paired sign test over 70 objects, p > 0.05, and median RMS within 0.5 mm of 2.55 mm), measured friction buys nothing over a handbook and the friction claim is withdrawn; the programme keeps only restitution, CoM-by-build, the engine track and the benchmark. (3) Transfer: fitted values are exported only if the held-out-trial-type prediction (fit on drops -> predict the post-bounce slide; fit on slides -> predict stay/slide at the second tilt; if the engine gate passed, predict the strike and the stack) lands within 1.5x the object's trial-to-trial spread for >= 2/3 of objects and alpha from one height predicts the other within the repeat IQR under the fitted law at a stated reference speed (not under a constant e, which the HC law forbids); otherwise the values are effective constants of one condition, are tagged as such and are not exported. (4) Differentiable claim per clip class: the tape gradient must agree with central FD within 20% at the fitting substep count and the forward observable must be converged in substeps; a class that fails is fitted by FD/CEM and loses the word 'differentiable' in the write-up. (5) The field-level null: if the outcome-flip audit on open-loop push/drop/topple primitives shows that replacing VLM/handbook values with measured values flips fewer than ~10% of outcomes across 50–200 props, parameter accuracy does not matter at the outcome level for these primitives; that negative is published as the result and the library is not scaled further. (6) Engine portability: if the exported values reproduce the measured drops and slides in Newton-MuJoCo/PhysX no better than the engines' defaults (Acosta's three-frictions effect), the table is labelled engine-specific-effective and the 'drop-in replacement for VLM numbers' claim is withdrawn in favour of per-engine calibration.
nearest_prior_and_difference: Physics 101 (Wu et al., BMVC 2016) and Galileo (NeurIPS 2015): the same ramp footage, MCMC/Bullet fits, split-by-object outcome prediction (moving distance rho 0.33, bounce 0.23) — difference: metric trajectory error through an engine validated to <1 mm on these clips, repeat-trial floors and invariant admission tests, scoring of ASSIGNMENT routes incl. 2025–26 generators, outcome-flip rate as the unit, and restitution at 240 fps that 30 fps could not give; Physics 101 is our on-disk control, not our contribution.

SMASH (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016), Vid2Param (RA-L 2020), Hofherr et al. (WACV 2023), Delta-ynamics (2605.20576), DiffSDFSim (3DV 2021): restitution/friction/mass ratio from uninstrumented consumer video, n = 1–3 with measured truth or none — difference: n ~ 40 objects x 3 surfaces x 3 speeds with weighed masses, invariant gates, held-out-trial-type and held-out-surface validation, exact-mesh contact, and the benchmark as the product; cited as the method's antecedents.

Nimble (RSS 2021), Dojo (2203.00806), DiffMJX (2506.14186, ICLR 2026), Ostrich (2609.08800), Jade (2309.04710), DiffSDFSim, Newton 1.4 differentiable_contacts.py, MJX, Genesis: the differentiable-contact engines — difference: none ships FD-validated gradients through sustained frictional mesh–mesh narrow phase (Nimble freezes mesh normals and has no friction gradient; Newton freezes the narrow phase and normals, tests sphere/box; DiffMJX modifies five primitive pairs; Dojo has no meshes; Ostrich is body-vs-terrain with e = 0; Jade/Ostrich code unreleased); our pair kernel is symmetric in form with a localisable defect and an FD oracle, and the deliverable is the fixed adjoint plus a regime map (gradient error vs contact duration and approach angle) nobody reports; DiffMJX's contacts-from-distance and Ostrich's IFT adjoint are the templates we borrow, Suh et al.'s bundled gradients the fallback.

GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948): measured mu and e for 3–4 rigid materials with 180 Hz mocap fed INTO Isaac/Genesis/Newton; stock Newton under-predicts slope-slider acceleration (wood 2.06 vs 2.58 m/s^2) and fails bouncing ball 22.7x; never tests an assignment route — difference: assignment is the object of the test, a phone replaces mocap at ~10x the materials and outdoor surfaces, our p4/p7/p8 contact results are compared on its tasks, and its trajectories are an external instrument check (access to be verified: gated per one scout, public per another).

Acosta, Yang & Posa, RA-L 2022 (arXiv 2110.00541): law-vs-parameter diagnosis on 550 real cube tosses across Drake/MuJoCo/Bullet, the same cube identified at mu 0.10/0.22/0.36 — difference: everyday materials across speeds and surfaces in Newton/Warp with identified parameters, and the per-engine portability check their result makes mandatory for any exported table; cited up front.
EKFPhys (3DV 2024, 2309.15703): differentiable LCP engine + RGB-D, 4 YCB objects, friction only, mocap-tilt truth — difference: RGB only, restitution and CoM added, many objects, transfer tests.

NeRF2Physics (CVPR 2024), PUGS, GaussianProperty, PhysGS (CVPR 2026), Asset2Sim (2605.19136), UniPhysGen (2607.13586), Kaedim YAM harness (2610.00731): LLM/VLM names material -> table/interval, validated on pad meters, ABO masses, grasps, simulator stability or confounded policy-level correlation — difference: validated against the object's own real motion, held out, with an outcome-flip rate; their routes are rows in our benchmark.

SIMPLER (CoRL 2024) Table X, arXiv 2606.20712, BayesSim (RSS 2019), DROPO (2201.08434), ASID (ICLR 2024): the evidence on whether object parameters matter — SIMPLER's closed-loop evaluation is insensitive across an 8x x 8x sweep, 2606.20712 finds no mass/friction adaptation signal, while open-loop tasks (Fetch Slide, puck, rod balancing 6/9 vs 0/9) are parameter-set — difference: our outcome-flip audit is run on open-loop primitives, where the question is live, and reports the number none of them does.

Wang & Wang (arXiv 2604.24188): tribometer pair-friction factorisation with >= 2 proxy materials — difference: we test the k = 1 product rule against their k = 2 scheme on object slides rather than a tribometer, and adopt theirs if k = 1 fails.

MIT Push (1604.04038) and Omnipush (1910.00618): measured friction variability (per-surface sd 0.016–0.064, -11 to -22% wear drift) and mass-distribution effects on pushing with a 3.4–11.7 mm repeatability floor — difference: we adopt their floor and drift as the noise model (reference pair per session) rather than claiming a precision below it.

PhysVid (2510.02311), IRIS (2603.16432), WorldBench (2601.21282): measured-GT real-video datasets scoring estimators or generators — difference: closed loop through the engine on held-out objects; PhysVid's 5 x 6 dynamometer matrix is a free external check and the multi-surface axis Physics 101 lacks.

Hunt & Crossley 1975, Kuwabara-Kono 1987 / Brilliantov 1996, Mueller-Heckel PRL 2013, Itasca PFC / LIGGGHTS DEM calibration: the restitution-law literature — difference: none; we adopt DEM practice (calibrate at the impact speed of use, report e at that speed) and state that choosing an exponent is kernel selection, not a measurement.

NVIDIA SimReady / UsdPhysicsMaterialAPI, PhysX combine modes, Isaac Lab RigidBodyMaterialCfg, MuJoCo <pair>, Genesis Rigid: the delivery containers — difference: none; we author into them exactly (sqrt(mu) under multiply or explicit pairs; scalar e at a stated speed; provenance as custom attributes) instead of pretending a pair atlas or an e(v) law has a slot.
what_to_stop_doing: Stop every use of generative/predictive video models and LLM numbers as a supervision signal (Cosmos judge, V-JEPA surprise V2–V4, FPT, MYRIAD, Wan, LLM numeric physics): the negatives are externally corroborated (PhysVid, PokeWorld, ACWM-Phys, WRBench, GAUGE, WorldBench, Principia) and need no re-run; keep them only as baseline rows.
Stop the render-and-read-off-video O-track (classifier readouts o10/o12/o13/o14): retired, superseded by direct real-footage measurement; do not re-validate them on the fixed simulator.

Stop ASSUMING body-body contact gradients either way: do not build probes on them (g0c/g0d: tape -0.03 vs FD -0.38 under a sustained push, 1.7–2x off for strikes), and do not write them off as 'a different project' — gap scout 3 shows the hole is real and unfilled; give the diagnosis a bounded three-week budget with a pre-registered FD gate and let the number decide.

Stop the 'beyond rooms' / persistent-world / determinism deliverables (P1's world API, P2's 1,000-object street): the kernel is all-pairs nV x N with no broadphase and nondeterministic at the stiff setting; passing a look-away protocol 'by construction' is not a contribution.
Stop the learned appearance-to-physics model (M2P): Physics 101 built it on the same dataset in 2016.
Stop the soft-body and cloth probes (soft press diverges; the differentiable-MPM lane — PhysTwin, MOSIV, Vid2Sim, MonoPhysics, EgoPhys — is crowded and ahead).

Stop fitting more Physics 101 ramp slides for their own sake and stop scoring generic routes on the 20-degree board (its response is flat above mu = 0.364): it is the on-disk control, not the benchmark.

Stop exporting physics the consumers cannot ingest as written: a geometric-mean pair rule (no PhysX/MuJoCo/Genesis combine mode is a geometric mean — author sqrt(mu) under 'multiply' or explicit pairs), an e(v) law (every schema takes a scalar — state the reference speed), a measured table without the engine it was fitted under (Acosta: one cube, three engines, three frictions), and an invented static = 1.2 x dynamic (tag it 'default').

Stop advertising 'differentiable' as the headline until a clip class or the pair adjoint demonstrably needs the tape; stop claiming per-parameter CIs or Fisher identifiability as novel (ASID, DROPO, 2411.10935, textbook sysID).

Stop claiming 'first' anything: first held-out-object test (Physics 101 2016), first measured table (GAUGE, MIT Push, Omnipush, 2604.24188), first phone restitution (SMASH 2016, physics-education literature), first LLM-name-to-table resolver (NeRF2Physics, Asset2Sim, UniPhysGen, Kaedim), first engine-vs-real-impact diagnosis (Acosta 2022).

Stop scheduling one researcher for 1,600–3,600 clips plus photogrammetry of 150–250 objects: the 90-day corpus is ~1,000 clips of ~40 objects (+~150 object–object clips only if the engine gate passes), primitives by callipers, irregular objects by direct-route readouts only.

Stop making impact claims on closed-loop policy evaluation: SIMPLER's Table X shows it is insensitive to an 8x x 8x object-physics sweep; the only live question is outcome flips on open-loop primitives, and that is the audit to run.
recommendation.what_would_change_this: Six things, each with the evidence that would trigger it. (a) If the week-1 handbook-table route matches the measured table on held-out Physics 101 motion (p > 0.05), measured friction is not worth capturing: narrow to restitution + CoM-by-build + the engine track + the benchmark, or switch to the runner-up. (b) If the day-21 instrument gate fails on spheres (IQR(e) > 0.10, routes > 0.05 apart, g spread > 10%), the phone is not an instrument at 240 fps either: switch to the runner-up (on-disk benchmark/audit, workshop-length) and keep only the engine track if it passed. (c) If the pair adjoint passes its FD gate under sustained contact and the symmetric-pair invariant within three weeks, the headline changes: the engine result (FD-validated gradients through sustained frictional mesh–mesh contact, the regime map, and multi-body identification of strikes/stacks/pushes from phone video) becomes the method contribution and the measurement/benchmark becomes its validation — a riskier, more differentiable paper in a hole DiffMJX lists as future work and Ostrich/Jade have not shipped; conversely, if the week-1 diagnosis shows the lost term is the contact-assignment non-differentiability (one face vs three at a corner) rather than a bug, the engine track stops immediately and only the regime map is reported. (d) If a robot lab (SIMPLER/RoboArena-style) agrees to swap in the exported values and report SRCC/replay error on OPEN-LOOP tasks, the robot claim can be made and the venue changes; without it, keep robots out of the claims. (e) If a 2025–26 paper already provides a phone-video, multi-material, multi-surface (mu, e, CoM) table with held-out-motion validation (gap scout 1's proceedings-level sweep of CoRL/RSS/ICRA/IROS/SIGGRAPH Asia/NeurIPS D&B 2026 was NOT performed; Delta-ynamics 2605.20576 is the closest found and lacks measured truth and restitution), the direction narrows to the benchmark/audit, which still has no published counterpart. (f) If the outcome-flip audit returns < ~10% flips on open-loop primitives, the honest conclusion is that VLM/handbook values are good enough at the outcome level for these primitives, and the project should publish that negative and not scale the library; the engine track is unaffected by this result.

runner_up.title: e1-bench on disk: score every assignment route (released generators PhysX-Anything -> UniPhysGen, LLM numbers, handbook tables, VLM-range midpoints, shipped library values) on Physics 101 held-out real motion, with a rule-1 audit of the benchmark itself and outcome accuracy as the unit — the surviving form of [3] (P7 + P5 + P9), no capture, no gradients
runner_up.why_second: It is the cheapest and most certain result in the set (the harness runs today; the first numbers are days away once the generator environments install) and its novelty claim — nobody scores an assignment pipeline by re-simulating its values against held-out real trajectories — was the best-defended in the set and is now confirmed by two gap scouts (no assignment-route benchmark; no published outcome-flip number; no provenance field anywhere). The other alternative — an engine-first paper on the mesh–mesh adjoint alone — was not adversarially tested here and rests on a defect whose cause is unknown until the week-1 diagnosis (rule 6), so it is placed as the conditional pivot in what_would_change_this (c), not as the runner-up. This runner-up is the week-1 control and the week-11 deliverable of the recommendation, not an alternative to it.
runner_up.when_to_prefer_it: Prefer it if (a) no 240 fps phone or capture time is available in the next month, (b) the day-21 instrument gate fails on spheres and the engine gate also fails, (c) the user wants a publishable negative or audit result in 4–6 weeks at workshop / Datasets-and-Benchmarks length (the first real-motion score of released sim-ready generators plus the handbook-vs-measured comparison is such a note), or (d) the week-1 handbook-table route already matches the measured table, in which case measuring friction is not worth the capture and the audit is the whole story.

rejected_framings: City scale / 'very large scale beyond rooms' / 'interactable worlds at scale' — DROP as a target. The physics content of a city-scale world is O(materials x surfaces), which the recommendation measures and exports as USD — city geometry is a solved, separate problem (UrbanVerse, Vid2Sim, HUGSIM, NuRec) this layer plugs into. 'Beyond rooms' survives only as outdoor surfaces (concrete, asphalt, pavers) measured as rows; the scale axis that genuinely grows with the engine track is contact TYPE (object–object), not area.

They carry neither object-specific theta nor persistent state. Keep at most one baseline row (f13_wan.py) and do not build V2–V4 on surprise.

Robots / 'a practical system for robots' — DEFER, with the test now specified. Evidence: no robot; gap scout 2 verified that closed-loop policy evaluation is insensitive to object physics (SIMPLER Table X: r 0.957–0.990 over an 8x mass x 8x friction grid; 2606.20712: 'mass and friction yield no stable adaptation signal') while open-loop tasks are parameter-set (BayesSim Fetch Slide, DROPO puck to 2 cm, ASID 6/9 vs 0/9); the parameters manipulation consumes most (gripper-pad/object friction, object-object contact) need the body-body path that is exactly the gated engine track. The robot-facing deliverable is a USD/MJCF asset with measured values authored in each engine's conventions, DR ranges from measured IQRs and provenance, plus the in-sim open-loop outcome-flip test; a policy claim needs a partner lab and is outside the 90 days.

'Differentiable physics' as the headline — DEMOTE to a stated, per-clip-class role with ONE gated engine claim. Evidence: the tape is validated only through one body on a plane (mu and, this week, damping through impact); the first-tier observables (slides, sphere rebounds) are closed-form; FD at 6–10 parameters costs seconds; the Fisher/Laplace idea is textbook (ASID, 2411.10935, 2109.08815). The single place where gradients would be a contribution rather than a convenience is sustained frictional mesh–mesh contact (gap scout 3: no shipped engine, FD-validated; Newton 1.4 frozen narrow phase; DiffMJX future work; Ostrich/Jade unreleased), where this project's kernel is symmetric in form with a localisable defect — so it is attempted under a 3-week FD gate, not assumed and not dismissed.

'First / nobody has done X' novelty framing — DROP throughout. Evidence from primary sources: Physics 101 (2016) ran split-by-object and cross-scenario transfer on the same data; Galileo (2015) ran stays/slides transfer; SMASH (2016), Vid2Param (2020), Hofherr (2023), Delta-ynamics (2026) identify physics from uninstrumented video; DiffSDFSim (2021) fits restitution through a differentiable sim; NeRF2Physics/PUGS/Asset2Sim/UniPhysGen/Kaedim resolve LLM-named materials to tables; GAUGE/MIT Push/Omnipush/2604.24188 are measured tables; DROPO gives DR ranges from data; Acosta 2022 did the engine-vs-real-impact diagnosis. The contribution is measurement breadth, invariant-based validation, the held-out benchmark of assignment routes, the outcome-flip number, and — if it passes — the mesh–mesh adjoint.

A learned appearance-to-physics predictor (M2P) — DROP. open_questions: Is the pair-adjoint split defect (g0c: FD d(x_A)/d(mu_B) = -0.385 vs tape -0.032, total right, kernel mu_eff symmetric at src/sim/mesh_contact.py:151) a lost adjoint term on the pair path — a bug the week-1 per-launch isolation and symmetric-pair invariant can localise — or the contact-assignment non-differentiability (one face vs three at a corner) that no engine addresses? The answer decides whether the engine track exists.

Can measured values be made engine-portable at all, given Acosta et al. identified one cube at mu 0.10/0.22/0.36 across Drake/MuJoCo/Bullet? The recommendation's per-engine re-simulation check answers it for Newton-MuJoCo and PhysX; if the disagreement is large, the deliverable is per-engine calibration, not a table.

Is restitution a material property or a pair/surface property? Bounce and Learn says the surface dominates; the same factorisation test must run on e as on mu, and the table may end up surface-specific.

Is e(v) monotone for everyday materials over 1.4–2.8 m/s, and should the kernel get a velocity exponent (rule-5 revalidation) or should e simply be reported at a reference impact speed as DEM practice does? Mueller et al. (PRL 2013) report oscillations; Hunt-Crossley, Kuwabara-Kono and the linear dashpot give three different laws.

Does object-parameter accuracy change outcomes at the open-loop primitive level (the SIMPLER / 2606.20712 / BayesSim question)? The outcome-flip audit answers it for push/drop/topple on 50–200 props; a small flip rate is a legitimate negative that would end the library's scaling but not the engine track.

Is the forward rotational response to corner impacts convergent at any affordable substep count (P3 skeptic: angular velocity -4.29/-3.98/-3.81 rad/s at 60/120/240 substeps, cd-gradient sign change), given gap scout 3 found no published convergence criterion for polyhedral corner impacts under penalty contact (all DEM rules are sphere-only)? Until it is, 6-DoF fits of irregular bodies are off the table.

Is GAUGE's dataset publicly reachable (gap scout 1: Hugging Face 401 gated; P3 verdict: public under MIT)? It is the best external instrument check for the slope-slider and bounce tasks and the only place stock Newton has been scored on measured impacts.

How large is within-session friction drift on the user's surfaces (MIT Push: -11 to -22% after 100 pushes; per-surface sd 0.016–0.064), and does a re-slid reference pair per session track it well enough that per-material rows keep a stated shelf life?

Can the user's own reference board be bridged to the Physics 101 rows? p1 found mu falling 0.28 -> 0.21 across nine cardboard cubes of one material (Spearman -0.80, unexplained); if overlap-material ratios do not agree within the trial IQR, the two tables stay separate and the 101-object corpus is only a control.

Which PhysX combine mode should the exported materials assume (precedence is max of the enum AVERAGE<MIN<MULTIPLY<MAX, so a 'multiply' material loses to any partner authored 'max'), and is authoring sqrt(mu) per material under 'multiply' acceptable to Isaac Lab's DR bucket sampling (num_buckets, 64,000-material PhysX limit)?

Does the user have a true (non-interpolated) 240 fps phone with adequate lighting for ~1/1000 s exposure, and how large is rolling-shutter skew at 2–3 m/s in that camera? Both must be measured in week 1, not assumed.

Can monocular 6-DoF pose against a mesh be obtained for non-spherical objects from RGB only (no PnP, projection kernel or photogrammetry path exists in the repo; Hunyuan3D-2's licence excludes South Korea, so TripoSR/TRELLIS or photogrammetry would be needed), and is phone photogrammetry good enough at the contact patch?

What are Physics 101's redistribution terms (no licence is stated anywhere)? The benchmark can ship tracks, splits and a download script, but the authors should be asked before derived data is released.

Was a 2025–26 'phone video to rigid digital twin', multi-material restitution, or mesh–mesh differentiable-contact paper missed? Every skeptic's and scout's search budget was exhausted before a proceedings-level 2026 sweep (CoRL/RSS/ICRA/IROS/SIGGRAPH Asia/NeurIPS D&B); Delta-ynamics (2605.20576) and Ostrich (2609.08800) are the closest found — a targeted search is a day-1 task, and Ostrich/Jade code releases should be re-checked monthly.

Will PhysX-Anything -> UniPhysGen actually run end to end on 7 cm Physics 101 objects (transformers 4.50 pin, Sonata/Pointcept stack, an untested mesh -> segmented-point-cloud hand-off), and is scoring furniture-scale generators on small lab objects a fair test or a distribution-mismatch complaint waiting to happen?

If the pair adjoint is fixed, what is the right real-data validation for mesh–mesh identification without mocap — weighed-reference-ball strikes and two-block stacks from phone video, GAUGE's Newton's-cradle trials (sphere–sphere, measured e, 180 Hz mocap), or the ContactNets toss on a non-planar surface — and which of these has truth independent of the simulator?
