Does a handbook friction table assigned by LLM-named material pair already match the measured table on held-out Physics 101 motion? Never run (verified: e1 routes are oracle/material/pipeline/LLM-direct only); it is the single cheapest experiment that could end the friction half of the programme.

Can measured values be made engine-portable at all, given Acosta et al. identified one cube at mu 0.10/0.22/0.36 across Drake/MuJoCo/Bullet? The per-engine re-simulation check answers it for Newton-MuJoCo and PhysX; if the disagreement is large, the deliverable is per-engine calibration, not a table.

Is restitution a material property or a pair/surface property? Bounce and Learn says the surface dominates; the same factorisation test must run on e as on mu, and the table may end up surface-specific.

Is e(v) monotone for everyday materials over 1.4–2.8 m/s, and should the kernel get a velocity exponent (rule-5 revalidation) or should e be reported at a reference impact speed as DEM practice does? Mueller et al. (PRL 2013) report oscillations; Hunt-Crossley, Kuwabara-Kono and the linear dashpot give three different laws.

Does object-parameter accuracy change outcomes at the open-loop primitive level (the SIMPLER / 2606.20712 / BayesSim question)? The outcome-flip audit answers it for push/drop/topple on 50–200 props; a small flip rate is a legitimate negative that ends the library's scaling but not the engine track.

Is the forward rotational response to corner impacts convergent at any affordable substep count (angular velocity -4.29/-3.98/-3.81 rad/s at 60/120/240 substeps, cd-gradient sign change), given no published convergence criterion exists for polyhedral corner impacts under penalty contact (all DEM rules are sphere-only)? Until it is, 6-DoF fits of irregular bodies are off the table.

Is GAUGE's dataset publicly reachable (gap scout 1: Hugging Face 401 gated; P3 verdict: public under MIT)? It is the best external instrument check for the slope-slider and bounce tasks and the only place stock Newton has been scored on measured impacts.

How large is within-session friction drift on the user's surfaces (MIT Push: -11 to -22% after 100 pushes; per-surface sd 0.016–0.064), and does a re-slid reference pair per session track it well enough that per-material rows keep a stated shelf life?

Can the user's own reference board be bridged to the Physics 101 rows? p1 found mu falling 0.28 -> 0.21 across nine cardboard cubes of one material (Spearman -0.80, unexplained); if overlap-material ratios do not agree within the trial IQR, the two tables stay separate and the 101-object corpus is only a control.

Which PhysX combine mode should the exported materials assume (precedence is max of the enum AVERAGE<MIN<MULTIPLY<MAX, so a 'multiply' material loses to any partner authored 'max'), and is authoring sqrt(mu) per material under 'multiply' compatible with Isaac Lab's DR bucket sampling (num_buckets, 64,000-material PhysX limit)?

Does the user have a true (non-interpolated) 240 fps phone with adequate lighting for ~1/1000 s exposure, and how large is rolling-shutter skew at 2–3 m/s in that camera? Both must be measured in week 1, not assumed.

Can monocular 6-DoF pose against a mesh be obtained for non-spherical objects from RGB only (no PnP, projection kernel or photogrammetry path exists in the repo; Hunyuan3D-2's licence excludes South Korea, so TripoSR/TRELLIS or photogrammetry would be needed), and is phone photogrammetry good enough at the contact patch?

What are Physics 101's redistribution terms (no licence is stated anywhere)? The benchmark can ship tracks, splits and a download script, but the authors should be asked before derived data is released.

Was a 2025–26 'phone video to rigid digital twin', multi-material restitution, or mesh–mesh differentiable-contact paper missed? Every skeptic's and scout's search budget was exhausted before a proceedings-level 2026 sweep (CoRL/RSS/ICRA/IROS/SIGGRAPH Asia/NeurIPS D&B); Delta-ynamics (2605.20576) and Ostrich (2609.08800) are the closest found — a targeted search is a day-1 task, and Ostrich/Jade code releases should be re-checked monthly.

Will PhysX-Anything -> UniPhysGen actually run end to end on 7 cm Physics 101 objects (transformers 4.50 pin, Sonata/Pointcept stack, an untested mesh -> segmented-point-cloud hand-off), and is scoring furniture-scale generators on small lab objects a fair test or a distribution-mismatch complaint waiting to happen?

If the pair adjoint is fixed, what is the right real-data validation for mesh–mesh identification without mocap — weighed-reference-ball strikes and two-block stacks from phone video, GAUGE's Newton's-cradle trials (sphere–sphere, measured e, 180 Hz mocap), or the ContactNets toss on a non-planar surface — and which of these has truth independent of the simulator?

ranking.title: [1] Phone instrument: per-object / per-clip identification of (mu, e(v), CoM-by-build) through the validated plane-contact tape, validated by invariants and held-out trial type — MERGED from P10 'A phone is a physics instrument' + P6 'Phone-to-twin per-object' (same idea, same capture, same fitter)
ranking.why: Highest total, but note what that total is: 4.7/10. Every proposal in the set was refuted on novelty, so the ranking is a comparison of surviving forms. This one survives best because its feasibility is the strongest in the set (two independent skeptics RAN the day-1 gate instead of arguing it: d(apex)/d(alpha) tape vs central FD = 0.998/1.002/1.053 at BOUNCE_RIG, 0.999–1.17 at the tilt rig incl. edge landings, mass-null exact, 0.3 s per clip) and because the thing it measures — restitution across materials x surfaces x speeds, CoM where an object topples, friction on the user's own surfaces — is the column no catalogue, benchmark or pipeline carries. Method novelty is nil (SMASH 2016 did restitution and mass ratio from iPhone 240 fps; Hofherr WACV 2023 did friction from one ordinary video; DiffSDFSim fitted restitution of a real tennis ball through a differentiable sim; Delta-ynamics 2026 did 235 iPhone clips). What survives is a measurement-and-validation contribution: n >= 40 objects with weighed masses, invariant gates, held-out-trial-type prediction (fit drops, predict slides), per-clip Fisher identifiability used prescriptively, and e(v) with the Hunt-Crossley form tested rather than assumed. Impact is capped (restitution has few consumers; MuJoCo has none, PhysX defaults it to 0) and the proposals' own kill criteria were misdesigned (the two-height invariant on e tests the simulator's e ~ 1 - alpha v law, p8: 0.70 -> 0.54 at alpha 0.4). Differentiable physics is genuinely used for multi-parameter per-clip inversion and joint shared-parameter fits, but FD at 6–10 parameters costs seconds, so it is convenience plus identifiability bookkeeping, not capability. P1's scene-level batching and P6's robot partnership are dropped from the merged form.
refuted_by: SMASH, Monszpart et al., SIGGRAPH Asia 2016 (arXiv 1603.08984): restitution + mass ratio from consumer 120/240 fps iPhone collision video, no markers
Hofherr et al., WACV 2023 (arXiv 2204.14030): friction of a real sliding block from a single ordinary-camera video by gradient fit, validated against ruler measurements
DiffSDFSim, Strecke & Stueckler, 3DV 2021 (arXiv 2111.15318): restitution + friction + shape of a real bouncing tennis ball through a differentiable LCP simulator (RealSense, n = 1)
Vid2Param, RA-L 2020 (arXiv 1907.06422): restitution and drag of real balls from video via a sim-trained estimator
Delta-ynamics (arXiv 2605.20576): 235 real rigid-body videos, 155 at iPhone 210–240 fps, mass/friction/damping inferred for a simulator (no measured truth, no restitution)
EKFPhys (arXiv 2309.15703): differentiable LCP engine in an EKF, friction of 4 YCB objects with mocap-tilt truth (median 0.025); the proposal's characterisation was accurate
PhysVid (arXiv 2510.02311): real elasticity split over many ball materials (annotated apex heights, oracle Pearson 0.87) — contradicts 'no public dataset holds restitution beyond three materials'
Galileo (NeurIPS 2015) / Physics 101 (BMVC 2016): video-to-physics-engine fits on ramp footage with held-out-object evaluation; restitution already a stated target

Exciting Contact Modes (arXiv 2411.10935) and Heiden et al. ICRA 2022 (arXiv 2109.08815): Fisher information and posteriors from differentiable simulators — the 'J^T J as identifiability' idea is established

Impact lens: restitution is unconsumed (MuJoCo has no e; PhysX/Isaac default 0; manipulation sim2real randomises it); the HC e(v) law (docs/results/p8_alpha.json: e 0.64–0.70 at 0.99 m/s vs 0.50–0.54 at 1.98 m/s at alpha 0.4) makes the cross-height invariant a test of the law, not the camera; no monocular 6-DoF pose path and no meshes for irregular objects exist in the repo

ranking.title: [2] ContactAtlas-240: multi-object tagged tilt-board + drop-station atlas (object x surface) fitted through the differentiable plane contact — P3 (kept separate for its multi-object capture design and atlas output; otherwise the same instrument as [1])
ranking.why: Same instrument as [1] with a throughput lever (10–20 objects per clip on an AprilTag-bordered board) and an atlas rather than a twin as the product. Not refuted on feasibility (the impact adjoint passed at <1% on 60/120/240 substeps), but the skeptic found the forward rotational response to a corner impact is NOT converged in substeps (angular velocity -4.29/-3.98/-3.81 rad/s; its cd-gradient flips sign), so the headline 6-DoF alpha fit of irregular bodies would fit an unconverged model — rule 2 fails before any data. Breadth claims were overstated ('~100x' is ~30x the largest pad-measured set, NeRF2Physics' 15 x 6 iOLab matrix, and GAUGE's calibrated trajectories are public on Hugging Face); simulators ingest per-material scalars, so the 150 x 15 pair table collapses to ~20 numbers at the consumer; the handbook-pair baseline was never run; the phone floor (+/-0.02–0.03 in mu) equals the separation it must resolve. Scale score is the highest among feasible entries because object x surface pairs on outdoor surface sheets is the only breadth axis that is actually reachable. Its multi-object board and tag-based scale/angle readout are absorbed into the recommendation as an optional week-5+ throughput step; its 'first contact table validated on motion of objects it never saw' headline is dropped (Physics 101 did split-by-object in 2016, e1 already did the trajectory version).
refuted_by: GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948): measured mu (inclined plane) and e (air-bearing rail) for wood/plastic/metal/rubber, ~1,560 mocap trials, dataset public on Hugging Face (MIT) — the proposal's 'if the data is public' hedge is moot

NeRF2Physics (arXiv 2404.04242): measured kinetic friction for 15 household objects on 6 surfaces (iOLab pads, 10 trials) — ~90 pairs, larger than the 30 PhysVid pairs the proposal credited as the maximum
Physics 101 (BMVC 2016): split-by-object real-outcome prediction incl. bounce height on 5 drop surfaces; the project's own e1 is already the trajectory-level version
ContactNets (arXiv 2009.11193): AprilTag-tracked 148 Hz contact sysid of a cube, 570 tosses — tagged boards are not new
EKFPhys (arXiv 2309.15703), Galileo (NeurIPS 2015), Dojo (arXiv 2203.00806), Bounce and Learn (arXiv 1904.06827): characterised fairly, but together occupy the method

Feasibility: rotational response of corner impacts not converged in substeps; no AprilTag/ArUco or photogrammetry code in the repo; 150 watertight scanned meshes + ~3,300 clips in days 31–60 is ~2x one researcher's capacity

Impact: consumers ingest per-material scalars (SimReady/PhysX combine modes); no downstream task shown; the handbook-pair baseline missing from e1 (verified: routes are oracle/material/pipeline/LLM-direct only)

ranking.title: [3] Measured material table + assignment benchmark/audit on Physics 101 (e1-bench scorer, LLM-name resolver, library audit, one-slide surface anchor) — MERGED from P7 'HELD-OUT' + P5 'PhysMat' + P9 'Material Ledger' (same table, same e1 harness, same audit, different emphasis)
ranking.why: The best-defended novelty claim in the set (the P7 skeptic's 4.5 was the highest awarded): no primary source scores a parameter-ASSIGNMENT route by re-simulating assigned values against per-object held-out real trajectories with a repeat-trial floor, and nobody has reported a real-motion error for the GPT numbers shipped by 100k-asset libraries. Everything else in the cluster exists: Physics 101 itself ran split-by-object and Galileo ran the 10-from-20-degree stays/slides transfer on the same footage; Kaedim's YAM harness (arXiv 2610.00731, this month) already deploys a per-class friction table and reports policy-level sim-to-real correlation 0.51 -> 0.90; LLM-names-material -> table/interval is NeRF2Physics/PUGS/Asset2Sim/UniPhysGen; the one-slide product-rule anchor is the k = 1 case of arXiv 2604.24188's proxy-embedding factorisation, which finds pair friction needs >= 2 proxies. Feasibility is real (first experiment runs in days; verified today: e1 routes exist, data on disk) but the P7 skeptic measured that the 20-degree benchmark is exactly flat above mu = 0.364 (identical 87.8 mm for every generic route), so it cannot rank generators or LLMs that emit ~0.4 until a steeper ramp is captured — i.e. it needs [1]'s instrument; the pre-registered rule-1 kill test fails as written (28–39/70 vs 40 required); the 8-object sign test needs 8/8; and the ledger's rows are pair values against MIT's board that the user cannot bridge without a self-measured reference board (p1's own 0.28 -> 0.21 cardboard size dependence). Impact is bounded by its own data: material 2.55 mm vs dataset median 4.40 mm vs oracle 1.77 mm (dmu 0.017 vs 0.031 vs 0.010), inside any DR band, and no consumer checks friction numbers today. Zero differentiable physics by its own admission. Ranked below [1]/[2] because it is the scorer and the on-disk control of the recommended direction, not a direction on its own; it is the runner-up.
refuted_by: Physics 101, Wu et al., BMVC 2016: 'Split by object' protocol with held-out-object outcome prediction (moving distance rho 0.33, bounce 0.23) and cross-scenario transfer on this exact footage — the proposals' 'no held-out-object test' claim is false
Galileo, NeurIPS 2015: 10-degree stays/slides prediction from 20-degree videos over 50 Physics 101 objects with a Bullet engine
Kaedim, arXiv 2610.00731 (Oct 2026): VLM-assigned material class -> per-class friction table in a deployed real-to-sim harness, policy-level validation r 0.51 -> 0.90 (confounded)

NeRF2Physics (2404.04242), PUGS (2502.12231), GaussianProperty (2412.11258), Asset2Sim (2605.19136), UniPhysGen (2607.13586): LLM/VLM names material -> property table or interval, validated on ABO-500 masses, iOLab friction, grasps or simulator stability

Wang & Wang, arXiv 2604.24188: 50+-material tribometer library with proxy-embedding pair-friction factorisation, leave-one-material-out R^2 ~ 1, finds >= 2 proxies needed — contradicts the one-slide k = 1 product rule
GAUGE (2608.05948), MIT Push (1604.04038), Omnipush (1910.00618), PhysVid (2510.02311): measured friction/restitution tables with trial variability already exist
DROPO (2201.08434) / BayesSim: DR distributions from real trajectories; Scalable Real2Sim (2503.00370): robot-measured mass/CoM/inertia for sim-ready assets (uncited)

Feasibility (measured today by the P7 skeptic): held-out RMS vs assigned mu is 87.8 mm identically for mu 0.37–0.60; kill test 2 passes on 28–39/70 objects vs 40 required; only 4/70 resolve +/-0.02; PhysX-Anything/UniPhysGen environments are 3–4 weeks of CUDA-extension installs; Physics 101 has no licence for clip redistribution

Impact: effect size 2.55 vs 4.40 mm (dmu 0.014) is inside the 0.3–1.5 friction DR band every consumer applies; SIMPLER <= 15% and arXiv 2606.20712 ('mass and friction yield no stable adaptation signal') leave the 'does it matter' question open; no downstream task in any of the three plans

ranking.title: [4] IMPACT ATLAS: restitution-only from 240 fps drops with an audio second route and a Newton/Warp contact-law card — P8 (a strict subset of [1], kept separate for its audio route and law-vs-parameter claim)
ranking.why: Feasible (the skeptic ran the impact adjoint: tape/FD 0.999–1.17 at 420 substeps, sign flip at 100 substeps and dead cd) and cheap, but it is the restitution column of [1] sold as a programme, and two uncited primary results cut its design: Heckel et al., Phys. Rev. E 93, 032901 (2016) show the sound-timing route is valid only for near-perfect spheres (so audio e_t for blocks and assets is dead on arrival), and Mueller et al., PRL 2013, show e(v) is non-monotone with oscillations (so one scalar alpha per material is a pre-registered risk, not a discovery). The law-vs-parameter diagnosis was done on 550 real cube tosses across Drake/MuJoCo/Bullet by Acosta, Yang & Posa (RA-L 2022, arXiv 2110.00541), uncited. Its single consumer is the project's own kernel (HC = 1.0 in src/sim/mesh_contact.py, alpha read only in src/sim/rigs.py); Newton's shipped solvers take no alpha, MuJoCo has no restitution, PhysX users randomise over handbook e. Survives as a 2–3-week instrument gate inside [1] (spheres only for the audio route; a hard reference plate so steel bearings do not dent the board; a camera-calibration day the plan omits).
refuted_by: Kuwabara & Kono 1987; Labous et al. 1997; Cross, Am. J. Phys. 67:222 (1999); Mueller, Heckel, Sack, Poeschel, PRL 2013 (non-monotone e(v) with oscillations): sphere e(v) by high-speed drop video is a mature measurement literature
Bernstein 1977 (AJP) and Heckel et al., Phys. Rev. E 93, 032901 (2016): the sound-timing restitution route exists and is valid only for near-perfect spheres
Yurata et al., Adv. Powder Technol. 2021; Itasca PFC docs: drop-test calibration of damping/restitution across materials and speeds is routine in DEM

Acosta, Yang, Posa, 'Validating Robotics Simulators on Real-World Impacts', RA-L 2022 (arXiv 2110.00541): 550 real cube tosses, stiffness/damping/friction identified per simulator, conclusion that the engines under-produce restitution (law error) — the proposal's engine-fidelity claim, uncited
DiffSDFSim (2111.15318), PIN-WM (2504.16693), ContactNets/Dojo/DiffMJX: gradient-based restitution identification from real video or tosses already exists
GAUGE (2608.05948) has four rigid materials with 20 trials, not three

Impact: only consumer is the repo's own Hunt-Crossley kernel; settle probe and video readouts that would consume alpha are dead/retired per CLAUDE.md; restitution is a pair property dominated by the surface (Bounce and Learn)

ranking.title: [5] Phone-to-Twin (batched, scene-level): identify every movable object in a filmed space on one Warp tape, persistent world API, four pokes incl. a reference-ball strike — P1 (world-bridge; its per-object core is absorbed into [1], its scene claims are what is ranked here)
ranking.why: The most ambitious design and the one whose pre-registered gate already fails on the project's own measurements: scripts/g0d_grad_free.py gives the body-body cd gradient 1.66x off head-on and 2x off at a 5 cm glancing offset against a 10% gate, so the reference-ball strike (mass ratio, object-ball restitution) reverts to sweeps on day 1 and the 'four parameters in one batched gradient pass' headline cannot stand. The two-height invariant is stated on e, which the project's own Hunt-Crossley calibration makes speed-dependent. No monocular 6-DoF pose path exists; weeks 7–9 ask one researcher to capture 1,600 clips, photogrammetry 150–250 objects, track, identify and ship a deterministic world API at a contact setting measured as nondeterministic (1.5 mm atomic-add). Outdoor floors are unvalidated for an engine with no static friction. Batching 'at 200 objects nobody will sweep' is arithmetically false (FD Jacobians ~11 A6000-hours). The surviving pilot (10–30 primitive objects, 2–3 floors, mu and CoM by tape, alpha and mass by analytic/sweep) is [1].
refuted_by: gradSim (ICLR 2021), DiffSDFSim (3DV 2021), EKFPhys (3DV 2024): differentiable-simulation identification of rigid friction/mass from video exists

Galileo (NeurIPS 2015): mass from a collision with another object, fitted to Physics 101 with Bullet — the proposal's claim that Physics 101 'gives neither restitution nor mass from motion' is unfair on mass
PhysTwin (2503.17973), Spring-Gaus (2403.09434): held-out-interaction validation of an identified twin (deformable)
GAUGE (2608.05948): the variability-normalised real-vs-sim metric
ASID (2404.12308), DROPO (2201.08434): Fisher-information identifiability and DR ranges from real data
DiffSDFSim, Ostrich (2609.08800), DiffMJX (2506.14186), Warp SolverSemiImplicit: 'no shipped engine gives gradients through mesh contact' is an overclaim

Feasibility (run today): g0d body-body/strike gradients 1.66x–2x off a 10% gate; pos0 assignment breaks the tape for s0/v0; CoM and mass are numpy at construction; no PnP/6-DoF pose; the sweep gate (|mu_tape - mu_sweep| <= 0.005) is set at the sweep's own grid half-step and cannot fail

Impact: pair friction against the filmed floor is not what manipulation consumes (gripper/object contact); 'interactable worlds at scale' redefined as object count; the persistent world API is a wrapper consumers would not take over USD

ranking.title: [6] M2P: motion-supervised photo -> (mu, e, build) model trained end-to-end through the simulator on real tracked motion, no parameter labels — P4
ranking.why: Refuted at the thesis level by the dataset it would train on: Physics 101 (Wu et al., BMVC 2016) already built exactly this — LeNet on tracked image patches -> material/volume -> physics-interpreter layers (friction, density, restitution, mass) -> hand-coded differentiable physical laws -> MSE against velocities/distances tracked from the real videos, 'no labels for physical properties', with split-by-object evaluation on held-out objects. Galileo (NeurIPS 2015) is the proposal's 'two-stage baseline' on the same footage. PhysVid's real-motion-adapted V-JEPA-2 reaches 0.73 Pearson on held-out objects AND surfaces, which the proposal omitted in favour of the unadapted 0.21–0.28. Feasible (gradient gate passes, warp+torch co-import works, 64-body batch at 4.6 s / 6.8 GiB) but its decisive number is predetermined: the kill bar (>= 4.4 mm / <= 80%) is cleared 2x by the no-model material table (2.55 mm / 94%), the slides are closed-form, 'stays' are parameter-space bounds a Tobit loss handles without a simulator, and the headroom 2.55 -> 1.77 mm is mostly per-object finish noise a photo cannot carry. What survives — a general exact-mesh simulator in place of analytic laws, shown to beat the analytic/grid surrogate on non-slide clips — is a sub-experiment of [1], not a direction.
refuted_by: Physics 101, Wu et al., BMVC 2016 (phys101.csail.mit.edu/papers/phys101_bmvc.pdf): image network -> physical properties -> differentiable physics laws -> loss on tracked motion, unlabeled, split-by-object; the same architecture on the same dataset
Galileo, NeurIPS 2015: MCMC fit of mass/friction to tracked ramp videos, then LeNet regression to unseen objects — the two-stage baseline, called 'self-supervised' by its authors
PhysVid (2510.02311) Table 1 / App. B.2: V-JEPA-2 fine-tuned on real motion with disjoint objects and surfaces reaches 0.73 Pearson on real friction
Kandukuri et al., GCPR 2020 (2009.08292); Heiden et al., IROS 2022 (2203.10488); DensePhysNet, RSS 2019 (1906.03853); ETH terrain, RA-L 2024 (2408.16567)

Feasibility: bodies that leave the plane return exactly zero gradient (3/3 off-plane cases); Physics 101 ships no meshes for the 24 rolling clips; SSv2 is 19.4 GB behind registration, not 2 GB; the surface corpus does not exist

Impact: kill bar below the existing no-model baseline; per-object finish effects (p1 Spearman -0.80 with cube size) bound the learnable headroom; consumers would adopt the table + namer, not the model

ranking.title: [7] PhysReady: measured material layer + a 200–1,000-object Newton street scene as persistent, deterministic state with a WRBench look-away protocol — P2 (world-bridge; its table/benchmark half is absorbed into [3], its world half is what is ranked here)
ranking.why: The only proposal that tried to honour 'interactable worlds beyond rooms', and the evidence is unambiguous that this project cannot build it in 90 days: src/sim/mesh_scene.py:365 launches pair_contact_mesh over nV x N threads with no broadphase (verified), so a 1,000-body world is ~1e13 BVH queries per simulated second; 'seeded deterministic replays' contradict the project's own 1.5 mm atomic-add nondeterminism at the validated contact setting; capture is undercounted 2.4x (2,400 clips); there is no controllable real excitation for shove or topple without a rig; the week-2 kill test runs over 11 slidable materials whose mu spans only 0.16–0.33. On novelty, UrbanVerse already ships a dynamic street scene with GPT-assigned mass/friction in Isaac Sim, the 6/163 state-feedback gap is already quantified by survey 2608.23070, GAUGE already scores i2v world models on measured trajectories, and passing a persistence protocol 'by construction' is not a contribution. Its restitution export to PhysX is lossy by construction (HC e(v) vs a scalar). The highest scale score in the set, and the least reachable.
refuted_by: UrbanVerse (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.15018): 'assign annotated physical parameters (e.g., mass, friction) and enable rigid-body dynamics, producing stable, interactive scenes' in Isaac Sim; mass validated at 19.58% MAPE vs specs; friction unchecked
Survey arXiv 2608.23070: 6 of 163 world-model implementations expose runtime state — the persistence gap is already published
GAUGE (2608.05948): already scores six image-to-video world models against measured real trajectories
NeRF2Physics / PUGS / GaussianProperty: LLM material naming -> property lookup validated on measured masses and grasps
MIT Push (1604.04038), Omnipush (1910.00618), Physics 101: measured object x surface tables

Feasibility (verified): all-pairs nV x N contact kernel with no broadphase; per-substep state storage; stiff-setting nondeterminism (1.5 mm); p9 topple needs a 40–46 degree rubber-grip ramp, not a hand push; restitution IQR from 6 clips per cell is not an IQR

Impact: numbers 2–3x wrong but outcomes rarely change (its own biggest-risk paragraph; SIMPLER <= 15%); UrbanVerse's 288 ground materials need the same unvalidated naming on the floor side; 'beyond rooms' redefined as materials x floors

recommendation.title: The instrument and the benchmark: phone-measured (mu, e(v), CoM-by-build) of everyday objects on everyday surfaces, validated on held-out real motion, delivered as an assignment library with uncertainty and as a scorer for every assignment route the field ships — merging the surviving forms of [1] (instrument), [3] (benchmark/audit/library), [2] (multi-object capture) and [4] (restitution column)
recommendation.thesis: The physical parameters of simulation assets have to be measured, not asked for: every external model this project tested (Cosmos judge, V-JEPA surprise, FPT, MYRIAD, Wan, LLM numbers) returns a generic prior, and the 2026 literature now says the same (PhysVid, PokeWorld, ACWM-Phys, WRBench, GAUGE, WorldBench). The cheapest validated instrument for measuring them is a 240 fps phone plus this project's exact-mesh plane-contact simulator, which reproduces real slides to 0.4–1.0 mm and whose plane-contact adjoint matches finite differences for friction (g0) and, as of this week's checks, for damping through an impact. The claim is therefore not 'a new identification method' and not 'a world': it is that a material x surface x impact-speed table of friction, restitution and build-aware density/CoM, measured by phone from ~40 everyday objects on three built-environment surfaces with repeat-trial uncertainty, assigned by an LLM that only names the material and build, predicts the real motion of objects and surfaces it never fitted within ~1.5x the per-object oracle, and that the same held-out real motion scores every other assignment route the field uses — released generators, LLM numbers, handbook tables, shipped library values — in the unit a maintainer acts on (outcome-flip rate: stays/slides/topples/bounces), which no one has reported.
recommendation.one_paragraph: Build one thing with three faces. (a) The instrument: a capture protocol (phone on a tripod, 240 fps, inclinometer angle, the object's own measured edge for scale, a reference board + laminate + concrete paver, kitchen-scale mass) and a fitter that turns CoTracker3 tracks into (mu_pair, alpha with a velocity exponent, CoM offset where the object topples) through DiffMeshScene with per-clip nuisances (release time, offset, initial pose/velocity), tape gradients where they pass a per-class FD gate, FD/CEM where they do not, and a per-clip Fisher matrix that states what the clip identifies. Slides and sphere rebounds are closed-form and are read as such; the tape is used only for the non-closed-form classes (post-impact tumble of blocks, topple-with-slide, the rolling clips p2 had to discard) and for joint fits with shared per-session/per-material parameters. (b) The library: material x surface x speed rows with n, IQR and provenance (measured / inferred / default), build-aware density and CoM, exported through src/simready/usd_physics.py as USD physics materials plus MJCF, with the alpha -> PhysX scalar-e mapping stated at an impact speed and checked by reproducing the measured drops in Newton-MuJoCo (pip mujoco) and PhysX if available. (c) The benchmark: the e1 harness generalised to a scorer that takes any f(image, mesh) -> (mu, rho, e) and reports re-simulated trajectory error, stay/slide/topple/bounce outcome accuracy and outcome-flip rate on held-out real objects AND held-out surfaces, with routes = own-trials oracle, measured table, LLM-name + table, LLM direct number, handbook table by material pair (never run; one afternoon), VLM-range midpoint, PhysX-Anything density, PhysX-Anything -> UniPhysGen friction, and shipped library values where metadata is public (BEHAVIOR-1K lookup, SimReady defaults; UrbanVerse/MolmoSpaces only if released). The pre-registered kill tests are the anti-reinvention device: if a handbook table or a released generator already matches the measured table on held-out motion, that is the result, published, and the capture stops.
recommendation.why_now: (1) The video-model route is closed, by this project's controlled negatives and by independent 2026 results (PhysVid: V-JEPA-2 friction r 0.21–0.28; PokeWorld: mass R^2 0.21–0.25; WRBench: 0/23 models persist state; GAUGE/WorldBench: right law form, wrong accelerations) — so parameters must be measured, and the question is only which instrument. (2) The instrument now exists and is validated: Newton with the project's exact-mesh contact reproduces real Physics 101 slides to 0.4–1.0 mm (p4), seating and CoM/inertia defects were fixed and checked against textbook values within 1%, restitution is parameterised mass-independently (p8), and two reviewers ran the plane-impact adjoint this week (tape/FD 0.998–1.05 flat, <= 1.17 edge) — but none of these gradient results is recorded in docs/results (the g0_*.json files there are judge-era), which the first week must fix. (3) The gap is freshly documented from both sides: 2025–26 sim-ready pipelines (PhysX-Anything/Omni, UniPhysGen, EmbodiedGen V2, ManiTwin, UrbanVerse, MolmoSpaces) ship VLM mass/friction at 10^4–10^5 assets validated only against VLM/human labels, spec sheets or policy rankings, while GAUGE (Aug 2026) built the measured-trajectory benchmark without an assignment step, and Kaedim (Oct 2026) deployed a per-class table without measuring it. (4) 240 fps phones make restitution readable where p3 at 30 fps failed (2.7x g spread), and Newton GA inside Isaac Lab plus the SimReady USD schema give a measured, provenance-tagged physics material a delivery path.
recommendation.how_it_uses_our_assets: Simulator: MeshProbeScene exact vertex-plane contact on a tilted plane (gn/gt/gp), seat_on_plane with zero clearance, build-aware mass_points (shell/solid/areal) for CoM and inertia, set_restitution_alpha and src/sim/rigs.py (TILT_RIG/BOUNCE_RIG validated jointly), DiffMeshScene from scripts/g0_grad_check.py as the tape path, src/optimize/lm.py (projected-iterate trust-region LM from o8). Real-footage pipeline: scripts/p1/p2 (CoTracker3 at the 19 px grid, slide/roll/stay classification, two-angle and camera-scale invariants — p2's hard-coded SCALE = 1661 px/m and filename angle must become per-clip inputs), p4 (release-aligned Newton replay), p3's two-route restitution design and g-from-parabola scale check, p5's build-aware mass transfer and product-rule test, p9's time-to-topple CoM probe (read off the simulator at 2 ms) and its rule-1 matrix, o7's sensitivity discipline now computed as a per-clip Fisher matrix. Validation: scripts/e1_heldout.py (held-out protocol, LLM naming cache, routes) and docs/results/e1_heldout.json as the ladder (oracle 1.77 / material 2.55 / pipeline 2.72 / global 4.40 / LLM 7.53 mm; outcome 94/92/85/80/62%; mass build-aware 69% within 25%). Physics 101 on disk as the on-disk control corpus (not redistributed: no licence). Export: src/simready/usd_physics.py with provenance attributes (its invented static = 1.2 x dynamic must be tagged 'default'). Baselines: scripts/f14_llm_outcomes.py and the gateway (Claude/GPT/Gemini) for the VLM routes in the pipelines' own prompt formats; scripts/f13_wan.py as the neural world-model row. Scene: blender_city.py + GSO/PolyHaven props and the 13 project assets for the outcome-flip audit (one object active at a time, so the all-pairs kernel needs no broadphase). src/gpu.py to hold one card only while computing.
recommendation.differentiable_physics_role: Bounded and stated per clip class, never in the title unless it earns it. Validated today: the tape through one body on a plane for mu (d(slide)/d(mu) -0.5448 vs FD -0.5453) and for damping through a plane impact (d(apex)/d(alpha) tape/FD 0.998–1.053 flat, 0.97–1.17 edge landings at >= 420 substeps; sign flips at 100 substeps and dead cd, so coarse substeps are forbidden). Not usable and kept off the path: the body-body adjoint (g0c/g0d: tape -0.03 vs FD -0.38 under a sustained push; 1.66–2x off for strikes) — every observable is one object against a plane. Where gradients are load-bearing: (i) per-clip inversion of non-closed-form observables with 6–10 unknowns including nuisances (post-impact tumble of blocks, topple-with-slide, rolling clips), where a grid is impractical; (ii) joint fits with shared parameters over hundreds of clips (per-session ramp angle and camera scale, per-material alpha, per-surface stiffness: one backward per iteration on the scalar objective where FD needs one rollout per parameter); (iii) the Fisher matrix J^T J per clip, turning rule 1 from a manual sweep per probe into a reported quantity with covariances and a prescription for which clip to shoot next. Where they buy nothing, said plainly: a sliding block (closed form; p4's sweep is already exact to 0.005 in mu), a sphere's rebound (two closed-form routes), mass (a scale). Honest caveats: FD at 6–10 parameters costs seconds per clip, so the tape is minutes-not-hours convenience plus bookkeeping, not capability; the forward rotational response to corner impacts is not converged in substeps (P3 skeptic), so 6-DoF fits are restricted to clip classes whose forward model is shown to converge first (rule 2); the velocity exponent p in e = 1 - alpha v^p is NOT in the kernel (fixed p = 1, src/sim/mesh_contact.py) and adding it triggers rule-5 revalidation of e(alpha, v). Every exported fit carries its tape-vs-FD agreement on its own clip class; a class that fails is fitted by FD/CEM and the write-up says so. If the pair adjoint is ever fixed, the engine becomes a contribution in its own right (no shipped engine gives gradients through mesh-mesh narrow phase) — that is a different project.
recommendation.scale_path: Scale here is materials x surfaces x impact speeds and catalogue coverage, not square metres, and the path is stated without the city. Milestone 1 (weeks 1–2): 10 objects on the user's own reference board — the instrument gate. Milestone 2 (weeks 3–8): ~40 weighed objects (spheres, blocks, cans, cups, mugs, bricks, a cone, a bin; two sizes of several materials for the mass-independence invariant; two known-CoM-offset test objects) on 3 surfaces (board, laminate, concrete paver), slides at 2 tilts x 5, drops at 2–3 heights x 5–10, topple nudges on a high-grip mat where the object can topple; ~1,000 clips, optionally 10 objects per clip on an AprilTag-bordered board once a tag readout exists (P3's lever, ~1 day of OpenCV). Milestone 3 (weeks 9–10): the library — rows with IQR; factorisation tested as k = 1 product rule vs the k = 2 proxy scheme of arXiv 2604.24188; bridge to the Physics 101 rows via overlapping materials only if their ratios agree within the trial IQR (p1's cardboard size dependence says they may not); USD/MJCF export; engine-portability check of the exported drops/slides in Newton-MuJoCo. Milestone 4 (weeks 11–13): the benchmark and audit; catalogue coverage = fraction of PhysXNet / UniPhys-40K / RoboCasa material strings with a measured row; the outcome-flip audit over 50–200 GSO/PolyHaven props in blender_city with push/drop/topple primitives, one object at a time. What 'beyond rooms' honestly means at the end of 90 days: the concrete/asphalt/paver rows that street-scale simulators (UrbanVerse, URBAN-SIM, Vid2Sim) currently fill by VLM or texture label now have measured counterparts with uncertainty, and the same rows serve a 100k-asset library at zero marginal cost through USD. What it never becomes without new work: a 1,000-body interactive street in Newton (needs a broadphase and ordered reductions; the kernel is all-pairs nV x N and nondeterministic at the stiff setting), a reconstructed city (someone else's problem: UrbanVerse/Vid2Sim/HUGSIM), or a robot result (needs a partner lab).
first_90_days: Week 1 (on disk, zero capture): record the gradient checks that currently exist only in reviewers' scratchpads as scripts/g1_impact_grad.py + docs/results/g1_*.json (d(apex)/d(alpha) tape vs FD at both rigs, flat and edge landings, substep convergence of the rotational response); add the never-run handbook-friction-table route and a leave-one-MATERIAL-out route to e1_heldout.py and report them on the existing ladder; make p2's camera scale and ramp angle per-clip inputs; write a real-video ball/blob tracker (src/track/balls.py is tuned to rendered balls); buy/borrow a 240 fps phone, tripod, inclinometer app, kitchen scale, callipers, a plywood board and a hard reference plate.

Weeks 1–2 (the first experiment): instrument gate on 10 objects on the own reference board: 5 spheres/near-spheres x 3 heights x 10 drops (two routes, g-scale check), 8 block-like objects of 4 materials at 2 tilts x 5 slides (two-angle invariant); kill decision at day 14.

Weeks 3–4: contact-law check: alpha vs drop height and vs object size (two sizes per material) on spheres and flat-landing blocks; implement the velocity exponent p in the contact kernel (or fit alpha per impact speed) and re-validate e(alpha, p, v) per rule 5; per-class tape-vs-FD gate and forward-convergence check decide tape vs FD/CEM for each clip class; write the Fisher/Laplace reporting.

Weeks 5–8: capture at scale: ~40 weighed objects x 3 surfaces (board, laminate, concrete paver), ~1,000 clips; topple nudges on a high-grip mat for objects that can topple plus two known-offset CoM test objects; irregular objects get direct-route e per impact class only; optional multi-object tagged board after a 1-day ArUco readout; LLM names material and build per object (cached); in parallel start the PhysX-Anything and UniPhysGen environments (3–4 weeks of installs, run on 2 shared A6000s at most).

Weeks 9–10: library v1 with IQR and provenance; held-out-object and held-out-surface tests (own objects) and the held-out-trial-type test (fit on drops, predict post-bounce slide; fit on slides, predict stay/slide at the second tilt); factorisation test (k = 1 vs k = 2 proxies); bridge test to the Physics 101 rows; USD/MJCF export; reproduce the measured drops and slides from the exported files in Newton-MuJoCo (and PhysX if Isaac Sim is reachable) and report the cross-engine disagreement.

Weeks 11–12: the benchmark: scorer for f(image, mesh) -> (mu, rho, e) on held-out real motion in trajectory RMS, outcome accuracy and outcome-flip rate; routes: oracle, measured table, LLM-name + table, LLM number, handbook table, VLM-range midpoint (UrbanVerse/EmbodiedGen prompt formats), PhysX-Anything density -> mass, PhysX-Anything -> UniPhysGen friction, BEHAVIOR-1K lookup, SimReady defaults; the outcome-flip audit over 50–200 props with push/drop/topple primitives at the table's own IQR bounds.

Week 13: write-up with every kill-test number stated whichever way it fell and every plot carrying its noise floor; release tracks, splits, scorer, table, USD/MJCF writer and a Physics 101 download script (not the clips); ask the Physics 101 authors about derived-data terms.
recommendation.first_experiment: Instrument gate on the user's own reference board, with the on-disk control run in parallel. Capture: 5 spheres/near-spheres of distinct materials (rubber ball, steel bearing, wooden ball, plastic ball, glass marble or glazed ceramic sphere) dropped from 0.10 / 0.20 / 0.40 m, 10 repeats each (150 clips), and 8 block-like objects of 4 materials (cardboard box, wooden block, plastic block, porcelain plate or cup; two of each) slid from rest at two tilts bracketing their slip threshold, 5 trials each (80 clips), side view at 240 fps in daylight, scale from each object's own measured edge, angle from an inclinometer app, mass on a kitchen scale. Readout: CoTracker3 -> free-fall parabola -> e by the velocity route (parabolas either side of impact extrapolated to the table line) and the height route sqrt(h_b/h_d); mu by p2/p4 with release-time/offset alignment; alpha fitted through DiffMeshScene with its tape-vs-FD agreement recorded. Numbers it yields, with the gates decided now: (1) per sphere and height, the repeat-trial IQR of e (gate <= 0.05; p3 at 30 fps gave physically inverted values); (2) the median |e_velocity - e_height| (<= 0.03); (3) the within-session spread of free-fall g in px/s^2 (<= 5%; p3 gave 2.7x); (4) the e span across the five materials (>= 0.3, i.e. the table has information); (5) the two-angle mu agreement on the 8 blocks (within the within-cell IQR, <= 0.03) and the ratio of each material's mu on the user's board to its Physics 101 board row (the bridge number: if the four ratios agree within the trial IQR the two tables can be joined, otherwise they cannot); (6) on disk, zero capture: the handbook-table-by-material-pair route's held-out median trajectory RMS on Physics 101 against the measured table's 2.55 mm and the dataset median's 4.40 mm, paired sign test over 70 objects. One capture day, one A6000 for a few hours.
recommendation.kill_test: Pre-registered now, four parts, each ending a specific claim. (1) Instrument: if on spheres the repeat IQR of e exceeds 0.10, or the two routes disagree by more than 0.05 in median, or free-fall g spreads more than +/-10% within a session, a phone at 240 fps is not a restitution instrument; no further capture happens, the restitution and CoM columns are dropped, and the direction collapses to the runner-up (on-disk benchmark/audit). (2) Value of measuring over looking up: if the handbook-friction-table route assigned by LLM-named material pair matches the measured table on held-out Physics 101 motion (paired sign test over 70 objects, p > 0.05, and median RMS within 0.5 mm of 2.55 mm), measured friction buys nothing over a handbook and the friction claim is withdrawn; the programme keeps only restitution, CoM-by-build and the benchmark. (3) Transfer: fitted values are exported only if the held-out-trial-type prediction (fit on drops -> predict the post-bounce slide; fit on slides -> predict stay/slide at the second tilt) lands within 1.5x the object's trial-to-trial spread for >= 2/3 of objects and alpha from one height predicts the other within the repeat IQR under the fitted e(v) law (not under a constant e, which the HC law forbids); otherwise the values are effective constants of one condition, are tagged as such and are not exported. (4) Differentiable claim: for each clip class, the tape gradient must agree with central FD within 20% at the fitting substep count and the forward observable must be converged in substeps; a class that fails is fitted by FD/CEM and loses the word 'differentiable' in the write-up; if every non-closed-form class fails, the differentiable engine is not part of the contribution and the project stops advertising it. (5) The field-level null: if the outcome-flip audit shows that replacing VLM/handbook values with measured values flips fewer than ~10% of push/drop/topple outcomes across 50–200 props, parameter accuracy does not matter at the outcome level for these primitives; that negative is published as the result and the library is not scaled further.
nearest_prior_and_difference: Physics 101 (Wu et al., BMVC 2016) and Galileo (NeurIPS 2015): the same ramp footage, MCMC/Bullet fits, split-by-object outcome prediction (moving distance rho 0.33, bounce 0.23) — difference: metric trajectory error through an engine validated to <1 mm on these clips, repeat-trial floors and invariant admission tests, scoring of ASSIGNMENT routes incl. 2025–26 generators, and restitution at 240 fps that 30 fps could not give; Physics 101 is our on-disk control, not our contribution.

SMASH (SIGGRAPH Asia 2016), Vid2Param (RA-L 2020), Hofherr et al. (WACV 2023), Delta-ynamics (2605.20576), DiffSDFSim (3DV 2021): restitution/friction/mass ratio from uninstrumented consumer video, n = 1–3 with measured truth or no measured truth — difference: n ~ 40 objects x 3 surfaces x 3 speeds with weighed masses, invariant gates, held-out-trial-type and held-out-surface validation, exact-mesh contact, and the benchmark as the product; we cite them as the method's antecedents.

GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948): measured mu and e for 3–4 rigid materials with 180 Hz mocap fed INTO Isaac/Genesis/Newton; never tests an assignment route — difference: assignment is the object of the test, a phone replaces mocap at ~10x the materials and outdoor surfaces, and GAUGE's public trajectories are an external instrument check in week 1.

Acosta, Yang & Posa, RA-L 2022 (arXiv 2110.00541): law-vs-parameter diagnosis on 550 real cube tosses across Drake/MuJoCo/Bullet — difference: everyday materials across speeds and surfaces in Newton/Warp with identified rather than prescribed parameters; positioned as an extension, cited up front.
EKFPhys (3DV 2024, 2309.15703): differentiable LCP engine + RGB-D, 4 YCB objects, friction only, mocap-tilt truth — difference: RGB only, restitution and CoM added, many objects, transfer tests.

NeRF2Physics (CVPR 2024), PUGS, GaussianProperty, PhysGS (CVPR 2026), Asset2Sim (2605.19136), UniPhysGen (2607.13586), Kaedim YAM harness (2610.00731): LLM/VLM names material -> table/interval, validated on pad meters, ABO masses, grasps, simulator stability or policy-level correlation — difference: validated against the object's own real motion, held out, with an outcome-flip rate; their routes are rows in our benchmark.

Wang & Wang (arXiv 2604.24188): tribometer pair-friction factorisation with >= 2 proxy materials — difference: we test the k = 1 product rule against their k = 2 scheme on object slides rather than a tribometer, and adopt theirs if k = 1 fails.

PhysVid (2510.02311), IRIS (2603.16432), WorldBench (2601.21282): measured-GT real-video datasets scoring estimators or generators — difference: closed loop through the engine on held-out objects; PhysVid's 5 x 6 dynamometer matrix is a free external check.

ASID (2404.12308), DROPO (2201.08434), Exciting Contact Modes (2411.10935): Fisher-information identifiability and DR ranges from robot data — difference: no robot; the Fisher matrix is per passive clip and is used to choose the next clip, cited as an application not an invention.
DiffMJX (2506.14186) and Ostrich (2609.08800): fixes for stiff-contact gradients — not needed on the plane path where our adjoint passes; the techniques to borrow if a clip class fails the FD gate.
what_to_stop_doing: Stop every use of generative/predictive video models and LLM numbers as a supervision signal (Cosmos judge, V-JEPA surprise V2–V4, FPT, MYRIAD, Wan, LLM numeric physics): the negatives are externally corroborated (PhysVid, PokeWorld, ACWM-Phys, WRBench, GAUGE, WorldBench, Principia) and need no re-run; keep them only as baseline rows.
Stop the render-and-read-off-video O-track (classifier readouts o10/o12/o13/o14): retired, superseded by direct real-footage measurement; do not re-validate them on the fixed simulator.

Stop treating body-body contact gradients as a 90-day deliverable: g0b/g0c/g0d show the pair adjoint under-transmits and is 1.7–2x off for strikes; keep every observable on the plane path and do not design probes (strikes, stacks, pushes) that need it.

Stop the 'beyond rooms' / persistent-world / determinism deliverables (P1's world API, P2's 1,000-object street): the kernel is all-pairs nV x N with no broadphase and nondeterministic at the stiff setting; passing a look-away protocol 'by construction' is not a contribution.
Stop the learned appearance-to-physics model (M2P): Physics 101 built it on the same dataset in 2016.
Stop the soft-body and cloth probes (soft press diverges; the differentiable-MPM lane — PhysTwin, MOSIV, Vid2Sim, MonoPhysics, EgoPhys — is crowded and ahead).

Stop fitting more Physics 101 ramp slides for their own sake and stop scoring generic routes on the 20-degree board (its response is flat above mu = 0.364): it is the on-disk control, not the benchmark.

Stop advertising 'differentiable' as the headline until a clip class demonstrably needs the tape; stop claiming per-parameter CIs or Fisher identifiability as novel (ASID, DROPO, 2411.10935, textbook sysID).

Stop claiming 'first' anything: first held-out-object test (Physics 101 2016), first measured table (GAUGE, MIT Push, Omnipush, 2604.24188), first phone restitution (SMASH 2016, physics-education literature), first LLM-name-to-table resolver (NeRF2Physics, Asset2Sim, UniPhysGen, Kaedim).

Stop scheduling one researcher for 1,600–3,600 clips plus photogrammetry of 150–250 objects: the 90-day corpus is ~1,000 clips of ~40 objects, primitives by callipers, irregular objects by direct-route readouts only.
recommendation.what_would_change_this: Five things, each with the evidence that would trigger it. (a) If the week-1 handbook-table route matches the measured table on held-out Physics 101 motion (p > 0.05), measured friction is not worth capturing: narrow to restitution + CoM-by-build + the benchmark, or switch to the runner-up. (b) If the day-14 instrument gate fails on spheres (IQR(e) > 0.10, routes > 0.05 apart, g spread > 10%), the phone is not an instrument at 240 fps either: switch to the runner-up (on-disk benchmark/audit, workshop-length) and stop. (c) If the body-body adjoint is fixed and validated against FD under sustained contact (g0c currently -0.03 vs -0.38), the engine itself becomes a contribution in a documented hole (no shipped engine gives gradients through mesh-mesh narrow phase; DiffMJX lists it as future work) and the direction should pivot to multi-body identification (stacks, strikes, pushes) with an engine-paper framing — a riskier, more differentiable project than this one. (d) If a robot lab (SIMPLER/RoboArena-style) agrees to swap in the exported values and report SRCC/replay error, the robot claim can be made and the paper's venue changes; without it, keep robots out of the claims. (e) If a 2025–26 paper already provides a phone-video, multi-material, multi-surface (mu, e, CoM) table with held-out-motion validation (every skeptic's search budget ran out before a full 2026 sweep; Delta-ynamics 2605.20576 is the closest found and lacks measured truth and restitution), the direction narrows to the benchmark/audit, which still has no published counterpart. Also: if the outcome-flip audit returns < ~10% flips, the honest conclusion is that VLM/handbook values are good enough at the outcome level for these primitives, and the project should publish that negative and not scale the library.

runner_up.title: e1-bench on disk: score every assignment route (released generators PhysX-Anything -> UniPhysGen, LLM numbers, handbook tables, VLM-range midpoints, shipped library values) on Physics 101 held-out real motion, with a rule-1 audit of the benchmark itself and outcome accuracy as the unit — the surviving form of [3] (P7 + P5 + P9), no capture, no gradients
runner_up.why_second: It is the cheapest and most certain result in the set (the harness runs today; the first numbers are days away once the generator environments install) and its novelty claim — nobody scores an assignment pipeline by re-simulating its values against held-out real trajectories — was the best-defended in the set. But it cannot be the direction: the 20-degree board's response is exactly flat above mu = 0.364 (measured: 87.8 mm for every route emitting 0.37–0.60), so generators and LLMs that return a generic ~0.4 all score one identical number and cannot be ranked without a steeper, self-captured ramp — which is the recommended direction's instrument; its effect size (2.55 vs 4.40 mm, dmu 0.014) sits inside any DR band; it has no restitution or CoM column; it uses no differentiable physics; and its three parent proposals undercounted the bridge problem (the ledger's rows are pair values against MIT's board the user does not own). It is the week-1 control and the week-11 deliverable of the recommendation, not an alternative to it.
runner_up.when_to_prefer_it: Prefer it if (a) no 240 fps phone or capture time is available in the next month, (b) the day-14 instrument gate fails on spheres, (c) the user wants a publishable negative or audit result in 4–6 weeks at workshop / Datasets-and-Benchmarks length (the first real-motion score of released sim-ready generators plus the handbook-vs-measured comparison is such a note), or (d) the week-1 handbook-table route already matches the measured table, in which case measuring friction is not worth the capture and the audit is the whole story.

rejected_framings: City scale / 'very large scale beyond rooms' / 'interactable worlds at scale' — DROP as a target. Evidence: no street-, campus- or city-scale pipeline validates any physics (UrbanVerse: GPT-4.1 mass vs spec sheets at 19.6% MAPE, friction unchecked; URBAN-SIM/MetaUrban: per-texture friction labels; GRUtopia: 0% mobile manipulation; HUGSIM/OmniRe/WOSAC: no contact physics at all); 'interaction' at that scale means collision avoidance, never moving an object; this project's kernel is all-pairs nV x N with no broadphase and nondeterministic at the validated contact setting; one researcher. The physics content of a city-scale world is O(materials x surfaces), which is exactly what the recommendation measures and exports as USD — city geometry is a solved, separate problem (UrbanVerse, Vid2Sim, HUGSIM, NuRec) this layer plugs into. 'Beyond rooms' survives only as outdoor surfaces (concrete, asphalt, pavers) measured as rows.

Neural world models (Genie 3, Cosmos 3, Matrix-Game 2.0, GameCraft, V-JEPA 2-AC, Wan) as the world or as supervision — DROP. Evidence: the project's own controlled negatives (judge wrong 9/9 on one-bit questions, surprise at chance, FPT/MYRIAD/Wan motion-magnitude only, LLM numbers a generic ~0.4) are independently reproduced (PhysVid: V-JEPA-2 friction r 0.21–0.28; PokeWorld: mass R^2 0.21–0.25; ACWM-Phys; WRBench: 0/23 models keep a looked-away object moving; survey 2608.23070: 6/163 expose state; GAUGE/WorldBench: wrong accelerations and momentum transfer). They carry neither object-specific theta nor persistent state. Keep at most one baseline row (f13_wan.py) and do not build V2–V4 on surprise.

Robots / 'a practical system for robots' — DEFER. Evidence: no robot; the evidence that object-parameter accuracy changes policy transfer is thin and task-dependent (ASID positive on rod balancing/shuffleboard; SIMPLER <= 15% sensitivity to object physics; arXiv 2606.20712: 'mass and friction yield no stable adaptation signal'; Kaedim 2610.00731: r 0.51 -> 0.90 but confounded with scale and visuals); the parameters manipulation consumes most (gripper-pad/object friction, object-object contact) need the broken body-body path. The robot-facing deliverable is a USD/MJCF asset with measured values, DR ranges from measured IQRs and provenance, plus an in-sim outcome-flip test; a policy claim needs a partner lab and is outside the 90 days.

'Differentiable physics' as the headline — DEMOTE to a stated, per-clip-class role. Evidence: the tape is validated only through one body on a plane (mu and, this week, damping through impact); the body-body adjoint is unusable (g0c -0.03 vs FD -0.38); the first-tier observables (slides, sphere rebounds) are closed-form; FD at 6–10 parameters costs seconds; the Fisher/Laplace idea is textbook (ASID, 2411.10935, 2109.08815). It is load-bearing for non-closed-form impacts/tumbles/topples and for joint shared-parameter fits, and that is what the paper should say.

'First / nobody has done X' novelty framing — DROP throughout. Evidence from primary sources: Physics 101 (2016) ran split-by-object and cross-scenario transfer on the same data; Galileo (2015) ran stays/slides transfer; SMASH (2016), Vid2Param (2020), Hofherr (2023), Delta-ynamics (2026) identify physics from uninstrumented video; DiffSDFSim (2021) fits restitution through a differentiable sim; NeRF2Physics/PUGS/Asset2Sim/UniPhysGen/Kaedim resolve LLM-named materials to tables; GAUGE/MIT Push/Omnipush/2604.24188 are measured tables; DROPO gives DR ranges from data. The contribution is measurement breadth, invariant-based validation, the held-out benchmark of assignment routes and the outcome-flip number.

A learned appearance-to-physics predictor (M2P) — DROP. Evidence: Physics 101 (BMVC 2016) is the same architecture (image net -> physics interpreter -> differentiable laws -> loss on tracked motion, no labels, held-out objects) on the same dataset; on Physics 101 the no-model material table already sits within 0.8 mm of the own-trials oracle, so the achievable gain is a motion-trained material classifier.

A persistent, deterministic, queryable Newton world as a contribution — DROP. Evidence: any engine passes WRBench's look-away protocol by construction; the project measured 1.5 mm atomic-add nondeterminism at the stiff setting and 0.6–2.2 cm on long slides; consumers take USD, not a bespoke state API.

Soft bodies / cloth / deformable material inference — DROP. Evidence: the soft-press probe diverges; the differentiable-MPM lane (PhysTwin, MOSIV, Vid2Sim, MonoPhysics, EgoPhys, PhysDreamer/PhysGaussian) is crowded and ahead, and already covers stiffness from video with differentiable simulators.
open_questions: Does a handbook friction table assigned by LLM-named material pair already match the measured table on held-out Physics 101 motion? Never run (verified: e1 routes are oracle/material/pipeline/LLM-direct only); it is the single cheapest experiment that could end the friction half of the programme.

Is restitution a material property or a pair/surface property? Bounce and Learn says the surface dominates; the recommendation must run the same factorisation test on e as on mu, and the table may end up surface-specific.

Is e(v) monotone for everyday materials over 1.4–2.8 m/s, and is the Hunt-Crossley form with a fitted exponent adequate? Mueller et al. (PRL 2013) report oscillations superimposed on the decay; the project's kernel currently fixes p = 1 and changing it triggers rule-5 revalidation.

Does any consumer act on a restitution column at all? MuJoCo has no coefficient of restitution; PhysX/Isaac default it to 0; manipulation sim2real randomises it. If the answer is no, the restitution work is calibration for this project's own kernel and the benchmark/friction/CoM parts carry the paper.

Does object-parameter accuracy change outcomes at the primitive level (the SIMPLER / 2606.20712 question)? The outcome-flip audit answers it for push/drop/topple on 50–200 props; a small flip rate is a legitimate negative that would end the library's scaling.

Can the body-body adjoint be fixed (g0c: tape -0.03 vs FD -0.38 under sustained contact; g0d: 1.7–2x off for strikes)? If yes, the engine becomes a contribution in a documented hole and the direction changes; nobody has tried the DiffMJX contacts-from-distance or Ostrich IFT techniques on these kernels.

Is the forward rotational response to corner impacts convergent at any affordable substep count (P3 skeptic: angular velocity -4.29/-3.98/-3.81 rad/s at 60/120/240 substeps, cd-gradient sign change)? Until it is, 6-DoF fits of irregular bodies are off the table and their e is reported per impact class by the direct route only.

Can the user's own reference board be bridged to the Physics 101 rows? p1 found mu falling 0.28 -> 0.21 across nine cardboard cubes of one material (Spearman -0.80, unexplained); if overlap-material ratios do not agree within the trial IQR, the two tables stay separate and the 101-object corpus is only a control.

Does the user have a true (non-interpolated) 240 fps phone with adequate lighting for ~1/1000 s exposure, and how large is rolling-shutter skew at 2–3 m/s in that camera? Both must be measured in week 1, not assumed.

Can monocular 6-DoF pose against a mesh be obtained for non-spherical objects from RGB only (no PnP, projection kernel or photogrammetry path exists in the repo; Hunyuan3D-2's licence excludes South Korea, so TripoSR/TRELLIS or photogrammetry would be needed), and is phone photogrammetry good enough at the contact patch?

What are Physics 101's redistribution terms (no licence is stated anywhere)? The benchmark can ship tracks, splits and a download script, but the authors should be asked before derived data is released.

Was a 2025–26 'phone video to rigid digital twin' or multi-material restitution paper missed? Every skeptic's search budget was exhausted before a full 2026 sweep; Delta-ynamics (2605.20576) is the closest found and lacks measured truth and restitution — a targeted search is a day-1 task.

Will PhysX-Anything -> UniPhysGen actually run end to end on 7 cm Physics 101 objects (transformers 4.50 pin, Sonata/Pointcept stack, an untested mesh -> segmented-point-cloud hand-off), and is scoring furniture-scale generators on small lab objects a fair test or a distribution-mismatch complaint waiting to happen?

missing_angles: Post-cutoff scoop window (Jul–Oct 2026) was never swept: CoRL 2026 camera-readies, RSS 2026, ICRA 2026 proceedings, SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 (Oct), NeurIPS 2026 Datasets & Benchmarks, and the IROS/CoRL sim-to-real and 'physical world models' workshops. The recommendation itself says every skeptic's search budget ran out before a full 2026 sweep; Delta-ynamics (2605.20576) and GAUGE (2608.05948) are the closest finds and both are recent enough that follow-ups (GAUGE with an assignment step, Delta-ynamics with measured truth) would land exactly in this window.

Physics-education / smartphone-metrology literature: phyphox's acoustic '(in)elastic collision' experiment and Open Source Physics 'Tracker' already turn a phone into a restitution instrument and have published repeatability numbers; the proposal cites Bernstein 1977 and Heckel 2016 but not the phone-native tools, so the 'phone is a physics instrument' framing may be weaker than stated and the day-14 gate thresholds (IQR(e) <= 0.05, routes within 0.03) have published comparators that were not consulted.

Consumer-side evidence that per-object friction/restitution/CoM accuracy changes any downstream outcome was not scouted as a question; it was only asserted from scattered sources (SIMPLER <= 15%, 2606.20712, Kaedim). No scout checked RoboCasa / BEHAVIOR-1K / Isaac Lab / MetaUrban-UrbanVerse parameter-sensitivity ablations, DROPO/BayesSim-style posterior widths on real pushes, or whether a 'physics material' contribution path (SimReady schema, UrbanVerse's 288 ground materials) accepts external measured rows. If outcome-flip rates are already published as small, the library's impact collapses before capture.

Differentiable-engine landscape for mesh–mesh contact gradients was only partially covered: Nimble (DART, analytic LCP gradients with mesh colliders), Dojo, Genesis's rigid solver, Newton/Warp's own collide pipeline and its adjoint status, Jade, and the randomized-smoothing line (Suh et al.) were not checked, so 'no shipped engine gives gradients through mesh-mesh narrow phase' is unverified and the 'what would change this (c)' pivot rests on it.

Velocity-dependent restitution models: Kuwabara–Kono (1 − e ∝ v^1/5), Flores/Lankarani–Nikravesh variants and the DEM calibration literature already parameterise e(v) with an exponent; 'implement the velocity exponent p' in weeks 3–4 risks reinventing a standard contact law rather than adopting one, which is the user's stated worry.

Measured household-object property datasets beyond the ones named: ObjectFolder Real (100 real objects, mass + impact sounds), PhysObjects (ICRA 2024, physical concept annotations), YCB/HOPE/KIT object sets, PISA Experiments (real ball-drop videos with measured physics used to align video models), Physion/Physion++/ContPhy — not cited as controls or as evidence of what already exists with measured truth.

The 'beyond rooms' rejection leans on 'no broadphase' in the project's own kernel, but Newton ships a broadphase and Warp has wp.Bvh/HashGrid; the honest blocker is validation and researcher time, not the missing broadphase. The user's stated wish for scale is dismissed on a partly wrong technical reason, and no scout asked whether a measured physics-material layer could be delivered INTO an existing open street simulator (UrbanVerse, MetaUrban, Isaac Lab) with one sensitivity experiment — the only form of 'at scale' reachable in 90 days.

Camera metrology was not scouted: which phones record true (non-interpolated) 240 fps, rolling-shutter skew at 2–3 m/s, exposure at ~1/1000 s indoors, and lens distortion at the board edge. The whole instrument gate depends on this and it is listed only as an open question.
unverified_claims: Tape-vs-FD impact adjoint numbers (d(apex)/d(alpha) 0.998–1.053 flat, 0.97–1.17 edge, sign flip at 100 substeps) and the corner-impact non-convergence (−4.29/−3.98/−3.81 rad/s) exist only in reviewer scratchpads; docs/results/g0*.json are the earlier gradient scripts, not these runs.

'The 20° benchmark is exactly flat above μ = 0.364 (87.8 mm identical for every generic route)' — a skeptic's in-session measurement, not recorded on disk; it is the load-bearing reason [3] is demoted to runner-up.

Kaedim YAM harness arXiv 2610.00731 (r 0.51 → 0.90), GAUGE 2608.05948, Wang & Wang 2604.24188, PhysVid 2510.02311 (0.73 Pearson adapted), arXiv 2606.20712 ('mass and friction yield no stable adaptation signal'), survey 2608.23070 (6/163 expose state), WRBench 0/23 — all cited by id but not reached by this critic; PokeWorld, ACWM-Phys, Principia, IRIS 2603.16432 have no verifiable citation in the text.

'PhysX/Isaac default restitution to 0' and 'MuJoCo has no restitution' — the MuJoCo claim is correct (solref/solimp, no COR), the PhysX default is plausible but uncited.
'No shipped engine gives gradients through mesh-mesh narrow phase; DiffMJX lists it as future work' — Nimble Physics and Dojo advertise mesh-collider gradients; not checked.

e1 ladder numbers quoted at 2.55 / 2.72 / 4.40 / 7.53 / 1.77 mm match CLAUDE.md's rounded 2.6 / 2.7 / 4.4 / 7.5 / 1.8 and docs/results/e1_heldout.json exists — consistent, but the 'handbook route never run' is confirmed by inspection (scripts/e1_heldout.py routes: oracle / material / pipeline / LLM-direct only).
extra_search_queries: SCOOP SWEEP, Jul–Oct 2026 only. Find any paper, dataset or technical report that identifies rigid-body friction, restitution and/or centre of mass of MANY everyday objects on MULTIPLE surfaces from consumer/phone video (no mocap), with weighed or dynamometer truth, OR that scores material/parameter ASSIGNMENT routes (VLM, LLM, handbook, generator) against held-out REAL motion. Venues: CoRL 2026 (camera-ready Sept–Oct), RSS 2026, ICRA 2026 proceedings, IROS 2026, SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 (Oct), NeurIPS 2026 Datasets & Benchmarks, ICCV 2026? (check cycle), and workshops (CoRL sim-to-real, 'physical world models', 'learning for physics'). Seeds: follow-ups to GAUGE (2608.05948), Delta-ynamics (2605.20576), PhysVid (2510.02311), Scalable Real2Sim (2503.00370), Kaedim YAM (2610.00731), MolmoSpaces, UrbanVerse physics validation, EmbodiedGen V2, ManiTwin; keywords 'coefficient of restitution video dataset', 'friction from monocular video household objects', 'real2sim rigid digital twin phone', 'physical parameter benchmark real trajectories', 'sim-ready asset physics validation'. Also check phyphox acoustic restitution and OSP Tracker publications for phone-restitution repeatability numbers. Report for each hit: n objects, n surfaces, truth source, held-out protocol, whether restitution/CoM included, licence. Verdict: does any hit already deliver a measured multi-material, multi-surface (μ, e, CoM) table with held-out-motion validation, or an assignment-route benchmark on real motion?

CONSUMER / IMPACT BRIEF. Question: is there published evidence that the accuracy of per-object friction, restitution or centre of mass changes a downstream outcome — policy transfer, task success, or simulated outcome class (stays/slides/topples/bounces)? Collect quantitative sensitivity results: SIMPLER (exact table/figure on object-physics sensitivity), ASID, DROPO/BayesSim posterior widths on real pushes/tosses, arXiv 2606.20712 (verify title and the 'mass and friction yield no stable adaptation signal' claim), Kaedim 2610.00731 (verify the 0.51→0.90 and its confounds), RoboCasa / BEHAVIOR-1K / Isaac Lab / RoboVerse domain-randomisation range ablations, MetaUrban/UrbanVerse friction-label effects, Acosta-Yang-Posa 2110.00541 outcome-level findings, Omnipush/MIT Push outcome variability. Also establish the delivery path: does the SimReady USD physics-material schema, UrbanVerse's ground-material table, MuJoCo (solref/solimp), Genesis or Isaac Lab accept a per-material (μ, e(v), density, provenance) row, and how do they combine pair friction (PhysX combine modes)? Verdict: is there already a published outcome-flip-style number, and is any consumer able to ingest an e(v) law rather than a scalar e?

ENGINE / CONTACT-LAW BRIEF. (a) Which shipped differentiable simulators provide validated gradients through MESH–MESH narrow-phase contact: Nimble Physics (DART), Dojo, DiffMJX (2506.14186), Ostrich (2609.08800), Genesis rigid solver, Newton/Warp's own collide pipeline + tape, Jade, Brax/MJX mesh support, randomized-smoothing gradients (Suh et al.), DiffSDFSim; for each state the contact model, what gradient validation (FD agreement) they report, and whether sustained contact and glancing strikes are covered. This decides whether 'no shipped engine gives gradients through mesh-mesh narrow phase' survives and whether fixing the project's pair adjoint would be a contribution. (b) Velocity-dependent restitution laws already standard in contact mechanics and DEM: Hunt–Crossley (e ≈ 1 − αv), Kuwabara–Kono (1 − e ∝ v^1/5), Flores et al., Lankarani–Nikravesh, Schwager–Pöschel; Mueller/Heckel PRL 2013 oscillations; DEM calibration practice (Itasca, LIGGGHTS) for fitting damping vs impact speed and for substep convergence criteria of corner impacts in penalty methods. Verdict: should the project adopt a named law with its published exponent instead of fitting its own p, and what substep/stiffness criterion does the literature use to call a corner impact converged?
critic.assessment: The recommendation is internally coherent and its repo-level claims that I could check hold (no handbook route in e1_heldout.py; usd_physics.py invents static = 1.2x dynamic; HC = 1.0 fixes the restitution exponent; the contact kernels launch over nV with no broadphase). Its weakness is that the three numbers that carry the ranking — the impact-adjoint tape-vs-FD agreement, the corner-impact non-convergence, and the '20° benchmark flat above μ = 0.364' measurement — exist only in reviewer scratchpads, not in docs/results, and several of the refuting citations (GAUGE, Kaedim, Wang & Wang, PhysVid adapted, 2606.20712, WRBench, PokeWorld, ACWM-Phys) are post-cutoff or uncited and were not independently reached. The biggest gap is the one the synthesis itself admits: no sweep of Jul–Oct 2026 (CoRL/RSS/ICRA/SIGGRAPH Asia/NeurIPS D&B camera-readies), which is exactly where a phone-video multi-material (μ, e, CoM) table with held-out-motion validation, or a GAUGE-style benchmark with an assignment step, would appear and would reduce the direction to the runner-up. Two further angles could change the verdict rather than the ranking: (i) whether any consumer measurably cares (published parameter-sensitivity ablations could show outcome-flip rates are already known to be small, killing the library before capture), and (ii) whether a shipped engine already provides mesh–mesh contact gradients, which both weakens the 'what would change this (c)' pivot and is relevant to the user's explicit differentiable-physics interest. The 'beyond rooms' rejection is also argued partly on a wrong technical ground (missing broadphase is a day of Warp work; the real blockers are validation and headcount), and no scout asked whether the measured material layer could be delivered into an existing street simulator with one sensitivity experiment, which is the only form of the user's scale request reachable in 90 days. One more round with the three briefs above is warranted; if the scoop sweep is clean and no outcome-sensitivity negative exists, the recommendation stands with its numbers re-recorded on disk in week 1.

proposals.title: Phone-to-Twin: batched differentiable identification of every movable object in a filmed space, validated on held-out real interactions
proposals.thesis: An interactable world that is right is a physics engine whose per-object parameters were identified from real motion and checked on interactions it never saw, not a video model that invents outcomes and forgets state (WRBench: 23 models, none keeps a looked-away object moving). We claim that from uninstrumented 240 fps phone video of a person shoving, dropping, toppling and striking objects with a weighed reference ball, our exact-mesh differentiable contact simulator identifies friction, restitution, centre of mass and mass ratio for every movable object in a room or a yard in one batched gradient pass per scene, with Jacobian uncertainty, and predicts withheld interactions of those same objects to within their own trial-to-trial variability.
proposals.what_we_build: (1) A capture protocol, 'four pokes', for one person with a phone at 240 fps and a printed scale marker: a shove along the floor (deceleration gives mu_pair against that floor; v0 is observed from tracking so no force sensing is needed, exactly the p5 table-segment readout), two drop heights (restitution via our alpha; the two heights are an invariant), a finger push to topple (time-to-topple reads the centre of mass, as p9 established on the pot), and a strike by a weighed reference ball (momentum exchange m_obj/m_ref = |dv_ref|/|dv_obj| from tracked velocities, independent of e; the separation/approach speed ratio gives the object-ball restitution as a second, different pair quantity; the post-strike slide is one more shove with a known v0). Objects are weighed on a kitchen scale for ground truth only. Friction in the twin is the pair value against the filmed floor, so a twin of the filmed scene needs no table anchor; moving the object to another floor uses the product rule p5 measured at 0.75-1.05 with one stated anchor. (2) A perception front end from tools already in the repo or off the shelf: CoTracker3 (the p1/p2 path, loaded from the local cache), SAM2 masks, a per-frame rigid pose from tracks against the object mesh (ruler-measured primitives for the pilot, photogrammetry meshes later). (3) The identification core: the tape-safe DiffMeshScene of scripts/g0_grad_check.py generalised to a batch world of N independent bodies against the floor plane in one Warp tape, with per-object theta_i = (log mu, alpha, CoM_xy, log mass ratio) and per-clip nuisance (release time, initial pose and velocity) fitted jointly by the projected-iterate trust-region Levenberg-Marquardt of o8_joint_sim.py, the Jacobian now from the tape instead of finite differences; J^T J gives Fisher information, hence per-parameter confidence intervals and an automatic rule-1 check (a zero column means this clip does not identify that parameter). (4) The persistent world: a Newton MeshProbeScene holding every identified object with its theta and CI, a state-query API (pose, velocity, theta, CI), seeded deterministic replays at the soft contact setting (the stiff setting is nondeterministic at 1.5 mm from atomic-add order and is avoided or given ordered reductions), and interactions as impulses, pushes and drops on any object. Appearance stays with Cycles or a splat of the filmed scene; a neural renderer on top of the engine state (the OrbiSim shape) is a follow-on, not part of the 90 days. (5) The evaluation harness: the e1_heldout.py protocol applied to withheld interactions (second drop height, second strike speed, a different floor), with baseline rows for the zero-order sweep (p4), the material-table prior (e1), the LLM number (f14) and an image-to-video world model (f13_wan.py, Wan 2.2 / Cosmos3-Nano from the same first frame with the action in the prompt), all scored by tracked motion normalised by trial-to-trial variability as GAUGE does.
