proposals.builds_on_our_assets: DiffMeshScene (scripts/g0_grad_check.py: reproduces the validated rollout exactly and matches central finite differences, d(slide)/d(mu) = -0.5448 vs -0.5453, 0.4 s per 1200-step forward+backward for a 386-vertex body); MeshProbeScene with exact vertex contact, seat_on_plane (2 mm gap fixed), build-aware CoM/inertia (within 1% of textbook) and set_restitution_alpha (src/sim/mesh_scene.py, src/sim/rigs.py); the projected-iterate, trust-region, adaptive-damping LM of o8_joint_sim.py (its three optimiser defects already paid for); CoTracker3 tracking plus the slide/roll/stay classifier and the object's-own-edge camera scale of p1_ramp_friction.py, p2_ramp_all.py, p5_transfer.py; the Physics 101 loop closure p4_sim_loop.py (Newton reproduces real slides to 0.4-1.0 mm RMS, 93 trials, median |dmu| 0.005) and the held-out protocol e1_heldout.py (70 objects, 359 trials); restitution calibration p7/p8 (e set by alpha, identical for 0.1 and 0.4 kg, speed-dependent 0.70 to 0.54 between 1 and 2 m/s) and the measured fact that 30 fps drops cannot give e (p3), which is why 240 fps is specified; the shove probe f7_shove.py (sim slide matches v0^2/2 mu g to 3% below mu 0.5; the box trips above 0.6, so shove speeds are bounded by object); the pot topple probe p9 (time-to-topple moves 2.2x with CoM and 1.00x with mass, 1.02x with alpha); the sensitivity-matrix discipline of o7_sensitivity.py, now computed by the Jacobian; f13_wan.py as the neural world-model baseline; src/gpu.py for holding one card only while computing.
proposals.differentiable_physics_role: Gradients buy four things here and nothing else. (a) Joint inversion: each clip has 2-4 physical parameters plus 3-5 nuisance parameters (release time, initial pose and velocity) that the project today aligns by search; a tape Jacobian makes that one LM fit per clip. (b) Batching: all objects of a scene share one tape, because bodies interact only with the floor, which is exactly the regime where our adjoint is validated; identification cost per scene is one forward+backward per LM iteration (about 10 s for 25 objects at g0's 0.4 s per body) instead of a 10x sweep per object per parameter. (c) Uncertainty and identifiability for free: J^T J gives confidence intervals and the rule-1 sensitivity matrix per clip (the mass column exactly zero on a slide, which o7 found by sweeping) without the sweep we run today; at 200 objects nobody will sweep. (d) End to end from tracks: the loss is on tracked image points through a differentiable pose step, so pose-fit error does not compound into theta. What gradients do NOT buy: identifiability (a mass-independent observable stays mass-independent; the Jacobian only reports it), and nothing on the 1-D slide, where the sweep is already exact to 0.005. Honest status: gradients are validated through plane contact only. Through sustained body-body contact the tape under-transmits the push (g0c: d(A)/dmu_B = -0.032 vs -0.385 FD, the total right but the split wrong), and under stiff contact one adjoint component explodes (5e4). So the reference-ball strike is read primarily by analytic momentum exchange from tracked velocities, with the simulator forward-only for the post-impact slide; gradients through brief impacts (right to within 1-2x in g0d) are a week-1 gate against finite differences, not an assumption. If the impact adjoint fails the gate, restitution and mass ratio fall back to 1-D sweeps: the proposal loses batching for those two parameters, not its validity.
proposals.scale_claim: Scale here is the number of objects whose physics is identified and checked, not square metres. Concretely: 8-10 filmed spaces (kitchen, office, corridor, workshop, garage, courtyard, sidewalk, car park), 15-25 movable objects each, four pokes with two repeats: 150-250 objects and about 1,600 clips at 240 fps on seven floor materials, three of them outdoor (concrete, asphalt, paving). 'Beyond rooms' means the floors and object classes of outdoor spaces a person can walk into with a phone; it does not mean reconstructed city geometry, which UrbanVerse and Vid2Sim already produce without any validated physics and for which this pipeline would be the missing physics layer. On the engine side a 25-body scene is one Warp world and a 250-body one is still one card; the binding limit is capture time (about 100 clips per hour), not GPU.
proposals.practicality: Robotics labs get a dynamic twin of their own workspace from a phone, where SIMPLER, TwinAligner, PIN-WM and ASID need the robot, F/T sensing or RGB-D rigs to identify objects; the twin exports to Newton/USD with per-object theta and confidence intervals, and those intervals are the measured domain-randomisation ranges that Isaac Lab users currently pick by hand (friction 0.1-1.0, restitution 0-0.1). World-model researchers get interactable ground-truth scenes with real-motion validation, which GAUGE provides only inside a 2 m mocap volume; the capture set (clips, tracks, weighed masses, identified theta with CIs) is released as the first uninstrumented, many-object, measurement-grounded benchmark, the IRIS/GAUGE role without a lab. The same real interactions double as an action-conditioned test for interactive video models, which no benchmark currently provides.
proposals.novelty_argument: The landscape has no robot-free, multi-object, held-out-validated rigid identification: EKFPhys (4 YCB objects, RGB-D at 60 Hz, mocap truth, friction only), One-Shot Real-to-Sim (robot pusher with F/T, 3 objects, real mass error 0.257 kg), PIN-WM and TwinAligner (scripted robot pushes, 4 objects, no measured truth), D-REX (dexterous hand, mass only), DANOs (one soap bar), VideoPhysEdit (monocular and CoTracker3 like ours, quantitative only on 20 synthetic scenes). The measurement principles are textbook and Galileo fitted Physics 101 with Bullet in 2015, so the physics is not new and we say so. What is new: (i) hundreds of objects and outdoor floors from a phone; (ii) a batched differentiable fit with per-parameter uncertainty and automatic identifiability, which no engine paper offers and which our mesh-vertex kernels are placed to do since no shipped engine gives gradients through mesh contact; (iii) validation on withheld interactions plus an invariant per parameter (two heights, two speeds, product rule across floors) rather than against handbook values; (iv) the same real interactions scored against an image-to-video world model, closing the loop the project's f13 and GAUGE's world-model track left open. The difference from the project's own p1-e1 work is substantive: Physics 101 is one ramp, one board, 30 fps, and gives neither restitution nor mass from motion.
nearest_prior_work: EKFPhys, Kandukuri et al., 3DV 2024 (arXiv 2309.15703): differentiable LCP engine inside an EKF, friction from RGB-D on 4 YCB objects with mocap truth (median error 0.0246). Differs: we add restitution, CoM and mass ratio, 150-250 objects, phone RGB only, withheld interactions as the test.

One-Shot Real-to-Sim (arXiv 2412.00259): mass, CoM, inertia, friction from one robot push with RGB-D, 3 objects. Differs: no robot, mass from a reference-ball strike, many objects, invariants instead of a single fit.

PIN-WM (RSS 2025, arXiv 2504.16693) and TwinAligner (arXiv 2512.19390): per-object identification from scripted robot pushes, 4 objects, no measured parameter truth. Differs: no robot; weighed masses and invariants as truth; batched fit with CIs.

VideoPhysEdit (arXiv 2609.35134): monocular rigid scene reconstruction with SAM2 + CoTracker3 + VGGT, mass/friction/restitution; quantitative only on synthetic scenes. Differs: real measured truth, held-out validation, differentiable fit with uncertainty.

Galileo (NeurIPS 2015) and Physics 101 (BMVC 2016): Bullet fitted by MCMC to the same ramp footage, outcome-level evaluation. Differs: exact-mesh engine validated to <1 mm on that footage, 240 fps restitution, trajectory-level held-out test.

DiffMJX / Contacts-From-Distance (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2506.14186) and Ostrich (arXiv 2609.08800): the two techniques to borrow if our impact adjoint fails the week-1 gate; neither identifies friction/restitution/mass independently or handles mesh-mesh contact.

IRIS (arXiv 2603.16432) and GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948): measurement-grounded benchmarks with 4K/60 fps lab video and 180 Hz mocap, textbook objects or three materials; ours is the uninstrumented, everyday-object counterpart.
first_90_days: Weeks 1-2 (on disk, no capture): extend DiffMeshScene to a batch world of N bodies against the plane; LM with the tape Jacobian; refit all 359 Physics 101 trials jointly over (log mu, release time, s0, v0) and compare with the p4 sweep (the first experiment). Gate the impact adjoint on the bounce rig (drop, strike) against central finite differences; Jacobian rule-1 sweep of the four pokes (alpha, CoM, mass ratio, mu) checked against o7/p9 (mass column zero on a slide, topple immune to mass and alpha).

Weeks 3-4: capture pilot: 10 weighed objects (boxes, cans, balls, blocks, cups: ruler-measured primitives), 2 floors (laminate, concrete), four pokes x 2 repeats at 240 fps with a printed scale marker and a weighed reference ball; tracking (CoTracker3 + SAM2), pose from tracks; invariants: two heights -> same e, two strike speeds -> same mass ratio, product rule across the two floors.
Weeks 5-6: joint per-object identification on the pilot with CIs; prediction of withheld interactions vs the material-table prior and the LLM number. KILL TEST evaluated here (about day 45).

Weeks 7-9: scale capture to 8-10 spaces including three outdoor floors, 15-25 objects each; batched identification per scene; photogrammetry meshes for irregular objects; the persistent world API (state query, seeded replay) with a determinism report of repeat-run variance, which no interactive world model publishes.

Weeks 10-11: baselines on the same withheld clips: zero-order CEM/sweep at equal wall-clock, material prior, LLM number, Wan 2.2 / Cosmos3-Nano i2v from the same first frame with the action in the prompt, all scored by tracked motion (RMSE and DTW normalised by trial-to-trial variability).
Weeks 12-13: write-up with every plot carrying its noise floor; release clips, tracks, weighed masses, identified theta with CIs, and the twin scenes as Newton/USD.
proposals.first_experiment: Refit every Physics 101 ramp trial (359 trials, 70 objects, 20 deg) through the tape: per trial, Gauss-Newton on (log mu, release time, s0, v0) with the Jacobian from DiffMeshScene, all trials of one object in one batched world. Numbers it produces: median |mu_tape - mu_sweep| (the p4 sweep vs analytic was 0.005; the gate is <= 0.005), trajectory RMS (must stay <= 1.0 mm as in p4), wall-clock per trial for tape vs sweep, and CI coverage: the fraction of objects whose per-trial 68% intervals cover the per-object IQR (0.01-0.03 for the cardboard cubes). A second number from the same run: the Jacobian mass column on a slide, which must be exactly zero (rule 1 reproduced by computation rather than by sweep). Runs in the warp env on one A6000 in well under two weeks; nothing is captured.
proposals.kill_test: Pre-registered now. Gate before any capture (weeks 1-2, sim only): the tape must match central finite differences within 10% for d(rebound)/d(alpha) on the bounce rig and d(post-strike velocity)/d(mass ratio) through a reference-ball impact, and the Jacobian ranges for alpha, CoM and mass ratio under the four pokes must exceed 2x over plausible parameter ranges; a failed impact adjoint demotes restitution and mass to 1-D sweeps but does not kill the proposal. The KILL (week 6, 10-object pilot): (i) fewer than 7/10 objects give the same e within 0.05 from two drop heights and the same mass ratio within 15% from two strike speeds, or (ii) the identified twin fails to beat the material-table prior on withheld interactions for at least 7/10 objects (paired, tracked-motion error). Either means per-object physics is not readable from phone video with this engine, and the only thing left standing is the table (Proposal 2).
proposals.resources: One shared A6000 at a time, roughly 80-120 A6000-hours over 90 days: tracking about 1 GPU-minute per 2 s clip at 240 fps (1,600 clips ~ 30 h), identification ~20 h (a 25-object scene is ~10 s per LM iteration, ~100 iterations), Wan 2.2 baseline ~15 min per clip x 60 clips ~ 15 h, renders ~10 h. Hardware: a phone with 240 fps video, a tripod, a printed scale marker, a kitchen scale, a weighed reference ball, an inclinometer app and ~40 cheap objects (under 150 USD). Software: CoTracker3 (have), SAM2, a photogrammetry tool (Meshroom or COLMAP) for irregular objects; everything else is in the repo. No robot, no mocap.
proposals.biggest_risk: Geometry. Every validated result in this project used a known mesh, and penalty contact is sensitive to the base shape (the pot's CoM result flipped with the mass model; a bowl seated on an edge sank 14.5 mm and slid 4 m). Phone-filmed objects have no mesh; the pilot dodges this with measured primitives, and the scale-up depends on photogrammetry meshes being good at the contact patch. If they are not, the result is limited to primitive-shaped objects, which is still most of Physics 101 and most of what sits on floors, but a weaker paper. Second: the impact adjoint (stiff-contact gradients, 1.5 mm nondeterminism at the stiff setting) may push restitution and mass back to sweeps, which costs batching, not correctness. Third: a hand in frame, which already fooled the tracker in p1 when the cube did not move; the protocol uses a quick-release and a push stick.
proposals.expected_headline_result: From 240 fps phone video alone, with no robot, depth sensor or motion capture, a differentiable exact-mesh contact simulator identifies friction, restitution, centre of mass and mass ratio for 200 everyday objects across eight indoor and outdoor spaces in one batched gradient pass per scene with Jacobian-derived uncertainty, and predicts withheld drops, slides, topples and strikes of those objects to within 1.3x their real trial-to-trial variability, where a measured material prior reaches about 2x and an image-to-video world model exceeds 5x (targets, to be replaced by measured values).

evidence: METHOD CORE EXISTS. gradSim (arXiv 2104.02646, ICLR 2021): differentiable simulation + rendering identifies 'mass, friction, and elasticity' from video. DiffSDFSim (arXiv 2111.15318, 3DV 2021): differentiable rigid-body dynamics with nonconvex SDF contacts infers 'friction coefficients, mass, forces or shape parameters' from 'trajectory and depth image observations', tested on 'a real image sequence'. These already are 'differentiable contact simulator identifies friction/mass of real rigid objects from video'.

MASS FROM A COLLISION WITH ANOTHER OBJECT IS GALILEO (Wu et al., NeurIPS 2015; papers.nips.cc d09bf41544a3365a46c9077ebb5e35c3): Bullet engine, MCMC, latent 'mass, position, 3D shape, and friction', fitted to the same Physics 101 footage; the proposal's statement that Physics 101 'gives neither restitution nor mass from motion' is unfair on mass (medium confidence: the PDF text confirms mass+friction+Bullet, scenario details compressed).

HELD-OUT REAL-INTERACTION VALIDATION OF AN IDENTIFIED TWIN EXISTS: PhysTwin (arXiv 2503.17973): 3 RealSense D455 RGB-D cameras, 22 real scenarios, 7:3 train/test split, zero-order then 'first-order gradient descent, leveraging our custom-built differentiable spring-mass simulator', evaluated on 'novel interactions'. Spring-Gaus (arXiv 2403.09434) likewise evaluates future prediction on real captures. The proposal's protocol is the rigid-body counterpart, not a new protocol.

THE EVALUATION METRIC IS GAUGE'S: GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948, html) normalises simulator error by real trial variability: 'a normalized value below one indicates that the simulator-to-real discrepancy is smaller than the within-trial RMSE'. GAUGE setup confirmed as 16 NOKOV IR cameras at 180 Hz in a 2 m cube with 3 rigid materials, so the proposal's characterisation of GAUGE is fair; GAUGE evaluates engines (Isaac, Genesis, Newton) with calibrated parameters and does not identify per-object parameters.

FISHER-INFORMATION IDENTIFIABILITY FROM A SIMULATOR IS NOT NEW: ASID (arXiv 2404.12308, html) optimises argmin_pi tr(I(theta,pi)^-1) with the simulator's Fisher information and identifies inertia and friction on a Franka with two D455s. DROPO (arXiv 2201.08434) infers domain-randomisation DISTRIBUTIONS from an offline real trajectory dataset, which is the 'measured DR ranges for Isaac Lab users' practicality claim, minus the phone. The proposal's claim that per-parameter CIs from J^T J is something 'no engine paper offers' is at best a packaging novelty (Laplace/Fisher CIs are textbook sysID).

'NO SHIPPED ENGINE GIVES GRADIENTS THROUGH MESH CONTACT' IS AN OVERCLAIM: DiffSDFSim (nonconvex SDF contact gradients, 2021); Ostrich (arXiv 2609.08800) differentiates through stiff contact on 'triangle-mesh terrain' via the implicit function theorem; DiffMJX / Contacts-from-Distance (arXiv 2506.14186, ICLR 2026) gives contact gradients under hard contact; Warp/Newton SolverSemiImplicit itself is differentiable (the project's own g0 check runs on it).

NEAREST PRIOR WORK IS CHARACTERISED FAIRLY WHERE CHECKABLE: EKFPhys (arXiv 2309.15703): RGB-D, differentiable-physics EKF, mesh shapes, friction + pose/velocity, real dataset (the '4 YCB objects, 0.0246' numbers not verifiable from the abstract: medium). One-Shot Real-to-Sim (arXiv 2412.00259): robot action + 'sparse visual and tactile observations', RA-L. PIN-WM (arXiv 2504.16693, RSS 2025) and TwinAligner (arXiv 2512.19390): robot-object interaction, GS observational loss, no measured parameter truth. VideoPhysEdit (arXiv 2609.35134, html): PyBullet, constraint-based parameter solving (not differentiable), SAM2 + CoTracker3 + VGGT, 20 synthetic scenes quantitatively, only TWO real videos qualitatively with 'no paired counterfactual targets'; it also already states masses are constrained 'only up to one scale per connected component of the dynamic contact graph', the same mass-ratio limitation the proposal adopts. IRIS (arXiv 2603.16432): 240 lab videos at 4K/60 fps with measured ground-truth parameters, single- and multi-body.

CLOSEST 2026 MULTI-OBJECT WORK DOES NOT COVER THE CLAIM: MOSIV (arXiv 2603.06022, ICLR 2026, html): per-object continuous parameters via a differentiable MPM simulator, but multi-view RGB with calibration, Genesis-generated SYNTHETIC data only ('Extending the framework from controlled settings to real-world videos remains challenging'), 2-3 objects per scene, material parameters (Young's modulus, yield stress, friction angle, viscosity), not rigid friction/restitution/mass. MonoPhysics (arXiv 2605.30320, NeurIPS 2026): monocular, deformable, Young's modulus. Analytic Dynamics (arXiv 2608.31025): simulation-trained inference. RigPI (arXiv 2606.25212): F/T measurements plus robot.

NOT FOUND (the surviving gap): any work identifying friction + restitution + CoM + mass ratio for >10 everyday RIGID objects from uninstrumented single-phone RGB video, on indoor and OUTDOOR floors, with kitchen-scale masses as truth and withheld interactions plus per-parameter invariants as the test. Caveat: only one WebSearch call ran before the session's search budget was exhausted, so the 2025-2026 literature was checked by direct arXiv fetches of known ids rather than an exhaustive sweep; a 2025-2026 'phone video to rigid digital twin' paper could exist that I did not reach (medium confidence on absence). The WRBench claim in the thesis was not verified (low confidence).
verdicts.surviving_form: Drop every method-novelty claim: 'differentiable contact identification from video' (gradSim, DiffSDFSim, EKFPhys), 'mass via collision with a reference object' (Galileo 2015 on the very same Physics 101 footage), 'Fisher/J^T J identifiability and CIs' (ASID, textbook sysID), 'DR ranges from real data' (DROPO), 'held-out-interaction validation of an identified twin' (PhysTwin, Spring-Gaus), 'variability-normalised trajectory error' (GAUGE), and 'no engine gives mesh-contact gradients' (DiffSDFSim, Ostrich, Warp). What survives is a MEASUREMENT / BENCHMARK contribution, to be stated as such: (1) the first uninstrumented (single phone, 240 fps, printed marker, kitchen scale), many-object (>=100), everyday-rigid-object dataset with identified friction, restitution, CoM and mass ratio, indoor AND outdoor floors, released with tracks, weighed masses, theta and CIs; (2) a validation protocol built on per-parameter invariants (two drop heights, two strike speeds, product rule across floors) plus withheld interactions, which no sim-ready pipeline (PhysX-*, SimReady, VideoPhysEdit, HoloScene) has applied; (3) a side-by-side of identified-twin vs material-prior vs LLM-number vs i2v world model on the same real withheld clips. Batched Warp identification with tape Jacobians should be framed as engineering that makes (1) affordable, not as the contribution; the four-poke protocol should cite Galileo (collision) and Bounce-and-Learn (reference probe) as its antecedents. The paper's defensible headline is 'phone-measured physics for N everyday objects, validated on held-out real interactions', and its value stands or falls on N, on outdoor floors and on the invariant pass rate, not on the optimiser.
verdicts.summary: The method core is not new: differentiable-simulation identification of rigid friction/mass from real video (gradSim 2021, DiffSDFSim 2021, EKFPhys 2023), mass from a collision with another object (Galileo 2015, fitted to Physics 101 itself with Bullet), Fisher-information identifiability (ASID 2024), DR ranges from offline real data (DROPO 2022), held-out-interaction validation of an identified twin (PhysTwin 2025, deformable) and variability-normalised real-vs-sim error (GAUGE 2026) all exist, and several of the proposal's sharpest novelty sentences ('no engine paper offers CIs', 'no shipped engine gives gradients through mesh contact') are overclaims. The nearest prior work it names is otherwise characterised fairly (VideoPhysEdit: PyBullet constraint solving, 2 real videos, qualitative only; MOSIV: synthetic multi-view MPM; IRIS/GAUGE: instrumented lab). What I could not find is the specific combination of uninstrumented single-phone capture, hundreds of everyday rigid objects, outdoor floors, weighed masses and withheld-interaction plus invariant validation; that is a dataset/benchmark contribution, not a method one, and it is the only form in which the proposal survives this lens. Caveat: the search budget allowed one WebSearch; coverage of 2025-2026 came from direct arXiv fetches of known ids, so absence of a 'phone-to-rigid-twin' paper is medium confidence.

evidence: FIRST EXPERIMENT IS FEASIBLE IN TWO WEEKS. Ran scripts/g0_grad_check.py today on a free A6000: tape d(slide)/d(mu) = -0.5448 vs central FD -0.5453, rollout bit-identical to MeshProbeScene, 0.5 s per 1200-step forward+backward (386 vertices). docs/results/p2_ramp_all.json holds 643 clip records each with the real tracked trajectory `s`, `fps`, `start`, so the 359 trials and their tracks are on disk; scripts/e1_heldout.py already consumes them. Projected-iterate trust-region LM exists in scripts/o8_joint_sim.py. Cost: p4 world = 1.2 s x 30 fps x 336 substeps = 12,096 steps, ~5 s per forward+backward, so 70 objects x ~10 LM iterations is about an hour of GPU.

But three inputs the first experiment names are not differentiable today: src/sim/mesh_scene.py bakes CoM at construction (lines 101-125 re-centre the local vertex cloud, `self.local` is a plain wp.array), mass enters via set_masses into `self.mass`/`self.G` without requires_grad, and DiffMeshScene.rollout does `self.pos[0].assign(self.pos0)` which breaks the tape for s0/v0. Release time is discrete. So per-trial 'Gauss-Newton on (log mu, release time, s0, v0) with the Jacobian from the tape' needs a kernel-based initial-state copy and an outer interpolated time shift; 1-3 days of work, not a blocker, but the week-1 Jacobian over (alpha, CoM, mass ratio) requires making all three parameters tape inputs first.

THE PRE-REGISTERED IMPACT GATE ALREADY FAILS. Ran scripts/g0d_grad_free.py today (soft contact pen_frac 5e-3, two free cubes, no plane): head-on d(A x)/d(cd) tape -2.958e-5 vs FD -1.787e-5 (1.66x off); glancing 3 cm offset tape +0.0007 vs FD +0.0007 (exact); glancing 5 cm tape +0.0018 vs FD +0.0037 (2x off). The proposal's own gate is 'within 10% ... d(post-strike velocity)/d(mass ratio) through a reference-ball impact'. On the measured numbers restitution and mass ratio fall back to 1-D sweeps on day 1, so the headline 'four parameters in one batched gradient pass' cannot hold as written; what remains differentiable is mu (where the sweep is already exact to 0.005, as the proposal admits) and CoM via topple, whose gradient through a bifurcation is untested anywhere in the repo (p9 reads time-to-topple from the simulator, never a gradient).

The sweep gate '|mu_tape - mu_sweep| <= 0.005' is set exactly at the sweep's own quantisation: scripts/p4_sim_loop.py uses MUS = arange(0.10, 0.401, 0.01), so +-0.005 is the grid half-step. The gate cannot fail for a working tape and therefore measures nothing beyond 'LM converges'.

The kill-test invariant 'same e within 0.05 from two drop heights' contradicts the project's own contact law: p8 measured e = 0.70 at 1 m/s and 0.54 at 2 m/s under Hunt-Crossley alpha (e ~ 1 - alpha v). Two heights give different e by construction; the invariant must be stated on alpha. For non-spherical objects (boxes, cups, cans in the pilot list) first-bounce behaviour depends on landing orientation and tumbling, so 7/10 'same e' is at real risk of failing for reasons unrelated to the engine.

Metric scale and camera geometry for in-the-wild phone video do not exist in the repo. p1/p2 used a fixed DSLR side view with planar motion and scale from the object's own edge (1633-1724 px/m). The plan needs: a floor homography from a printed marker (shove, strike), a vertical-plane scale (drops), full 6-DoF pose per frame from monocular CoTracker3 tracks against a mesh (topple, 'differentiable pose step'), camera intrinsics and rolling-shutter handling at 240 fps (readout of a 1080p sensor ~2-4 ms shears a 2 m/s object by 4-8 mm, comparable to the 2.6 mm accuracy being claimed). None is written; the schedule folds all of it into 'weeks 3-4 capture pilot' alongside the capture itself.

No RGB-only 6-DoF pose path exists. CoTracker3 gives 2-D tracks; PnP against a mesh needs 2-D/3-D correspondences, and for photogrammetry meshes an initialiser (MegaPose/FoundationPose-class). The repo contains no PnP, no projection kernel, no photogrammetry (Meshroom/COLMAP) run. 'Pose from tracks against the object mesh' is listed as if available.

Weeks 7-9 scope for one researcher: capture 1,600 clips in 8-10 spaces (~16 h filming alone), photogrammetry for up to 250 objects (30-100 photos each plus reconstruction, metric scaling, watertight cleanup for the shell/solid mass model), tracking of 1,600 clips (30-80 GPU-h), per-scene batched identification, plus a persistent world API with a determinism report, in three weeks. Not credible; the realistic 90-day output is the 10-object pilot plus 2-3 spaces.

Determinism conflict: the plan replays at the soft setting for determinism, but friction and topple are validated only at the stiff tilt rig (pen_frac 1e-4), which the project measured as nondeterministic at 1.5 mm from atomic-add order. The persistent world cannot have both validated physics and seeded replay without ordered reductions, which is unbudgeted engineering.

Outdoor floors are unvalidated physics: the engine has no static friction (9 mm/s creep remains after the seating fix) and treats the floor as a plane; p4/e1 validation is on one smooth ramp board. Asphalt, paving and carpet produce stick-slip, tumbling and stopping behaviour the solver cannot represent, so the 'three outdoor floors' claim rests on nothing measured.

Tape memory/time at scale: a 2 s clip at the tilt-rig dt (1e-4 s) is 20,000 steps; per-step world-vertex buffers for 25 bodies x 2,000 photogrammetry vertices are ~12 GB plus forces/torques, feasible on a 48 GB A6000 only if the card is free (GPUs 0/6/7 showed 44-45 GB in use today) and meshes are decimated. Per-iteration time ~8-10 s, consistent with the proposal.

Licences and compute are not blockers: Physics 101 readme (phys101/readme.txt in data/phys101/phys101_v1.0.zip) states no licence and is used only for the internal first experiment; the release would be the project's own captures. CoTracker3 (CC BY-NC) and SAM2 (Apache 2.0) are fine for a research release. GPU: tracking 30-80 h + Wan baseline 15 h + identification ~20 h fits <= 2 shared A6000s.

No robot or capture rig is needed by the protocol itself (phone, tripod, scale, marker, reference ball); 240 fps slo-mo exists on current phones and 240 fps is the right call given p3's failure at 30 fps. The analytic mass-ratio from a ball strike is a valid momentum readout only for the centre-of-mass velocity; tracked surface points carry rotation from off-centre hits, so it needs the pose step from item 6, not just CoTracker3.
verdicts.surviving_form: Keep the first experiment unchanged (tape refit of the 359 Physics 101 trials: data, LM and plane-contact gradient all verified today), but raise its gate above the sweep's 0.01 quantisation (e.g. agreement with the analytic law and CI coverage, not |mu_tape - mu_sweep| <= 0.005). Reframe the 90 days as the PILOT, not the scale-up: 10-30 weighed, primitive-shaped objects on 2-3 floors (one outdoor), four pokes at 240 fps, with (i) a metric camera pipeline built and validated first (calibrated intrinsics, floor homography from an ArUco board, vertical-plane scale for drops, rolling-shutter check against a known-speed object), (ii) mu and CoM identified through the tape, restitution (as alpha, not e: the two-height invariant must be on alpha) and mass ratio by analytic momentum exchange plus 1-D sweeps, since the impact adjoint measured today is 1.7-2x off its 10% gate, (iii) held-out interactions as the test exactly as e1 does. Drop the 150-250 object / 8-10 space / photogrammetry / persistent-world-API deliverables to a follow-on, and state the headline as 'phone-only, robot-free per-object identification validated on withheld interactions' with the batched-gradient claim limited to mu and CoM. Add ordered reductions or a documented determinism budget before promising seeded replay at the validated (stiff) contact setting.
verdicts.summary: The two-week first experiment is feasible: I ran the plane-contact gradient check today (tape -0.5448 vs FD -0.5453, 0.5 s per 1200 steps), the 643 real trajectories are on disk, and the LM exists; only initial state, CoM and mass must still be made tape inputs. The 90-day plan as written is refuted on feasibility: the pre-registered impact-adjoint gate already fails on today's measurement (g0d: 1.66x off head-on, 2x off glancing against a 10% gate), so restitution and mass ratio revert to sweeps and the 'four parameters in one batched gradient pass' headline cannot stand; the metric-scale / 6-DoF monocular pose pipeline that every poke depends on does not exist in the repo and is unscheduled; the two-height restitution invariant is stated on e, which the project's own Hunt-Crossley calibration makes speed-dependent (0.70 to 0.54); outdoor floors are unvalidated for an engine with no static friction; and weeks 7-9 ask one researcher to capture 1,600 clips, photogrammetry up to 250 objects, track, identify and ship a deterministic world API in three weeks at a contact setting the project measured as nondeterministic. Compute, licences and the absence of a robot are not blockers. A pilot-scale version (10-30 primitive objects, 2-3 floors, mu and CoM by tape, alpha and mass by analytic/sweep, held-out validation) survives and is worth doing.

verdicts.lens: Impact and practicality: who consumes the output, is the effect size large enough to act on, does it answer the user's ask (actionable, differentiable physics, practical for robots/sim, scale)
evidence: Effect size over the free baseline is small on the project's own data: docs/results/e1_heldout.json gives oracle (object's own trials) 1.77 mm median vs material-table 2.55 mm vs dataset-wide median 4.40 mm. Per-object identification can at best close a 0.8 mm gap on friction; the headline's 'material prior ~2x' target is already contradicted by this file (1.44x of oracle). Nobody retools an Isaac Lab/Newton pipeline for 0.8 mm.

The differentiable engine is used exactly where the proposal admits it buys nothing. Its own text: 'nothing on the 1-D slide, where the sweep is already exact to 0.005'; mass ratio is read 'primarily by analytic momentum exchange from tracked velocities'; restitution from two drop heights is an analytic ratio; CoM from time-to-topple is a 1-parameter sweep (p9: 0.61 mm recovered by sweep). Every one of the four pokes is solved without a tape. The user asked for differentiable physics as the lever; here it is decorative.

The batching/uncertainty argument ('at 200 objects nobody will sweep') is arithmetically false at the proposal's own cost figure: g0 reports 0.4 s per 1200-step forward+backward for a 386-vertex body. A central-FD Jacobian over 5 parameters x 200 objects x 100 LM iterations is 200,000 forwards x ~0.2 s = ~11 A6000-hours, inside the 80-120 h budget. Fisher CIs from FD are identical in information to tape CIs. Batching N independent bodies against a plane is GPU parallelism, not a gradient benefit.

The project's own record says gradients fail where identification is hard: docs/PROJECT_LOG.md M13 'Contact-gradient explosion: backprop through EXTENDED/continuous contact (a settling object) NaNs'; M15 'Gradient is unreliable ... CEM (gradient-free) recovers stiffness to 0.1%'; g0c (untracked, scripts/g0c_grad_diag.py docstring): 'FD d(A disp)/d(mu_B) = -0.38 but the tape gives -0.03'. The proposal pre-emptively demotes restitution and mass ratio to sweeps if the week-1 gate fails -- so the planned paper's differentiable contribution may be the slide alone, where it is explicitly nil.

Consumer mismatch for robotics: friction is identified as a PAIR value against the filmed floor; transferring to the robot's table or gripper needs the p5 product rule with one stated anchor (measured spread 0.75-1.05, with shape outliers 0.31 and 1.89). The parameters that drive manipulation sim-to-real (gripper-object friction, object-object contact) are not in the four pokes. SIMPLER/TwinAligner/PIN-WM users identify what the robot touches; a floor-pair twin does not replace that.

Scale does not match the ask. The user wrote 'very large scale beyond rooms. Interactable worlds at scale'; the proposal redefines scale as 'the number of objects whose physics is identified and checked, not square metres' and explicitly excludes reconstructed city geometry. 150-250 objects over 8-10 spaces is a dataset, not an interactable world, and the 'persistent world API' is a wrapper over a Newton scene -- consumers take USD, not a bespoke state-query API.

The capture plan's throughput and the geometry risk make the headline fragile: 1,600 clips at ~100 clips/hour is 16 h of capture for one person, fine; but every validated result used a known mesh, and the proposal states the scale-up 'depends on photogrammetry meshes being good at the contact patch' with the fallback 'limited to primitive-shaped objects ... a weaker paper'. A penalty-contact simulator sensitive to base shape (bowl sank 14.5 mm, pot CoM flipped with mass model) on photogrammetry meshes is the untested step the whole 200-object claim rests on.

What a top venue would see: physics principles are textbook (Galileo 2015 fitted Physics 101 with Bullet; the proposal concedes it); the engine novelty (gradients through mesh contact) is not exercised in any headline number; the measurement novelty is phone capture + weighed masses + held-out interactions, which is a dataset/benchmark contribution (IRIS, GAUGE, Physics 101, Bounce and Learn are the comparators), not a differentiable-physics or world-model result. The falsifiable, pre-registered kill test is a genuine strength and is why the score is not lower.

Where real per-object value could exist and is untested: mass and CoM of hollow or irregular objects (tables are structurally blind: areal vs volumetric cardboard differed 4.1 kg vs 939 g; mass-by-table within 25% for only 69% of objects) and restitution (no real measurement exists in the project; p3 failed at 30 fps). These are the parameters where an identified twin would beat a prior by far more than 0.8 mm -- but none of them needs the tape, and the proposal buries them under the slide refit as the first experiment.
verdicts.surviving_form: Drop 'differentiable' from the title and thesis; the tape is an implementation detail, not the contribution, and the project's own log shows zeroth-order wins wherever contact is sustained. Re-centre on the one claim with a large effect size: per-object identification beats any table on the parameters tables cannot carry -- mass/CoM of hollow and irregular objects and restitution -- validated on withheld real interactions. Run a 2-week, 10-object, 240 fps pilot FIRST (reference-ball strike for mass ratio, two drop heights for e, finger-push topple for CoM, all analytic or 1-D sweeps through the validated forward simulator) and report the gap to the material prior in units of trial-to-trial variability; only if that gap exceeds ~2x does the 200-object capture proceed. Make the deliverable what robotics and world-model groups can actually consume: a phone-captured benchmark (clips, tracks, weighed masses, identified theta with FD-derived CIs, withheld interactions) exported as Newton/USD physics attributes, pitched as the missing validation layer for PhysX-Anything/VoMP/SimReady and as an action-conditioned test for i2v models. Keep the tape only as a measured speed comparison against FD Jacobians at N >= 50 objects, reported honestly if it loses. Say plainly that this answers 'practical for simulations' and not 'interactable worlds beyond rooms'; if the user wants the latter, this proposal is the physics layer for UrbanVerse/Vid2Sim-style geometry and should be scoped as such.
verdicts.summary: Refuted at this lens. The expected headline is incremental: on the project's own held-out data a material table already reaches 2.55 mm against an 1.77 mm oracle, so per-object friction identification can gain at most ~0.8 mm, and the differentiable engine is deployed only on the slide, where the proposal itself says gradients buy nothing, while being pre-emptively demoted to sweeps for impacts, where the project log records NaN/explosion and CEM winning. Batching and Jacobian CIs are obtainable by finite differences within the stated budget (~11 GPU-hours for 200 objects). Consumers are weakly matched: robots need gripper/object contact, not floor-pair friction; 'interactable worlds at scale' is redefined to object count. The pre-registered kill test is sound and the phone-captured, weighed, held-out dataset is a real contribution, but as a dataset/benchmark, not as differentiable physics or a world. It survives only narrowed to mass/CoM/restitution of hollow and irregular objects, piloted analytically on 10 objects before any 90-day commitment.

proposals.title: PhysReady: a measured, held-out-validated material layer that makes generated worlds beyond rooms interactable, with the physics engine as the persistent state
proposals.thesis: Beyond a room no object will ever be filmed, so the physics of an interactable world at scale can only come from a material-and-build table, and that table is worth exactly as much as its validation on the real motion of objects it never saw; today every at-scale world (UrbanVerse's 100k assets, EmbodiedGen V2, MolmoSpaces, SimReady packs) fills mass and friction from a VLM and validates nothing. We claim that a table measured from real motion on five floor materials and about 35 materials/categories, assigned through LLM material naming and exported with uncertainty and provenance, makes an existing street-scale world's interactions (shove, drop, topple, kick) match real counterparts of held-out categories 2-3x better than the VLM numbers those pipelines ship, while the Newton engine underneath supplies the queryable, persistent, deterministic state that interactive video world models lack (WRBench: 0 of 23 persist; survey 2608.23070: 6 of 163 expose state).
proposals.what_we_build: (1) The table: the Physics 101 friction/density/build measurements (p1-p5: 15 materials, 11 with kinetic mu, 3 bounded as never-sliding) extended by 240 fps phone captures of about 20 movable categories that dominate generated outdoor and indoor worlds (traffic cone, bin, bottle, can, brick, plank, box, ball types, cup, crate, bucket, chair), 3 instances each, on 5 floors (laminate, tile, carpet, concrete, asphalt): mu_pair per floor, restitution e from two drop heights, effective density by build (areal / shell / solid), CoM by build, with per-category IQR from repeats. (2) The assignment layer: an LLM names material and build from renders (e1: 80% right on photos, costing 0.1 mm; re-measured on renders), maps to the nearest measured category with provenance ('measured category' / 'measured material' / 'prior only') and uncertainty; exported to SimReady USD fields (density, static/dynamic friction, restitution, mass, CoM) with a documented mapping from our Hunt-Crossley alpha to the PhysX restitution scalar, checked by running the same drop and slide in Newton with our kernels and in Newton's MuJoCo backend or Isaac Sim (two routes to one quantity, rule 2; GAUGE shows engines disagree, so the mapping is reported with its error). (3) The world: one existing beyond-room scene (an UrbanVerse street scene through USD import, or an EmbodiedGen V2 world; fallback: our blender_city.py street with PolyHaven and GSO props) instantiated in Newton with our exact-mesh kernels, 200-1,000 movable objects, scripted interaction probes on every object (shove at known v0, drop, topple push, kick), a state-query API, seeded deterministic replays, and the WRBench look-away protocol run on the engine (passed by construction) and on Wan 2.2 / Matrix-Game 2.0 for the same event. (4) The validation: leave-one-instance-out and leave-one-category-out predictions of real held-out interactions, scored by tracked motion normalised by trial-to-trial variability, against the VLM numbers (UrbanVerse's GPT-4.1 and EmbodiedGen's GPT-5.4 range prompts reproduced through our gateway on the same objects), SimReady/Isaac-Lab default ranges, and an image-to-video world model on the same first frames; GAUGE's measured rigid tasks scored with our kernels if its trajectories are released. (5) An outcome-difference audit at scale: for every movable object in the world, the fraction of probes whose qualitative outcome (stays / slides / topples / bounces) differs between the table and the VLM values, with a linearised outcome interval from the engine Jacobian.
proposals.builds_on_our_assets: p1_ramp_friction.py / p2_ramp_all.py / p5_transfer.py (CoTracker3 tracking, slide/roll/stay classification, mu_pair on two surfaces, the product-rule check 0.75-1.05 across block-like materials, build-aware mass transfer: areal 0.106 g/cm^2 for cardboard, shell/solid elsewhere); docs/results/p101_density.json and p5_transfer.json (the table as it stands); e1_heldout.py (the held-out protocol and the LLM naming step); src/data/assets.MASS_MODEL and MeshProbeScene(mass_model=) (CoM/inertia by build within 1% of textbook; the pot showed what a wrong build does to a probe); set_restitution_alpha, p7/p8 and p5_transfer.cd_for_restitution (restitution as alpha, mass-independent, exportable); the probe scripts f7_shove.py, p9_pot_topple.py, probe_bounce_settle.py as the scripted world interactions, each with a measured sensitivity (shove matches v0^2/2 mu g to 3%; topple time 2.2x with CoM; bounce 5.73x with damping); f14_llm_outcomes.py and the LLM gateway (Claude, GPT-6, Gemini) for reproducing the VLM baselines in the pipelines' own prompt formats; blender_city.py and src/data/assets.py (PolyHaven/GSO loaders) as the fallback street scene; f13_wan.py as the neural world-model row; src/gpu.py for packing batched rollouts on one card; the sim-side topple-count filter from o11 (render only what the sim says is a valid probe).
proposals.differentiable_physics_role: Little, and we say so: the layer is a lookup table and a lookup needs no gradient. Gradients are used in two places where they genuinely save work and nowhere else. (a) The hierarchical friction fit: with M objects on S floors the pair frictions fix M+S parameters up to one anchor; through the tape, non-analytic probes (topple time, bounce height) join the same least squares as the slides, and the Jacobian says which floor parameters each clip identifies. (b) Uncertainty propagation at scale: one backward pass per probe turns a category's measured IQR into an outcome interval for every object in the world (4,000 backward passes for 1,000 objects x 4 probes instead of ~400,000 sampled rollouts), which is what makes 'uncertainty per asset' affordable. Both use only plane-contact gradients, which are validated (g0: -0.5448 vs -0.5453 FD); the world's object-object pushes run forward only, since the pair adjoint is known to split forces wrongly (g0c). If the user wants a proposal where gradients are central, that is Proposal 1; this one is where the scale is, and the two share the capture pipeline.
proposals.scale_claim: Concrete: about 35 measured materials/categories (15 from Physics 101 plus ~20 captured, 3 instances each) on 5 floors, ~1,000 captured clips; assignment to every asset of one 100k-asset library by material naming (naming is run on a 2-5k sample plus the library's own category metadata, not on 100k renders); one street scene and two multi-room worlds instantiated in Newton with 200-1,000 movable objects, every one pushable, droppable and toppleable with queryable persistent state. 'Beyond rooms' means a street scene whose cones, bins, boxes and bottles behave right on concrete and asphalt. The framing we reject: scale as square metres. Every interaction with a movable object outdoors is still a slide, a topple or a bounce on a floor, so the axis that scales is materials x floors x builds, and city geometry (UrbanVerse, Vid2Sim) is a solved and separate problem whose output this layer plugs into. What this does not reach: deformables, articulated objects and vehicles, which stay VLM-assigned and are labelled 'prior only'.
proposals.practicality: Direct users are the pipelines that already ship physics fields without provenance: UrbanVerse-100K, EmbodiedGen V2 / ManiTwin, MolmoSpaces, BEHAVIOR-1K and SimReady asset packs get a table, a naming recipe and USD fields with uncertainty and provenance to replace GPT numbers; Isaac Lab users get measured IQRs instead of hand-picked randomisation ranges (friction 0.1-1.0, restitution 0-0.1 today); world-model researchers get a street-scale interactable scene with validated dynamics and queryable state to test persistence and physics against, in the WRBench protocol. The honest value proposition is a measured number for what the VLM route costs (e1: 3x on one board) extended to the categories and floors that matter at scale, which no one has reported.
proposals.novelty_argument: Method novelty is small and we say so: it is a measured table, an LLM naming step and a USD exporter. Evidence novelty is large: no at-scale world validates any assigned parameter against real motion (UrbanVerse checks GPT-4.1 mass against spec sheets at 19.6% MAPE and never checks friction; EmbodiedGen, MolmoSpaces, PhysX-Omni and UniPhysGen score against their own VLM/human labels, simulator stability or policy rankings), GAUGE validates engines fed measured values and never an assignment, and the project's e1 is the only held-out transfer test anywhere, on one ramp board at 30 fps. This proposal makes e1 the evaluation of an at-scale world: category-level held-out, five floors including outdoor, uncertainty per asset, the VLM baselines reproduced in the pipelines' own prompt format, and the first street-scale scene whose movable objects carry motion-validated parameters and persistent state. If reviewers answer 'a table is not a method', the reply is the measured cost of not having one.
nearest_prior_work: UrbanVerse (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.15018): 100k urban assets, 288 ground materials, mass and friction from GPT-4.1, mass checked against spec sheets (19.6% MAPE), friction unchecked, interaction = navigation. Differs: measured, motion-validated values with uncertainty, and objects that move.

EmbodiedGen V2 / ManiTwin (arXiv 2607.07459, 2603.16866): multi-room worlds with GPT-5.4 mass and friction ranges stored 'for calibration'; the authors state the values are not ground-truth calibrated. Differs: we calibrate them and measure the gap.

MolmoSpaces (arXiv 2602.11337): 230k environments, GPT-4o mass; validation at policy-ranking level (r = 0.96), which is insensitive to whether a value is right. Differs: parameter-level validation on real motion.

NVIDIA SimReady specification and BEHAVIOR-1K: the container (density, static/dynamic friction, restitution) and a material-to-friction lookup of unstated provenance. Differs: provenance, uncertainty and a tested alpha-to-restitution mapping with its cross-engine error.

GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948): measured parameters injected into Isaac/Genesis/Newton 1.3, scored on 180 Hz mocap, three rigid materials. Differs: we test assignment, not only engines, add ~35 materials/categories and outdoor floors, and score our kernels on their tasks if released.

NeRF2Physics (CVPR 2024) / PhysGS (CVPR 2026): per-point friction from LLM values validated by pad-on-surface meters. Differs: validation by the object's own motion, which is what a simulator consumes.

SIMPLER (CoRL 2024): object physics perturbed within plausible ranges changes policy success <= 15%, the counter-evidence that accuracy may not matter for some tasks; our outcome-difference audit bounds the claim by task instead of asserting it.
The project's own e1_heldout.py: one board, 15 materials, 30 fps, no restitution; this proposal is its extension to categories, floors and an at-scale world.
first_90_days: Weeks 1-2 (on disk): the first experiment, leave-one-MATERIAL-out on Physics 101 with the LLM forced to pick the nearest covered material, plus the VLM baselines reproduced in UrbanVerse's and EmbodiedGen's own prompt formats on the 101 objects (mass and friction range vs measured). Sim-side rule-1 gate: do the world probes' outcomes span >= 2x over each category's measured IQR?

Weeks 3-4: the exporter and the engine cross-check: alpha -> PhysX restitution and mu_pair -> static/dynamic friction, verified by the same drop and slide in Newton with our kernels vs Newton-MuJoCo (or Isaac Sim), reported as two routes to one quantity with the disagreement stated.

Weeks 4-8: captures: ~20 categories x 3 instances x 5 floors, shove / two drop heights / topple, 2 repeats, 240 fps, weighed masses; tracking and per-category fits with IQR; hierarchical object x floor friction fit through the tape; product-rule and two-height invariants per category.

Weeks 6-9: the world: import one UrbanVerse street scene (USD) or EmbodiedGen V2 world into Newton with our kernels (fallback: blender_city.py street + PolyHaven/GSO props); assign theta by naming; 200-1,000 movable objects; scripted probes on every object; state API; determinism report; WRBench-style look-away protocol on the engine and on Wan 2.2 / Matrix-Game 2.0 for the same event.

Weeks 9-11: validation: leave-one-instance-out and leave-one-category-out on the captures vs VLM numbers, SimReady/Isaac-Lab ranges and the i2v model; outcome-difference audit over the whole world with Jacobian-propagated intervals; GAUGE rigid tasks with our kernels if the data are out.
Weeks 12-13: write-up; release the table, naming prompts, USD layer with provenance, captures and the Newton street scene.
proposals.first_experiment: Leave-one-material-out on Physics 101, which is the at-scale situation (most generated assets belong to no measured category): for each of the 15 materials, remove all its objects, have the LLM name each removed object into the remaining 14 materials from its photo, predict its 20 deg slides from that material's median mu, and score the real tracked trajectory exactly as e1 does. Numbers produced: median trajectory error for material-held-out, read against the object-held-out 2.6 mm, the dataset-wide median 4.4 mm and the LLM's direct number 7.5 mm; and for mass, the fraction within 25% under nearest-material density by build (object-held-out was 69%, LLM guess 46%). In the same two weeks: UrbanVerse's and EmbodiedGen's VLM prompts reproduced on the 101 objects (mass, friction range) through our gateway, giving the fraction of measured values inside the returned range and the median |log error|. Zero capture, zero GPU: e1_heldout.py plus about 200 LLM calls.
proposals.kill_test: Pre-registered now, in three parts. (a) Week 2, on disk: if nearest-material assignment with a whole material held out is not better than the dataset-wide median (4.4 mm) by a paired sign test over the 15 materials, uncovered categories cannot be served and the layer is cut back to covered categories only (a scope kill, not a death). (b) Rule 1 before capture: a sim sweep must show each world probe's outcome (shove distance, rebound, topple time) spans >= 2x over the measured IQR of its parameter for at least half the categories; if measured IQRs are too wide to move outcomes, the table carries no usable information at scale and the proposal is dead. (c) The KILL, week 10: leave-one-category-out on the ~20 captured categories; if the table beats the VLM numbers (the same prompts the pipelines use) on fewer than 15/20 categories in held-out normalised trajectory error (sign test p >= 0.05), the layer is no better than what UrbanVerse already ships and the proposal is dead; SIMPLER's <= 15% result is the prior that this can happen.
proposals.resources: GPU: about 100-150 A6000-hours over 90 days on one card at a time: tracking ~1,000 clips ~20 h, world rollouts (1,000 objects x 4 probes x 3 parameter sets, batched in one Warp world) ~20 h, Jacobian passes ~10 h, Wan 2.2 and look-away baselines ~30 h, renders ~20 h. LLM gateway: a few thousand naming calls on a sample, not 100k. Hardware: the same phone, tripod, scale marker and kitchen scale as Proposal 1 plus ~60 cheap category instances (cones, bins, bottles, bricks, cups), under 300 USD. Software: usd-core for scene import; optionally Isaac Sim for the cross-engine check (falls back to Newton's MuJoCo backend). Data dependencies: UrbanVerse scenes/assets and EmbodiedGen V2 worlds must be downloadable in a usable form (fallback is our own street scene); GAUGE trajectories are a bonus, not a dependency.
proposals.biggest_risk: The result may be that it does not matter: SIMPLER found object physics within plausible ranges moves policy success <= 15%, and if the outcome-difference audit shows the VLM world and the measured world agree on most qualitative outcomes, the paper reduces to 'the numbers are 2-3x wrong but rarely change what happens', a finding, but not the one the user wants. Second: one person's capture burden (1,000 clips, 60 objects, 5 floors) plus USD conversion of someone else's scene into alpha-stage Newton; the blender_city fallback keeps the world demo alive but weakens the 'existing at-scale world' claim. Third: the table anchor (p5: pair frictions fix per-material mu only up to one scale) must be stated per floor, and a wrong anchor shifts every object on that floor together, which the two-floor invariant can detect but not remove.
proposals.expected_headline_result: A material-and-build table measured from the real motion of about 100 everyday objects on five floors, assigned to a 100k-asset generated world through LLM material naming, predicts held-out real interactions of never-seen object categories 2-3x more accurately than the VLM-assigned values those worlds ship with and than standard randomisation ranges, and runs as a persistent, deterministic Newton street scene of 1,000 movable objects whose every push, drop and topple carries a measured uncertainty (targets, to be replaced by measured values).

evidence: MEASURED object x surface friction/restitution tables from real motion already exist, several times over: GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948, confirmed from HTML) measures friction by inclined plane, restitution on an air-bearing rail, mass/dimensions directly, for wood/plastic/metal, ~1,560 trials at 180 Hz mocap, and feeds them to Isaac Sim / Genesis / Newton on 7 rigid task families (slope contact, slope slider, turntable, Newton's cradle, pendulum, bouncing ball, non-smooth contact); MIT Push (arXiv 1604.04038, confirmed) is >1M robot pushes of 11 shapes on 4 surface materials with force and pose at high precision, built explicitly 'to characterise friction variability'; Omnipush (arXiv 1910.00618, confirmed) adds 250 objects x 250 pushes with RGB-D; Physics 101 (BMVC 2016) is the project's own data. A ~35-material, 5-floor phone-captured table is a larger instance of these, not a new kind of thing.

'LLM names the material -> lookup table supplies friction/mass/hardness' is the published method of NeRF2Physics (arXiv 2404.04242, CVPR 2024, confirmed: 'LLMs propose candidate materials for each object ... zero-shot kernel regression'), PUGS (arXiv 2502.12231, confirmed: mass/friction/hardness, validated on ABO-500 measured-weight mass benchmark) and GaussianProperty (arXiv 2412.11258, confirmed: GPT-4V material -> properties, validated by MPM simulation and real robot grasping). The proposal's assignment layer is this method with a different table; the proposal under-credits that these already validate against MEASURED masses (ABO-500) and real grasps, not only 'pad-on-surface meters'.

A street-scale world with VLM-assigned mass/friction and rigid-body dynamics ENABLED already exists: UrbanVerse (arXiv 2510.15018, ICLR 2026, confirmed from HTML): 'We then assign annotated physical parameters (e.g., mass, friction) and enable rigid-body dynamics, producing stable, interactive scenes', 100k+ assets, runs in Isaac Sim. Instantiating one such scene in Newton instead is 'does it with a different engine' and is not novelty. The proposal's characterisation 'interaction = navigation' is only half fair: the TASKS are navigation, but the assets are dynamic.

UrbanVerse's validation is characterised fairly on the number (Appendix C.4, confirmed: mass MAPE mean 19.58% against public specs for 1,335 objects in 17 categories; geometry 1-8% MAPE) and, as far as the fetched text shows, friction is not validated (medium confidence: the C.4 excerpt lists height/length/width/mass only).

GAUGE is characterised fairly on what it does (measured params injected into three engines, 180 Hz, three rigid materials; confirmed) but the proposal OMITS that GAUGE already scores 6 image-to-video world models against the same measured real trajectories -- so the proposal's 'i2v world model on the same first frames' baseline row is already published, on better-instrumented data.

The 'engine as persistent state vs. video world models' argument is not a contribution: the survey the proposal cites (arXiv 2608.23070, confirmed: 'only 6 of 163 implementation papers expose a runtime interface for querying entity states') already establishes the gap, and any physics engine passes a persistence protocol by construction, as the proposal itself concedes ('passed by construction'). Matrix-Game 2.0 (arXiv 2508.13009, confirmed) makes no persistence claim to refute. WRBench could not be located from a primary source (no id given) -- low confidence it exists under that name.

Mass-from-appearance validated against measured weights predates all of this: image2mass (Standley et al., CoRL 2017, proceedings.mlr.press/v78/standley17a, confirmed) trains on product listings with weights and validates on an in-house scale-and-camera set. The proposal's 'mass by build-aware density within 25% for 69%' competes with this line and does not cite it.

PhysX-3D (arXiv 2507.12465) / PhysX-Anything (arXiv 2511.13648) and EmbodiedGen (arXiv 2506.10600 / V2 2607.07459) and ManiTwin (2603.16866) and MolmoSpaces (2602.11337): all confirmed to exist with 'physical properties' assigned to generated/collected assets; none of their abstracts describes validation of those properties against real motion (consistent with the proposal's gap claim). The specific claims that EmbodiedGen V2 uses GPT-5.4 ranges 'for calibration' and MolmoSpaces uses GPT-4o mass could NOT be confirmed from the abstracts (low confidence).

What I could NOT find in any primary source: a leave-one-category-out evaluation of VLM-ASSIGNED friction/restitution (in the prompt format an at-scale pipeline actually uses) against the real tracked motion of held-out everyday objects on multiple floors, with per-category uncertainty, i.e. 'the measured cost of the VLM route'. GAUGE tests engines fed measured values and never an assignment; NeRF2Physics/PUGS validate mass and grasps, not trajectories; UrbanVerse validates mass against spec sheets. The project's own e1 (docs/results/e1_heldout.json, one board, 30 fps, no restitution) is the closest thing and is in-house, so the increment is e1 -> categories + floors + restitution.

Cross-engine disagreement with measured inputs is already documented by GAUGE (Isaac Sim best on most rigid tasks; Newton RMSE > 30 m on turntable), so a Hunt-Crossley-alpha -> PhysX-restitution mapping with stated error is engineering on top of a known result, not a finding.

Differentiable-physics content (Jacobian-propagated outcome intervals, hierarchical object x floor fit through the tape) is standard sensitivity analysis / system identification; ASID (arXiv 2404.12308, confirmed) and gradSim already do real-data sysID of mass/friction, and the proposal itself says gradients are 'little' here. No novelty credit on this axis, and it does not meet the user's stated wish for a direction built on the differentiable engine.
verdicts.surviving_form: Drop every claim about the world, the engine, persistence and the exporter as contributions (UrbanVerse already ships a dynamic, VLM-parameterised street scene in Isaac Sim; the survey already states the 6/163 state-feedback gap; GAUGE already scores engines and i2v models on measured trajectories). Drop 'measured material table' as a contribution (GAUGE, MIT Push, Omnipush, Physics 101). What survives is one narrow EVIDENCE claim, which no primary source I could find reports: 'the physical parameters that at-scale sim-ready pipelines assign from a VLM (reproduced in their own prompt formats) mispredict the real motion of held-out everyday-object CATEGORIES on common floors by a measured factor X relative to a motion-calibrated material table, and that error changes/does not change the qualitative outcome (stays/slides/topples/bounces) in Y% of interactions.' Keep: the Physics 101 leave-one-material-out experiment (zero capture) as the first result; the 240 fps capture only if it adds restitution and outdoor floors, which Physics 101 and GAUGE lack; the outcome-difference audit as the one number the field does not have (bounded against SIMPLER's <=15% policy-level result). Also required for the claim to stand: report NeRF2Physics/PUGS/GaussianProperty as the method baseline for 'LLM names material -> table', not only UrbanVerse's raw GPT numbers, and run GAUGE's released rigid tasks if available, since that is the better-instrumented prior data. Framed this way it is a measurement paper / benchmark extension of e1, not a system.
verdicts.summary: Refuted as a new system. Each component already exists in primary sources I verified: measured object x surface friction/restitution tables from real motion (GAUGE 2608.05948 with 180 Hz mocap and inclined-plane/air-rail measurements for wood/plastic/metal; MIT Push 1604.04038 on 4 surfaces; Omnipush 1910.00618), LLM material naming into a property lookup validated on measured masses and real grasps (NeRF2Physics 2404.04242, PUGS 2502.12231, GaussianProperty 2412.11258), a 100k-asset street world with GPT-assigned mass/friction and rigid-body dynamics enabled in Isaac Sim (UrbanVerse 2510.15018, mass validated at 19.58% MAPE on 1,335 objects), i2v world models scored on measured real trajectories (GAUGE again), and the persistence/state-feedback gap already quantified by the survey 2608.23070 (6 of 163). Running the same world in Newton is a different engine, not novelty, and the differentiable-physics role is admittedly marginal and standard. The proposal's characterisations of UrbanVerse and GAUGE are numerically fair but omit that GAUGE already covers the video-world-model baseline and that UrbanVerse's assets are dynamic; several cited specifics (WRBench, EmbodiedGen GPT-5.4 'calibration' ranges, MolmoSpaces GPT-4o mass) could not be confirmed from primary pages. The one sub-claim I could not find anywhere is the evidence claim: a leave-one-category-out, trajectory-level measurement of how badly VLM-assigned friction/restitution (in the pipelines' own prompt format) predicts real held-out motion across floors, and whether that changes qualitative outcomes. That is an extension of the project's own e1, worth doing, but it is a measurement paper, not an interactable-world system. Score 3/10. Note: the session's web-search budget was exhausted after one query, so coverage relied on direct fetches of known ids; PhysGS, VoMP, UniPhysGen, PhysX-Omni and HoloScene were not re-verified.

evidence: FIRST EXPERIMENT IS RUNNABLE IN 2 WEEKS: scripts/e1_heldout.py (293 lines) already implements classify (LLM via gw.letsur.ai, key present at ~/.config/letsur/key, cached in outputs/scene/e1_llm.json) and score; Physics 101 is on disk (data/phys101, 6.1 GB incl. the zip with objects/mass and objects/vol); docs/results/e1_heldout.json holds the baseline rows (oracle 1.77 mm, material 2.55, pipeline 2.72, LLM direct 7.53, global 4.40; mass within-25%: build-aware 69.3%, LLM 45.5%). Leave-one-material-out is a loop change plus ~100 re-prompts restricted to 14 classes: days, not weeks, zero GPU.

BUT KILL TEST (a) IS UNDERPOWERED BY CONSTRUCTION: docs/results/p2_ramp_summary.json shows only 11 of 15 materials have a kinetic mu (foam 0/35, h_rubber 0/36, m_coin 0/20, rubber never slide at 20 deg), so the trajectory sign test runs over 11 materials: 10/11 wins is needed for two-sided p<0.05 (9/11 gives p=0.065). The 11 medians span only 0.159-0.330 with the dataset median ~0.22, so nearest-material vs global-median predictions differ by ~0.02-0.05 in mu; the global row already scores 4.4 mm vs material 2.6 mm on object-held-out. A scope kill at week 2 is the likely outcome of the test as designed, not a measurement of the layer.

NO BROADPHASE EXISTS FOR A 200-1,000 BODY WORLD: src/sim/mesh_scene.py line 365 launches pair_contact_mesh with nV*N threads (every vertex of every body queried against every other body's BVH, src/sim/mesh_contact.py line 110). With target_faces=2000 (src/data/assets.py line 84, ~1k vertices/asset), 1,000 objects = 1e6 x 1e3 = 1e9 mesh queries per substep; the tilt rig runs 24 fps x 420 substeps (~1e4 substeps per simulated second) -> ~1e13 queries per simulated second. Even 200 objects on the 60-substep bounce rig is ~6e10 per simulated second. A persistent world with object-object contact needs a hash-grid/AABB broadphase that is not in the codebase and not in the 90-day budget.

DETERMINISM CLAIM CONFLICTS WITH THE PROJECT'S OWN MEASUREMENT: CLAUDE.md (gradients section) records that at the stiff tilt-rig setting the forward of a two-body collision is nondeterministic at 1.5 mm from atomic-add order; p6_recheck records 0.6-2.2 cm GPU nondeterminism on long slides. 'Seeded deterministic replays' of a 1,000-body contact world is not passed by construction.

CAPTURE COUNT IS UNDERSTATED 2.4x: 20 categories x 3 instances x 5 floors x (shove + 2 drop heights + topple) x 2 repeats = 2,400 clips, not ~1,000, plus weighing 60 objects, in weeks 4-8 which overlap the exporter (3-4) and the world build (6-9) for one researcher.

NO CONTROLLABLE REAL EXCITATION WITHOUT A RIG: the sim probes are 'shove at known v0' (f7_shove.py) and 'topple push' (p9_pot_topple.py uses a tilted plane at 40-46 deg with body mu 4.0, i.e. a rubber ramp). A hand shove has unknown v0 (must be read from post-release frames, hand occluding) and a hand push has no controllable force, so topple time cannot be validated on real captures as planned; Physics 101 itself used a ramp board for exactly this reason. A tilting board and a launch ramp are cheap but are not in the plan or the budget.

RESTITUTION: 240 fps phone is sufficient (0.3 m drop -> 2.4 m/s impact -> 1 cm/frame), but for non-spherical categories (box, brick, cone, crate) rebound depends on impact orientation; with 2 repeats x 3 instances = 6 clips per category-floor cell the per-category IQR is not an IQR. p3_restitution.py already failed at 30 fps; the plan's two-height invariant will likely fail for shape reasons on half the categories.

GRADIENT CLAIMS ARE CONSISTENT WITH DISK but narrower than the text implies: d(slide)/d(mu) = -0.5448 vs FD -0.5453 is recorded in CLAUDE.md only (no g0 json in docs/results; the g0_*.json files there are judge-era pairwise verdicts). Pair-adjoint failure (-0.032 vs FD -0.385) is recorded. Topple time is an event time and not tape-differentiable without a surrogate; 'Jacobian-propagated outcome intervals' are meaningless across stays/slides/topples thresholds, which is why the plan also budgets 3 forward parameter sets - the gradient role is honestly small.

CROSS-ENGINE CHECK: newton 1.4.0 lists SolverMuJoCo but `mujoco` is not installed in the warp env (import fails); pip-installable. MuJoCo collides meshes as convex hulls, so the two-routes check is meaningful only for the cube, not for teapot/pot shapes.

EXTERNAL WORLD DATA: UrbanVerse training scenes exist as USD stages on HuggingFace (UCLA-VAIL/UrbanVerse-Training-Scenes, built for Isaac Sim) and usd-core 0.26.8 is installed, so import is possible; asset licences (curated from mixed sources) are unverified, and the 100k-asset library's per-asset physics fields are what must be downloaded to reproduce the VLM baseline. EmbodiedGen V2 (2607.07459), WRBench, survey 2608.23070 and Matrix-Game 2.0 baselines are unverifiable from here and are decorative, not dependencies; blender_city.py + 56 local rigid assets is the only guaranteed world.
GPU BUDGET IS FINE: 100-150 A6000-hours over 90 days on <=2 cards; GPUs 2, 4, 5 were idle at check time; Wan 2.2 at ~15 min/clip gives ~120 clips in the budgeted 30 h.
Sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.15018 ; https://huggingface.co/datasets/UCLA-VAIL/UrbanVerse-Training-Scenes
verdicts.surviving_form: Keep the first experiment unchanged (it runs in days), but replace the week-2 kill with a paired per-trial test (359 trials) and report per-material results descriptively; 11 materials cannot carry a sign test. Narrow the capture to ~10 categories x 3 instances x 3 floors (laminate, concrete, carpet) with two cheap fixtures bought in week 1: a tilting board (Physics-101 style, gives mu by the validated p1/p4 pipeline and a controlled topple) and a short launch ramp (repeatable v0 for shove); drop hand-pushed topple from real validation; ~700 clips. Build a hash-grid broadphase for pair_contact_mesh in weeks 3-4 (replacing the cross-engine check, which moves to a stretch goal with mujoco pip-installed), then target 100-200 movable objects and report the measured nondeterminism rather than claiming determinism by construction. Make blender_city.py + GSO/PolyHaven the primary world and UrbanVerse USD import the stretch; drop Matrix-Game/WRBench rows. Restitution only for compact/rounded categories (balls, cans, cups) with >= 5 repeats; boxes, bricks, cones get mu and density only. Gradients: per-object plane-contact Jacobians only, applied to slide and rebound (not topple time), with threshold outcomes evaluated by three forward runs at the IQR bounds.
verdicts.summary: The two-week first experiment is genuinely on disk and runnable (e1_heldout.py, Physics 101, LLM gateway all present), but its pre-registered kill is underpowered (11 slidable materials, mu spread 0.16-0.33 against a global median already at 4.4 mm). The 90-day plan as written depends on things that do not exist: a broadphase for the all-pairs nV x N pair-contact kernel (a 1,000-body world is ~1e13 BVH queries per simulated second), a controllable real excitation for shove and topple without a rig, and a clip budget it undercounts 2.4x (2,400 clips, not 1,000) stacked on one researcher alongside the exporter, world import and validation. Determinism of a many-body contact world contradicts the project's own 1.5 mm atomic-order measurement, and restitution on non-spherical categories from 6 clips per cell will not yield an IQR. UrbanVerse USD scenes do exist and usd-core is installed, GPU budget is adequate, and plane-contact gradients are validated, so a narrowed version (3 floors, 10 categories, two cheap fixtures, a broadphase, 100-200 objects, blender_city primary) is feasible in 90 days; the proposal as stated is not.

evidence: Effect size the headline rests on is millimetres on a 1 s ramp slide: docs/results/e1_heldout.json gives material 2.55 mm / LLM-direct 7.53 mm / dataset median 4.40 mm median RMS (oracle 1.77 mm). The '3x' is between a measured table and a GPT number on a single whiteboard ramp; the proposal's own 'biggest_risk' concedes that if qualitative outcomes rarely flip (SIMPLER, CoRL 2024: <=15% policy-success change within plausible ranges) the paper reduces to 'numbers 2-3x wrong but rarely change what happens'. The outcome-difference audit that would answer this is item (5) of five, not the headline.

The VLM generic prior is ~0.4 (f14_llm_outcomes: implied mu_eff 0.31-0.47 for every object). The measured Physics 101 board values are 0.16-0.33, which is why e1 shows a large gap. On the proposal's headline floors (concrete, asphalt, carpet) with cones, bins and bottles, real mu is plausibly 0.4-0.7, i.e. close to the VLM prior, so the expected gap on exactly the 'beyond rooms' cells may shrink toward zero -- the claimed 2-3x is extrapolated from the one regime where the prior happened to be far off.

The table gives mu_PAIR on 5 named floors, but a generated world does not know its floor material either (UrbanVerse: 288 ground materials). Assigning each floor to one of 5 measured floors is the same unvalidated VLM naming step on the other side of the contact, and p5_transfer.json shows pair frictions fix per-material mu only up to one anchor per floor -- a wrong floor anchor shifts every object on it together. No consumer gets a usable number without re-doing this naming for their own grounds.

Who acts on it: Isaac Lab / SimReady users pick domain-randomisation ranges for robustness, not accuracy; a narrower measured IQR is not obviously what they want. Digital-twin and world-model users need per-INSTANCE values, and e1 shows instance variation is real (oracle 1.8 mm vs category 2.6 mm; cardboard mu falls with cube size, Spearman -0.80 in p1). UrbanVerse/EmbodiedGen/MolmoSpaces would need to adopt a 35-row table from a one-person project with a 5-floor domain; no concrete adoption path is given beyond 'they get a table'.

Restitution export is structurally lossy: the project measured Hunt-Crossley e = 0.54 at 2 m/s vs 0.70 at 1 m/s (p8), while PhysX/SimReady restitution is a single velocity-independent scalar. The proposal exports it 'with its error', meaning the one field the at-scale pipelines actually consume for bounces is ~30% wrong across drop heights by construction. And real restitution has never been captured in this project (p3 failed at 30 fps); 240 fps phone drops of crates and bins landing on edges will give tumbling, not a scalar e, so rule-1 gate (b) is likely failed for restitution before the kill test is reached.

The '200-1,000 movable objects in Newton with our exact-mesh kernels' is not feasible as the code stands: src/sim/mesh_scene.py:365 launches pair_contact_mesh over nV*N threads -- every world vertex of every body queried against every other body's BVH, with no broadphase -- and state arrays are stored for every substep (line 173). At ~5k verts x 1,000 bodies x 1,000 bodies x 420 substeps per frame this is O(10^12) mesh queries per rendered frame. The street-scale world needs a broadphase, island/sleeping and memory rewrite of alpha-stage code, none of which is in the 90-day plan.

The 'persistent, queryable, deterministic state that interactive video world models lack (WRBench 0/23 persist)' is a straw man: every physics engine passes a look-away test by construction, as the proposal itself writes ('passed by construction'). A reviewer will not credit a simulator for being a simulator.

Does it answer the user's ask: (a) differentiable physics -- 'Little, and we say so'; the two uses (hierarchical fit through the tape, Jacobian intervals) are conveniences a finite-difference sweep replaces at 35 parameters; (b) robots -- no robot, no policy, no manipulation result, only sim-pipeline consumers; (c) scale -- explicitly re-defined from 'beyond rooms' to 'materials x floors x builds', with city geometry declared 'solved and separate'. The user's three words are each either dropped or renamed.

Workload: ~1,000 phone clips at 240 fps (60 objects x 5 floors x 3 probes x 2 heights/repeats), CoTracker3 on all of them, a USD import of someone else's 100k-asset scene into Newton 1.4 alpha, a world engine rewrite, Wan 2.2 baselines (~15 min/clip on an A6000 with CPU offload, f13), and the validation -- in 13 weeks by one researcher whose history on this project shows each probe took several iterations to get the frame conventions right (four wrong-frame bugs recorded in CLAUDE.md).

Venue: method novelty is self-declared small (table + LLM naming + USD exporter). As a dataset/benchmark paper it is Physics 101 (BMVC 2016, 101 objects) re-shot outdoors at 240 fps with masses -- a legitimate NeurIPS D&B / CoRL-datasets submission if released cleanly, but that is not how it is framed, and the 'at-scale world' and 'world-bridge' claims are the parts least likely to survive review.

What does survive: the first experiment (leave-one-MATERIAL-out on Physics 101 + reproducing UrbanVerse/EmbodiedGen prompts on the 101 objects) is genuinely actionable, zero GPU, zero capture, ~2 weeks, and produces a number nobody has reported (fraction of measured mu/mass inside the VLM range; held-out-category error). That is a workshop/short-paper result on its own.
verdicts.surviving_form: Cut to what is cheap, falsifiable and new, and stop calling it a world. (1) Run the on-disk first experiment now: leave-one-material-out on Physics 101 with LLM nearest-material naming, plus the UrbanVerse / EmbodiedGen / MolmoSpaces prompts reproduced on the 101 objects, reported as 'fraction of VLM-returned values inside the measured IQR' and median |log error| for mu and mass. If the material-held-out error is not better than the 4.4 mm dataset median by sign test, stop here and publish the VLM-gap number as a short paper.
