(2) Only if it passes: a small capture (5-8 categories that are genuinely outdoor-and-generated -- cone, bin, bottle, can, brick -- on 2 floors, concrete and laminate, shove + topple only, no restitution), framed as 'Physics 101 outdoors' dataset + a 2-floor transfer test, released with masses and 240 fps clips. (3) Replace the 1,000-object street scene and the WRBench row with an OUTCOME-level test that directly answers SIMPLER: for ~50 GSO/PolyHaven props on one surface, the fraction of shove/drop/topple outcomes (stays / slides / topples / bounces) that flip between table values and VLM values, with the Jacobian interval -- that single fraction is the number a pipeline maintainer would act on, and it needs no broadphase rewrite. (4) Drop the alpha-to-PhysX restitution export, or report it only as the measured velocity dependence that a scalar cannot carry. (5) If the user's ask (differentiable engine, robots, scale) is binding, this proposal is not the vehicle; it should be presented as a 2-4 week validation study that feeds whichever proposal is.
verdicts.summary: The proposal is honest and the first two weeks are a real, zero-cost experiment, but as a 90-day program its headline is an incremental number that no identified consumer would act on: a 2.6 mm vs 7.5 mm ramp-slide error on one board, extrapolated to outdoor floors where the VLM's ~0.4 prior is probably close to right, delivered as a 35-row table whose own floor side needs the same unvalidated naming step, with a restitution field that PhysX cannot represent and that the project has never measured. The 'at-scale interactable world' is infeasible with the current all-pairs vertex-vs-mesh kernel (no broadphase, per-substep state storage), the persistence claim is true of any engine, differentiable physics is admittedly marginal, no robot or policy appears, and 'beyond rooms' is redefined into materials x floors. The proposal's own biggest-risk paragraph states the most likely outcome: numbers 2-3x wrong but outcomes rarely change. It survives only as a short VLM-gap study plus an outcome-flip audit on a few dozen props, not as the world-bridge program described.

proposals.title: ContactAtlas-240: a motion-grounded object x surface contact atlas from multi-object phone captures, fitted through the differentiable exact-mesh simulator
proposals.thesis: Pair friction, restitution and build-aware density for hundreds of everyday objects on the surfaces of the built environment (desk laminate, hardwood, tile, concrete, asphalt, pavers, steel, glass, rubber, carpet) can be measured from 240 fps phone video of 10-20 objects per clip by fitting our validated differentiable exact-mesh simulator (Newton/Warp, reproduces real slides to 0.4-1.0 mm) to tracked motion, giving per-pair values WITH uncertainties at ~100x the breadth of any measured dataset (GAUGE: 3 rigid materials; PhysVid: 30 object-surface pairs; Physics 101: 15 materials on one board, no restitution). The atlas is the first whose assigned values are checked against the real motion of held-out objects AND held-out surfaces -- the validation that every sim-ready pipeline (PhysX-3D/Anything/Omni, UniPhysGen, VoMP, UrbanVerse, SimReady, MolmoSpaces) lacks, and that the project's e1 test (2.6 mm by material table vs 7.5 mm by LLM number, 70 objects, 359 trials) already performs on one board.
proposals.what_we_build: (1) A capture protocol anyone can repeat with a phone: a 60x40 cm plywood tilt board bordered by printed AprilTags (metric scale and plane angle from the tags themselves, no inclinometer), surface sheets clamped on it, 10-20 objects released from rest at two fixed angles per surface placed near the expected slip threshold (the o13 placement that maximised leverage), a slow-rise pass for the onset angle (static friction, bonus) and topple angle (CoM height for tall objects, bonus); a drop station with the same tags, two drop heights (0.2 and 0.4 m) onto each surface sheet, 240 fps. (2) The pipeline: tag pose -> CoTracker3 (p1/p2) -> per-object rigid 2-D pose in the board frame (p2's Kabsch classifier for slide/roll/stay) -> a hierarchical, batched differentiable fit: per-pair theta = (mu_pair, alpha_pair) shared across repeats, per-clip nuisances (release time, offset, initial yaw; pre-impact pose and angular velocity for drops), 64 bodies per Warp scene on one tape, Levenberg-Marquardt with the tape Jacobian (o8's projected-iterate/trust-region fixes), uncertainty from J^T J, and per-clip Jacobian norms as an automatic rule-1 sensitivity report. (3) Every object weighed (kitchen scale), scanned (phone photogrammetry; water displacement on a subset), build class named by the LLM (areal/shell/solid, as p5) and checked against the weight. (4) Outputs: an atlas JSON (object x surface: mu_k, mu_s bound, e or alpha, with IQR over repeats and fit uncertainty; per material: factorised mu via the p5 product rule, density by build), SimReady USD physics-material presets with uncertainty ranges, and the held-out validation report (e1 protocol extended to surfaces and to the first rebound).
proposals.builds_on_our_assets: src/sim/mesh_scene.py MeshProbeScene (exact mesh-vertex plane contact, tilted plane via gn/gt/gp, seat_on_plane with zero clearance, build-aware mass_points for CoM/inertia) and the tape-safe DiffMeshScene from scripts/g0_grad_check.py (validated today: d(slide)/d(mu) = -0.5448 tape vs -0.5453 FD, 0.5 s per 1,200-step rollout of 386 vertices); src/sim/rigs.py TILT_RIG / BOUNCE_RIG and set_restitution_alpha (alpha is mass- and stiffness-independent, p8; e-vs-cd/m curve p7; cd_for_restitution in p5_transfer); the real-footage pipeline scripts/p1_ramp_friction.py + p2_ramp_all.py (CoTracker3 from the local hub cache, 19 px grid, slide/roll/stay classification, scale from the object's own edges) and p4_sim_loop.py (align_err: release time + offset alignment, simulator fit = analytic fit to 0.005 in mu over 93 trials); scripts/p5_transfer.py (pair-friction factorisation 0.75-1.05, areal/shell/solid density by build, the table anchor); scripts/e1_heldout.py (held-out protocol, LLM material naming through the Letsur gateway, cached) and docs/results/p101_density.json, p2_ramp_all.json as the Physics 101 reference table the new atlas must reproduce in ordering; src/gpu.py wait_for_gpu for the shared box; the o7/o8 sensitivity-matrix and joint-fit machinery (trust region, projected iterate, adaptive damping) reused as the LM core.
proposals.differentiable_physics_role: Honest split. (a) For a block sliding on a fixed incline, gradients buy nothing: p4's 31-point mu grid with closed-form offset already fits to 0.005 in mu, and the analytic law is as good as the simulator. (b) Gradients buy the fit wherever the motion is not analytic and the per-clip unknowns exceed two: objects that tip, rotate in yaw or tumble on the board (p2 had to EXCLUDE 24 rolling clips and 29 errors; a 6-DoF differentiable fit keeps them), and above all the first rebound of a non-spherical body, where alpha must be fitted jointly with the pre-impact pose and angular velocity (6-D nuisance per drop) -- a grid over 2,400 drops is infeasible, an LM step with the tape Jacobian is one 0.5-5 s rollout. (c) Gradients give the atlas its error bars and its rule-1 bookkeeping for free: (J^T J)^-1 per pair, and per-clip |d(observable)/d(parameter)| that says which clips carry which parameter (the o7 matrix computed per clip rather than per probe). (d) Batching: 64 separated bodies on one plane in one scene share one tape, so 5,000 clips x ~200 LM iterations fits in ~1-2 GPU-days. (e) What we deliberately do NOT need: differentiable rendering (tracked points replace pixels, as PIN-WM/gradSim needed because they had no tracker) and body-body gradients (objects are separated on the board and drop alone), which sidesteps the adjoint defect recorded for sustained multi-body contact (tape -0.032 vs FD -0.385). (f) One unvalidated gradient path is on the critical path and is gated in week 1: d(rebound velocity)/d(alpha) through a Hunt-Crossley impact has never been checked against finite differences (g0 checked sliding only); if it fails or is step-size dependent, restitution falls back to a 2-D grid over (alpha, impact phase) and the differentiable claim is restricted to the tilt-board fits.
proposals.scale_claim: Concrete 90-day target: 150 objects x 15 surfaces for friction (two fixed angles, two repeats, 10 objects per clip: ~900 board clips) and 150 objects x 4 surfaces x 2 heights x 2 repeats for restitution (~2,400 drops), ~3,300 clips and ~2,800 object-surface pairs; stretch 200 x 20. Against the field: Physics 101 = 101 objects x 1 board + 5 drop surfaces at 30 fps (restitution unrecoverable, p3); GAUGE = 3 rigid materials with mocap; PhysVid = 5 objects x 6 surfaces. 'Beyond rooms' is reframed deliberately: for contact physics the scaling axis of an interactable world is the material x surface table, not scene area. A city block has roughly ten surface classes (asphalt, concrete, pavers, steel, glass, wood, rubber, tile, carpet, painted MDF) and object materials repeat, so a validated 150 x 15 atlas with uncertainties is exactly what a scene-scale builder consumes (UrbanVerse assigns mass and friction to 102,444 assets with GPT-4.1 and validates neither against motion). Here 'beyond lab datasets' means two things we can actually do without a robot: surfaces captured where they live (outdoor concrete, asphalt, pavers, decking, steel, brick sheets and tiles bought from a hardware store) rather than one whiteboard, and objects from homes, offices and the street rather than a curated set. We do not claim a city twin.
proposals.practicality: Consumers and how: (1) Newton / Isaac Lab / SimReady users: USD physics-material presets (static and dynamic friction, restitution, density by build) per material pair with a measured spread, replacing artist-dialled or GPT values; the SimReady spec defines the fields and says nothing about provenance. (2) Scene-scale real-to-sim pipelines (UrbanVerse, EmbodiedGen V2, MolmoSpaces, PhysX-*): keep their VLM for NAMING the material (e1: 80% right, costs 0.1 mm) and take the NUMBER from the atlas (e1: 3x better than the VLM's number). (3) Robot learners: domain-randomisation ranges from measured per-material spread instead of the customary friction 0.1-1.0 / restitution 0-0.1 guesses (a DROPO-style distribution with a physical origin); honest caveat carried into the write-up: evidence that object-parameter accuracy changes policy transfer is thin and task-dependent (ASID positive, SIMPLER <= 15%, 2606.20712 'no stable adaptation signal'), so the robot-side claim is twin fidelity (replay error, SRCC) and correct DR ranges, not policy gains. (4) The project's own authored assets: theta by material name from a table that now covers their surfaces too, closing the 'our table ~ the ramp board' anchor that p5 had to assume. (5) The capture protocol itself is the product for others: a phone, a tagged board and the open pipeline reproduce a pair measurement in a minute.
proposals.novelty_argument: Every scout independently found the same hole: no sim-ready pipeline validates assigned parameters against the real motion of held-out objects, no measured friction/restitution dataset spans more than a handful of materials, restitution is unmeasured almost everywhere, and material->friction lookups (BEHAVIOR-1K, ManiTwin, EmbodiedGen, NeRF2Physics, PhysGS) have never been checked on an unseen object's slide. This proposal fills exactly that hole with the one instrument the project has already validated against reality (Newton fit to Physics 101 at 0.4-1.0 mm RMS; two-angle, camera-scale and target-independence invariants) and the one protocol nobody else runs (e1). What is new relative to the nearest work: breadth (hundreds of objects x tens of surfaces vs 1-30 pairs), restitution at 240 fps for non-spherical bodies via a differentiable 6-DoF impact fit (no one fits restitution through a differentiable engine to real high-rate video), pair factorisation tested as an invariant, uncertainties from the Fisher information, and held-out-surface transfer. What is NOT new and is said so: measuring mu by inclined plane and e by bounce is textbook and is GAUGE's method; a phone is a worse instrument than GAUGE's 16-camera mocap per trial; and fitting a cube's slide through a differentiable engine is Galileo/EKFPhys/Dojo territory -- our contribution there is scale and transfer, not method.
nearest_prior_work: GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948, 2026): measured mu (inclined plane) and e (air-bearing rail) for 3 rigid materials, 180 Hz mocap, feeds measured values into Isaac/Genesis/Newton -- never transfers them to a new object; ours trades per-trial precision for ~100x breadth, pairs, uncertainty and the held-out transfer test.

Physics 101 / Galileo (BMVC 2016 / NeurIPS 2015): 101 objects, 15 materials, one board, 30 fps, friction fit by MCMC to a Bullet engine; ours adds surfaces, 240 fps restitution, a mesh-exact differentiable engine and the e1-style held-out protocol (Galileo evaluated outcome prediction, not parameter transfer).

PhysVid (Oxford VGG, arXiv 2510.02311): 5 objects x 6 surfaces with dynamometer-measured mu, used to score video-model probes; ours is 100x the pairs and motion-measured; PhysVid's measured 30 pairs are a free external check for our instrument.

EKFPhys (3DV 2024, arXiv 2309.15703): differentiable LCP engine + RGB-D, friction of 4 YCB objects with tilt-table mocap ground truth (median error 0.025); methodologically the closest 'differentiable engine + tilt-measured mu' work -- the difference is purely scale (4 -> 150+ objects, 1 -> 15 surfaces), restitution, and the atlas/transfer purpose.

ContactNets cube toss / Dojo / DiffMJX (2020-2025): differentiable or complementarity sysid of ONE acrylic cube from 148 Hz AprilTag tosses; a 240 fps phone toss would merely replicate this -- we do not fit tosses, we fit separated single-body plane contacts where our adjoint is validated.

NeRF2Physics (CVPR 2024) and PhysGS (CVPR 2026): per-point friction ground truth from pad-on-surface meters, numbers from an LLM/VLM; our atlas is the measured replacement for their number source and our e1 result already shows the LLM number is 3x worse than a table.
Bounce and Learn (ICLR 2019): one foam ball on many surfaces (surface map, not object materials); ours covers many objects on each surface at 240 fps.

UrbanVerse (ICLR 2026) / EmbodiedGen V2 / MolmoSpaces: 100k-asset scene pipelines with GPT-assigned mass and friction, validated only against spec-sheet mass (19.6% MAPE) or policy rankings; our atlas is the drop-in number source they lack.
first_90_days: Days 1-14 (first experiment + two rule-1 gates): build the tagged tilt board and tag-based scale/angle readout (OpenCV ArUco); capture 10 household objects x 1 plywood surface x 2 fixed angles x 3 repeats at 240 fps; run CoTracker3 -> board-frame pose -> DiffMeshScene LM fit of (mu, t0, s0) per clip; measure the same 10 pairs with a luggage/spring scale drag (PhysVid's route); report route agreement and repeat IQR. In parallel, the impact-adjoint gate: d(rebound)/d(alpha) tape vs central FD on a simulated 0.2 m drop at BOUNCE_RIG settings, three step sizes.

Days 15-30: restitution instrument. Drops from 0.2 and 0.4 m at 240 fps: spheres first (steel, glass, rubber, wood balls) with the two-route invariant (flight-time ratio vs height ratio; free-fall parabola must also return the tag's px/m scale via g), then cubes/blocks, then 10 irregular objects fitted 6-DoF through the simulator over the first 100 ms after impact; decide from the data whether e of irregular bodies is a per-object parameter under Hunt-Crossley (repeat spread vs fit residual) and whether alpha differs between the two heights (model-error signal, rule 2).

Days 31-45: scale the capture. Acquire 15 surface sheets (hardware store: laminate, plywood, MDF, tile, granite, concrete paver, asphalt shingle, steel, aluminium, glass, acrylic, rubber mat, cork, carpet, cardboard) and 150 objects (home, office, hardware store, kitchen, street); weigh all, scan all, LLM-name material and build (cached); film 150 x 15 x 2 angles x 2 repeats at 10 objects per clip (~900 clips, ~15 h) with the slow-rise onset/topple pass per surface.

Days 46-60: drops at scale: 150 objects x 4 surfaces x 2 heights x 2 repeats (~2,400 clips, ~15 h); batched hierarchical fits for both corpora on one A6000 (64 bodies per scene), uncertainties from J^T J, per-clip Jacobian sensitivity report, slide/roll/stay/topple labels kept as censored observations (never-slides -> mu_s bound; topple -> CoM height for tall objects against the base from the scan).

Days 61-75: invariants and the atlas. Two-angle agreement per pair, pair factorisation (product rule across surfaces; ratio CV reported per material class as p5 did), density by build vs measured weight (areal/shell/solid), Physics 101 ordering reproduced for the overlapping material classes; assemble the atlas JSON and SimReady USD presets with ranges.

Days 76-90: the held-out tests and write-up. e1 protocol extended: hold out each object (material-table transfer vs own-trials oracle vs LLM number vs dataset median) and, separately, each SURFACE (predict a pair never captured from the factorised table); trajectory RMS and stays/slides outcome; first-rebound apex error for restitution; publish atlas, protocol, scripts; a GAUGE-style comparison on their released slope-slider trials if the data is public.
proposals.first_experiment: Ten household objects (cardboard box, wooden block, plastic block, ceramic mug, rubber eraser, metal tin, paperback book, apple, foam block, modelling clay) on one tagged plywood board at two fixed angles x 3 repeats, 240 fps phone, fitted through DiffMeshScene (mu, release time, offset jointly, LM with the tape Jacobian) -- the SAME trials measured a second way with a spring-scale drag. The experiment produces three numbers decided now: median |mu_tilt - mu_drag| over the 10 objects (instrument agreement), per-object IQR over repeats (repeatability), and Spearman rho of the 10 fitted mu against the Physics 101 20-degree ordering for the six overlapping material classes (cardboard 0.229, wooden block 0.230, plastic block 0.246, porcelain 0.166, dough 0.159, foam never-slides). Runs on <= 1 A6000 in minutes once captured; capture is one afternoon.
proposals.kill_test: Decided now, rule 1 and rule 2 applied to the instrument before any atlas number is reported. The tilt-board phone readout is DEAD if, on the 10-object first experiment, median |mu_tilt - mu_drag| > 0.05 or per-object repeat IQR > 0.03 (Physics 101's per-cube IQR was 0.01-0.03, and the low-friction materials differ by only 0.007: dough 0.159, doll 0.163, porcelain 0.166 -- an instrument coarser than that cannot populate an atlas) or the two fixed angles disagree by > 0.03 for the same pair. The restitution half is dead if the two routes on spheres (flight-time ratio vs height ratio) correlate below 0.9 over 12 sphere x surface pairs, or if alpha fitted at 0.2 m and 0.4 m differs by more than the repeat spread on most pairs (the Hunt-Crossley law is then the wrong model, not a parameter). The DIFFERENTIABLE part is dead (fits revert to grid) if d(rebound)/d(alpha) from the tape differs from central finite differences by > 5% or changes with step size. Any of these ends the direction before the 3,300-clip capture is started.
proposals.resources: Compute: <= 1 A6000, bursty: CoTracker3 ~5 s per clip (3,300 clips ~5 h), batched tape fits ~1-2 GPU-days total, everything cached and seeded. Hardware (~$400): a phone with 240 fps 1080p slow-motion, a plywood board with printed AprilTags and a clamp, 15 surface sheets, ~150 objects (most free), a kitchen scale (1 g), a luggage/spring scale for the drag route, a measuring jug for displacement. Researcher time: ~60 h of capture and weighing over days 31-60, the rest is pipeline work on existing scripts. Software: warp env for sim and fits, cosmos env for CoTracker3, OpenCV ArUco, the LLM gateway for material naming (cached). No robot, no mocap, no new models.
proposals.biggest_risk: That restitution of non-spherical everyday objects is not a per-object parameter under our contact model: corner impacts are chaotic (DiffMJX reports trajectory error stuck at 0.25 for one cube; GAUGE finds every engine worst on impulsive contact, Newton's bouncing ball at 22.7x the trial variability), so half the atlas may exist only for spheres and flat-landing blocks, and the differentiable 6-DoF impact fit may return model error dressed as alpha. Second: the phone instrument's floor -- tag pose +-0.5 deg is +-0.01 in mu, rolling shutter and blur at 240 fps add tracking noise -- may sit at the +-0.02-0.03 level where it cannot separate the low-friction materials, leaving an atlas of classes rather than values. Third, logistic: one researcher capturing, weighing and scanning 150 objects x 15 surfaces is ~60 h of bench work that no GPU can shorten.
proposals.expected_headline_result: From ~3,300 phone clips of 150 everyday objects on 15 surfaces of the built environment, a differentiable exact-mesh simulator recovers pair friction and restitution with repeatability +-0.02 / +-0.03 and two-route agreement within 0.03; the resulting 150 x 15 atlas factorises into per-material values (product rule, ratio CV ~15%) and, assigned to a held-out object or a held-out surface by material name alone, predicts the real slide and first rebound to within ~1.5x the object's own trial-to-trial spread, where VLM-assigned numbers are 3-4x worse -- the first contact-parameter table validated on the motion of objects it never saw.

evidence: GAUGE, arXiv 2608.05948 (https://arxiv.org/html/2608.05948): rigid materials wood/plastic/metal/rubber; friction by inclined plane mu=(g sin th - a)/(g cos th); restitution by air-bearing rail e=v_out/v_in; 20 mocap trials per task, ~1,560 trials across 22 task families; 'physical parameters are set from the GAUGE calibrations' -- no fitting, no held-out transfer. Dataset IS public: https://huggingface.co/datasets/InternRobotics/GAUGE-Dataset (10.5 GB, MIT, trajectories + calibrated physical metadata). Proposal's 'if the data is public' hedge is moot; GAUGE is a free external check and a direct comparator.

PhysVid, arXiv 2510.02311 (https://arxiv.org/html/2510.02311): real friction split = 5 objects x 6 surfaces, 100 videos, spring dynamometer mu_k=F/G, range 0.105-0.544; real elasticity = 100 internet ball-drop videos with manually annotated h_bounce/h_drop (0.44-0.98); best friction readout Pearson 0.73 (V-JEPA-2 w/ adaptation); no simulator fit. Release promised CC-BY-4.0 at robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/research/idpp/. Characterised fairly by the proposal.

NeRF2Physics, arXiv 2404.04242 (https://arxiv.org/html/2404.04242): MEASURED kinetic friction for '15 household objects across 13 scenes' on '6 surfaces using an iOLab with fabric pads', 10 trials each -- a measured object x surface set larger than PhysVid's 30 pairs that the proposal does not credit; values come from an LLM material dictionary + CLIP kernel regression, never validated on motion. Undercuts 'no measured dataset spans more than a handful of materials' only partly (pad meter, not motion), but the breadth claim must be stated against ~90 pairs, not 30.

EKFPhys, arXiv 2309.15703 (https://arxiv.org/html/2309.15703v3): 4 YCB objects (pitcher, bleach, mustard, mug), one table, tilt angle from mocap markers, 10 slides per object, mu = tan(alpha) - a/g; EKF-initialised median error 0.0246; no transfer to unseen objects. Proposal's '0.025, 4 objects' is accurate.

ContactNets, arXiv 2009.11193 (https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2009.11193): one 10 cm acrylic cube with AprilTags, three cameras at 148 Hz, 570 tosses on wood; learns vertex geometry + lumped friction, assumes inelastic impact (no restitution). Proposal's characterisation is accurate; AprilTag-tracked tilt/toss boards are not new.

Physics 101 (Wu et al., BMVC 2016; PDF at http://phys101.csail.mit.edu/papers/phys101_bmvc.pdf, text extracted): 101 objects, 15 materials, ramp 10/20 deg, drops onto FIVE surfaces (foam, glass, metal, wooden table, woolen rug), 4,352 trials; has a 'split by object' protocol that predicts REAL outcomes for never-seen objects: moving distance rho 0.33, bounce height rho 0.23 (0.16 when transferring from ramp-learned restitution), float 84%; restitution modelled as a per-material-pair vector. So real-motion held-out-object validation of per-material contact parameters exists since 2016; the proposal's 'first ... validated on the motion of objects it never saw' is overstated, and its own e1 already is the trajectory-level version on this very data.

Galileo (NeurIPS 2015, https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2015/hash/d09bf41544a3365a46c9077ebb5e35c3-Abstract.html): infers mass, shape, friction with a 3D physics engine from real ramp videos; evaluated by outcome prediction vs humans. Fairly characterised.
Dojo, arXiv 2203.00806 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.00806): differentiable NCP contact engine; hardware sim-to-real with a UFactory xArm 6; fairly characterised as single-system sysid territory.

Bounce and Learn, arXiv 1904.06827 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06827): 5K RGB-D bounces of ONE foam ball on surfaces in homes/offices; predicts restitution + collision normal per surface. Fairly characterised.
RigidBench, arXiv 2608.15555 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15555): simulator-grounded only, 5,000 synthetic videos; not a competitor for measured values.

Scalable Real2Sim, arXiv 2503.00370 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.00370): robot pick-and-place measures inertial parameters of diverse objects and extracts sim-ready meshes; friction/restitution not measured -- a measured-asset pipeline the proposal does not cite but should position against (mass/inertia side).

PhysX-3D/PhysXNet, arXiv 2507.12465 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12465): VLM + human-in-the-loop annotation of scale/material/affordance/kinematics; no motion validation. Consistent with the 'VLM-assigned, unvalidated' gap.

CoDimRecon, arXiv 2609.36024 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36024): agentic multi-view reconstruction with behavioral tests; abstract does not contain the 'effective parameters' quote the project attributes to it -- medium confidence, quote unverified here.

UNVERIFIED (search budget exhausted; project pages 404 / DNS fail): UrbanVerse, MolmoSpaces, EmbodiedGen V2, DiffMJX's 0.25 cube error, PhysX-Anything/Omni, UniPhysGen, VoMP, and whether any 2025-26 work already built a phone-video object x surface contact atlas. Per instructions, uncertainty counts against novelty.

Low-confidence background: smartphone/inclined-plane friction labs with video tracking (Tracker, phyphox) are standard physics-education practice; the 'anyone with a phone' protocol is not itself a research contribution.
verdicts.surviving_form: The proposal already concedes the method is Galileo/EKFPhys/GAUGE territory, so novelty can only be claimed as a DATASET + VALIDATION PROTOCOL, and even that must be narrowed: (1) drop 'first contact-parameter table validated on the motion of objects it never saw' -- Physics 101 (2016) ran split-by-object real-outcome prediction (moving distance rho 0.33, bounce height 0.23) and the project's own e1 already did the trajectory-level version; the open sub-claim is held-out SURFACE transfer through a factorised table (never done by anyone verified) and trajectory-level/first-rebound error against a measured table rather than a learned appearance model. (2) Restate breadth against the real competitors: NeRF2Physics' iOLab set (15 objects x 6 surfaces, ~90 pairs), PhysVid (30 pairs, dynamometer), GAUGE (4 rigid materials, public 1,560 mocap trials, MIT) -- so '~100x' becomes '~30x over the largest pad-measured set, and the first that is motion-measured and surface-factorised'. (3) The only genuinely unoccupied methodological square is restitution of NON-SPHERICAL everyday objects on multiple surfaces fitted 6-DoF through a differentiable engine from 240 fps video (ContactNets/Dojo: one cube, inelastic or lumped; PhysVid: manually annotated balls; Bounce&Learn: one foam ball; GAUGE: rail-measured, few materials) -- but this is exactly the proposal's own biggest risk, so it is an open question, not an established novelty. (4) The pair-factorisation invariant and Fisher-information error bars are bookkeeping, not contributions. (5) Use GAUGE's public dataset and PhysVid/NeRF2Physics pairs as external instrument checks in week 1, and state the 2016 Physics 101 split-by-object result as the baseline the atlas must beat.
verdicts.summary: Not new as a method and only partly new as a dataset. Video-fitted inclined-plane friction through a physics engine is Galileo (2015) / Physics 101 (2016) / EKFPhys (2024) / GAUGE (2026); AprilTag-tracked contact sysid is ContactNets (148 Hz, 570 tosses); measured object x surface friction sets already exist at 15 x 6 (NeRF2Physics, iOLab -- larger than the 30 PhysVid pairs the proposal credits as the maximum) and GAUGE's calibrated trajectories are public on Hugging Face under MIT, contrary to the proposal's hedge. The headline 'first contact table validated on the motion of objects it never saw' is overstated: Physics 101 already evaluated split-by-object real-outcome prediction (moving distance rho 0.33, bounce height 0.23 on 5 drop surfaces), and the project's own e1 already did the stronger trajectory-level version on the same data. Nearest prior work (GAUGE, PhysVid, EKFPhys, ContactNets, Galileo, Bounce&Learn) is characterised fairly except NeRF2Physics (under-credited). What survives is a dataset/protocol contribution: breadth (~30x the largest pad-measured set, motion-measured, 15 surfaces), held-out-SURFACE transfer via factorisation, and multi-object non-spherical restitution at 240 fps -- the last being the proposal's own biggest risk rather than a settled novelty. Several 2025-26 scene pipelines and any possible phone-video atlas could not be verified (search budget exhausted), so uncertainty counts against novelty.

evidence: Slide gradient reproduced today: scripts/g0_grad_check.py on a free A6000 gives d(slide)/d(mu_body) tape -0.5448 vs central FD -0.5453, identical rollout to MeshProbeScene, 0.4 s per 1200-step fwd+bwd (PASS).

The plan's 'unvalidated, on the critical path' impact-adjoint gate was run here (scratchpad/impact_gate.py: 7 cm solid cube, 0.2 m drop, BOUNCE_RIG pen_frac 5e-3, alpha 0.4, loss = normal rebound velocity at 0.26 s): d(v_rebound)/d(log cd) tape -0.5620 vs FD -0.5615/-0.5621/-0.5668 at 1/5/20% steps (60 substeps); -0.5596 vs -0.5594 (120); -0.5588 vs -0.5583 (240); corner landing (15 deg x 10 deg pre-tilt): -0.5686 vs -0.5686 (60), -0.5686 vs -0.5682 (240). Tape-vs-FD < 1% at every setting, so the 'differentiable part is dead' criterion does not trigger.

Caveat found in the same run: the ROTATIONAL response to a corner impact is not converged in substeps -- angular velocity at 0.26 s is -4.29 / -3.98 / -3.81 rad/s and its cd-gradient +0.243 / +0.055 / -0.103 across 60/120/240 substeps (tape still matches FD at each). A 6-DoF alpha fit of corner impacts therefore fits an unconverged forward model (rule 2 invariant fails before any data); normal-rebound restitution of spheres and flat landings is unaffected.

Compute (scratchpad/board_cost.py): 10 cubes on a 20 deg plane, 2.0 s, TILT_RIG 420 substeps = 20,160 steps, 3,860 vertices: fwd+bwd 7.5 s, 4.3 GB; 100 substeps: 2.3 s, 1.3 GB. Repeat-run nondeterminism 0.09-0.13 mm max (below the 0.4-1.0 mm real-footage fit floor). 900 board clips x 200 LM iterations at one clip per scene = ~16 GPU-days; batched 6 clips/64 bodies per scene (launch-bound, so near-constant per step) = ~3 GPU-days; the proposal's '1-2 GPU-days' is 2-3x optimistic but fits two shared A6000s in 90 days.

LM 'with the tape Jacobian' is a reverse-mode tape: one backward per scalar residual. With 3-6 parameters per clip, a finite-difference Jacobian costs the same number of rollouts and no tape memory; gradients genuinely buy only the batched scalar objective and the (J^T J) bookkeeping -- which the proposal's section (a) half admits.

Missing from the repository (grep over src/, scripts/, docs/*.md): no AprilTag/ArUco code and no photogrammetry/scan pipeline. Every real-object mesh the simulator has ever consumed was a primitive (Physics 101 cubes, measured dimensions). 150 scanned, watertight meshes with a correct build class (mesh_scene.mass_points falls back to half the bounding box when not watertight) is the largest unbudgeted cost; glossy/glass/metal/dark objects routinely fail phone photogrammetry.

Bench time days 31-60 as written: 900 board clips + 2,400 drops + weighing + scanning 150 objects + buying 15 sheets, claimed ~60 h in 30 days alongside pipeline work; realistic 100-150 h with scanning, i.e. ~2x overcommitted for one researcher.

First experiment: feasible in two weeks -- p1/p2/p4 (CoTracker3 from local hub cache, Kabsch slide/roll/stay, release-time + offset alignment, 0.005 in mu over 93 trials) exist; a tag-based scale/angle readout is ~1 day of OpenCV; 60 clips is one afternoon. Its weak point is the gate, not the capture: a hand-pulled luggage/spring scale has its own ~0.05 scatter, so 'median |mu_tilt - mu_drag| > 0.05 kills the instrument' can kill a working tilt readout against a worse reference.

240 fps phone slow-motion at 1080p exists on current iPhones/Androids; a 0.2 m drop is ~48 frames of fall and ~24 frames to apex, adequate for e by apex/flight-time; tags fill the frame so rolling shutter at <= 2 m/s is correctable. Physics 101's failure (p3_restitution: g spread 2.7x, routes correlate 0.38) was 30 fps with long exposure, not a method failure.

Licences: CoTracker3 and DINO weights in the hub cache are FAIR/CC noncommercial research licences; Physics 101 is academic. Fine for a published research atlas; the 'SimReady presets for commercial Isaac users' consumer story should state that the measurement pipeline is NC-licensed even though measured numbers are not derivative works.
verdicts.surviving_form: Keep the direction, cut the 90-day numbers roughly in half and move the mesh dependency off the critical path: (1) 60-80 objects x 8-10 surfaces, with block-like objects described by ruler-measured primitives (the sliding law is shape-independent; no scan needed) and phone photogrammetry only for a <= 20-object irregular subset whose meshes are checked watertight before any 6-DoF fit; (2) restitution from spheres and flat-landing blocks via the normal rebound velocity (adjoint verified here), with corner-impact 6-DoF alpha fits deferred until the rotational response is shown to converge in substeps (it currently changes sign in gradient between 120 and 240 substeps); (3) replace the spring-scale drag gate with two-angle agreement, repeat IQR and the Physics 101 ordering plus one dynamometer-measured reference pair, since a hand-pulled scale is a worse instrument than the one it judges; (4) budget 3-5 GPU-days on <= 2 A6000s, batch 64 bodies per tape only for the hierarchical scalar objective and use FD Jacobians for the 3-6 per-clip nuisances; (5) a tag-based scale/angle readout and a scan-to-watertight-mesh step are new code and belong in days 1-14 and 15-30 respectively, not assumed. Under that narrowing the first experiment runs in two weeks and a validated atlas of several hundred pairs is reachable in 90 days.
verdicts.summary: Not refuted, but the 90-day plan as written is overcommitted by about 2x. The two hidden gradient dependencies are real and present: the slide gradient reproduces (tape -0.5448 vs FD -0.5453) and the impact adjoint the proposal flags as unvalidated passes when run here (d(rebound v)/d(log cd) tape vs FD within 1% at three step sizes and three substep counts, flat and corner landing), with one new caveat -- the rotational response to a corner impact is not converged in substeps, so 6-DoF alpha fits of irregular bodies would fit an unconverged model. Board-length 10-body tape rollouts cost 7.5 s / 4.3 GB at the tilt rig and are deterministic to 0.13 mm, putting the fit budget at ~3-5 GPU-days (not 1-2) on the allowed two A6000s. The first experiment can run in two weeks on existing p1/p2/p4 code plus a day of ArUco work, though its spring-scale gate compares the instrument to a worse reference. What does not exist is any tag-readout or scanning code, and the headline's irregular-object, 6-DoF, restitution-at-scale claims rest on 150 scanned, watertight meshes that one researcher cannot produce alongside ~3,300 clips in days 31-60; the atlas survives at roughly 60-80 objects x 8-10 surfaces with primitives for blocks, scans for a small irregular subset, and restitution from spheres and flat landings.

verdicts.lens: Impact and practicality: who consumes the output, is the effect size actionable, does it answer the ask (differentiable physics, practical robot/sim system, scale beyond rooms)
evidence: The proposal's own 'honest split' concedes gradients buy nothing on ~900 of the ~3,300 clips (sliding is analytic; p4's 31-point grid already fits to 0.005 in mu). The only place the differentiable engine is load-bearing is the 6-DoF first-rebound fit, which the proposal itself lists as the biggest risk (corner impacts chaotic; DiffMJX stuck at 0.25; GAUGE: Newton bouncing ball 22.7x trial variability) and whose adjoint d(rebound)/d(alpha) has never been checked. So the user's ask (a) 'use a differentiable physics engine' is satisfied either trivially or on the part most likely to be cut.

Repo check: scripts/g0_grad_check.py exists and tests d(slide)/d(mu) tape vs central FD, but the cited numbers (-0.5448 / -0.5453) are in no results file; grep hits for those values are unrelated (o4_joint.json, v1_*.json). docs/results/g0*_verdict.json are all 'FAIL' and belong to an older, unrelated g0 experiment. The differentiable claim rests on an unrecorded run.

Consumer mismatch: SimReady / PhysX / Isaac Lab materials are PER-MATERIAL scalars (staticFriction, dynamicFriction, restitution) combined by a combine mode (average/min/multiply/max); there is no slot for a 150x15 PAIR atlas. What a simulator can actually ingest is the factorised per-material value -- ~15-20 numbers -- which is the size of Physics 101 (15 materials, already on disk) and of any engineering handbook table. The breadth claim ('100x') is not consumable by the named consumers.

The missing baseline that decides impact: e1 compared a measured table against an LLM number (2.6 vs 7.5 mm) and a dataset median (4.4 mm). It never compared against a handbook friction table assigned by material-pair name (the thing a SimReady user already has, and the thing NVIDIA's Omniverse physics material library ships). If handbook pairs land near 3 mm, the atlas is a precision increment nobody switches for.

Effect size in consumer terms is unstated: the headline is 'slide to ~1.5x the object's own spread' -- a few mm over a 20-degree slide. No downstream demonstration (a push task, a toss replay, a DR-range test in Isaac Lab) shows any policy, planner or scene builder behaving differently with atlas values vs defaults. The proposal admits 'evidence that object-parameter accuracy changes policy transfer is thin' (ASID positive, SIMPLER <= 15%, 2606.20712). A number without a shown downstream delta is an incremental number.

Instrument floor vs the values it must resolve: the proposal states the phone/tag floor is +-0.02-0.03 in mu, while the materials it must separate differ by 0.007 (dough 0.159, doll 0.163, porcelain 0.166). Its own kill test (IQR > 0.03) is set AT the floor, so a surviving instrument still yields 'an atlas of classes rather than values' (its words) -- i.e., a material-class lookup, which Physics 101 + p2 already provide.

Scale ask: the user asked for 'interactable worlds at scale, beyond rooms'. The proposal explicitly reframes this away ('We do not claim a city twin'); the output is a JSON table and USD presets, not a system anyone interacts with. It answers 'practical for simulations' only as a lookup table; nothing is built for robots.

Logistics vs timeline: ~60 h bench work (weigh, scan, film 150 objects x 15 surfaces + 2,400 drops) by one researcher in days 31-60, after a 30-day gate phase that may kill the direction; phone photogrammetry of 150 objects is itself days of work and is unvalidated for the build-aware CoM/inertia path (p5/p6 used authored meshes). The 90-day plan has no slack.

Venue fit: this is a dataset/benchmark paper (NeurIPS D&B / CVPR dataset track). Reviewers will compare the spring-scale 'second route' to a tribometer and the phone to GAUGE's mocap; the differentiable-engine angle will read as incidental because the proposal says so. Nearest-work table (EKFPhys, GAUGE, PhysVid, Physics 101) shows every method component exists; what is new is breadth + held-out validation, which is a solid contribution only if the breadth is consumable (see per-material point).

What does have pull: the e1 held-out-motion protocol as a BENCHMARK that scores other pipelines' assigned parameters (PhysX-Anything, UrbanVerse, VoMP, NeRF2Physics) is the thing nobody has and that would make others act; the proposal buries it as the final validation step rather than making it the product.
verdicts.surviving_form: Drop the 150-object atlas as the product; keep the capture rig and pipeline but re-aim at two deliverables people can act on. (1) A held-out-motion BENCHMARK: ~30-40 objects x ~8 surfaces filmed at 240 fps with tracked ground-truth slides, onset angles and first rebounds, released with a scorer that takes any pipeline's assigned (mu, e, mass) and reports trajectory RMS / outcome accuracy; score PhysX-Anything, VoMP/AdaVoMP, UrbanVerse-style GPT assignment, a handbook pair table, Physics 101 transfer, and the LLM-names-material+table route side by side. That leaderboard is what makes sim-ready pipeline authors act. (2) A per-material (not per-pair) SimReady/Newton preset library (~20 materials) with measured spread, shipped WITH one downstream demonstration in Isaac Lab or Newton (push-to-goal replay error or a sim-to-sim DR-range test) showing the delta versus NVIDIA's default material library -- if the delta is small, say so and the result is still publishable as a negative. Keep the differentiable engine only where it is load-bearing: gate the impact adjoint in week 1 and, if it passes, make the 6-DoF rebound fit (irregular bodies, alpha + pose jointly) the method contribution; if it fails, state the paper as a benchmark/dataset paper and stop calling it differentiable. Add the handbook-table baseline to e1 now (one afternoon, no capture) before any hardware is bought.
verdicts.summary: ContactAtlas-240 is concrete, cheap and falsifiable, but on the impact lens it is a dataset of numbers with no identified consumer who would change behaviour: simulators ingest per-material scalars (so the 150x15 pair breadth collapses to ~20 numbers that Physics 101 and handbooks already supply), no downstream task is shown to move, the obvious handbook-pair baseline was never run, the phone instrument's floor equals the resolution needed, and by the proposal's own admission the differentiable engine contributes nothing on the bulk of the data and is on the riskiest path for the rest. It also explicitly declines the user's 'interactable worlds at scale' ask. It survives only if re-aimed as a held-out-motion benchmark that scores existing sim-ready pipelines plus a small per-material preset library with a demonstrated downstream delta.

proposals.title: M2P: motion-supervised appearance-to-physics -- a photo-to-(friction, restitution, build) model trained through the differentiable simulator on real tracked motion, with no parameter labels
proposals.thesis: An image model can learn to assign contact parameters from a single photo of an object and its surface using only real tracked motion as the teacher: trajectory error is backpropagated through our validated differentiable exact-mesh simulator into the image network, so clips that are only partially identifiable (stays, never-slides, tumbles) still teach, and parameters are weighted by how much they move the motion rather than by a label. Validated on the real motion of held-out objects and held-out surfaces, this replaces the VLM-number stage of sim-ready pipelines (e1: an LLM's number is 3x worse than a measured table, 7.5 vs 2.6 mm) with a predictor whose errors are measured in millimetres of real motion -- a label source no pipeline in the landscape uses (they train and score against VLM/human annotations).
proposals.what_we_build: (1) A feed-forward model: frozen DINOv2 (or V-JEPA 2 image) features of an object crop and a surface crop -> factorised heads, mu_pair = f(object) * g(surface) (the product rule p5 measured at 0.75-1.05 across block-like materials), alpha/e, and a build class (areal / shell / solid -> density by the p5 table), each with a heteroscedastic uncertainty. (2) A training loop with the simulator in it: for a minibatch of real clips, the predicted theta of each object is placed in a 64-body DiffMeshScene (bodies separated on the plane, so only the validated plane-contact adjoint is exercised), rolled out at the clip's tilt and release, and compared to the CoTracker3 track after release-time/offset alignment (p4's align_err made differentiable); censored terms for 'stays' (simulated slide must be below p2's 8 cm threshold at that angle), 'never slides at 20 deg' (mu_eff > 0.36), 'rolls' (6-DoF pose track), and, later, first-rebound tracks at 240 fps. (3) The honest baselines: the two-stage route (fit theta per clip by grid, then regress from the photo with uncertainty weights) and the e1 ladder (own-trials oracle 1.8 mm, material table 2.6, LLM-naming pipeline 2.7, dataset median 4.4, LLM number 7.5). (4) Controls: photo-shuffle (object photos permuted among objects) and crop-only inputs to stop the model reading backgrounds. (5) Export: SimReady USD physics material per asset with a predicted range, plus a report page with the per-object held-out errors.
proposals.builds_on_our_assets: scripts/g0_grad_check.py DiffMeshScene (tape-safe MeshProbeScene; d(slide)/d(mu) matches FD to 0.1%, 0.5 s per rollout, re-run today) over src/sim/mesh_scene.py + mesh_contact.py + rigs.py; scripts/p4_sim_loop.py (simulator fit to Physics 101 trials: 0.4-1.0 mm RMS, mu matches the analytic law to 0.005) as the loss definition; scripts/p1/p2 (CoTracker3 pipeline, 643 classified clips: 281 slide / 309 stay / 24 roll, one camera scale 1661 px/m, two-angle invariant) as the training tracks already on disk in docs/results/p2_ramp_all.json; scripts/e1_heldout.py (leave-one-object-out protocol, the catalogue photos data/phys101/phys101/objects/*.JPG, the LLM material naming cache, the baseline ladder); scripts/p5_transfer.py (product rule, build-aware density, cd_for_restitution); docs/results/p101_density.json (measured mass/volume for the build head); the o8 joint-fit optimiser pieces (trust region, projected iterate); src/surprise/ V-JEPA 2 loading in the cosmos env for the image backbone; src/gpu.py. Later stages consume the Proposal-1 corpus (object x surface clips at 240 fps) or a reduced self-capture (40 objects x 6 surfaces, ~2 weeks).
proposals.differentiable_physics_role: Central, and bounded honestly. The gradient dL/dphi = dL/d(track) * d(track)/d(theta) * d(theta)/dphi exists only because d(track)/d(theta) comes from the tape through contact; without it the only way to train from motion is the two-stage route (fit a label per clip, then regress), which cannot use the 309 'stays' clips except as censoring, discards tumbling clips, and weights every parameter equally regardless of its effect on the motion. What gradients buy specifically: (a) censored and partially identifiable clips contribute a correct one-sided gradient (a 'stays' clip pushes mu up only while the simulated body slides); (b) the loss lives in motion space, so parameters the data cannot resolve receive no gradient -- identifiability handled by construction instead of by hand (rule 1b: all conditions of a clip are joint covariates in one rollout); (c) batching: 64 bodies per scene, one tape, so an epoch over 600 clips is ~10 rollouts (~1-5 s each at SUB 100-336), 200 epochs in a few GPU-hours. Where they buy little, said plainly: on the pure-slide subset the trajectory is closed-form, s = s0 + 1/2 g (sin a - mu_eff cos a)(t-t0)^2, and a mu-grid surrogate with interpolation is an exact differentiable stand-in 100x cheaper than the tape -- we use it as the cross-check and the tape as the general path that the stays/rolls/topples/bounces require. The decisive comparison is end-to-end vs two-stage on held-out objects: if two-stage ties, gradients bought nothing beyond per-clip fitting and the write-up says so. Body-body gradients (the recorded adjoint defect under sustained contact) are never on the path: objects are simulated separately against the surface.
proposals.scale_claim: Training data: Physics 101 now (70 objects with slide/stay tracks at two angles, 101 catalogue photos, one board), plus the Proposal-1 corpus as it arrives (150 objects x 15 surfaces, ~3,300 clips at 240 fps) or a reduced 40 x 6 self-capture if Proposal 1 is not run; ~6,000 real clips at the 90-day mark, which is the largest real-motion-supervised set for contact parameters in the landscape (PhysVid: 300 real clips; EKFPhys: 20; ETH terrain: one robot's footing). Deployment scale is a forward pass -- 100k assets in under a GPU-hour -- but we claim only what is validated: held-out objects (N ~ 60) and held-out surfaces (N = 3-5, including outdoor concrete/asphalt/pavers captured last and never trained on). 'Beyond rooms' here means beyond lab datasets in two gated steps: (i) the held-out-surface test on built-environment surfaces, and (ii) in-the-wild weak supervision mined from Something-Something v2's 'Lifting a surface with something on it until it starts sliding down' and 'tilting something with something on it until it falls off' templates (order 1,000 clips each, 12 fps, 240 px): the onset angle, read from the tracked motion onset and a monocular plane-normal estimate, is a dimensionless, scale-free, frame-rate-tolerant observation (tan of the onset angle bounds mu) -- it enters training only if the mined per-material-pair medians rank-correlate with the measured atlas at rho >= 0.7 over >= 8 pairs. We do not claim city-scale twins; we claim that the number-assignment stage of city-scale pipelines becomes motion-validated.
proposals.practicality: Who uses it: (1) sim-ready asset and scene pipelines (PhysX-Anything/Omni, UniPhysGen, EmbodiedGen V2, ManiTwin, UrbanVerse, MolmoSpaces) that currently ask GPT-4o/5 for mass and friction from renders -- M2P takes the same renders or photos and returns numbers with a measured held-out error and an uncertainty, exportable as SimReady USD physics materials; (2) the project's own goal, authored assets that never existed: theta from the asset's rendered appearance, with the render-vs-photo domain gap tested explicitly on our 13 assets against their p5 transferred values; (3) robot learners who need per-object DR ranges: the heteroscedastic head gives a range per object rather than a global 0.1-1.0; (4) Newton / Isaac Lab users building twins from a photo of the table or floor (the surface head alone is useful: 'what is this floor's friction class' from one image). Honest limit: the model predicts contact parameters of rigid objects on rigid surfaces; deformables, fluids and articulation are out of scope, and the robot-policy benefit of better object parameters remains an open, task-dependent question in the literature (ASID positive, SIMPLER <= 15%).
proposals.novelty_argument: The landscape has appearance->physics models supervised by VLM annotations (PhysX family, UniPhysGen, VoMP/AdaVoMP, PhysGS, NeRF2Physics, PhysDB), parameter regressors from video OF the motion (PhysVid, 0.21-0.28 Pearson for V-JEPA/DynamiCrafter probes), pixels-to-parameters through differentiable sim+render on synthetic video only (gradSim), and one vision->friction model supervised by real motion -- ETH's terrain paper, where the labels come from a quadruped's proprioception and the target is the robot's own footing. No work trains an image->contact-parameter model from real object motion through a differentiable engine, and none scores such a model on the motion of held-out objects (every scout lists this as the gap). The method is simple and the difference from ETH terrain is small in architecture; the substance is the label source (tracked motion + a differentiable exact-mesh simulator instead of a robot), the object x surface factorisation, the censored-clip supervision that only gradients through the simulator make possible, and the e1-style validation. If the model turns out to learn nothing beyond material identity, the contribution reduces to 'a motion-trained material namer that is as good as an LLM's naming' -- a modest result we would report as such; the test that decides this is built in (headroom on Physics 101 is only 2.6 -> 1.8 mm, so the surfaces axis is where the model can exceed a table).
nearest_prior_work: Identifying Terrain Physical Parameters from Vision (ETH RSL, RA-L 2024, arXiv 2408.16567): vision -> dense friction/stiffness, self-supervised from a quadruped's proprioception-decoded labels; closest in spirit -- ours uses a differentiable simulator and a tracker instead of a robot, targets objects and surfaces, and validates on held-out object motion.

PhysVid (arXiv 2510.02311): regresses friction/elasticity/viscosity from video of the motion with measured real GT (oracle 0.83 Pearson; foundation-model probes 0.21-0.28 without adaptation); ours predicts from a STILL photo before any motion and is trained by motion rather than scored by it; their 30 measured pairs are a free external test.

gradSim (ICLR 2021): pixels -> mass/friction/elasticity through differentiable sim + render, synthetic video only (10,000 clips); ours is real video, tracked points instead of pixels (no differentiable renderer), feed-forward from appearance, validated on held-out real objects.

NeRF2Physics (CVPR 2024) / PhysGS (CVPR 2026): per-point friction and density from LLM/VLM numbers fused over views, evaluated against pad meters and ABO product masses; our number source is motion, our metric is real motion of unseen objects; the project's e1 already shows the LLM-number route is 3x worse than a measured table.

VoMP / AdaVoMP (NVIDIA, ICLR/ICML 2026) and PhysX-3D/Anything/Omni, UniPhysGen: feed-forward physical-property prediction trained and scored on VLM+human labels (E, nu, rho; scale; material); ours covers the contact parameters they omit (friction, restitution) and scores against motion.

Vid2Sim (CVPR 2025) feed-forward prior and MonoPhysics (NeurIPS 2026): differentiable-sim system ID of deformables with a learned prior, synthetic parameter GT; the rigid-contact analogue with real motion labels does not exist.

PokeWorld / ACWM-Phys (2026): latent world models encode mass at R^2 0.21-0.25 in a 2-D toy; evidence that passive video latents carry little, which is why our supervision is explicit motion through an explicit simulator rather than a latent probe.
first_90_days: Days 1-14 (first experiment + kill): leave-one-object-out on Physics 101's 20-deg clips (70 objects, 281 slides + 309 stays): frozen DINOv2 features of the catalogue photo -> MLP -> mu; loss = aligned trajectory RMS through DiffMeshScene (64 bodies per scene) with a hinge for stays; the mu-grid surrogate as the exactness cross-check; the two-stage baseline and the photo-shuffle control; place the result on the e1 ladder.

Days 15-30: diagnostics and the censored terms done properly -- 10-deg clips as a second condition per object (rule 1b), 'never slides' bounds, the 24 rolling clips through a 6-DoF track loss; heteroscedastic uncertainty head calibrated against held-out residuals; identifiability report from per-clip Jacobian norms; decide end-to-end vs two-stage by paired sign test over the 70 objects.

Days 31-45: the surface axis. Ingest the Proposal-1 tilt-board corpus as it arrives (or run the reduced self-capture: 40 objects x 6 surfaces x 2 angles, tagged board, ~2 weeks); add the surface crop and the factorised mu_pair = f(obj) * g(surf) head; train with object AND surface held out in rotation.

Days 46-60: restitution head from 240 fps drops (sphere and block subset first, where Proposal 1's two-route invariant holds); loss on the first-rebound track through BOUNCE_RIG with the alpha adjoint gated by finite differences; build head trained on measured weights (areal/shell/solid) against the LLM-named build as the baseline.

Days 61-75: the beyond-lab gate: download the two SSv2 tilt templates (~2,000 clips), track onset with CoTracker3, estimate the lifted surface's angle from a monocular geometry model at onset, LLM-name object and surface materials; compare mined per-pair onset medians with the measured atlas (rank correlation over >= 8 pairs, threshold 0.7); if it passes, add the onset bound as censored supervision and re-run the held-out tests; if it fails, report the failure with the numbers.

Days 76-90: held-out-surface test on outdoor sheets captured last (concrete, asphalt, pavers), render-vs-photo check on our 13 authored assets, SimReady export, write-up with the full ladder (oracle / material table / LLM naming / M2P end-to-end / two-stage / dataset median / LLM number) for objects and surfaces.
proposals.first_experiment: Leave-one-object-out on Physics 101 (70 objects, 359 slide trials plus 309 stays at 20 deg, catalogue photo as the only input): train the photo -> mu head with the motion loss through DiffMeshScene, predict mu for the held-out object from its photo, simulate, align release time and offset only (never the acceleration), and score the real tracked slides. The experiment produces one number on a ladder that already exists: held-out median trajectory RMS in mm against oracle 1.8 / material table 2.6 / LLM-naming pipeline 2.7 / dataset median 4.4 / LLM direct number 7.5, plus stays-or-slides accuracy on the 198 outcome cases (material table 94%), the same number for the two-stage baseline and for the photo-shuffle control. One A6000, about a day including tracking already on disk.
proposals.kill_test: Decided now. The idea is DEAD if the motion-trained photo -> mu model's leave-one-object-out median trajectory RMS is >= 4.4 mm (the dataset-wide median, i.e. a model that reads nothing from the photo) or its stays/slides accuracy is <= 80% (the same prior's accuracy), or if the photo-shuffle control is not significantly worse than the model by a paired sign test over the 70 objects (then the model predicts a dataset prior, not appearance). Success is bounded and stated in advance: on Physics 101 the best possible is the 1.8 mm oracle and the material table sits at 2.6, so reaching ~2.6-3.0 mm without being told the material means 'learned the material from motion alone', and only the surface axis (days 31-60) can show more. A second, separate verdict for the differentiable path: if end-to-end training does not beat two-stage fit-then-regress on held-out objects (paired sign test, p < 0.05), the simulator-in-the-loop is dropped from training and kept only for per-clip fitting, and the paper says gradients bought nothing here. Rule 1 gate before training: the per-clip gradient of the loss w.r.t. the predicted mu must match central finite differences within 5% on 20 random clips of each class (slides, stays), as g0 did for one cube.
proposals.resources: Compute: <= 1 A6000 for training (an epoch of ~600 Physics 101 clips is ~10 batched rollouts of 1-5 s; 200 epochs in a few hours), CoTracker3 for new clips, DINOv2/V-JEPA 2 features cached once in the cosmos env; everything seeded (GPU nondeterminism on long slides is recorded at 1.5 mm at the stiff setting -- the loss uses the soft BOUNCE_RIG for drops and TILT_RIG for slides with that floor noted). Data: Physics 101 on disk (6.1 GB), docs/results/p2_ramp_all.json tracks, the LLM naming cache; the Proposal-1 corpus or a 2-week 40 x 6 self-capture (phone, tagged board, 6 surface sheets); SSv2 tilt templates (~2 GB after registration) for the gated mining. No robot, no new foundation model, no differentiable renderer.
proposals.biggest_risk: That a single photo carries little beyond the material class: on Physics 101 the material table is already within 0.8 mm of the own-trials oracle, so the achievable gain over 'LLM names it, table supplies the number' is small, and the model may end up a motion-trained material classifier that matches but does not beat the e1 pipeline -- a modest result. Related: friction is a pair property with per-object finish effects (p1: mu fell with cube size, Spearman -0.80, unexplained), so the irreducible per-object noise may be most of the gap. Second: the model can learn capture artefacts (background, lighting, the board) instead of material -- crops and the shuffle control guard this but cannot prove it on a single-board dataset until the surface corpus exists. Third: the beyond-lab mining (SSv2 at 12 fps, 240 px, hand-held surfaces, monocular plane angles) may fail its gate, leaving 'beyond rooms' as the held-out-surface test only.
proposals.expected_headline_result: Trained only on real tracked motion through a differentiable exact-mesh simulator -- no parameter labels, no VLM numbers -- an image model predicts, from one photo of an unseen object and an unseen surface, friction and restitution that reproduce the object's real slide to ~2.5 mm median (oracle from its own trials 1.8 mm; measured material table 2.6 mm; VLM-assigned numbers 7.5 mm) and its first rebound within the trial-to-trial spread, generalising to surfaces never seen in training; censored clips (objects that do not move) contribute through the simulator, which is why the end-to-end model beats the fit-then-regress baseline on held-out objects.

evidence: Physics 101 (Wu, Lim, Zhang, Tenenbaum, Freeman, BMVC 2016; http://phys101.csail.mit.edu/papers/phys101_bmvc.pdf) already implements the proposal's core architecture ON THE SAME DATASET: LeNet on tracker-cropped image patches -> material/volume -> a 'physics interpreter' with friction, density, restitution and mass layers -> a 'physical world simulator' of hand-coded differentiable physics laws (ramp: (sin th - mu cos th) g = a; bounce: CR = sqrt(h/H); collision: CR from velocities; Hooke; buoyancy) whose outputs are regressed (MSE, SGD, backprop) against velocities/distances TRACKED from the real videos. Verbatim: 'our model learns object properties from completely unlabeled data. We do not provide any labels for physical properties ... our model automatically discovers observations from videos, uses them as supervision'; 'we do not have any individual loss layer for LeNet components'; 'Our only supervision is the physical laws encoded in the top physical world simulator'.

Physics 101 also already evaluates on HELD-OUT OBJECTS ('Split by object ... requires the model to generalize to objects that it has never seen before') and on real-motion OUTCOME prediction: Table 2a moving-distance correlation 0.65/0.42/0.33 (frame/trial/object) vs a plain CNN 0.63/0.39/0.21; bounce height 0.35/0.31/0.23; Table 1b mass/density/volume correlation under joint unlabeled training 0.26/0.33/0.30 by object; Table 2b per-material pixel errors of model vs humans vs mean baseline. So the proposal's claim 'none scores such a model on the motion of held-out objects' is false for the two-angle ramp/fall/spring setting.

Galileo (Wu, Yildirim, Lim, Freeman, Tenenbaum, NeurIPS 2015; https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2015/file/d09bf41544a3365a46c9077ebb5e35c3-Paper.pdf) is exactly the proposal's 'two-stage baseline' on the same ramp footage (150 real videos, ~100 objects): MCMC fits a 3D physics engine's mass/friction to tracked velocities, then 'we train LeNet ... using image patches cropped from videos ... and estimated physical properties as labels ... to predict these physical properties of objects based on purely visual cues, even though they might have never appeared in the training set'; held-out protocol 'one object per material as our test cases'; mass MSE 0.052 (corr 0.44) vs oracle 0.042 (0.71) vs uniform 0.081. The paper itself calls this 'self-supervised'.

PhysVid / 'Inferring Dynamic Physical Properties from Video Foundation Models' (Zhan, Ma, Xie, Zisserman, arXiv 2510.02311, https://arxiv.org/html/2510.02311): real friction GT measured with a spring dynamometer (mu_k = F/G) for 5 objects x 6 surfaces, 100 real test videos, GT 0.105-0.544; Table 1 real split: oracle 0.83, DynamiCrafter 0.25, V-JEPA-2 0.21, GPT-4o 0.38, and V-JEPA-2 fine-tuned on an additional real training split 'with disjoint objects and surfaces from the test set' = 0.73 Pearson (Appendix B.2: train = paper box, metal pencil box, wooden box, red towel, wooden table, cardboard; test = plastic disk, LEGO brick, gray towel, kitchen paper, tablecloth). The proposal quotes only the 0.21-0.28 unadapted numbers; the 0.73 held-out-object-AND-surface result trained on real motion is the directly comparable one and is omitted. Difference that remains: PhysVid predicts from video OF the motion, not from a still photo.

ETH terrain (Chen, Frey, Zhou, Miki, Martius, Hutter, arXiv 2408.16567, https://arxiv.org/html/2408.16567): characterised fairly by the proposal. Labels come from a physical decoder trained in simulation applied to real proprioception; vision net trained with L = 0.9 L_recon + 0.1 L_pred; terrain only, not objects; real-world evaluation is qualitative plus a sim-vs-real robot-motion digital-twin comparison, not held-out measured friction. So 'validated against measured held-out motion' is still a gap relative to this work.

Kandukuri et al., 'Learning to Identify Physical Parameters from Video Using Differentiable Physics' (DAGM-GCPR 2020, arXiv 2009.08292): image encoder trained end-to-end through a differentiable rigid-body engine with contact/friction, recovers mass and friction without labels via spatial-transformer decoding -- SYNTHETIC video only. Heiden et al., 'Inferring Articulated Rigid Body Dynamics from RGBD Video' (IROS 2022, arXiv 2203.10488): differentiable simulation fitted to REAL video for contact/dynamics parameters, but per-scene optimisation, not feed-forward. DensePhysNet (Xu et al., RSS 2019, arXiv 1906.03853): self-supervised dense friction/mass representations of real objects from robot interactions, generalising to novel scenes, no simulator.

Repo check: scripts/g0_grad_check.py defines DiffMeshScene and compares d(slide)/d(mu) to central FD with a 5% tolerance (line 136: ok = abs(g - fd) < 0.05*...), for ONE cube on a 20 deg plane; the 64-body batched scene, the differentiable align_err, and any censored/topple/roll adjoint do not yet exist. The project's own docs catalogue only arXiv 2506.09849, 2604.09527, 2609.36024 and contain no notes on Galileo/Physics 101 as architectures.

LIMITATION OF THIS REVIEW: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so no 2023-2026 literature search could be run; only primary sources reachable by known URL were checked. The absence of a 2023-2026 paper doing 'still photo -> contact parameters trained through a general differentiable rigid simulator on real tracked motion' is therefore UNVERIFIED (medium-low confidence). Vid2Sim, MonoPhysics, gradSim, VoMP/PhysX, SSv2-tilt mining prior art were not re-checked from primary sources.
verdicts.surviving_form: Drop the thesis that 'no work trains an image->contact-parameter model from real object motion through a differentiable engine' and that 'none scores it on held-out object motion': Physics 101 (2016) did both, with analytic differentiable physics laws, on the same dataset, and Galileo (2015) is the two-stage baseline. What is still open, and must be stated as the claim: (1) replacing the closed-form laws with a general exact-mesh differentiable rigid-body simulator so that censored clips (stays), topples, rolls and 6-DoF contact enter one loss -- and showing by a paired held-out test that this beats BOTH the Physics-101-style analytic/grid surrogate AND the Galileo-style fit-then-regress; the proposal already concedes the pure-slide subset is closed-form, so if the general tape does not win on the non-slide clips the contribution collapses to a re-run of Physics 101 with better tracking; (2) the object x surface factorised friction head from a STILL photo (before any motion) evaluated with held-out surfaces, benchmarked against PhysVid's real 5x6 object/surface split where a video-conditioned V-JEPA-2 fine-tuned on real motion already reaches 0.73 Pearson on disjoint objects and surfaces; (3) a millimetre trajectory-error metric on held-out real objects with the full e1 ladder (oracle / material table / LLM naming / LLM number), rather than Physics 101's correlation-only reporting -- a measurement contribution, not an architectural one. Also cite PhysVid's adapted 0.73, not only its 0.21-0.28, when positioning.
verdicts.summary: Refuted as stated. The core structure -- image network -> (friction, density, restitution, mass) -> differentiable physics -> loss against motion tracked from real video, no property labels, held-out-object evaluation including outcome/motion prediction -- is Physics 101 (Wu et al., BMVC 2016), built and evaluated on the very dataset the proposal plans to train on; the proposal's 'two-stage baseline' is Galileo (NeurIPS 2015) on the same footage. Both are mentioned by the project only as 'fit physics to these videos' precedent, not as the feed-forward architectures they are. PhysVid is also under-characterised: it already reports a real-motion-trained model at 0.73 Pearson on held-out objects AND surfaces (from video, not a still). ETH terrain is characterised fairly. Novelty that survives is narrower: a general exact-mesh differentiable simulator in place of analytic laws (which only matters if it demonstrably beats the analytic/grid surrogate and fit-then-regress on non-slide clips), still-photo object x surface factorisation with held-out surfaces versus PhysVid's video-conditioned result, and millimetre-level held-out trajectory validation with the e1 ladder. Caveat: the 2023-2026 search could not be executed (budget exhausted), so a more recent exact duplicate is not excluded.

evidence: Re-ran scripts/g0_grad_check.py today on a free A6000 (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1): tape d(slide)/d(mu_body) = -0.5448 vs central FD -0.5453, rollout identical to the validated MeshProbeScene, 0.4 s fwd+bwd for 1200 steps -> GRADIENT CHECK: PASS. The rule-1 gate the plan rests on exists and holds through plane contact.

Batched 64-body DiffMeshScene at the p4-validated setting (30 fps, SUB 336, 1.2 s = 12,096 steps, 24,704 vertices): forward 1.8 s, backward 2.8 s, 6.8 GiB (scratch script batch64.py). Per-body gradient vs FD on a seated body: tape -2.3545 vs FD -2.3506 (0.2%). So '~10 rollouts per epoch of ~600 clips, 1-5 s each' is accurate and fits one GPU.

Hidden dependency found and resolved: the cosmos env (torch 2.11, py3.12) has no warp and the warp env (py3.11) has no torch (docs/PLAN_OTRACK.md line ~275 says single-process tape-into-torch 'is not available'). Verified today that appending the warp env's site-packages to cosmos' sys.path imports warp 1.15.0 next to torch and wp.to_torch works on CUDA -- warp's native lib is ctypes-loaded, so the end-to-end loop needs no env surgery.

Hidden failure mode found: a simulated body that leaves the plane returns gradient exactly 0.0 (bodies not seated / off the bounded table gave tape +0.0000 vs FD nonzero in three of three cases). A low-mu prediction that runs the body off the 1 m board gives no gradient exactly where the error is largest; training must use an unbounded plane or initialise from the material prior.

Training data are on disk: docs/results/p2_ramp_all.json holds per-clip s(t) tracks at 29.97 fps for 643 clips (281 slides / 309 stays / 24 rolls / 29 error), 92 objects x 2 angles; 103 catalogue JPGs in data/phys101/phys101/objects; CoTracker3 and DINOv2 are in ~/.cache/torch/hub; e1_heldout.json holds the full ladder (oracle 1.77, material 2.55, pipeline 2.72, global 4.40, LLM mu 7.53 mm; outcome 94/92/80%). GPUs 1-5 were idle; 15 TB free on /home/nas5.

Physics 101 readme has no licence, only a citation request (research use is what Galileo/Physics 101 themselves did); CoTracker3 and MYRIAD/FPT are CC BY-NC -- acceptable for a research paper, blocks only a commercial release.
Physics 101 ships no 3D meshes: the 24 'rolls' clips and any tumble term (days 15-30) need proxy shapes built from volume; sliding is shape-independent so days 1-14 are unaffected.

Days 31-60 depend on a 'Proposal-1 corpus' that does not exist; the fallback (40 objects x 6 surfaces x 2 angles self-capture plus 240 fps drops, ~2 weeks) must be done by the same single researcher in the same window as days 15-30, and this project's only restitution attempt (p3) failed; no 240 fps capture has been validated here yet.

Days 61-75: SSv2 cannot be downloaded per template -- the full release is ~19.4 GB in 20 parts behind registration (the plan's '~2 GB' is wrong), and the onset-angle signal needs a monocular plane-normal estimate on 240 px, 12 fps hand-held video that has no rule-1 evidence in this project; it is gated, so it cannot sink the plan, but it is the least likely milestone.
verdicts.surviving_form: Days 1-30 survive as written and can start immediately: leave-one-object-out on Physics 101 with the motion loss through DiffMeshScene (use the cross-env warp+torch import, an unbounded plane or prior initialisation so no body runs off the board, and the mu-grid surrogate as the cross-check); the first experiment fits in well under two weeks. The 90-day plan must be re-scoped: drop the dependency on the external Proposal-1 corpus and schedule the 40x6 self-capture explicitly as its own two-week block (not in parallel with days 15-30); treat restitution at 240 fps as a stretch goal gated by a two-route invariant on the first ten drops; move the SSv2 mining to an optional appendix with its own pre-gate (plane-normal error measured on tilted-board clips of known angle) and budget the 19.4 GB download and registration; present the rolls/tumble terms as proxy-shape only. The deliverable at day 90 should be the held-out-object and held-out-surface ladders, not the beyond-lab claim.
verdicts.summary: The first experiment is feasible now: I re-ran the gradient gate (PASS, 0.1%), batched 64 bodies at the validated solver setting (4.6 s fwd+bwd, 6.8 GiB, per-body gradient matches FD to 0.2%), confirmed warp and torch run in one process despite the two-env split, and all tracks, photos and baselines are on disk. The 90-day milestone is over-committed rather than impossible: the surface axis and restitution head depend on a corpus that does not exist and a self-capture by the lone researcher, SSv2 mining is mis-sized and rests on an unvalidated monocular angle estimate, and Physics 101 has no meshes for the rolling clips. Not refuted; survives as a 30-day Physics 101 experiment plus a re-scoped, explicitly scheduled capture.

verdicts.lens: Impact and practicality: who consumes the output, is the effect size large enough to act on, does it answer the user's ask (actionable, differentiable physics, practical for robots/sims, scale)
evidence: The ladder M2P must climb is already nearly closed: docs/results/e1_heldout.json gives own-trials oracle 1.77 mm, measured material table 2.55 mm, LLM-names-material pipeline 2.72 mm, dataset median 4.40 mm (70 objects, 359 trials). The proposal's own expected headline is ~2.5 mm -- a 0.05-0.2 mm move against a table that already exists, inside the p90 spread (12.4 mm). Nobody changes a pipeline for that.

The kill-test bar is set at >= 4.4 mm / <= 80% stays-slides, i.e. below what the project already achieves with no model at all (2.55 mm / 94%). A kill test the existing baseline passes by 2x is not a decision procedure; the only verdict it can produce is 'alive', and the honest success case ('reaches 2.6-3.0 mm without being told the material') is a motion-trained material classifier -- which the proposal itself concedes in biggest_risk.

The differentiable-simulator role is admitted to be redundant on the data that exists: on the 281 slide clips the trajectory is closed-form (s = s0 + 1/2 g (sin a - mu_eff cos a) t^2) and the proposal says a mu-grid surrogate is 'an exact differentiable stand-in 100x cheaper than the tape'. The 309 'stays' clips are a one-sided bound mu_eff > tan(20 deg) = 0.36 in PARAMETER space, so a censored (Tobit-style) regression loss trains the same photo->mu head with no simulator in the loop. Gradients through contact buy something only for rolls (24 clips), topples and 240 fps rebounds -- none of which are on disk (p3 restitution from Physics 101 FAILED; a 240 fps capture does not exist yet).

Where the tape is actually needed the project's own record says the adjoint is unverified or broken: scripts/g0c_grad_diag.py header records body-body FD -0.38 vs tape -0.03 under sustained contact; d(slide)/d(mu) matching FD was shown for ONE cube on a plane (g0_grad_check.py). The 6-DoF roll/topple loss the proposal leans on for 'what gradients buy' has no gradient check, and the proposed rule-1 gate (20 clips of slides and stays) exercises only the closed-form path.

Irreducible per-object noise is most of the remaining gap: p1 found mu falling with cube size (Spearman -0.80, 0.28 -> 0.21, unexplained) within ONE material and one finish, and p5 found the object/board vs object/table friction ratio spread 0.75-1.05 across block materials. A still photo cannot carry finish/session effects of that size, so the headroom 2.55 -> 1.77 mm is largely not learnable from appearance.

Consumer check: the concrete users named (PhysX-Anything/Omni, UniPhysGen, Isaac Lab, SimReady USD) need friction and restitution per asset -- but the deliverable they would actually adopt is the measured material x surface table behind an LLM material namer, which already exists and scores 2.72 mm. M2P only beats that product if the surface axis works, and the surface axis depends on a corpus that does not exist (Proposal-1, or a one-researcher 2-week phone self-capture, 40 objects x 6 surfaces) with held-out surfaces at N = 3-5 -- too few to support a generalisation claim at a top venue.

Robot-side effect size is unproven and the proposal says so: 'the robot-policy benefit of better object parameters remains an open, task-dependent question (ASID positive, SIMPLER <= 15%)'. No robot, no policy, no manipulation benchmark is in the plan, so the 'practical for robots' half of the user's ask is a forward-pass export plus a citation.

'Scale / beyond rooms' is a 1,000-clip SSv2 mining gate at 12 fps and 240 px with a monocular plane-normal estimate of a hand-held surface, entering training only if a rank correlation over >= 8 material pairs exceeds 0.7. Even on success it yields per-material-pair onset bounds, not an interactable world. The output remains a ~15-material x few-surface friction atlas on tilted boards; 'city-scale' appears only as what the proposal explicitly does NOT claim.

Nearest prior work already covers the architecture: ETH terrain (arXiv 2408.16567, vision->friction self-supervised from real motion) and PhysVid (arXiv 2510.02311, measured real GT).
