The proposal's own novelty statement says the architectural difference from ETH is 'small' and the contribution is the label source -- which, on one board with a closed-form forward model, reduces to 'regress a tabulated mu from a photo'.
verdicts.surviving_form: Split it into the part that is already practical and the part that is actually a research bet, and stop pretending the first needs gradients. (1) Ship now, as the actionable deliverable: the measured object x surface friction/density atlas plus the LLM material namer, exported as SimReady USD physics materials with the e1 held-out motion error attached -- this is the only product in the landscape validated on held-out real motion and it needs no training. Its scale lever is coverage of SURFACES, so the first new capture should be surfaces (floors, concrete, pavers, rubber mats) under a handful of reference objects at 240 fps, not more objects on one board. (2) Decide the differentiable-physics question in week 2 with a cheap, falsifiable test: photo->mu head trained with a censored parameter-space loss vs the same head trained end-to-end through DiffMeshScene, on Physics 101, paired sign test over 70 objects, with the kill bar raised to 'must beat the material table (2.55 mm) AND the two-stage route, p < 0.05' -- if neither holds, drop the simulator from training and say so. (3) Reserve the tape for where the forward model is not closed-form and the labels do not exist yet -- restitution from the first rebound and roll/topple 6-DoF tracks on the 240 fps surface corpus -- and gate it on a body-plane 6-DoF adjoint check (the g0c body-body defect must be either fixed or kept off the path). (4) Drop the SSv2 mining as the 'scale' story; if a scale claim is wanted, it is the held-out built-environment surfaces, and it needs N >= 10 surfaces, not 3-5.
verdicts.summary: M2P is falsifiable but its decisive number is pre-determined to be uninteresting: on Physics 101 the measured material table (2.55 mm) is already within 0.8 mm of the own-trials oracle (1.77 mm), the LLM-namer pipeline is at 2.72 mm, and the proposal's own kill bar (4.4 mm) is one the no-model baseline clears by 2x, so the likely outcome is 'a motion-trained material classifier that matches the table' -- a result no simulator or robot pipeline would act on. The differentiable-engine role is weak on the data that exists (slides are closed-form; 'stays' are a parameter-space bound; the proposal concedes a grid surrogate is an exact 100x cheaper stand-in), and where the tape would genuinely matter (rolls, topples, 240 fps rebounds, body-body contact) the labels do not exist and the adjoint is unverified or recorded as broken (g0c: FD -0.38 vs tape -0.03). The practical consumers named would adopt the existing table + namer, not M2P; the surface axis that could change this rests on an uncaptured corpus with 3-5 held-out surfaces; robot benefit is uncited beyond 'open question'; and 'beyond rooms' is an SSv2 mining gate yielding friction bounds, not an interactable world. It does not answer the user's ask for scale or a practical robot system, and the part of it that is actionable (ship the motion-validated atlas) needs no gradients.

proposals.title: PhysMat: a measured, held-out-validated physics-material library and resolver for sim-ready asset catalogues
proposals.thesis: Every sim-ready library a robot-learning group uses today (RoboCasa, BEHAVIOR-1K, MolmoSpaces, SimReady packs, UrbanVerse-100K, EmbodiedGen) fills mass, friction and restitution from a VLM or an artist and never checks them against motion, while our held-out test already shows a measured per-material table predicts a never-seen object's real slide at 2.6 mm median against 7.5 mm for an LLM's number (e1, 70 objects, 359 trials). We claim that kinetic friction, effective density and restitution factorise by material and build well enough that ~30 materials measured once (Physics 101 on disk plus 240 fps phone captures), carried with repeat-trial uncertainty and resolved onto an asset by LLM material naming plus a build rule, reproduce the real motion of held-out objects at ~1.5x the per-object oracle, so that every manipulable object in a 10^3-10^4-object catalogue gets a value with an error bar and a provenance line instead of a guess.
proposals.what_we_build: (1) The table: for each material, mu against each measured partner surface (stored factorised as body x surface, with the p5 anchor stated), effective density by build (areal for hollow cardboard, shell or solid otherwise), restitution as Hunt-Crossley alpha plus the PhysX-style e it implies, each with n, repeat-trial sd and the protocol that produced it. Sources: the 643 Physics 101 ramp clips already fitted (11 materials with mu, 3 bounded, 15 densities), plus our own 240 fps phone captures (ramp slides at two tilts, drops from two heights, kitchen-scale mass) of ~30 household materials on 4-6 surfaces, plus external measured sets used only as held-out checks (PhysVid's 5x6 dynamometer mu matrix, GAUGE's slope-slider/bounce trials if released, IRIS). (2) The resolver: asset mesh + images + category -> LLM names material per part and build type (the one job e1 showed an LLM does well, 80%) -> table lookup -> USD PhysicsMaterialAPI (density, static/dynamic friction, restitution) + mass, centre of mass and inertia from the build rule + a domain-randomisation range from the table's uncertainty + a JSON provenance record; 'unmeasured' is an explicit output, never a default. (3) The validation harness: tracked real clips (CoTracker3) replayed through Newton with only release time/offset aligned, reporting trajectory error per material and per parameter, normalised by trial-to-trial variability (GAUGE's metric), so that any assignment method -- VLM, table, learned -- can be scored on the same real clips. (4) An audit of a deployed library: the resolver run over RoboCasa's 2,509 objects (free MJCF download) and MolmoSpaces' manipulable-object categories, reporting coverage (fraction nameable into measured materials) and how far the library's current friction/mass values sit from the measured material's repeat-trial range.
proposals.builds_on_our_assets: Reuses verbatim: the real-footage pipeline p1/p2 (CoTracker3 + ramp-segment fits, SLIDES/ROLLS/STAYS classification, the 19 px grid fix, the two-angle and camera-scale invariants); p4 (Newton replay of real slides, 0.4-1.0 mm RMS, simulator-fitted mu = analytic mu to 0.005); p5 (material -> asset transfer, the areal/shell/solid build rule, the ramp-board-vs-table factorisation ratios 0.75-1.05); e1 (the held-out protocol and its baselines, the LLM-names-material step); MeshProbeScene with exact mesh contact, seat_on_plane (clearance 0), tilted ground plane, build-aware CoM/inertia (textbook-exact within 1%), set_restitution_alpha (p7/p8: e independent of mass and stiffness); DiffMeshScene from g0 (tape reproduces the validated rollout, d(slide)/d(mu) = -0.5448 vs FD -0.5453); the sensitivity matrix (o7) to choose which excitation reads which parameter; the p3 failure protocol (the g-from-free-fall scale check) for the 240 fps captures; the LLM gateway for naming. Explicitly NOT reused: the render/judge/surprise/FPT/MYRIAD/Wan stack -- its negative results are now corroborated externally (PhysVid: V-JEPA-2 friction r = 0.28; WorldBench; GAUGE) and need no re-run.
proposals.differentiable_physics_role: Honest and bounded. Gradients are exact today only for one body against a surface (g0), which is exactly the geometry of every clip in this proposal (object on a board, object dropped on a slab), so the tape can be used throughout; multi-body gradients (g0b: the adjoint under-transmits a sustained push, -0.032 vs FD -0.385) are not needed and not used. What the tape buys: (a) the joint fit of ALL trials of a material with one shared (mu, alpha, CoM-offset) and per-trial nuisances (release time, offset, in-plane velocity) -- 100 clips x 3 nuisances + 3 shared = ~300 unknowns, one backward pass per clip per iteration against ~300 rollouts per step by finite differences; this is what makes a material-level fit with hundreds of clips cheap and is where reverse mode wins decisively; (b) the gradient for non-block objects (dolls, rings, toys, hollow wood -- the 'ROLLS' clips p2 had to exclude), whose motion has no closed form and whose fit needs the exact-mesh forward model; (c) with the Jacobian (from forward differences over the <=10 physical+nuisance parameters per clip, since the Warp tape is reverse-mode only), a Laplace covariance that becomes the material's domain-randomisation range -- the quantity practitioners actually consume and which no table carries. What gradients buy nothing for: mu of a sliding block (1-D, closed form; e1 was done without them), mass (a scale), and the library audit. Known risk: through impacts the penalty-contact adjoint may be noisy (the DiffMJX problem); every gradient use is gated by a per-clip central-FD comparison, and the fallback for the 3 physical parameters is a sweep, which rule 1 requires anyway.
proposals.scale_claim: 'Beyond rooms' is the wrong axis for contact physics, and the landscape shows why: at street or city scale no object is ever pushed, lifted or toppled (URBAN-SIM, UrbanVerse, Vid2Sim evaluate navigation = avoidance; GRUtopia reports 0% on mobile manipulation; UrbanVerse's only physics check is GPT-4.1 mass vs spec sheets at 19.6% MAPE with friction unchecked), so a parameter there has nothing to do. The axis on which 'interactable worlds at scale' actually lives is objects x materials x surface pairings with a validated error bar: a material is measured once and covers thousands of assets, and validation is per material, not per asset. Concretely: ~30 materials x 4-6 surfaces (~150 pairings, >=5 trials each, ~1,000 own 240 fps clips) + 643 Physics 101 clips; held-out validation on >=100 real objects (101 Physics 101 + ~40 own with kitchen-scale mass); resolution onto RoboCasa's 2,509 objects and MolmoSpaces' 48k manipulable objects with coverage reported, not assumed. Compute is trivial at this scale: a tape pass is 0.4 s per 1200 steps (g0), so the whole joint fit is tens of A6000-hours.
proposals.practicality: Users: groups building or maintaining sim-ready scenes (RoboCasa, BEHAVIOR-1K, MolmoSpaces, EmbodiedGen, PhysX-Anything's URDF/MJCF export, SimReady asset vendors) replace GPT-assigned mass/friction with table values; Isaac Lab / MuJoCo users set domain-randomisation events from measured per-material ranges instead of the folklore 0.1-1.0 friction band; evaluation-twin builders (SIMPLER, RoboArena-infinity) swap in values with provenance. How: `resolve(asset) -> USD physics material + mass/CoM/inertia + DR range + provenance.json`; `validate(clips, params) -> normalised replay error`, runnable by anyone with a phone and the public table; the table is a small JSON with n, sd and protocol per entry. What cannot be shown without a robot: that better object values change policy transfer -- the evidence is mixed (ASID positive on shuffleboard/rod balancing; SIMPLER <=15% sensitivity; 2606.20712 finds no mass/friction adaptation signal), so the deliverable is validated motion fidelity and a sim-to-sim sensitivity of non-prehensile primitives to the table's own error, with a stated partnership (a Franka lab running SIMPLER or RoboArena, reporting SRCC and offline replay error per the Reality Gap survey) for the policy claim.
proposals.novelty_argument: The landscape's clearest gap is that no sim-ready pipeline validates assigned parameters against the real motion of held-out objects, and no open material -> (mu, e, rho) atlas derived from real motion exists; GAUGE measures parameters and real trajectories but never tests an assignment method, PhysGS/NeRF2Physics validate friction with static pad readings, and BEHAVIOR-1K/UrbanVerse/MolmoSpaces assign at 10^4-10^5 scale with no check. Our e1 is the only held-out-transfer result in the landscape; this proposal turns it into a reusable library, adds the two columns every pipeline lacks (restitution, which only HoloScene even names, and build-aware mass, within 25% for 69% of objects vs 46% for an LLM), carries uncertainty as DR ranges, and audits a deployed library. Where the difference is small: for friction on block-like objects this is Galileo/Physics 101 with a better engine and a transfer test, i.e. a dataset-and-protocol contribution rather than a new method; the method novelty (shared-parameter joint fit with tape gradients, Laplace DR ranges) is modest and is said so.
nearest_prior_work: Own e1 held-out test (70 objects, 359 trials): the seed; this proposal adds restitution, non-block objects, uncertainty, external measured checks and a deployed-library audit.

GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948): measured mu/e and 180 Hz mocap trajectories, but engines are fed the measured values -- assignment is never tested; our harness uses its metric (error normalised by trial-to-trial variability) and its trials as an external held-out set if released.

PhysVid (arXiv 2510.02311): 5 objects x 6 surfaces dynamometer mu; regresses mu from video (foundation models r = 0.21-0.28) and never re-simulates; we use its matrix as a factorisation and transfer check.
NeRF2Physics (2404.04242) / PhysGS (2511.18570): LLM-proposed values validated against static pad friction and product masses; ours is motion-validated transfer with measured, not LLM, numbers.

BEHAVIOR-1K (2403.09227), RoboCasa (2406.02523), MolmoSpaces (2602.11337), UrbanVerse (2510.15018), EmbodiedGen V2 (2607.07459): the catalogues whose VLM/table values we audit and replace; none validates a value against motion.
NVIDIA SimReady spec: the USD container we emit into; it defines fields and no provenance or tolerance.
DROPO (2201.08434) / BayesSim: DR distributions identified from robot trajectories; ours come from passive real motion per material, no robot.
Galileo / Physics 101 (NeurIPS 2015, BMVC 2016): fitted a 2015 engine to the same footage; no held-out transfer, no engine fidelity check, no restitution.
DANOs (2210.09420): one real object, soap friction 0.61 vs 0.75 measured -- the only other motion-fitted vs measured comparison, at n = 1.
first_90_days: Weeks 1-2: first experiment on data on disk -- shared-mu joint gradient fit of each cardboard cube's trials, tape-vs-FD gate, Laplace sd vs observed repeat IQR; then the same for the other 10 materials with mu (643 clips). Decide here whether the uncertainty column is gradient-derived or repeat-trial-only.

Weeks 2-3: library audit -- download RoboCasa's 2,509 object MJCFs; LLM names material and build per object from its renders; report coverage into measured materials and the distribution of current friction/mass vs the table (and vs engine defaults); repeat for MolmoSpaces categories. This fixes the capture list: materials are chosen by catalogue demand.

Weeks 3-6: phone captures at 240 fps -- the 6x6 material-surface ramp matrix for the kill test (36 pairings x 5 trials), then ~30 materials at two tilts and two drop heights on 4-6 surfaces, kitchen-scale mass; scale check (g from free-fall within 5%) on every clip; CoTracker3 tracking; closed-form mu for blocks, exact-mesh joint fits for non-block shapes.

Weeks 6-8: run the factorisation kill test; build the restitution column (two routes: direct v_out/v_in and fitted alpha; if the phone route fails the column is 'unmeasured' except GAUGE's three materials); build-rule mass check against the kitchen scale.

Weeks 8-10: held-out validation -- object-held-out on Physics 101 (extending e1 to the tumbling/rolling objects via image-to-3D meshes scaled by measured volume) and on the own objects; external checks on PhysVid's mu matrix and GAUGE's slope-slider trials where released; report error normalised by repeat variability per material and parameter.

Weeks 10-12: resolver -> USD PhysicsMaterialAPI + MJCF export with provenance and DR ranges; apply to RoboCasa; sim-to-sim sensitivity of push/place/topple/toss primitives to the table's own error (which parameters matter where); write-up with every gate plot and the noise floor drawn.
proposals.first_experiment: On the 93 cardboard trials already tracked (9 cubes, 5-14 trials each, p1/p4), fit each cube's trials jointly with ONE shared mu and per-trial release time/offset as nuisances, using DiffMeshScene's tape gradient (L-BFGS, one backward pass per trial per iteration). Numbers it produces: (i) fraction of trials where the tape gradient of the real-clip loss agrees with central finite differences within 5% (pass >= 90%); (ii) |delta mu| between the shared-mu fit and p4's per-trial median per cube (expected <= 0.01, p4's own spread); (iii) the ratio of the Laplace-predicted mu sd (from a forward-difference Jacobian at the fit) to the observed per-cube repeat IQR of 0.01-0.03 -- the calibration of the uncertainty column, with 0.5-2x counting as usable. Runs in the warp env on one A6000 in well under a day of compute.
proposals.kill_test: The library premise is that friction factorises by material and build, independent of partner surface and shape. Decided now: on the own-captured 6 materials x 6 surfaces ramp matrix (36 pairings x 5 trials, 240 fps, p1 protocol, same scale check), fit a rank-1 product model mu_pair = m_i * s_j (11 free parameters) and predict each pairing held out in turn; if the held-out prediction error exceeds twice the within-pairing repeat sd for more than a third of pairings, friction does not factorise by material, the resolver cannot assign mu to unseen pairings, and the proposal collapses to per-pair measurement -- dead as a library. The weak two-surface version already passed on Physics 101 (p5 ratios 0.75-1.05 for block-like materials, with the ring 0.31 and doll 1.36 identified as shape, not friction). Companion gates: build-rule mass within 25% for >= 65% of new objects (currently 69%); material-transfer error must beat the dataset-wide median on a paired sign test (e1: 52/70, p = 6e-5) when the non-block objects are added, otherwise shape dominates material and the table needs a shape term.
proposals.resources: One researcher; one A6000 for all fits (a tape pass is 0.4 s per 1200 steps; the whole programme is tens of GPU-hours, well under the 2-GPU cap); the LLM gateway for naming (~2,600 RoboCasa objects + 150 own clips, tens of dollars); a phone with 240 fps, a tripod or stand, a plank, a floor tile, printed checkerboard, kitchen scale, and ~30 household materials plus 6 surface sheets (cardboard, plywood, plastic, cloth, rubber mat, paper; under $50 if the scale is missing); free downloads of RoboCasa and MolmoSpaces assets; Physics 101 already on disk (4.5 GB); optionally the GAUGE/PhysVid/IRIS releases (verify in week 1; nothing depends on them). No robot.
proposals.biggest_risk: That a material name is not a sufficient statistic for friction: surface finish, wear and humidity may dominate (Physics 101 shows mu falling with cube size 0.28 -> 0.21 for the same cardboard, unexplained; GAUGE notes surface treatment varies within a nominal material), so the within-material spread grows with material diversity until the error bar no longer beats a dataset-wide median -- an honest table that is useless. Secondary: the LLM's 80% naming degrades on ambiguous finishes (painted metal vs plastic, NeRF2Physics' documented failure), and our single-anchor factorisation (p5: table ~ ramp board) may not hold for soft or sticky partners, which the 6x6 matrix is designed to expose rather than hide.
proposals.expected_headline_result: A library of ~30 measured materials with repeat-trial uncertainty, resolved onto assets by material naming and build type, predicts the real slides and bounces of 100+ held-out objects at about 1.5x the per-object oracle and 3x better than VLM-assigned values, supplies measured domain-randomisation ranges, and replaces provenance-free physics on the 2,500 objects of a deployed robot-learning benchmark with values that carry an error bar.

evidence: COVERAGE CAVEAT: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before this review started, so no keyword search of 2025-2026 literature was possible; every item below was checked only by fetching primary arXiv/project pages for works already named in the proposal plus a few I knew of. A 2026 paper that builds exactly this atlas could exist unseen. Treat the verdict as medium confidence.

Measured material->(mu, e) table with repeat trials and real trajectories ALREADY EXISTS, small: GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948, HTML) measures mu by inclined plane 'mu=(g sin theta - vdot)/(g cos theta)', e = v_out/v_in, ~1,560 mocap trials at 180 Hz (16 NOKOV cameras), 3 rigid materials (wood/plastic/metal: plastic-on-wood 0.28, wood-on-wood 0.27, metal-on-wood 0.26, turntable 0.32/0.38/0.33; e 0.20-0.58), and reports error normalised by the real-world mean/std across repeated trials. It does NOT test any assignment method (parameters are 'kept fixed and reported with the benchmark'); public release could not be confirmed from the page. Proposal's characterisation is fair; its 'if released' hedge is warranted.

A material x surface measured friction matrix ALREADY EXISTS: PhysVid (arXiv 2510.02311, HTML) - 5 objects (plastic disk, LEGO brick, paper box, metal pencil box, wooden box) x 6 surfaces, spring dynamometer mu_k = F/G, disjoint pair splits. It never re-simulates or assigns by material. Minor mischaracterisation: the page gives V-JEPA-2 Pearson r = 0.21 (0.73 with domain adaptation) and DynamiCrafter 0.25 on real test-3, not 'r = 0.28'. The proposal's rank-1 factorisation kill test can be run on this matrix TODAY, before any capture.

The 'LLM names material -> property lookup' resolver validated against MEASURED friction ALREADY EXISTS: NeRF2Physics (arXiv 2404.04242, HTML) 'leverage[s] large language models to propose candidate materials' then kernel-regresses properties; evaluated on ABO-500 measured masses and on friction 'collected on 6 surfaces using an iOLab with fabric pads attached, averaging over 10 trials'. Validation is static-pad, not motion - proposal's characterisation is correct - but the resolver architecture is not new.

PhysGS (arXiv 2511.18570, HTML): per-point kinetic friction, mass, Shore hardness from vision + VLM priors; evaluated against 'a real-world friction-hardness dataset' of 'paired image and real-world measurement data'; no motion-based validation. Proposal's characterisation fair.

Catalogue-side claims CONFIRMED: UrbanVerse (arXiv 2510.15018, App. C.4) annotates physics with GPT-4.1 and validates only size and mass vs public specs, mass MAPE 19.58% +/- 12.11%, friction unchecked. MolmoSpaces (arXiv 2602.11337, HTML) 'verified that mass and density values were realistic by comparing simulated values with estimates annotated via large language models'. PhysX-Anything (arXiv 2511.13648, HTML) validates physical attributes by 14 volunteers' 0-5 ratings and MuJoCo usability. BEHAVIOR-1K (arXiv 2403.09227, HTML) says it annotates friction/mass but does not document the source. So 'no sim-ready pipeline validates assigned parameters against held-out real motion' held for every catalogue I could check.

UNCITED close relative: Scalable Real2Sim (arXiv 2503.00370, HTML) produces sim-ready assets with MEASURED mass/CoM/inertia from robot joint torques (mass error 1.34 +/- 0.21%, CoM 2.15%; inertia 358.6% on a printed bottle), no object friction, and only 'qualitative evaluation' of sim-vs-real rollouts because 'individual simulation rollouts are highly sensitive to initial conditions'. The proposal's build-aware mass (within 25% for 69%) is a cheaper, less accurate, robot-free alternative and should be positioned against it.

UNCITED: the MIT planar-pushing dataset (arXiv 1604.04038) records pusher/object poses and forces across surface materials and shapes and explicitly 'characteriz[es] the variability of friction' and tests 'the most common assumptions and simplifications made by models of frictional pushing' - directly relevant to the biggest_risk (material not a sufficient statistic) and to the factorisation kill test; it should be cited and its findings used.

DR-range novelty is thin: DROPO (arXiv 2201.08434) already derives domain-randomisation distributions from offline real trajectories by 'explicitly model[ing] parameter uncertainty to match real data using a likelihood-based approach'; the proposal's Laplace covariance from a Jacobian is a cheaper special case (passive clips instead of robot ones), which the proposal itself calls 'modest'.

Galileo/Physics 101 characterisation is PARTLY UNFAIR (medium confidence; PDFs could not be text-extracted here): Galileo (NeurIPS 2015 abstract) 'explore[s] directly mapping visual inputs to physical properties' and 'predict[s] the outcome of a variety of physical events, with an accuracy comparable to human subjects', and Physics 101's abstract names coefficient of restitution among recovered properties and 'outcome prediction' as a downstream task - i.e. generalisation to novel objects and a restitution column were attempted a decade ago. What they lack is the proposal's specific protocol (trajectory error vs per-object oracle, engine-fidelity check, repeat-trial normalisation).

UNVERIFIED (could not fetch): DANOs' 'soap 0.61 vs 0.75 measured' (PDF unreadable; abstract only confirms soap-on-table friction learned from real video), WorldBench, IRIS, the 'Reality Gap survey', ASID numbers, and SimReady physics-material provenance (docs.omniverse returned 403; the index page only says 'physical properties based on USDPhysics'). arXiv 2606.20712 confirmed: 'global physics parameters provide feedback that is too weak for reliable exploitation' - supports the proposal's honesty about the policy claim.
verdicts.surviving_form: The broad claim ('a measured physics-material library and resolver for sim-ready catalogues') is not new as a system: measured mu/e tables with repeat trials and real trajectories (GAUGE), a measured material x surface friction matrix (PhysVid), an LLM-names-material -> property-lookup resolver validated against measured friction and mass (NeRF2Physics, PhysGS), measured inertial parameters for sim-ready assets (Scalable Real2Sim), and data-derived DR distributions (DROPO) all exist. What survives, narrowly: (1) the VALIDATION PROTOCOL - scoring an assignment method by replaying held-out real objects' tracked motion through the engine with only release/offset aligned, normalised by repeat variability, and reporting it against a per-object oracle and a dataset median (e1 is the only instance found); (2) a restitution column derived from motion, which no catalogue carries (GAUGE has it for 3 materials; Physics 101 attempted it); (3) build-aware (areal/shell/solid) mass transfer, which should be benchmarked against Scalable Real2Sim's robot-measured values; (4) the audit of RoboCasa/MolmoSpaces values against measured ranges (confirmed nobody has done this, but it is an analysis, not a method). The proposal should be re-titled as a validation benchmark + protocol ('does material-level assignment reproduce held-out real motion?') rather than a library, should run the rank-1 factorisation test on PhysVid's existing 5x6 dynamometer matrix before buying captures, should cite Scalable Real2Sim and the MIT push dataset, and should drop the claim that Galileo/Physics 101 did no held-out transfer, saying instead that they reported no trajectory error against an oracle and no engine-fidelity check.
verdicts.summary: Novelty is refuted at the system level: every component of 'PhysMat' has a primary-source precedent - GAUGE already measures mu and e per material with repeat trials, 180 Hz mocap and a trial-variability-normalised metric; PhysVid already holds a 5x6 dynamometer friction matrix; NeRF2Physics/PhysGS already run an LLM-names-material -> property-table resolver validated against measured (static) friction and mass; Scalable Real2Sim already ships measured inertial parameters for sim-ready assets; DROPO already turns real trajectories into DR distributions. The proposal's own text concedes the method novelty is 'modest'. What I could not find anywhere is the specific thing e1 does - scoring an ASSIGNMENT method on held-out real objects' motion against a per-object oracle - and the catalogue audit; the catalogue claims (UrbanVerse mass-only MAPE 19.6%, MolmoSpaces validated against LLM estimates, PhysX-Anything human ratings) all checked out. Two characterisations need fixing (Galileo/Physics 101 did attempt novel-object property prediction and restitution; PhysVid's V-JEPA-2 r is 0.21 not 0.28), two relevant works are uncited (Scalable Real2Sim, MIT push dataset), and GAUGE's release is unconfirmed. Confidence is medium because web search was unavailable and only named/known works could be checked; a 2026 'material atlas' paper may exist unseen.

verdicts.lens: FEASIBILITY (hidden dependencies, two-week first experiment, 90-day milestone)
evidence: VERIFIED BY RUNNING (not by reading): scripts/g0_grad_check.py on a free A6000 (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1, warp env) reproduces the proposal's gradient claim exactly: d(slide)/d(mu_body) tape -0.5449 vs central FD -0.5453, identical rollout to MeshProbeScene (True), 0.5 s forward+backward for 1200 steps on a 386-vertex cube. The g0 scripts are untracked in git and this number appears in no doc (grep of docs/ finds nothing), so the plan rested on an unrecorded result until now; it holds.

The gradient is validated ONLY for one body vs a plane, w.r.t. mu, with a final-position loss. docs/results/g0b_verdict.json and scripts/g0c_grad_diag.py record the pair-contact adjoint under-transmitting (tape -0.03 vs FD -0.38). No gradient w.r.t. restitution alpha through an impact has been checked. The first experiment needs a NEW loss (trajectory over all frames + continuous release-time/offset nuisance; p4 aligns t0 by a 61-point grid search in scripts/p4_sim_loop.py:63) — a few days of kernel work, within two weeks.

Data for the first experiment is on disk: docs/results/p2_ramp_all.json persists s(t) per trial for all 643 clips (checked: list of 643, each with 'clip','s',...), docs/results/p4_sim_loop.json has 9 cardboard cubes with n = 9–11 trials each and per-trial mu_sim/mu_analytic. The p1 CoTracker cache lives only in a session scratchpad (/tmp/claude-1000021/.../p1_one.npz), but p2's JSON makes re-tracking unnecessary for the slides.

Compute: p4's solver config is FPS 30, SUB 336, 1.2 s horizon = 12,432 steps per clip; at the measured 0.5 s/1200 steps a tape pass is ~5 s, so 93 trials x ~50 L-BFGS iterations ~6.5 GPU-h, and all 643 clips ~45 GPU-h (+3 FD rollouts/clip for the gate). Per-step tape buffers for a 386-vertex cube at 12k steps are ~60 MB; a 20k-vertex asset at 20k steps (240 fps clip, dt 1e-4) is ~5–10 GB with adjoints — fits one A6000. nvidia-smi now: GPUs 1–5 idle (2 MiB used), so the <= 2-GPU cap is not binding.

Predictable gate outcome: Laplace sd from a tracking-noise Jacobian (fit RMS 0.3–3 mm, p1) will come out far below the repeat IQR 0.01–0.03 (which is true trial-to-trial variation: release, angle, dust), so the '0.5–2x usable' calibration gate will likely fail by ~10x; the plan already has the 'repeat-trial-only' fallback, so this is a wasted week, not a blocker.

Capture workload is undercounted: 30 materials x 4–6 surfaces x 2 tilts x >= 5 trials = 1,200–1,800 ramp clips, plus drops 30 x 4–6 x 2 heights x 5 = 1,200–1,800, i.e. 2,400–3,600 clips, not '~1,000'. At ~2 min per capture that is 80–120 h of one researcher's time in weeks 3–6, plus CoTracker3 on 720-frame 240 fps clips (~40–60 GPU-h) and 100–300 GB of video. Also requires a phone with true (non-interpolated) 240 fps and lighting adequate for ~1/480 s exposure — not confirmed to be in hand.

Restitution column (weeks 6–8): 30 fps failed (scripts/p3_restitution.py, g spread 2.7x). 240 fps makes v_in/v_out readable (~1 cm/frame at 2.4 m/s), but a block's e depends on landing orientation, not material; household materials rarely come as spheres. Column will be sparse; the proposal's explicit 'unmeasured' output makes this survivable.

Weeks 8–10 extension of e1 to tumbling/rolling Physics 101 objects needs image-to-3D meshes: no such model is in models/ (contents: _deps_wan, fpt, myriad, vjepa2_*). Open models (TRELLIS/Hunyuan3D) are obtainable but mesh fidelity for a doll/ring tumbling at 30 fps with the long-exposure blur that sank p3 is unvalidated — this is the most likely 90-day casualty and does not block the headline (blocks + build-rule mass).

Licences/external data: RoboCasa GitHub states code MIT, assets and datasets CC BY 4.0, download via `python -m robocasa.scripts.download_kitchen_assets` (object count stated as 3,200+, not 2,509). MolmoSpaces (arXiv 2602.11337) exists with open-source assets. GAUGE (arXiv 2608.05948, submitted 2026-08-06) exists; its abstract page lists no data release URL — the proposal correctly makes nothing depend on it. Physics 101 project page (phys101.csail.mit.edu) states NO licence or terms of use; publishing a derived per-material table is low-risk but should be cleared with the authors before release. Web search budget was exhausted this session, so PhysVid/IRIS release status was not checked.

USD PhysicsMaterialAPI export needs `usd-core` (pip, obtainable); MJCF export and the LLM gateway (used in f14/e1) exist. RoboCasa audit needs per-object renders (Blender at /home/nas5/jaeseonglee/blender-4.4.3-linux-x64/blender is available) and ~3,200 LLM calls — tens of dollars.
verdicts.surviving_form: The first experiment runs in two weeks as written (data on disk, gradient verified today, ~7 GPU-h). The 90-day milestone survives only if cut roughly in half: (1) captures limited to the 6x6x5 factorisation matrix (180 clips) plus ~20 materials x 3 surfaces x 2 tilts x 5 trials (~600 clips) and drops at ONE height for the sphere-like/flat-landing subset only — ~1,000 clips total, which is what the proposal actually budgets; (2) the non-block / image-to-3D extension of e1 moved out of the 90 days (or kept as a stretch with the tumble observable re-tracked in 2-D), so the held-out headline is on blocks plus build-rule mass, '100+ objects' becoming 101 Physics 101 + ~20 own; (3) the uncertainty column declared repeat-trial-based from week 2 unless the Laplace gate surprises, and the tape reserved for its one proven use (joint fits through plane contact) with per-clip FD gating as stated; (4) the audit restricted to RoboCasa (CC BY 4.0, verified), MolmoSpaces as a coverage count only; (5) the restitution column shipped sparse with 'unmeasured' as the normal case; (6) confirm a true-240 fps phone and clear Physics 101 redistribution with its authors in week 1.
verdicts.summary: Nothing the plan depends on is missing or unobtainable, so it is not refuted on feasibility: I re-ran the g0 gradient check and it reproduces the quoted numbers exactly (tape -0.5449 vs FD -0.5453, 0.5 s per 1200 steps), the 643 tracked trajectories are persisted in docs/results/p2_ramp_all.json, five A6000s are idle, RoboCasa assets are CC BY 4.0 with a download script, and MolmoSpaces/GAUGE exist. The first experiment is feasible in two weeks with a few days of new loss-kernel work. The 90-day milestone as written is not: the capture plan is undercounted 2–3x (2,400–3,600 clips, not ~1,000) for one researcher; the non-block e1 extension needs an image-to-3D model not on disk and unvalidated for tumbling objects at 30 fps; the restitution column will be sparse because block e is orientation-dependent; the Laplace-vs-IQR gate will predictably fail by ~10x (fallback exists); Physics 101 has no stated licence; and gradients are validated only for one body vs plane w.r.t. mu. Narrowed to blocks plus build-rule mass, ~1,000 clips, RoboCasa-only audit and repeat-trial uncertainty, the programme fits 90 days.

verdicts.lens: Impact and practicality: who consumes the output, is the effect size large enough to act on, does it answer the user's ask (differentiable physics, robots/sim, scale)
evidence: Effect size in the units practitioners use is tiny. docs/results/e1_heldout.json: median |dmu| oracle 0.010, material table 0.017, global single value 0.031, LLM-direct 0.052. The library's whole friction payoff over 'one number for everything' is dmu ~= 0.014, and over an LLM number ~= 0.035 -- both inside the 0.5-1.5x (roughly +/-0.3) friction domain-randomisation band Isaac Lab / RoboCasa users already apply. A table that moves mu by 0.03 does not change what anyone sets.

The measured sliding-material span is 0.159-0.330 (p2_ramp_all: dough 0.159 ... plastic ring 0.330), i.e. the entire material axis explains a 2x band of mu for things that slide at all; three materials never slide at 20 deg. The 'library' is ~11 numbers in [0.16, 0.33] plus 'stays'.

The 3x-better-than-VLM headline is 7.5 mm vs 2.6 mm RMS on a ramp slide, and the stay/slide outcome accuracy is 85% (LLM told the surface) vs 94% (table). The only large gap is against the generic 0.40 (86.9 mm, 62%), which the proposal itself labels unfair because the LLM was asked about wood.

The parameter robot manipulation actually consumes -- gripper-pad vs object friction -- is absent: the matrix is object x {cardboard, plywood, plastic, cloth, rubber mat, paper}. RoboCasa/BEHAVIOR objects are mostly grasped, not slid across a plank. Restitution, the second 'missing column', is currently empty: p3 (30 fps) FAILED and the 240 fps phone route is untested; the proposal already budgets 'unmeasured except GAUGE's three materials'.

The proposal concedes it cannot show the downstream effect: 'What cannot be shown without a robot: that better object values change policy transfer -- the evidence is mixed (SIMPLER <=15% sensitivity; 2606.20712 finds no mass/friction adaptation signal)'. For CoRL/RSS the reviewer question 'does it change any task metric?' has no answer; for a vision venue the method novelty is 'modest and is said so' (its own words). Realistic home is a NeurIPS D&B / workshop dataset-and-protocol paper.

Differentiable physics is decorative in the plan: 'What gradients buy nothing for: mu of a sliding block (1-D, closed form; e1 was done without them), mass (a scale), and the library audit.' The first 90-day experiment is a shared-mu fit of cardboard cubes whose answer (|dmu| <= 0.01) p4 already produced without a tape. The 300-unknown joint fit separates into 3 shared params x cheap per-trial nuisances; a sweep handles it, which rule 1 requires anyway. The one real gradient use (non-block ROLLS/tumble objects, Laplace DR ranges) is deferred to weeks 8-10 and gated.

Scale is redefined rather than met: the user asked for 'very large scale beyond rooms, interactable worlds at scale'; the proposal argues the axis is wrong and delivers ~30 materials x 6 surfaces resolved onto 2,509 RoboCasa MJCFs by LLM naming. That is an honest argument but it is not what was asked, and the 48k MolmoSpaces resolution is naming + lookup, with coverage 'reported, not assumed'.

Known consumer path exists but is weak: Isaac Lab DR already randomises static/dynamic friction and restitution per body, and Omniverse SimReady ships a named physics-material library with handbook values; replacing handbook mu with measured mu that differs by ~0.03 is a PR nobody is blocked on. The audit of RoboCasa (free download, LLM naming ~tens of dollars) is the one concrete, cheap, actionable deliverable and would at best produce a table of discrepancies without an outcome consequence.

Own e1 limits, stated in CLAUDE.md: 'friction is against the same board for train and test; a sliding block's law is shape-independent, so shape effects and centre of mass are not tested'. The held-out transfer that anchors the thesis is therefore proven only in the regime where shape does not matter, which is the regime where a library is least needed.
verdicts.surviving_form: Reframe from 'a material library' to 'a validation harness plus outcome-level sensitivity study', and lead with outcome flips, not millimetres: (1) First deliverable is the sim-to-sim sensitivity study on non-prehensile primitives (push-to-topple, place-and-slide, toss-and-settle) run on RoboCasa/BEHAVIOR objects with their CURRENT values vs measured-material values, reporting the fraction of primitives whose binary outcome flips; if that fraction is small, stop -- the library is not worth building, and that negative result is itself the actionable number. (2) Add gripper-pad (silicone/TPU finger surface) and the common tabletops (laminate, stainless, wood) to the surface matrix so the measured pairs are the ones a manipulation sim consumes. (3) Make the differentiable engine load-bearing or drop the claim: put the non-block (rolling/tumbling) exact-mesh joint fit and the Laplace DR covariance in weeks 1-4, not 8-10, since the block-mu part is closed form and already done in p4. (4) Ship the audit + resolver as a PR to RoboCasa/Isaac Lab SimReady material presets with provenance JSON, which is the only output a maintainer can act on today. (5) Secure the robot partner (SIMPLER/RoboArena lab) before week 1 and make the policy-transfer SRCC the headline; without it, target NeurIPS Datasets & Benchmarks with the harness as the contribution, not a method venue. (6) Drop the 'scale beyond rooms' framing entirely rather than arguing against it; tell the user plainly this is a tabletop-manipulation contribution.
verdicts.summary: The proposal is well-scoped, honest, and cheap, but on this lens it does not survive as written: the headline effect is dmu ~ 0.014-0.035 (e1: material 0.017 vs global 0.031 vs LLM 0.052), smaller than the friction domain-randomisation band every target consumer already applies, so no simulator maintainer or robot-learning group would change a value because of it; the parameter manipulation actually depends on (gripper-object friction) is not in the matrix; the restitution column is currently empty and depends on an untested phone route; the policy-transfer consequence is explicitly unshowable; and the plan uses differentiable physics only where it buys nothing (sliding blocks, closed form) while deferring the one place it would matter. It answers 'practical for simulations' partially (a RoboCasa audit/PR is actionable), answers 'differentiable physics' nominally, and answers 'scale beyond rooms' by rejecting the premise. Publishable as a datasets-and-benchmarks harness paper, unlikely at a top robotics venue without an outcome-level or policy-level result. Narrow it to an outcome-flip sensitivity study plus a validation harness with gripper surfaces, and let that study decide whether the library is worth building.

proposals.title: Phone-to-twin: per-object friction, restitution and centre-of-mass from one uninstrumented 240 fps phone clip through differentiable exact-mesh Newton
proposals.thesis: Every real-to-sim identification method in the landscape needs a robot, force-torque sensing, motion capture or RGB-D (ASID, TwinAligner, PIN-WM, D-REX, One-Shot, EKFPhys, ContactNets), so object twins exist only for objects a lab has already put in front of its robot, and none of them identifies restitution; we have shown Newton fitted to 30 fps footage reproduces a real slide to under 1 mm and that its contact gradients against a surface are exact. We claim that a few 240 fps phone clips of an object tilted to slide, dropped and nudged by hand, inverted jointly through the differentiable simulator with the release state as a nuisance, recover mu, restitution and centre-of-mass build well enough to predict the same object's motion under a different excitation within its own trial-to-trial variability -- a robot-free twin for the objects a robot actually manipulates.
proposals.what_we_build: (1) A capture protocol: phone on a stand, a printed checkerboard and the object's own measured dimensions for metric scale, a plank for two tilts, a slab for two drop heights, a hand nudge for a shove; the p3 scale check (g fitted from free-fall segments within 5%) as the per-clip admission gate. (2) A tracking front end: CoTracker3 tracks -> rigid 6-DoF pose fit per frame against the object mesh; mesh from a scan or an open image-to-3D model (Hunyuan3D-2 / TripoSR) scaled by measured dimensions, with the build (shell/solid/areal) named by the LLM or set by hand. (3) The inversion: DiffMeshScene (tape through plane contact) fitting, per object, shared (mu per surface, alpha, CoM offset, mass via build-aware density) with per-clip nuisances (release time, pose, in-plane velocity) by L-BFGS/LM, every gradient checked against central finite differences per clip; a Laplace covariance from the forward-difference Jacobian as the object's domain-randomisation range; the hand nudge modelled as a moving half-space pusher whose trajectory is tracked, which keeps the push on the validated plane-contact path (no body-body adjoint, g0b). (4) Validation by invariants, never by the fitted clip: mu from tilt 1 must predict tilt 2 (as p2's doll 0.155 vs 0.163); alpha from drop height 1 must predict the full multi-bounce trajectory at height 2; alpha fitted through the trajectory must agree with the direct v_out/v_in route; the nudge is held out entirely and predicted. (5) Export: USD PhysicsMaterialAPI + mass/CoM/inertia, MJCF, provenance and DR range per object.
proposals.builds_on_our_assets: MeshProbeScene exact mesh-vertex contact with the tilted ground plane, seat_on_plane (clearance 0), build-aware CoM/inertia (shell/solid/areal, checked to 1% against textbook values) and set_restitution_alpha (p7/p8: e independent of mass and stiffness, two rigs agree within 0.04-0.07); DiffMeshScene from g0 (per-step buffers, tape reproduces the validated rollout exactly, d(slide)/d(mu) = -0.5448 vs FD -0.5453, 0.4 s per 1200-step forward+backward); the p1-p4 real-footage pipeline (CoTracker3, release-time/offset alignment, Newton replay at 0.4-1.0 mm RMS, simulator mu = analytic mu to 0.005); the o7/o9/o14/p9 probe design knowledge (tilt reads mu, topple time reads CoM with mass/mu/alpha immune at 1.00-1.02x, bounce reads damping, balance reads mass; which objects can support which probe); the p3 restitution failure as the protocol for what a 240 fps capture must pass; e1's LLM material/build naming as the prior and initialisation; rules 1, 1b and 2 as the validation design. Not reused: renders, judge, surprise and the motion-prior stack.
proposals.differentiable_physics_role: Central, and limited to where it is validated. Each object's fit has ~10 physical and shared unknowns plus 3 nuisances per clip over ~10 clips (~40 unknowns, with slide, impact and rocking phases and no closed form for non-block shapes); the tape gives the full gradient in one backward pass per clip (0.4 s per 1200 steps), where finite differences need ~40 rollouts per step, so an object fits in minutes rather than an hour and the Laplace range comes with it. Gradients are exact today only through plane contact (g0), which is exactly this proposal's geometry -- object against board or slab, and the pusher as a tracked moving half-space -- so the broken multi-body adjoint (g0b: -0.032 vs FD -0.385 under sustained pushing) is never on the path. What is NOT established and is gated: the adjoint through the Hunt-Crossley impact for alpha may be noisy or step-size dependent (the stiff-setting nondeterminism seen in g0b; the DiffMJX problem); gate = per-clip central-FD agreement within 10% or at least sign-consistent, fallback = sweep/CMA-ES on the three physical parameters with the tape kept only for the smooth nuisances. For a block that only slides, gradients buy nothing (1-D), and the Jacobian for uncertainty still comes from forward differences because the Warp tape is reverse-mode only. Shape refinement (d loss / d mesh vertices, as One-Shot does) is the one place dense gradients would pay and is deferred.
proposals.scale_claim: The 'beyond rooms' framing is wrong for this proposal: a per-object twin scales by cost per object, not by scene extent, and the objects that matter to a robot group are the tens to hundreds in its evaluation set, not a city. Concretely: ~5 minutes of filming and under 10 minutes on one A6000 per object (386-vertex meshes; scanned meshes with 5k vertices cost a few times more); validated on 101 Physics 101 objects for mu and mass (30 fps limits e there) plus ~40 own household objects at 240 fps with kitchen-scale mass as truth, plus PhysVid's 30 dynamometer-measured pairs if released. The library of Proposal 1 covers the long tail by material; this covers the head by object.
proposals.practicality: Users: robot-learning groups building evaluation twins (SIMPLER, RoboArena-infinity, MolmoSpaces-style sim-to-real ranking) or non-prehensile/dynamic manipulation setups (ASID's shuffleboard and rod balancing are the cases where object values demonstrably mattered, 7/10 vs 3/10 and 6/9 vs 0/9) film each object once and get a USD/MJCF asset with mu, e, mass, CoM, inertia and a DR range, replacing GPT-4 values; the capture needs a phone, a plank and a tile. What cannot be shown without a robot: that the twin improves policy transfer or the sim-to-real correlation of policy rankings -- stated partnership: a Franka lab running SIMPLER swaps our object parameters for theirs and reports SRCC and offline replay error (the Reality Gap survey's metrics). What is shown without a robot: predictive validity on a held-out excitation of the same object within its trial-to-trial variability, restitution by two independent routes, mass against a scale, and a sim-to-sim sensitivity of push/place/topple/toss primitives to the fitted uncertainty (which parameters a given primitive cares about -- expected to agree with 2606.20712 that quasi-static pushing is insensitive while toppling and tossing are not).
proposals.novelty_argument: The landscape finds no rigid-object identification from a single uninstrumented video without a robot, F/T, mocap or depth; gradSim, the one pixels-only method, is evaluated on synthetic video only; EKFPhys needs RGB-D plus mocap ground truth and identifies mu only; DANOs is one soap bar; Galileo fitted Bullet to 30 fps footage with no restitution and no engine check; and restitution is identified by no real-to-sim method at all (PIN-WM lists it but excites it with one straight push). What is new: a phone-only protocol at 240 fps that reaches restitution, exact-mesh contact for non-block shapes, joint (mu, e, CoM-build) identification with per-object DR ranges, and validation by held-out excitation and two-route agreement rather than by the fitted clip. Where the difference is small: for mu of a block-like object this is Galileo with a better engine and a better camera, and the identification machinery (tape + LM + Laplace) is standard; the contribution is the protocol, the restitution column and the invariant-based validation, not a new estimator.
nearest_prior_work: EKFPhys (arXiv 2309.15703, 3DV 2024): EKF with a differentiable LCP engine from RGB-D at 60 Hz, 4 YCB objects, mu only, mocap-measured truth (median error 0.0246); ours is RGB phone only, adds e and CoM, validates by held-out excitation.
DANOs (2210.09420): Dojo + NeRF, soap friction 0.61 vs 0.75 measured, n = 1; same idea at n = 40-100 with restitution and invariants.
One-Shot Real-to-Sim (2412.00259): robot push + RGB-D, mass/CoM/inertia/friction through MLCP + PyTorch3D, 3 real objects, mass error 0.257 kg; no robot here, no restitution there.

PIN-WM (2504.16693) / TwinAligner (2512.19390) / ASID (2404.12308): robot-driven identification (one push, Control-Hit-Slide, Fisher-optimal exploration); our excitation is a hand and a plank, our Fisher analysis chooses which clip to film instead of which trajectory the robot executes.
D-REX (2603.01151): mass from a dexterous hand and 300 images, friction from a VLM; we measure friction and e instead of asking a VLM.
Galileo / Physics 101 (2015-2016): the canonical video fit; 30 fps, Bullet, no restitution, no transfer test.
gradSim (2104.02646): pixels-to-parameters on 10,000 synthetic videos; we use real footage and track rather than render.
IRIS (2603.16432): 240 lab videos at 60 fps of textbook objects with trajectory-fitted friction/damping; everyday objects and 240 fps here.
DiffMJX 'Hard contacts with soft gradients' (2506.14186): the fix for penalty-contact gradients through impacts, directly transferable if our alpha adjoint fails the FD gate.
Scalable Real2Sim (2503.00370): mass/CoM/inertia from torque sensing, friction and restitution left as future work -- the two we add.
first_90_days: Weeks 1-2: first experiment -- the restitution pilot (10 objects x 2 surfaces x 2 heights x 5 trials at 240 fps); scale check, two routes to e, cross-height prediction. The capture route lives or dies here.

Weeks 3-5: slides at two tilts and topple nudges for the same 10 objects; joint shared-parameter fit with per-clip nuisances via the tape; per-clip FD gates; Laplace sd vs repeat sd; two-tilt invariant (rule 1b).

Weeks 6-8: meshes via image-to-3D scaled by measured dimensions (or scans) for 40 household objects with kitchen-scale mass; full twin per object; the hand nudge as a tracked moving half-space pusher; held-out nudge prediction error per object.
Weeks 9-10: large-n validation on Physics 101 (101 objects, mu and mass only at 30 fps): per-object twin vs Proposal 1's material table vs LLM number, object-held-out; mass by build vs measured.

Weeks 11-12: USD/MJCF export with provenance and DR ranges; sim-to-sim sensitivity of push-to-goal, place/topple and toss primitives to each object's fitted uncertainty; approach one Franka lab with the exported twins and a one-page SRCC protocol; write-up with every gate and the noise floor drawn.
proposals.first_experiment: Restitution pilot: 10 household objects spanning expected e (rubber ball, wooden block, plastic block, ceramic mug, cardboard box, steel bolt, foam block, apple, book, tennis ball) dropped from two heights (0.15 m and 0.30 m) onto a wooden plank and a floor tile, 5 trials each -- 200 clips at 240 fps. Per clip: camera scale from the object's measured size; the admission gate is g fitted from the free-fall segments within 5% of 9.81 (p3 failed exactly here with a 2.7x spread at 30 fps); e by the direct route (v_out/v_in across the first impact from the tracked trajectory) and by fitting alpha through the whole multi-bounce trajectory in DiffMeshScene with the tape gradient, FD-checked. Numbers produced: per object-surface e with repeat-trial sd; the two-route agreement (fitted-alpha e vs direct e); and whether alpha fitted at 0.15 m predicts the 0.30 m trajectory within the repeat sd. Expected if the physics holds: between-material e spread (foam/rubber vs steel/ceramic) many times the repeat sd, and the mass-independence of alpha (p8) confirmed on real objects of different mass but the same material.
proposals.kill_test: Decided now, inherited from the p3 failure: if the camera scale from free-fall segments does not put g within +/-5% on at least 80% of pilot clips, or the two routes to e (direct v_out/v_in vs fitted alpha) disagree by more than the repeat-trial sd on more than a third of object-surface pairs, restitution cannot be read from a phone and the twin loses its only parameter no other pipeline provides -- the proposal then reduces to Galileo-with-a-better-engine and is not worth a paper. Identifiability gates (rule 1 / 1b): alpha from one drop height must predict the other within repeat sd, and mu from one tilt must predict the other; if either fails for the majority of objects the fitted values are effective constants of one condition, not properties, and are not exported. Rule 1 for the gradient: every exported fit must show tape-vs-FD agreement on its own clips; otherwise the parameter is reported from a sweep and the 'differentiable' claim is dropped from the write-up.
proposals.resources: One researcher; one A6000 (per object ~10 clips x 30 iterations x ~1 s tape passes, minutes; the full programme is tens of GPU-hours); a phone with 240 fps, stand, plank, tile, printed checkerboard, kitchen scale, 40 household objects (under $50 of purchases if the scale is missing); open image-to-3D weights (Hunyuan3D-2 or TripoSR) or a phone photogrammetry app for meshes; CoTracker3 from the local cache; Physics 101 on disk; the LLM gateway for build/material naming (negligible). No robot; one external partnership request (a Franka lab with SIMPLER) for the policy-transfer claim, clearly outside the 90 days.
proposals.biggest_risk: That one phone view does not identify centre of mass and inertia for the objects robots handle: the project's own geometry finding is that no asset supports all four probes (compact objects slide instead of toppling; tall ones topple before sliding), so most twins will carry a build-assumed CoM rather than a measured one, and the headline shrinks to mu and e. Secondary: image-to-3D meshes are 5-10% off in scale and shape, which matters little for a slide but dominates the fit for rocking, tumbling or bouncing objects where the contact geometry sets the motion; and the hand as excitation is not repeatable, so the held-out nudge may need several trials to average.
proposals.expected_headline_result: From a handful of uninstrumented 240 fps phone clips per object, differentiable exact-mesh simulation recovers friction, restitution and centre-of-mass build for 40 household objects; the fitted parameters predict a held-out excitation within the object's own trial-to-trial variability, restitution agrees between two independent routes to within repeat-trial scatter and is reproduced across drop heights, and mass from build-aware density is within 25% for about 70% of objects -- with no robot, depth camera or motion capture, at under 15 minutes per object.

evidence: Thesis claim 'every real-to-sim identification method needs a robot, F/T, mocap or RGB-D' is false. Hofherr, Koestler, Bernard, Cremers, 'Neural Implicit Representations for Physical Parameter Inference from a Single Video', WACV 2023, arXiv 2204.14030 (ar5iv confirmed): 'we captured videos of three physical systems: A block sliding on an inclined plane, a thrown ball ... and a pendulum' with an ordinary camera (block 30 fps, ball 120 fps), infers the friction coefficient mu and incline angle of the real sliding block via a differentiable neural-ODE fit, validated against ruler measurements (3.6% / 4.1%). Single uninstrumented RGB video, no robot, no depth, gradient-based. Limited to planar, known-parametric-form ODEs; no mesh contact, no restitution.

Galileo (Wu et al., NeurIPS 2015, papers.nips.cc d09bf415...) infers 'mass, position, 3D shape, and friction' from RGB video through a 3D physics engine and validates by outcome prediction vs human subjects -- uninstrumented video + engine fit is 2015 work. Physics 101 (phys101.csail.mit.edu, BMVC 2016) explicitly names 'mass, density, and coefficient of restitution' as the properties learned from 30 fps videos including 'objects falling onto various surfaces', so restitution-from-ordinary-video was already a stated target in the dataset this proposal plans to validate on (the project's own p3 found 30 fps insufficient).

Claim 'restitution is identified by no real-to-sim method at all' is overstated. DiffSDFSim (Strecke & Stueckler, 3DV 2021, arXiv 2111.15318, ar5iv confirmed): on a REAL tennis ball filmed with an 'Intel Realsense D455 camera (640x480 at 30 Hz)' it fits 'initial position and velocity, radius, restitution and friction' through a differentiable LCP simulator; validation is qualitative (radius 3.13 cm vs 3.24 cm truth), n = 1. Synthetic experiments fit friction, mass, force and shape from bouncing/pushing. So restitution + friction + shape from a real bounce video via differentiable physics exists; what is missing there is RGB-only, >=240 fps, n >> 1, and quantitative two-route / cross-height validation.

IRIS (arXiv 2603.16432, HTML confirmed): 240 real videos at 3840x2160 / 60 fps of 8 phenomena including 'sliding cone' with ground-truth friction mu and incline angle and 'dropping ball' with damping; ground truth from tape measure, inclinometer (+/-0.5 deg), laser meter, and Levenberg-Marquardt trajectory fits; protocol covers 'parameter accuracy, identifiability, extrapolation, robustness'. Appendix H: restitution 'is not representable by a static coupling coefficient' -- explicitly excluded. So a monocular, uninstrumented, LM-fitted, independently-measured benchmark for mu from video is already published; proposal's characterisation of IRIS (textbook objects, 60 fps, no restitution) is fair.

EKFPhys (arXiv 2309.15703, HTML confirmed): RealSense D455 at 60 Hz downsampled to 30 Hz, 4 YCB objects x 5 sequences, friction ONLY (masses 'measured using a scale'; restitution not estimated), truth by tilting a table with MoCap-measured angle and mu = tan(alpha) - a/g, median friction error 0.0246 vs 0.03 zero-baseline. Proposal's characterisation is accurate.

PIN-WM (arXiv 2504.16693, HTML confirmed): theta = {mass+inertia, restitution, friction}, identified from 'a single task-agnostic trajectory ... pushed forward along a straight line' by a robot, 4 real objects (T-object x2, mug, cube); restitution is in the parameter vector but is not excited by any bounce and is set to 0.00 in experiments. Proposal's characterisation ('lists it but excites it with one straight push') is fair.

DANOs (arXiv 2210.09420): learns friction of 'a bar of soap from a real video of the soap sliding on a table' with Dojo; mass/CoM/inertia via differentiable contact on synthetic bunny. n = 1 real object -- fair characterisation. Kandukuri et al. GCPR 2020 (arXiv 2009.08292): mass and friction from video via differentiable physics, simulated scenarios only -- consistent with proposal's note that pixels-to-parameters prior work is synthetic (gradSim likewise).

Could NOT confirm from a primary source (medium/low confidence): Scalable Real2Sim (2503.00370) abstract confirms 'joint torque sensors and an external camera' and 'inertial parameters' but not the 'friction and restitution left as future work' sentence; D-REX (2603.01151) abstract confirms mass via optimisation from vision + robot control signals but not 'friction from a VLM'; One-Shot (2412.00259) abstract says 'sparse visual and tactile observations' from one robot action, not RGB-D explicitly, and gives no 0.257 kg figure; ASID (2404.12308) abstract confirms robot + mass/articulation but not the shuffleboard 7/10 vs 3/10 numbers; TwinAligner (2512.19390) confirms robot-object interaction only. Kandukuri et al. IJCV 2022 extension could not be fetched (arXiv author page 404) -- if it added real-world sliding videos it would further erode the 'no uninstrumented video' claim. Smartphone-based coefficient-of-restitution measurement is a long-standing physics-education practice (sound-timed and video-timed bounce methods); no primary source fetched because the shared WebSearch budget was exhausted after one query -- treat as medium confidence.

Search coverage caveat: 1 of 6 planned WebSearch calls executed (session budget exhausted); all other evidence is from direct primary-source fetches of ids already known or surfaced by that one search. A 2025-2026 RGB-only phone-video twin paper with restitution could exist unseen; by the task's default rule that uncertainty counts against novelty.
verdicts.surviving_form: Drop the thesis sentences 'no rigid-object identification from a single uninstrumented video' (Hofherr WACV 2023, Galileo 2015) and 'restitution is identified by no real-to-sim method' (DiffSDFSim 2021 fits restitution of a real tennis ball; Physics 101 named it as a target; PIN-WM carries it). Do not claim the differentiable-engine inversion, the Laplace/Fisher DR range, or the LM-with-nuisance machinery as new (IRIS, EKFPhys, DiffSDFSim, Hofherr all do gradient fits to real video; ASID does Fisher-based identification). What remains open and defensible, stated as an evaluation contribution rather than a method: (1) joint mu + restitution + centre-of-mass-build identification of NON-primitive everyday objects through exact mesh contact from RGB-ONLY footage at >= 240 fps, where prior real-object results are n = 1 (DiffSDFSim, tennis ball, RGB-D, qualitative; DANOs, soap, mu only) or n = 4 with depth and mu only (EKFPhys) or planar known-form ODEs with n = 3 scenes (Hofherr); (2) validation by held-out excitation within trial-to-trial variability and by two independent routes to e (direct v_out/v_in vs trajectory-fitted alpha) across drop heights, at n ~ 40-100 objects -- no fetched work reports this; (3) the three-way comparison on held-out Physics 101 objects: per-object twin vs material table vs LLM number (the last two already exist in the project's e1). Frame the phone protocol as replicating IRIS-style independently-measured ground truth for everyday robot-relevant objects plus a restitution column IRIS explicitly excludes. Note two fairness fixes to the prior-work list: EKFPhys's truth uses MoCap only for the ramp angle, and the cross-height invariant may fail for physical reasons (e falls with impact speed, as the project's own p8 shows), so it must be a velocity-dependent e model, not a constant, or the gate will kill a correct pipeline.
verdicts.summary: Refuted at the thesis level. The two load-bearing novelty claims are both contradicted by primary sources: Hofherr et al. (WACV 2023, arXiv 2204.14030) already infer the friction coefficient of a real sliding block from a single ordinary-camera video (30 fps; a thrown ball at 120 fps) by gradient-based fitting with no robot, depth or mocap, and Galileo (NeurIPS 2015) fitted mass/friction/shape from RGB video through a physics engine; DiffSDFSim (3DV 2021, arXiv 2111.15318) fits restitution and friction of a real bouncing tennis ball through a differentiable simulator from a RealSense at 30 Hz, and Physics 101 itself lists coefficient of restitution as a learned property. IRIS (2603.16432) already provides an uninstrumented 60 fps monocular benchmark with independently measured mu and LM-fitted parameters, excluding restitution by design. The proposal's descriptions of EKFPhys, PIN-WM, DANOs and IRIS are accurate; several numeric claims about ASID, One-Shot, D-REX and Scalable Real2Sim could not be verified from abstracts (medium confidence). What has no fetched precedent is the evaluation design at scale: RGB-only >= 240 fps capture, joint mu/e/CoM-build for non-primitive objects via exact mesh contact, two-route restitution agreement, held-out-excitation prediction within repeat variability, and a per-object-twin vs material-table vs LLM comparison on held-out Physics 101 objects. That is a protocol-and-validation contribution with a restitution column, not a new identification idea, and only one WebSearch could be run before the session's budget ran out, so an unseen 2025-26 competitor cannot be excluded.

verdicts.lens: FEASIBILITY (first experiment in 2 weeks; 90-day milestone; hidden dependencies: metric scale, contact gradients, frame rate, licences, GPU, one researcher, no robot/rig)
evidence: RAN scripts/g0_grad_check.py on a free A6000: tape d(slide)/d(mu) = -0.5448 vs central FD -0.5453, identical rollout to MeshProbeScene, 0.4 s per 1200-step forward+backward, 386 vertices. The proposal's cited numbers are real and reproduce today.

RAN a new check (scratchpad drop_grad.py, DiffMeshScene, 7 cm cube dropped 0.15 m onto the plane, loss = height 0.25 s after release, parameter = cd): tape/FD ratio 1.00 / 1.02 / 0.95 at cd 300 / 1500 / 6000 on the bounce rig (pen_frac 5e-3) and 1.00 on the tilt rig (pen_frac 1e-4, 420 substeps). The damping adjoint through a PLANE impact -- the pilot's one untested software step -- holds. Oblique (corner-first) impacts were not tested (my rotated case fell through the plane due to my own setup, not the project's code).

RAN scripts/g0d_grad_free.py: body-body cd gradient tape -2.96e-5 vs FD -1.79e-5 (1.66x off) and glancing mu gradient 0.0018 vs 0.0037 at 5 cm offset -- confirms the pair adjoint is unreliable, so keeping the hand nudge on the plane path (moving half-space) is necessary, not optional. ground_contact_mesh accumulates with wp.atomic_add (src/sim/mesh_contact.py:105), so a second moving plane can be launched per step.

Warp 1.15: wp.copy IS recorded on the tape (warp/_src/context.py:12827 record_func(adj_copy)), so pos0/rot0/vlin0 nuisances assigned into pos[0] can take gradients. BUT the CoM offset is applied in numpy at construction (mesh_scene.py:101-125 re-centres self.local) and the inertia G is numpy -- 'CoM-build through the tape' does not exist yet and needs new differentiable plumbing (local vertex cloud + G on tape).

Contact softness: on the bounce rig the 0.15 m drop penetrates 0.8-1.9 cm of a 3.5 cm half-size (zmin 1.61-2.70 cm); tilt-rig stiffness penetrates 3 mm. Hard materials (steel bolt, ceramic mug on tile) need the stiff setting; it passes FD, so this is a choice to make, not a blocker.

Model-form risk inside the kill test: the sim's restitution law is e ~ 1 - alpha*v by construction (p8: 0.70 at 1 m/s, 0.54 at 2 m/s). Drops from 0.15 m and 0.30 m impact at 1.72 and 2.43 m/s, so for a real material whose e is nearly velocity-independent, alpha fitted at 0.15 m will mispredict 0.30 m by the law, not the camera. The 'alpha from height 1 predicts height 2' gate as written tests the contact law and would kill the proposal for the wrong reason unless e is fitted directly per impact speed or the law is changed.

p3 failure (docs/results/p3_restitution_summary.json): e_h 0.05-0.34 with inverted physics (cardboard on foam 0.34 > table 0.20) at 30 fps. At 240 fps a 0.30 m fall is ~59 frames, so the g-within-5% gate is plausible; this is the point the pilot exists to decide, and the code (p3_restitution.py, CoTracker3 scaled_offline.pth in ~/.cache/torch/hub) is on disk.

Monocular 6-DoF pose front end does NOT exist in the repo: p1-p4 reduce the track to 1-D along the slope; CoTracker3 gives 2-D tracks with no mesh correspondence. Trajectory-route e for non-spheres (box, book, mug, blocks, bolt: 7 of the 10 pilot objects), topple/rocking fits (weeks 3-5) and the held-out hand nudge (weeks 6-8) all need per-frame pose against the mesh. Obtainable (silhouette/keypoint PnP, Gen6D-style RGB pose) but it is a build item the plan does not budget.

Image-to-3D weights: none on disk (models/ holds fpt, myriad, vjepa2, wan deps only). Hunyuan3D-2 licence defines Territory as worldwide EXCLUDING the EU, UK and South Korea (https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hunyuan3D-2/blob/main/LICENSE; https://scancode-licensedb.aboutcode.org/tencent-hunyuan-3d-2.0-cla.html); the shared box and gateway point at a Korean institution, so Hunyuan3D-2 is not usable here -- TripoSR / TRELLIS (MIT) or phone photogrammetry must replace it.

GPU budget: 0.4 s per 1200 steps => a 1 s clip on the tilt rig (10080 steps) ~3.4 s per pass; 10 clips x 30 LM iterations ~17 min per object at 386 vertices, on ONE GPU; 5k-vertex scans ~10x. Within the <=2-GPU constraint. Cards 2-5 were free at the time of the check.

Scope load for one researcher in 90 days: pilot (200 clips) + 40 objects x ~10 clips + meshes for 40 objects + a 6-DoF pose tracker + CoM/inertia on the tape + moving-pusher kernel + Physics 101 large-n + USD/MJCF export + primitive sensitivity. Weeks 1-2 and weeks 9-10 reuse existing code; weeks 3-8 contain three new subsystems.
verdicts.surviving_form: The 2-week restitution pilot can run as planned (phone, plank, tile, CoTracker3 cache, p3 code, DiffMeshScene with the FD-verified plane-impact cd adjoint) with three amendments: (1) restrict the trajectory-route and cross-height claims to near-spherical or flat-landing objects (ball, tennis ball, apple, flat-dropped blocks), and report e for the irregular objects only by the direct v_out/v_in route until a pose front end exists; (2) replace the 'alpha from 0.15 m predicts 0.30 m' gate by 'direct e at each height, then fit alpha(v) and check that the fitted law reproduces both' -- otherwise the Hunt-Crossley velocity dependence fails the gate for the camera; (3) use the stiff (tilt-rig) contact setting for hard materials, where the adjoint also passes FD. The 90-day milestone must be narrowed: twins carry mu (two tilts, existing p1-p4 code), e (direct + fitted), mass by build-aware density, and a build-ASSUMED CoM/inertia; the measured-CoM column, the tracked hand-nudge hold-out and the 40-object count move to a second phase that first builds the monocular 6-DoF pose fit and puts the CoM/inertia on the tape. Image-to-3D must be TripoSR/TRELLIS or photogrammetry, not Hunyuan3D-2, given the licence territory. Keep the pilot at 10 objects and the large-n validation on Physics 101 (mu, mass) as the 90-day headline.
verdicts.summary: Not refuted: nothing the pilot needs is missing or unobtainable, and the two numbers it rests on were re-run today -- the plane-contact friction adjoint matches FD (-0.5448 vs -0.5453) and, newly checked, the damping adjoint through a plane impact matches FD within 5% on both contact settings. The first experiment is runnable in two weeks with a 240 fps phone, a plank and existing p3/CoTracker code. The 90-day plan as written is not: it silently depends on a monocular 6-DoF object pose tracker (none exists in the repo; 7 of the 10 pilot objects are non-spheres whose trajectory-route e, rocking and nudge fits need it), on CoM/inertia being on the Warp tape (they are numpy at construction), on an image-to-3D model whose licence excludes South Korea, and on a cross-height gate that actually tests the simulator's e ~ 1 - alpha*v law rather than the camera. Narrowed to mu + direct e + build-aware mass with assumed CoM, validated on Physics 101 at large n and on ~10 household objects at 240 fps, it fits one researcher and one A6000 in 90 days.

verdicts.lens: Impact and practicality: who consumes the output, is the effect size actionable, does it answer the user's ask (differentiable physics, practical for robots/sim, scale)
evidence: No named consumer can use the artifact as exported: the fitted restitution is a Hunt-Crossley alpha relative to a penalty stiffness in Newton (CLAUDE.md p7/p8: e depends on cd/k, alpha = 2*HC*cd/3k). USD PhysicsMaterialAPI / MJCF consumers (SAPIEN/PhysX for SIMPLER, MuJoCo for ManiSkill-style twins) take a coefficient of restitution or solref/solimp; the proposal exports an effective constant of one engine's contact law and never checks that the same drop reproduces in a second engine -- exactly the 'effective parameters' gap it accuses CoDimRecon / SimReady of.

The 'only parameter no other pipeline provides' rests on a contact model with an unphysical speed law: docs/results/p8_alpha.json gives e(alpha=0.4) = 0.643-0.704 at 0.99 m/s and 0.502-0.542 at 1.98 m/s; the pilot's 0.15 m and 0.30 m drops (1.7 vs 2.4 m/s) differ by ~0.1 in e under the sim before any object property enters. The cross-height gate therefore tests the model form; it either kills the proposal by its own kill test or passes only through a loose repeat-sd tolerance. Real materials show much weaker e(v).

Differentiable physics is admitted to be non-load-bearing: the proposal itself says gradients 'buy nothing' for a sliding block, the Laplace Jacobian comes from forward differences anyway, and the fallback is a sweep/CMA-ES. The one place the tape matters (alpha through impacts) is the regime where the project's own gradient checks fail: scripts/g0c_grad_diag.py docstring 'FD d(A disp)/d(mu_B) = -0.38 but the tape ...' and docs/PROJECT_LOG.md:786 'landing over the collapse breaks smoothness (tape != FD), same wall as rigid'. The user's ask (a) is answered in name only; the honest version of the paper is a sweep-fit with a differentiable nuisance solver.

Effect size for friction is small by the project's own held-out test: material-table mu predicts a never-seen real object's slide to 2.6 mm median vs the per-object oracle 1.8 mm (e1_heldout). A per-object twin can at best close 0.8 mm of a 2.6 mm error that is already below what any manipulation task resolves; the free material table (Proposal 1) captures most of the value for mu and mass. CoM is flagged by the proposal as its biggest risk (no asset supports all four probes), so the headline predictably shrinks to mu + e.

The robot-facing claim (policy transfer, SRCC on SIMPLER) is explicitly outside the 90 days and depends on an unsecured Franka-lab partnership; without it, a CoRL/RSS reviewer sees 'Galileo (2015) with a better camera and engine', which the proposal concedes in its own kill-test paragraph. The planned substitute -- sim-to-sim sensitivity of push/topple/toss primitives -- shows parameters matter, not that these twins help; 2606.20712 already reports that result.

Scale ask (c) is rejected rather than addressed: 'the beyond-rooms framing is wrong for this proposal'. Cost per object (5 min filming + 10 min GPU, hand nudge non-repeatable, image-to-3D meshes 5-10% off which the proposal says 'dominates the fit for rocking, tumbling or bouncing objects') caps it at tens of objects, i.e. the head of a single lab's evaluation set.

Feasibility of the pilot itself is real and cheap (phone, plank, tile, 200 clips, 240 fps fixes the p3 blur/scale failure, ~tens of GPU-hours), so the restitution MEASUREMENT has standalone value as a dataset even if the twin does not -- this is the surviving kernel.
verdicts.surviving_form: Narrow to a 240 fps engine-agnostic restitution-and-friction dataset plus an engine-portability check, not a per-object twin paper: (1) run the drop pilot but report e(v_in) curves by the direct v_out/v_in route for ~40 household objects x 2 surfaces x 3-4 heights, with repeat sd, as the deliverable; (2) fit alpha in Newton only AFTER showing the sim's e(v) slope matches the measured one (or replace the HC law with one whose e is v-independent at a chosen speed) -- otherwise alpha is exported as an effective constant tagged with its impact speed; (3) demonstrate portability by reproducing the same measured drops and slides in a second engine the consumers actually run (MuJoCo and PhysX/SAPIEN) from the exported USD/MJCF, which is the check none of the sim-ready pipelines do and is the publishable gap; (4) drop 'differentiable' from the title unless the alpha adjoint passes the per-clip FD gate on real impact clips; keep the tape for nuisance alignment only; (5) replace the hypothetical Franka partnership with an in-sim experiment on an existing benchmark's own objects (SIMPLER/ManiSkill assets in SAPIEN): swap their material values for the measured ones and report whether the ranking of released policies changes (SRCC against the benchmark's published real rankings), which needs no robot and makes the impact claim falsifiable within 90 days; (6) merge with Proposal 1 so the measured table (material level) is the product and the per-object twin is the head-of-distribution extension, since e1 shows the table already captures most of the mu/mass value.
verdicts.summary: The proposal is honest, cheap and executable, but under the impact lens it does not survive as stated. Its unique selling point -- restitution from a phone -- is fitted as a Hunt-Crossley alpha whose implied e already shifts ~0.1 between the two pilot drop heights purely from the simulator's velocity law (p8_alpha.json), is not portable to the PhysX/MuJoCo engines any named consumer runs, and its tape gradient lives in the one regime (impacts) where the project's own FD checks fail; the proposal concedes gradients are otherwise unnecessary, so the 'differentiable physics' element is nominal.
