Concretely over 90 days: about 25 materials (15 from Physics 101 plus about 10 captured by phone), 4-6 surfaces including at least one outdoor one (concrete paver or asphalt tile) so the rows that street-scale simulators guess have a measured counterpart; validation on 101 + about 30 held-out real objects (about 500 real trials); and application to one city-scale library (UrbanVerse-100K's 102k assets, or MolmoSpaces' 130k if its metadata is easier to obtain) to report what fraction of its assets a measured row could ground and how far its shipped numbers sit from measured ones. 'Beyond rooms' is satisfied because a cardboard row is the same on a sidewalk as on a desk; what changes outdoors is the surface, and the one-slide anchor is how a surface is added.
proposals.practicality: Anyone exporting assets for Isaac Lab/Newton, MuJoCo or Genesis (EmbodiedGen-style generators, SimReady vendors, lab digital twins) replaces 'ask GPT for the number' with 'ask GPT for the name, look the number up, carry its uncertainty and provenance': the output is a USD physics material plus mass, CoM and inertia by build, with a flag saying which numbers are measured. Domain-randomisation users get measured ranges (the IQR per material) instead of the commonly cited guessed bands (friction 0.3-1.5, restitution 0-0.1). Benchmark authors get e1-bench to score any assignment pipeline on real motion. The honest limit on the robot claim: the evidence that object-parameter accuracy changes policy transfer is task-dependent (ASID positive, SIMPLER at most 15% sensitivity, 2606.20712 'no stable adaptation signal'), so the value proposition is correct contact outcomes where they matter (slides, stays, topples, bounces) and a provenance tag, not a promised policy gain.
proposals.novelty_argument: Forecast for the next 12 months: NVIDIA ships Newton GA inside Isaac Lab with MuJoCo Warp as the non-differentiable default, more SimReady packs, and VoMP/AdaVoMP/PhysX-Omni-style generators whose parameters are VLM annotations checked by VLM judges; DeepMind ships Genie 4 / Project Genie with no object state; Meta ships V-JEPA successors; UrbanVerse, MolmoSpaces, BEHAVIOR and PhysX-* grow to more assets with the same provenance. None of them will publish that their VLM numbers are 3x worse than a measured table on real motion, because those numbers are the product, and none will run a held-out real-object test, because their validation currency is asset count, VLM agreement and policy success. This project already holds the only such test (e1), the only material rows derived from motion with invariant checks, and the controlled negatives showing that video models and LLMs carry no object-specific theta (judge wrong 9/9, surprise at chance, FPT/MYRIAD/Wan motion-magnitude only, LLM numbers a generic 0.4). Genuinely new: validation of ASSIGNED parameters on held-out real motion across surfaces (no work tests surface transfer), a one-slide surface protocol, and a real-motion benchmark for assignment pipelines (the six scouts found none). Small: a material table is conceptually a handbook; the step from the NeRF2Physics/PhysGS/BEHAVIOR lookups to ours is measurement, uncertainty and validation, not a new idea.
nearest_prior_work: Our own e1 (70 objects, 359 trials): the same protocol on one surface, no restitution, no library audit

NeRF2Physics (CVPR 2024) and PhysGS (CVPR 2026): LLM-proposed numbers spread by CLIP / Bayesian fusion, validated against pad-on-surface friction meters and product-listing mass, never against the object's own motion
BEHAVIOR-1K / OmniGibson: material-name -> friction lookup with unstated source, unvalidated
UrbanVerse-100K (ICLR 2026): GPT-4.1 mass and friction for 102k urban assets; mass checked against spec sheets (19.6% MAPE), friction never checked
MolmoSpaces (2602.11337), EmbodiedGen V2 and ManiTwin: GPT-4o / GPT-5.4 mass and friction ranges validated by policy-ranking correlation or human plausibility
GAUGE (2608.05948): measured mu and e fed into Isaac, Genesis and Newton against 180 Hz mocap, but no assignment step and no held-out objects
PhysVid (2510.02311): 30 dynamometer-measured object-surface pairs used to score estimators, not assignment
NVIDIA SimReady Foundation spec: the container (density, static/dynamic friction, restitution) with no provenance or tolerance
Galileo / Physics 101 (2015-16): the data, fitted per clip for outcome prediction, with no transfer test
first_90_days: Days 1-14: the surface-transfer experiment below: phone capture of 8 household objects of 4 ledger materials on 2 new surfaces at 2 angles x 5 trials, plus one reference cardboard cube per surface; fit through p2/p4; report anchored-prediction error against the oracle and the factorisation residual; kill decision at day 14.

Days 15-30: the audit, on disk: download or replicate each library's assignment rule (UrbanVerse GPT-4.1 prompt, MolmoSpaces GPT-4o mass, BEHAVIOR-1K lookup, PhysXNet density, SimReady defaults) for the 101 Physics 101 objects; score with e1's harness under both our geometric-mean rule and PhysX's default combine; paired sign test per library.

Days 31-45: ledger v1 with uncertainty: DiffMeshScene + LM joint fit per session (shared ramp angle, per-cube mu, per-trial t0/s0) over the 643 clips; Laplace sigma against the empirical IQR on cubes with >= 10 trials; fitted ramp angle against the nominal 20 deg as a sanity invariant.

Days 46-65: extend the ledger by phone: about 10 new materials (glass, ceramic tile, steel, aluminium, MDF, PVC, rubber, cork, painted wood, fabric-covered board) on the reference board and on one outdoor surface; held-out test on about 30 new objects; the restitution column is filled only if Proposal 2's drop kill test passes, otherwise tagged unmeasured.

Days 66-80: assignment tool and SimReady export with provenance, run on our 13 assets and on a 1,000-asset sample of one public library; coverage % and the measured-vs-shipped gap per material; a DR-range table.
Days 81-90: write-up with every kill-test number stated either way; release the ledger, the surface protocol, e1-bench and the audit scripts.
proposals.first_experiment: Surface transfer with one anchor slide. Capture, 240 fps side view, 8 everyday objects of 4 ledger materials (cardboard box, wooden block, plastic block, porcelain plate or cup; two of each) on 2 surfaces not in the ledger (laminate desk, pine plank) at 2 tilts each bracketing the slip threshold, 5 trials per cell (160 clips), plus a reference cardboard cube on each surface (5 trials); angle from the phone inclinometer, scale from each object's own measured edge, the two-angle invariant as the gate (p2). Fit mu_pair per clip through p2/p4. Anchor each surface by the reference cube's ratio to its board row, predict every other object's mu_pair from its ledger row, and score the prediction on that object's real slides with e1's trajectory RMS (only release time and offset aligned). Numbers produced: the median trajectory RMS (mm) of the anchored material prediction on the 8 held-out objects, against the per-object oracle on the same surface and against the dataset-wide median predictor; and the factorisation residual sd(log mu_pair - a_object - b_surface) against the within-cell trial IQR. Expected if the ledger transfers: anchored error <= 1.5x oracle (roughly 2-3 mm against about 1.8 mm) and a residual within 1.5x of the trial IQR.
proposals.kill_test: Decided now. The ledger is dead as an 'any surface' layer if, on the two new surfaces, the anchored material prediction's median trajectory error is not below the dataset-wide median predictor's error on the same clips (paired sign test over the 8 objects, p < 0.05 required), or if the factorisation residual exceeds 2x the within-cell trial IQR on the log scale; pair friction then does not factorise across surfaces, the table ships only surface-specific rows, and the 'beyond rooms' claim is dropped. The audit wedge is dead if any library's own rule matches or beats the ledger on real motion (paired sign test, p < 0.05 for the ledger over the rule required). The assignment tool is dead as an automatic step if the LLM names the new objects' materials at under 60% accuracy with the e1 prompt; it then becomes human-named, table-numbered, and the paper says so.
proposals.resources: One shared A6000 used in bursts: CoTracker3 at about 1 min per 240 fps clip (160-500 clips), Newton sweeps and tape fits at under 1 s per clip; about $100-200 of LLM gateway calls for the audit prompts; a phone with 240 fps, an inclinometer app, two boards and about 30 household objects; 2-3 days of capture per phase; no robot, no rig. Everything runs in the existing warp and cosmos envs with no new model installs.
proposals.biggest_risk: That friction is not a material property at the precision claimed: finish, wear and humidity make mu_pair an object-surface property, and p1's unexplained size dependence (Spearman -0.80 across cubes) is a warning that the factorisation may hold only for block-like, dry, clean surfaces. The kill test is built to catch this, but a partial failure (holds for wood/cardboard/plastic, fails for rubber and porcelain) would shrink the ledger to the materials where it works and weaken the audit. Second: the mapping of our pair rule and alpha onto PhysX's combine modes and restitution scalar is contestable, so the audit must report results under both conventions or it will be dismissed as a convention mismatch.
proposals.expected_headline_result: A material table measured from real video with repeated-trial uncertainty, assigned through an LLM that only names the material, predicts the real slides of 130 never-seen objects on surfaces it never measured to within 1.5x of a per-object oracle after one reference slide per surface (about 2.5 mm against 1.8 mm), while the VLM-assigned numbers in today's 100k-asset sim-ready libraries predict the same motion 3x worse; we release the table, the one-slide surface protocol, SimReady export with provenance, and the first real-motion benchmark for parameter-assignment pipelines.

evidence: PRIOR ART FOR THE 'ONE-SLIDE SURFACE ANCHOR / FACTORISATION' (strongest refutation): arXiv 2604.24188 (Wang & Wang, 27 Apr 2026, 'Generalizable Friction Coefficient Estimation via Material Embedding and Proxy Interaction Modeling', https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.24188). Pairwise friction f(A,B) is predicted from measurements against a small fixed set of PROXY materials via per-material embeddings; a 50+ material tribometer library (45 fabrics + tiles, terracotta, glass, metals, wood, plastics, kraft/corrugated paper, leather; second campaign 30 fabrics + 10 substrates), static mu by slip angle and kinetic mu by laser-gated transit on an inclined groove; leave-one-material-out cross-validation (Sec. 7.4), 'R^2 approaches unity', proxy set reduced to TWO materials (Sec. 7.3). Crucially it states f(A,B) 'cannot be reliably inferred from the independent features of A and B' -- i.e. a learned coupled embedding is needed, which argues directly against the proposal's single multiplicative anchor (k=1). It does NOT validate on object motion or video (full-text fetch, high confidence).

PRIOR ART FOR 'LLM NAMES MATERIAL -> LOOKUP -> SIMREADY MASS/FRICTION': (a) Asset2Sim, arXiv 2605.19136 (https://arxiv.org/html/2605.19136), Sec. 4.3: 'The VLM is used to infer a material class and an effective density rho_i', mass computed analytically m = v*rho*s^3*eta, plus VLM-prior friction/damping/stiffness; validated by simulator stability, policy learning and sim-to-real correlation, not real motion. (b) UniPhysGen, arXiv 2607.13586 (https://arxiv.org/html/2607.13586): GPT-5 part-level reasoning where 'for a part assigned to a known material category ... its density, friction coefficient ... are required to fall within the corresponding material-dependent plausible intervals'; UniPhys-Bench friction MAE 0.062, density ALDE 0.438, material acc 77.92%, labels = pipeline annotations corrected by humans, no real measurement; intervals have no cited source. (c) Rigyd commercial SimReady pipeline (https://simready.artlabs.ai/resources/automatically-estimating-physics-properties-for-simulation-assets): mass 'estimated from volume and a material assumption', friction 'assigned from material class', OpenUSD/MJCF export, no uncertainty/provenance. (d) NeRF2Physics, arXiv 2404.04242: GPT-3.5 returns {material name: value} dictionaries, fused by CLIP. So 'name the material, look up the number' is already the standard construction; what none of them has is measured rows, repeat-trial uncertainty or real-motion validation.

PRIOR ART FOR MEASURED FRICTION TABLES FROM REAL SLIDES WITH UNCERTAINTY: GAUGE, arXiv 2608.05948 (https://arxiv.org/html/2608.05948): inclined-plane mu = (g sin th - vdot)/(g cos th), air-bearing-rail restitution, wood/plastic/metal + 6 textiles, baseline table gives 'standard deviation across trials', values 'entered directly into each engine's friction parameter' for Isaac/Genesis/Newton; one material per task family (e.g. wood-on-wood mu 0.39, e 0.37); no assignment step, no held-out objects (confirmed). WorldBench, arXiv 2601.21282 (https://arxiv.org/html/2601.21282): 103 real ramp videos of a steel block on wood/rubber/80-grit/3000-grit/plastic with ground-truth mu by the same quadratic-fit law, used to score video models (Cosmos, Wan 2.2, Hunyuan, CogVideoX). PhyPush, arXiv 2605.26284 (https://arxiv.org/html/2605.26284): ground-truth mu_gt = tan th - 2d/(g t^2 cos th) from inclined-plane camera timing, 47 object-surface configurations on 3 surfaces including novel objects (tin can, plastic container), zero-shot real transfer, Isaac Lab; no table, no motion-trajectory validation. PhysVid, arXiv 2510.02311: spring-dynamometer mu for 5 objects x 6 surfaces (test 2 objects x 3 surfaces, disjoint), explicitly per-PAIR, oracle CV estimator corr 0.83 vs DynamiCrafter 0.25, V-JEPA-2 0.21. IRIS, arXiv 2603.16432: 240 real 4K/60fps videos with independently measured parameters and uncertainty for inverse-identification. Net: measured mu tables with per-trial SD already exist (GAUGE, 2604.24188, WorldBench, PhysVid, NeRF2Physics' iOLab set); the 'ledger' is a larger instance, not a new object.

HELD-OUT-OBJECT VALIDATION ON PHYSICS 101 ALREADY EXISTS IN THE ORIGINAL PAPER (proposal's characterisation 'no transfer test' is unfair): Physics 101 (Wu et al., BMVC 2016, http://phys101.csail.mit.edu/papers/phys101_bmvc.pdf, Sec. 5.1-5.3) defines a 'Split by object' protocol ('requires the model to generalize to objects that it has never seen before'), reports held-out-object correlations for mass 0.26 / density 0.33 (joint training; oracle 0.67/0.65), outcome prediction on held-out objects (moving distance 0.33, bounce height 0.23, float 84%), a cross-SCENARIO transfer test (train on all but fall, predict bounce height: 0.16 on held-out objects) and an AMT human comparison (Table 2b). What it lacks is exactly the proposal's narrow form: trajectory-mm scoring of ASSIGNED parameters through a simulator, and surface transfer. Galileo (NeurIPS 2015) likewise fits mass/friction from ramp videos and does outcome prediction vs humans (abstract only; medium confidence on details).

LIBRARY CHARACTERISATIONS CHECKED: UrbanVerse, arXiv 2510.15018v2 App. C.4 -- GPT-4.1 from thumbnail + 4 snapshots; validation of H/L/W/M on 1,335 objects in 17 categories against public specs; mass MAPE 19.58% +/- 12.11; 'No friction validation is reported' (fair, confirmed). MolmoSpaces, arXiv 2602.11337 -- mass/density 'verified ... by comparing simulated values with estimates annotated via LLMs'; robot sys-id on 'cubes of known weights'; object friction assignment unspecified; validation by scene-stability/liftability tests in MuJoCo (proposal's 'policy-ranking correlation or human plausibility' is slightly off, but 'no real-motion validation of object parameters' holds). PhysX-Omni, arXiv 2605.21572 -- GPT preliminary annotations + human verification; PhysX-Bench judged by Qwen3.5-122B-A10B on rendered free-fall/water-drop videos; no measured validation (fair). PhysX-Anything, arXiv 2511.13648 -- VLM and 14-volunteer scores (fair). NeRF2Physics -- iOLab with fabric pads, 6 surfaces, 15 objects/13 scenes, friction ADE 0.155 vs GPT-4V 0.209, no motion (fair). PhysGS, arXiv 2511.18570 -- static metrics only (fair). BEHAVIOR-1K lookup source and NVIDIA SimReady spec text: could NOT be confirmed (403/404) -- low confidence on those two rows. Phys2Real, arXiv 2510.11689 (not in proposal's list): GPT-5 priors with self-reported uncertainty fused with online estimation, validated on a real robot (T-block 100% vs DR 79%), CoM only.

AUDIT-OF-SHIPPED-NUMBERS PRECEDENT (low confidence, non-peer-reviewed): 'Friction, assumed everywhere and estimated nowhere' (https://physicalai-bmi.org/education/sim-to-real/friction-assumed-everywhere, 'Institute for Physical AI at the John Bailey Institute', TR-2026-35) audits friction priors in robot configs (Unitree G1 ground friction 0.1-1.25, a 12.5x band) and calls for measured coefficients with stated variance. It audits randomisation bands, not asset-library VLM values, and scores nothing on real motion -- so the specific 'score each library's assignment rule on 359 real trials' remains undone by anyone I could find.

NOT FOUND after searching (search budget exhausted at ~24 queries; primary-source fetches used thereafter): any released benchmark that scores an assignment function f(image, mesh) -> (mu, rho) by simulated-vs-real trajectory error on held-out real objects; any paper validating a material table's cross-SURFACE transfer on object motion (2604.24188 does it on a tribometer only); any published real-motion error for UrbanVerse/MolmoSpaces/BEHAVIOR/PhysX-style VLM numbers. The survey arXiv 2604.26509 (https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26509) names 'the gap between geometric quality and physical validity' as the bottleneck and cites no benchmark validating assigned mass/friction against real measurements, which corroborates that gap.
verdicts.surviving_form: Drop the claims to novelty of (i) a measured material friction/density table with per-trial uncertainty (GAUGE, 2604.24188, WorldBench, PhysVid, NeRF2Physics already ship such tables), (ii) 'LLM names the material, a table supplies the number' (Asset2Sim 2605.19136, UniPhysGen 2607.13586, Rigyd and NeRF2Physics already do this), and (iii) 'first held-out-object validation on Physics 101' (Physics 101 itself has split-by-object and cross-scenario transfer). Re-characterise Physics 101 accordingly. What remains open and defensible, in order: (1) e1-bench as the first benchmark that scores an ASSIGNMENT pipeline f(image, mesh)->(mu, rho) by simulator-vs-real trajectory error on held-out real objects (no such release found); (2) the library audit -- the first real-motion error for the GPT-assigned numbers in UrbanVerse/MolmoSpaces/PhysX/BEHAVIOR-class libraries, reported under both the geometric-mean and PhysX combine conventions; (3) surface transfer must be reframed as a TEST of the multiplicative one-anchor rule AGAINST 2604.24188's finding that pair friction needs a learned coupled embedding with >= 2 proxies -- i.e. report whether a k=1 product rule on object slides matches their k=2 embedding, rather than asserting factorisation; if it fails, the fallback is to adopt their proxy-embedding scheme with 2 reference slides per surface, which is still the first validation of any such scheme on object motion rather than a tribometer. The 'beyond rooms' and 'first measured table' framings should be removed from the headline; the headline should be the benchmark plus the audit number.
verdicts.summary: The proposal bundles four ideas, and three of them already exist in close form. Measured per-material friction tables with trial standard deviations are in GAUGE (2608.05948), the 50-material tribometer library of 2604.24188, WorldBench's 103 real ramp videos (2601.21282) and PhysVid's dynamometer set (2510.02311); 'LLM names the material, a table or interval supplies the number' is the construction used by Asset2Sim (2605.19136, VLM material class -> effective density -> analytic mass), UniPhysGen (2607.13586, material-dependent plausible intervals, friction MAE 0.062 on human-corrected VLM labels) and the Rigyd SimReady pipeline; and the one-slide surface-anchor is a k=1 special case of 2604.24188's proxy-based friction factorisation, which finds that two proxies are needed and that pair friction cannot be inferred from independent per-material features -- a direct warning against the proposal's product rule. The proposal also mis-describes Physics 101 as having 'no transfer test': the BMVC 2016 paper has a split-by-object protocol, cross-scenario transfer (ramp -> fall) and a human comparison. The other prior-work rows (NeRF2Physics, PhysGS, UrbanVerse mass MAPE 19.58% with friction never checked, PhysX-Omni's Qwen3.5 judge, GAUGE's no-assignment/no-held-out design, PhysVid) are characterised fairly; BEHAVIOR-1K's lookup source and the SimReady spec text could not be verified. What survives is narrower but real: no released benchmark scores an assignment pipeline f(image, mesh)->(mu, rho) on held-out real trajectories through a simulator; no one has reported a real-motion error for the GPT-assigned numbers shipped by the 100k-asset libraries; and no work validates cross-surface friction transfer on object motion rather than a tribometer. Refuted as 'the material ledger is new'; survives as 'e1-bench plus a library audit, with surface transfer run as a test against 2604.24188'. Score 4/10 for this lens.

evidence: VERIFIED BY RUNNING: scripts/g0_grad_check.py on GPU 1 (warp env) reproduces the claimed tape gradient: d(slide)/d(mu_body) tape -0.5448 vs central FD -0.5453, tape forward+backward 0.4 s for 1200 steps / 386 vertices, rollout identical to MeshProbeScene. The number was not recorded anywhere in docs/ (the g0_verdict.json files are judge-pairwise results, not gradient results), so the proposal cites an unrecorded run -- but it is true.

The differentiable path uses the project's own kernels (src/sim/mesh_contact.py ground_contact_mesh + diff_collide_6dof.integrate_6dof), not Newton's solvers, so Newton 1.4 alpha / SolverVBD zero-gradient is not a dependency. g0b/g0c/g0d exist and show the pair-contact adjoint is not usable (FD -0.38 vs tape -0.03 per g0c docstring); the plan needs only plane contact, so this is consistent.

src/optimize/lm.py (88 lines) is an FD-Jacobian LM, NOT a tape-based trust-region fit: 'Uses only forward rollouts (16 per Jacobian for 8 params)'. The ~200-parameter per-session joint fit would cost ~400 rollouts x 0.4 s = ~3 min per iteration via FD, or new tape-Jacobian code. Feasible either way, but the 'tape makes LM possible' framing is wrong: the tape saves minutes, not a capability.

e1_heldout.json: oracle 1.77 mm, material 2.55 mm (ratio 1.44x on the SAME surface), pipeline 2.72 mm, global 4.40 mm, LLM direct 7.53 mm; outcome acc material 94.4%, LLM material naming 80.2%; mass build-aware within-25% 69.3% vs LLM 45.5%. All numbers in the proposal check out.

p5_transfer.json rule_test ratios (board->table): cardboard 0.83 (n=92), p_block 0.96 (54), w_block 0.88 (43), w_pole 0.85 (19), m_pole 0.75 (15), dough 1.05 (14), porcelain 1.01 (12), p_toy 0.93 (12); outliers p_ring 0.31, p_doll 1.36, h_wood 1.89 (n=3). Spread 0.75-1.05 is sd(log) ~0.11 across block-like materials -- the factorisation residual the kill test asks for is already measurable and already marginal relative to a 2x trial-IQR bound.

scripts/p2_ramp_all.py hard-codes SCALE = 1661.0 px/m (line 34) and reads the ramp angle from the filename ('/20_' -> 20 deg, else 10 deg, line 58). Phone capture needs per-clip scale from the object's edge and the angle from an inclinometer: a small but real code change before day 14.

src/track/cotracker.py loads the whole clip as a float tensor on GPU (`torch.from_numpy(frames)...float().to(device)`). A 2 s 240 fps 1080p clip = 480 x 3 x 1080 x 1920 x 4 B = ~12 GB -- near the limit of a shared A6000 slice and well past it for longer clips; must downscale or window. Nothing in the first experiment needs 240 fps (Physics 101 sliding at 30 fps gave 2.6 mm; 240 fps is only for restitution, which the plan defers to an unnamed 'Proposal 2').

Physics 101 ships no licence: readme.txt in data/phys101/phys101_v1.0.zip and the project site state no terms (WebFetch of phys101.csail.mit.edu: 'no explicit license, terms of use, redistribution conditions'). Releasing 'e1-bench' with the clips redistributed depends on permission that has not been obtained; releasing tracks + a download script does not.

UrbanVerse-100K (arXiv 2510.15018, ICLR 2026): attributes annotated by GPT-4.1 from a thumbnail + 4 yaw snapshots; the paper only says 'we will release the full UrbanVerse-100K' and gives no URL, and reports no validation of mass/friction against measurements. The audit of its SHIPPED numbers depends on a release not confirmed available today; replicating the prompt is possible only if the prompt is published. MolmoSpaces availability could not be checked (search budget exhausted). BEHAVIOR-1K's lookup and SimReady defaults are public.

THE BRIDGE PROBLEM (hidden dependency the proposal does not state): every ledger row is mu_pair against the Physics 101 board at MIT. The user has no Physics 101 object and no Physics 101 board. The first experiment's 'one reference cardboard cube' anchors a new surface to a row that was measured on a DIFFERENT cardboard: p1 already found mu falls 0.28 -> 0.21 across Physics 101's own nine cardboard cubes (Spearman -0.80, unexplained). An anchored-prediction failure on day 14 cannot be attributed to 'friction does not factorise' versus 'our cardboard is not their cardboard'. The 25-material ledger (15 P101 + 10 phone) is therefore two tables with no measured link, unless overlap materials are used to test the link.

Kill-test power: a paired sign test over 8 objects reaches p < 0.05 two-sided only at 8/8 (p = 0.0078; 7/8 gives 0.07). At e1's own win rate for material-vs-global (52/70 = 74%), P(>=7/8) ~ 0.34 and P(8/8) ~ 0.09, so the test as written would kill a true effect of the size already measured roughly two times in three. The project's own rule ('a published effect size is part of the calibration') is violated by the design.

Angle sensitivity: the project measured 1 deg of ramp angle = 0.02 in mu, and e1's material-vs-oracle gap is dmu 0.0175 vs 0.0103. A phone inclinometer's +-0.5-1 deg is the same size as the effect being tested; the anchor cube absorbs a common per-session bias only multiplicatively while an angle error enters mu additively, so it cancels only approximately.

Budget: CoTracker ~1 min/clip x 170 clips (first experiment) to ~500 (90 days) = 3-8 GPU-hours; Newton sweeps < 1 s/clip; no Blender renders anywhere in the plan; LLM calls ~$100-200 via the existing Letsur gateway (scripts/e1_heldout.py do_classify). Within 2 shared A6000s with large margin.

src/simready/usd_physics.py (97 lines) writes UsdPhysics MaterialAPI dynamic/static friction + restitution with provenance attributes; static friction is currently a hard-coded 1.2x dynamic (line 30), while the simulator has NO static friction -- the export invents a number the ledger never measured. Must be tagged 'default', which the provenance schema supports.
verdicts.surviving_form: The first experiment can run in two weeks and the 90-day plan is affordable, but only after three design changes. (1) Replace the single-cube anchor with a self-contained ledger: measure the user's own 8 objects (4 materials x 2) on the user's OWN reference board first, then on the 2 new surfaces; test factorisation within the user's data (residual sd of log mu_pair - a_object - b_surface over 8 x 3 cells vs trial IQR), and test the link to Physics 101 separately as an invariant -- the 4 overlapping materials' ratios (user board / P101 board) must agree within the trial IQR before any P101 row is used on a user surface. If they do not agree, the ledger is two tables and the 'extend by phone' milestone shrinks to the user's own rows. (2) Fix the kill-test statistic: pair over object x surface cells (16) or raise objects to >=16, and pre-register the e1 effect size (1.7x over the global median) so the test has >=80% power; keep the factorisation-residual bound. (3) Drop 240 fps for sliding (60 fps, downscaled frames; cotracker.py must window or downscale before 240 fps clips are tractable) and keep 240 fps only for a separately gated drop test; tag restitution 'unmeasured' in v1. Code work before day 14: per-clip scale and inclinometer angle in p2 (currently hard-coded 1661 px/m and filename angle), frame downscaling in cotracker.py, and static-friction provenance in usd_physics.py. For the audit, state now that the UrbanVerse-100K and MolmoSpaces rows depend on metadata not yet confirmed released; run BEHAVIOR-1K's lookup, SimReady defaults and PhysXNet's published pipeline first (all public), and treat the city-scale library as optional. Release e1-bench as tracks + fit code + a download script, not redistributed clips, until Physics 101's authors grant terms. The differentiable-physics role should be stated as 'saves minutes and gives per-trial sigma', since lm.py is FD-based and the plane-contact tape is the only usable gradient.
verdicts.summary: Not refuted, but weaker than written. Everything the first experiment leans on in-repo exists and was re-run or read: the plane-contact tape gradient reproduces exactly (-0.5448 vs FD -0.5453, 0.4 s), e1/p5 numbers match the proposal, CoTracker and the ramp-fit pipeline are in place, and the GPU/LLM budget is trivially within 2 A6000s with no renders needed. Two hidden dependencies the proposal does not name are real: (a) the ledger's rows are pair frictions against MIT's board and the user owns no Physics 101 object, so the 'one reference cardboard cube' cannot link a new surface to the ledger without assuming their cardboard equals ours -- which p1's own 0.28->0.21 size dependence already contradicts; and (b) the audit's city-scale target (UrbanVerse-100K) has only a 'we will release' statement with no URL, and MolmoSpaces could not be verified. Smaller feasibility defects: the kill test's 8-object sign test needs 8/8 to reach p<0.05 and would kill a true e1-sized effect ~2/3 of the time; p2 hard-codes the camera scale and takes the angle from filenames; cotracker.py puts whole clips on the GPU as float (12 GB for a 2 s 240 fps 1080p clip); lm.py is FD-based, so the 'tape enables LM' claim overstates the gradient's role; usd_physics.py invents static friction at 1.2x dynamic; Physics 101 carries no licence, so e1-bench cannot redistribute clips. With a self-contained user-board ledger, an overlap-material bridge test, a properly powered kill test and public-library audit targets first, the 14-day experiment and a narrowed 90-day milestone are achievable by one researcher.

verdicts.lens: Impact and practicality: who consumes the output, is the effect size actionable, does it answer the user's ask (differentiable physics, robots/simulation, scale)
evidence: docs/results/e1_heldout.json, friction: oracle 1.77 mm, material 2.55 mm, pipeline 2.72 mm, dataset-wide median 4.40 mm, LLM-direct 7.53 mm, generic 0.40 86.9 mm (median trajectory RMS, 20 deg ramp, one board). The headline '3x worse' is LLM-direct vs material; against the FREE baseline (dataset-wide median) the ledger buys 4.4 -> 2.6 mm on a ~1 s slide. Outcome accuracy: material 94.4%, pipeline 92.4%, LLM-direct 84.7%, dataset median 80.3% (n = 198). The actionable effect is ~14 points of stays-vs-slides accuracy at the slip threshold, not millimetres.

Same-surface ratio material/oracle is already 2.55/1.77 = 1.44x. The proposal promises <= 1.5x AFTER adding a surface-anchor step with its own error; the 1.5x headline is nearly spent before surface transfer begins. The kill test is wisely written against the dataset-wide median instead, which is a much weaker bar.

docs/results/p5_transfer.json: factorisation ratios 0.75-1.05 for block-like materials, but 0.31 (ring), 1.36 (doll), 1.89 (hollow wood, n=3). The one-slide anchor is a procedure only for block-like, dry, clean objects; everything a sim-ready library actually ships (toys, tools, furniture) is where the ratio broke.

Consumer mismatch: the one-slide surface protocol requires a PHYSICAL slide on the target surface. A user of UrbanVerse/MolmoSpaces/Genie/Isaac SimReady worlds has no physical surface to slide a cube on; only lab digital twins can run the anchor. So 'beyond rooms is satisfied because a cardboard row is the same on a sidewalk' only holds for surfaces someone measured, i.e. O(surfaces) real captures by this one researcher (4-6 planned).

src/simready/usd_physics.py and scripts/write_full_simready.py exist (USD export with provenance) -- the export is real. But PhysX ships combine modes (multiply/average/min/max) and its own material presets; a 25-material table with provenance competes with engineering friction tables that already carry ranges. The product differentiator is 'effective, build-aware, measured from motion', which matters only to the ~zero users who currently check their friction numbers at all.

Differentiable physics role is self-described as 'Little': Laplace sigma from tape curvature and an LM nuisance fit over ~200 parameters, both explicitly replaceable by sweeps + bootstrap ('would survive on sweeps'). The user asked to USE a differentiable engine; this uses it as an optional accelerator.

Robot claim: proposal itself cites SIMPLER <= 15% sensitivity and 2606.20712 'no stable adaptation signal'; no robot, no policy experiment. The practical value is 'correct contact outcomes where they matter' with no experiment showing where they matter. A top-venue reviewer's 'so what' is unanswered by design.

Domain-randomisation users: the proposal offers measured IQRs (within-cube 0.01-0.03) in place of bands like 0.3-1.5. DR bands are wide on purpose, for robustness to unmodelled effects; a tighter measured band is not obviously wanted, and the proposal gives no evidence that any DR user has asked for it.

Benchmark scope: e1-bench is 101 objects, one board, one 20 deg ramp, 30 fps 2016 footage. PhysVid (dynamometer pairs) and GAUGE (180 Hz mocap, three engines) already offer measured ground truth with better instrumentation; a D&B reviewer will ask why a 2016 dataset at one angle is the benchmark. The restitution column depends on another proposal's kill test passing.

Audit feasibility: UrbanVerse / MolmoSpaces assignment rules are to be 'replicated from the published prompt' where metadata is not public; model versions (GPT-4.1, GPT-4o) and prompt details drift, so each library can dismiss the audit as a replication mismatch -- the proposal already concedes the PhysX-convention mapping is contestable, which is a second dismissal route.
verdicts.surviving_form: Drop the ledger-as-product and the 'any surface via one slide' claim from the headline; keep the surface-transfer experiment as a 14-day kill test only. Re-centre on the audit + benchmark as an evaluation paper (D&B track or a sim-to-real workshop): 'the physics numbers shipped by sim-ready libraries, scored on real motion'. State the effect in the unit a consumer acts on -- stays/slides/topples outcome accuracy (94% vs 85% vs 80%), not mm -- and extend the benchmark beyond one ramp board (add the 240 fps phone drops/topples and at least two surfaces) so it is not a single-angle test on 2016 footage. Add one downstream consumer demonstration that costs no robot: an Isaac Lab / ManiSkill task (object on tilted tray, push-to-target) where the library's shipped friction flips the simulated outcome and the measured row does not; without that the robot/sim-user claim is empty. Run the audit under BOTH the library's exact released metadata (downloaded, never replicated) and PhysX's own combine convention, and only audit libraries whose metadata is public. Keep the differentiable engine only where it changes a number (joint ramp-angle + per-trial nuisance fit on the 643 clips, reported against the nominal 20 deg) and say the headline does not depend on it. Tell the user plainly that this answers 'practical and validated' and rejects 'differentiable' and 'beyond rooms' -- it is a reframing, not an answer to the ask.
verdicts.summary: Honest and falsifiable, but refuted on impact as proposed. The validated core (material lookup beats LLM numbers 3x on real slides) is a 2.6 vs 4.4 mm gain over a free dataset-median baseline, equivalently ~14 points of stays/slides accuracy at the slip threshold, on one board at one angle; the same-surface material/oracle ratio is already 1.44x, so the 1.5x surface-transfer headline is nearly exhausted before the anchor step adds its own error, and the anchor requires a physical slide that users of generated or city-scale worlds cannot perform. Nobody identified consumes the ledger today: sim users do not check friction numbers, DR users want wide bands, and the robot payoff is admitted to be unproven and task-dependent with no experiment planned. Differentiable physics is self-described as 'Little' and replaceable; scale is explicitly rejected. It answers 'validated and practical', not the user's ask. The audit and benchmark wedge is the part a venue might take, narrowed to outcome accuracy, public metadata only, more than one surface and event type, and one concrete sim task where the shipped numbers flip an outcome.

proposals.title: A phone is a physics instrument: per-clip differentiable identification of friction, restitution and centre of mass from uninstrumented 240 fps video, and the first multi-material restitution table
proposals.thesis: A differentiable exact-mesh contact simulator that already reproduces real slides to under 1 mm and whose object-on-surface gradients match finite differences can turn one uninstrumented 240 fps phone clip of an everyday object dropped, slid or tipped on a known surface into a Laplace posterior over (friction, restitution alpha, centre-of-mass offset) with a per-clip Fisher matrix stating what the clip can and cannot identify, with no robot, depth camera, markers or mocap. We claim restitution is recoverable from phone drops to within the trial-to-trial spread and confirmed by two independent readouts, which yields the first multi-material restitution table from video and calibrates the simulator's contact law against real impacts, a quantity that no sim-ready pipeline annotates and no public dataset holds beyond three materials.
proposals.what_we_build: (1) phonephys: a capture protocol (side view, inclinometer angle, the object's own edge as scale, 240 fps in daylight) and a tracker-to-parameter fitter: CoTracker3 tracks -> camera scale and free-fall check -> DiffMeshScene (g0) rollout of the object's own mesh on the surface -> Levenberg-Marquardt on log theta with tape gradients where they pass a finite-difference check and FD Jacobians where they do not -> Laplace covariance and Fisher matrix per clip. Parameters per clip: mu_pair, alpha and a velocity exponent p in e = 1 - alpha v^p, CoM offset, initial pose and velocity; per session: camera scale and surface stiffness. (2) Invariant gates per material, never reference values: repeat-trial IQR, velocity route against height route (p3's design, now at the frame rate it needed), drop-height independence of alpha, mass independence (two sizes of one material), two-angle agreement for mu, and a held-out-trial-type test (fit on drops, predict the post-bounce slide; fit on slides, predict stay/slide at a second angle). (3) The table: about 30 materials x 3 surfaces (reference board, laminate, concrete paver) with mu, alpha, e at 1 m/s and CoM-offset checks, with uncertainty, exported through usd_physics.py and as DR ranges. (4) A contact-model card for Newton/Warp penalty contact: how far the stock Hunt-Crossley velocity dependence sits from real impacts across speeds and masses, and what a two-parameter calibration fixes on held-out heights, scored by trajectory error normalised by trial spread as GAUGE scores engines.
proposals.builds_on_our_assets: scripts/g0_grad_check.py::DiffMeshScene (tape-safe MeshProbeScene; d(slide)/d(mu) -0.5448 against FD -0.5453) with src/sim/diff_collide_6dof.integrate_6dof and src/sim/mesh_contact.ground_contact_mesh (exact vertex-plane contact on a tilted plane via gn/gt/gp); src/sim/rigs.py (TILT_RIG and BOUNCE_RIG, validated jointly), MeshProbeScene.set_restitution_alpha and scripts/p7_cd_restitution.py / p8_alpha.py (e spans 0.97-0.04, mass-independent under alpha, e ~ 1 - alpha v, 0.54 at 2 m/s against 0.70 at 1 m/s); scripts/p3_restitution.py (the two-route design and the g-from-parabola scale check, which failed only for lack of frame rate: g spread 2.7x, routes correlated 0.38 at 30 fps); src/track/cotracker.py and src/track/balls.py; scripts/p1/p2/p4 (ramp pipeline, Newton fit to real slides, release-aligned fitting); scripts/p9_pot_topple.py (CoM via time-to-topple read at 2 ms, 0.61 mm held-out on the simulator; rule-1 matrix 2.19x with offset, 1.00x with mass, 1.02x with alpha); src/optimize/lm.py (trust-region LM on log theta with projected iterate and adaptive damping); scripts/o7_sensitivity.py as the manual precedent the Fisher matrix replaces; src/simready/usd_physics.py for export. Deliberately not reused: multi-body contact gradients (g0b/g0c: not usable), the renderer-in-the-loop (V2) and every video-model signal.
proposals.differentiable_physics_role: Central, with named limits. Gradients buy (a) multi-parameter inversion per clip: a drop-and-settle clip depends on alpha, the velocity exponent, surface stiffness, mu for the post-bounce slide and spin, CoM offset through the post-impact tumble, and the initial pose and velocity, 6-10 parameters where sweeps are infeasible and tape-plus-LM is natural; (b) identifiability as a number: J^T J from the tape is the Fisher matrix per clip, turning rule 1 from a manual sweep per probe (o7) into a reported quantity with covariances, so an unidentifiable combination (alpha against stiffness, mass against anything in a drop) is reported rather than fitted; (c) joint fits with shared parameters across hundreds of clips (per-material alpha, per-session scale, per-surface stiffness). They do not buy batching at our scale (a tape rollout is 0.4 s per 1200-step clip; hundreds of clips is a loop), and they are at risk exactly where DiffMJX and Ostrich were written: gradients through stiff penalty impacts. g0 verified mu through plane contact; damping through plane contact has not been FD-checked, and g0d found brief body-body collision gradients right only to within 1-2x. So the day-1 task is d(apex)/d(alpha) at the BOUNCE_RIG setting against central finite differences; any parameter whose tape gradient misses by more than 20% is fitted with FD Jacobians (as this project already did for VBD cloth) and the paper says which.
proposals.scale_claim: The right scale is objects per hour and materials covered, not rooms. One person with a phone and a tilt board can capture about 30 objects a day (drop at 3 heights, slide at 2 angles, tip; 5 trials each, about 45 clips per object-surface), so the 90-day target is 30 materials x 3 surfaces, roughly 2,500 clips: 10x the materials of GAUGE's rigid set and 30x Bounce-and-Learn's one ball, at about 50 GPU-hours in total. 'Beyond rooms' means the surfaces outdoors: the same instrument on a concrete paver and an asphalt tile yields the mu and e rows that street-scale simulators (UrbanVerse, URBAN-SIM, Vid2Sim) currently fill by VLM or per-texture label and that nobody has measured. The scene-scale framing is wrong for this proposal because the physics layer of a city-scale world is the same ~30 rows; measuring them is cheap, and nobody who owns a city pipeline does it.
proposals.practicality: Anyone building a digital twin without a robot uses the protocol and fitter to measure their own objects (TwinAligner, PIN-WM, ASID, One-Shot and D-REX all require a robot push, hand or F/T sensor; EKFPhys needs RGB-D plus mocap for truth). Simulator users get a contact-model card: whether stock penalty contact reproduces measured restitution across speeds and masses, and what calibration fixes it, in the task family where GAUGE found Newton's bouncing ball at a normalised RMSE of 22.7 (the best engine still 15.6x the real trial-to-trial spread). Asset pipelines get the restitution column no library annotates (PhysXNet, PhysXVerse, UniPhys-40K, ManiTwin all omit it), and DR users get measured e ranges instead of the guessed 0-0.1 band. The Fisher matrix per clip is itself practical: it tells a user which extra clip to shoot to pin a parameter the current one cannot.
proposals.novelty_argument: Forecast: in 12 months NVIDIA ships Newton with better contact (hydroelastic, contact reduction) and MuJoCo Warp as a non-differentiable default; GAUGE-style benchmarks add tasks but keep measuring parameters with instruments and feeding engines, not identifying them from video; the differentiable-sysid papers (DiffMJX, Dojo, Ostrich, PIN-WM, TwinAligner) keep fitting one cube or one robot-pushed object with mocap, AprilTags, RGB-D or F/T sensing; video-foundation-model papers (PhysVid: V-JEPA-2 at Pearson 0.28 on friction, 0.47 on elasticity) keep probing latents. None will publish restitution for 30 materials from a phone, because it needs no new model and no robot and is therefore outside their incentive set. This project's wedge is its controlled negatives: video models and LLMs carry no object-specific theta, so the parameters must be measured, and the simulator-as-instrument is the measurement. New: uninstrumented single-phone identification with per-clip identifiability (the scouts found no rigid-object identification without a robot, depth or markers), restitution across many materials checked by invariants rather than instruments, and a calibration of penalty contact against real impacts. Small: for friction alone this is Galileo 2015 and our p4 with gradients, and the velocity-exponent fit is a textbook refinement. The restitution column and the Fisher-matrix reporting are the substance.
nearest_prior_work: EKFPhys (3DV 2024, 2309.15703): differentiable LCP engine inside an EKF, friction from RGB-D at 60 Hz on 4 YCB objects with mocap-tilt ground truth; needs depth and a known mesh, no restitution
One-Shot Real-to-Sim (2412.00259): mass, CoM, inertia and friction from one robot push with RGB-D and F/T sensing; 3 real objects

DiffMJX (2506.14186) and Dojo (2203.00806): contact gradients fitted to the ContactNets acrylic-cube toss (148 Hz AprilTags), geometry plus contact stiffness; mesh-mesh contact explicitly not modified
DANOs (2210.09420): soap-bar sliding friction from one real video through Dojo, 0.61 against 0.75 measured; n = 1
gradSim (ICLR 2021): pixels-to-parameters with differentiable rendering, evaluated on 10,000 synthetic videos only
GAUGE (2608.05948): restitution by air-bearing rail for wood, plastic and metal, and Newton's bouncing-ball failure; measured, not identified
Bounce and Learn (ICLR 2019): one foam ball, 5K bounces, an effective restitution per surface

PhysVid (2510.02311) and IRIS (2603.16432): measured or trajectory-fitted ground truth for scoring estimators (100 bounce clips with hand-annotated heights; 240 lab videos of textbook objects at 4K/60 fps)
PIN-WM (RSS 2025) and TwinAligner (2512.19390): differentiable or PSO identification of mass, friction and restitution from a scripted robot push with Gaussian-splat rendering
first_90_days: Days 1-7 (existing data, no capture): tooling check. DiffMeshScene + LM joint fit on the 93 real cardboard slides (mu per cube, per-trial t0/s0, per-session ramp angle); mu against p4's sweep and p1's analytic (expect |delta| <= 0.01); Laplace sigma against the empirical IQR; FD check of d(apex)/d(alpha) and d(settle)/d(mu) on a plane bounce at BOUNCE_RIG; decide tape against FD-Jacobian per parameter.

Days 3-14: the restitution pilot (the first experiment): 5 materials, 3 heights, 10 repeats on the reference board, spheres and flat-face blocks; two routes, g-scale check, alpha fitted through the simulator; kill decision at day 14.

Days 15-35: contact-law calibration: fit (alpha, p) per material across heights; invariants: alpha independent of drop height and of object mass (two sizes per material); stock against calibrated contact on held-out heights, scored by trajectory RMSE normalised by trial spread.

Days 36-60: joint per-clip posteriors on rigid asymmetric objects (mug, hammer, wrench): drop + slide + tip on a high-grip mat; Fisher matrix per clip; held-out-trial-type test (fit on drops, predict the post-bounce slide; fit on slides, predict stay/slide at 10 deg); CoM offset against the mesh's build-aware value and against a ruler-edge balance check.

Days 61-80: scale-out: 30 materials x 3 surfaces (board, laminate, concrete paver), >= 5 trials per cell; the table with uncertainty; USD export; DR-range table; the restitution column handed to Proposal 1's ledger if that is also pursued.
Days 81-90: write-up including every kill-test number either way; release the protocol, the fitter, the table and the contact-model card.
proposals.first_experiment: Restitution from phone drops, with the simulator as one of two readouts. Capture 5 materials (rubber ball, steel ball bearing, wooden ball or block, plastic block, ceramic tile) dropped from 3 heights (0.1, 0.2, 0.4 m) onto the reference board, 10 repeats each (150 clips), side view at 240 fps in daylight, a release that keeps block faces parallel (a card pulled from under the block), the object's own measured diameter or edge as scale. Track with CoTracker3 (src/track/balls.py for spheres); read e two ways as p3 designed: the velocity route (parabola fits on either side of impact, extrapolated to the table line) and the height route sqrt(h_bounce/h_drop); check the free-fall g in px/s^2 across the clips of a session; then fit alpha (and p) through DiffMeshScene with the object's mesh and compare the simulated apex to the real one. Numbers produced: per material and height, the median e and its IQR over 10 repeats; the median velocity-route minus height-route difference; the g spread; the fitted alpha per material with its Laplace sigma; and the FD-against-tape agreement of d(apex)/d(alpha) on 3 clips. Expected if it works: IQR(e) <= 0.05 for spheres, routes within 0.03, g within +/-5%, e spanning >= 0.3 between rubber and ceramic.
proposals.kill_test: Decided now. Restitution from phone video is dead if, over 10 repeated drops of the same object from the same height, the IQR of e exceeds 0.10, or the velocity and height routes disagree by more than 0.05 in median, or the free-fall g spreads more than +/-10% within a session (camera geometry uncontrolled; fix before any fit); and the multi-material table is pointless if e spans less than 0.15 across the five pilot materials. The differentiable claim narrows if the tape gradient d(apex)/d(alpha) at the BOUNCE_RIG setting disagrees with central finite differences by more than 20% and cannot be brought within that by substep or integrator changes inside two weeks: alpha is then fitted by FD Jacobians, the paper says so, and 'differentiable' applies to the slide and tip parameters only. If both the measurement and the gradient fail, the proposal is dead and the project keeps the sweep-based instrument it already has.
proposals.resources: One shared A6000 in bursts (CoTracker3 about 1 min per 240 fps clip, tape fits under 1 s per clip, FD Jacobians about 10 s per clip; the full 2,500-clip table is about 50 GPU-hours); a phone with 240 fps and an inclinometer app, two boards, a rubber mat for tips, a concrete paver, 30-40 everyday objects of known materials, a kitchen scale and callipers for the invariants (mass and size used as checks, never as fitted values); one day of capture per 10 objects; no robot, no rig; warp env for simulation, cosmos env for tracking, as now.
proposals.biggest_risk: Gradients through stiff impact: the tape through penalty contact may be biased or explode exactly where restitution lives (g0d: brief body-body collisions right only to 1-2x; damping through plane contact unchecked), which would reduce the proposal to a sweep/FD instrument, still useful but without the per-clip Fisher story. Second: the real restitution of hand-dropped blocks is dominated by impact geometry (edge and corner hits), so e is only clean for spheres and flat drops, and the simulator route must carry the tumble from a fitted initial orientation, the hardest fit in the plan. Third: e may be an object-surface pair property as much as friction is, so the table needs the same factorisation test and may end up surface-specific. Fourth: Newton/Warp alpha churn can break the tape path between versions; pin versions and keep the FD fallback.
proposals.expected_headline_result: From single uninstrumented 240 fps phone clips, a differentiable exact-mesh contact simulator recovers friction, restitution and centre of mass of everyday objects with a per-clip Fisher-information statement of identifiability; restitution is repeatable to +/-0.03 across 10 trials and agrees between two independent readouts, yielding the first 30-material restitution table from video, which shows where stock penalty contact departs from real impacts across speeds and corrects it on held-out drop heights, with no robot, depth camera or markers.

evidence: SMASH (Monszpart et al., SIGGRAPH Asia 2016, arXiv:1603.08984): lifts 2D tracks from consumer video to physically valid 3D collisions and recovers 'collision parameters (e.g., object mass ratio, coefficient of restitution)'; search snippet of the PDF states real sequences were captured at 1280x720, 120 or 240 fps on an iPhone 6 (fps detail medium confidence: PDF text could not be re-extracted locally). This is 'a phone is a physics instrument for restitution' ten years earlier, without markers or depth.

Vid2Param (Asenov et al., RA-L 2020, arXiv:1907.06422): estimates restitution and drag from real videos of rubber, tennis and ping-pong balls with a probabilistic (VAE) estimator trained in simulation; validated only by forward-prediction accuracy because 'the exact physical properties of the balls are not available'. Not cited by the proposal.

Delta-ynamics (arXiv:2605.20576, HTML v1): 235 real rigid-body videos, 155 of them shot on an iPhone 13 at 210-240 fps of everyday boxes, balls, cylinders and irregular objects on floors, tracks and courts; infers mass/inertia, sliding and rolling friction, damping, initial state and camera for a physics simulator. Evaluated by IoU / flow EPE, no measured truth, no restitution. Uninstrumented 240 fps phone-to-simulator rigid identification therefore already exists; not cited.

PhysVid (arXiv:2510.02311, HTML v1): real elasticity split of 100 bounce videos over 'a wide range of materials (rubber balls, tennis balls, basketballs, balloons...)' with effective restitution from fronto-parallel image heights; real friction split of 5 objects x 6 surfaces with spring-dynamometer truth; a classical-CV oracle reaches Pearson 0.87 (elasticity) and 0.83 (friction) on real data vs V-JEPA-2 0.47 / 0.28. Contradicts the proposal's claim that no public dataset holds restitution beyond three materials (it holds effective e for many ball types, though YouTube-sourced, without material/surface labels, heights or velocity dependence).
Bounce and Learn (ICLR 2019, arXiv:1904.06827): 5,172 RGB-D bounce videos, effective restitution and collision normal per surface, one foam probe ball. Correctly characterised by the proposal.

GAUGE (arXiv:2608.05948, HTML): restitution by inclined air-bearing rail e = v_out/v_in for wood (0.22-0.33), plastic (0.36-0.38), metal (0.23-0.33); friction by incline; +/-1 sigma across repeated trials; restitution treated as a constant (no velocity dependence); engine parameters 'set from the GAUGE calibrations', not identified; Newton bouncing ball normalised RMSE 22.71 vs Isaac Sim 15.63. Proposal's characterisation is accurate.

IRIS (arXiv:2603.16432, HTML v1): 240 videos at 3840x2160 / 60 fps across eight lab systems; friction and damping 'derived from trajectory fits (Levenberg-Marquardt)', per-setting sigma over 10 trials (sigma_mu < 0.02); no restitution, no simulator-side identification. Proposal's characterisation is accurate.

EKFPhys (3DV 2024, arXiv:2309.15703, HTML): RealSense D455 at 60 Hz, mocap at 240 Hz, 4 YCB objects x 5 sequences, tilt-table friction truth 0.110-0.280, EKF covariance over friction reported in supplement, no restitution. Proposal's characterisation is accurate.

Exciting Contact Modes (arXiv:2411.10935, HTML v2): contact-aware Fisher information I ~ sum xi xi^T with xi = grad_theta log p(y|...) from a differentiable simulator, used for experiment design over inertial/kinematic/mass-geometry parameters; simulation only, force/accelerometer sensing. Shows the 'tape J^T J as identifiability' idea is established; the proposal's per-clip use on video is an application, not a new tool.

Heiden et al., Probabilistic Inference of Simulation Parameters via Parallel Differentiable Simulation (ICRA 2022, arXiv:2109.08815): full posteriors over simulation parameters (SVGD) with a differentiable simulator on a real 7-DOF arm experiment; posterior-with-uncertainty from differentiable sim on real data predates the proposal's Laplace covariance.

DANOs (arXiv:2210.09420): one real soap-bar video, friction through Dojo; One-Shot Real-to-Sim (arXiv:2412.00259): visual + tactile from one robot action; MOSIV (ICLR 2026, arXiv:2603.06022, HTML v1): synthetic only, 11 views, MPM, no uncertainty; MonoPhysics (arXiv:2605.30320): deformable Young's modulus from monocular video via differentiable sim + 3DGS. None covers rigid restitution/CoM from phone video with measured validation, so the proposal's prior-work list is fairly characterised but incomplete (missing SMASH, Vid2Param, Delta-ynamics, PhysVid's friction split).

Physics-education literature (e.g., phyphox marble study, 2024, jpf.jurnal.unej.ac.id article 52694; the Vigo videometric CoR paper; AAPT 2013 high-speed phone video): restitution of several materials (five marble densities, e = 0.42-0.89) measured from phone video/sound; small-n and pedagogical, but establishes that phone-video restitution tables per se are routine (medium confidence: numbers taken from search snippets, not primary text).

Search budget was exhausted before the classical Hunt-Crossley-vs-drop-test calibration literature (Flores, Stronge et al.) could be checked; that body of work is well known and almost certainly already compares velocity-dependent restitution laws to measured impacts, so the 'contact-model card' component is low-novelty at the physics level and engine-specific at the software level (low confidence, uncited).
verdicts.surviving_form: Drop the headline claims 'a phone is a physics instrument' and 'first multi-material restitution table from video' (SMASH 2016, Vid2Param, Delta-ynamics and the physics-education literature already extract restitution/friction from uninstrumented phone video; PhysVid already publishes effective restitution over many ball materials). Narrow to what no prior work does: (1) a restitution table that is MATERIAL x SURFACE x IMPACT-VELOCITY, with e(v) fitted as 1 - alpha v^p and the Hunt-Crossley form tested, validated by invariants (repeat IQR, two independent readouts, drop-height and mass independence, surface factorisation) rather than by annotated heights or a VLM; (2) the held-out-trial-TYPE test (fit on drops, predict the real post-bounce slide and stay/slide at a second angle; fit on slides, predict drops) on real footage, which none of SMASH, Vid2Param, Delta-ynamics, PhysVid, EKFPhys or GAUGE perform; (3) per-clip Fisher/Laplace identifiability reported on single uninstrumented clips and used prescriptively ('which clip to shoot next'), presented as an application of 2411.10935-style contact-aware Fisher information, not as new; (4) the engine card restricted to Newton/Warp penalty contact scored by trajectory error normalised by trial spread, positioned as extending GAUGE's bouncing-ball row (Newton 22.71) with identified rather than prescribed parameters. Cite SMASH, Vid2Param, Delta-ynamics and PhysVid's friction split in nearest prior work and correct the 'no public dataset beyond three materials' sentence to 'no dataset with measured, surface- and velocity-resolved restitution validated on held-out motion'.
verdicts.summary: The core idea -- recover restitution, friction and initial state of rigid everyday objects from uninstrumented consumer phone video by fitting a physics simulator -- is not new: SMASH (2016) recovered restitution and mass ratio from iPhone 120/240 fps collision video, Vid2Param (2019/20) estimated restitution of rubber/tennis/ping-pong balls from real video with a probabilistic sim-trained estimator, and Delta-ynamics (2026) infers mass, friction and damping from 235 real iPhone-13 clips at 210-240 fps of everyday objects. The claim that no public dataset holds restitution beyond three materials is contradicted by PhysVid (100 real bounce videos over many ball materials with annotated effective e, oracle Pearson 0.87) and Bounce and Learn (5K bounces, per-surface effective e). The Fisher-matrix-from-tape identifiability story is an application of contact-aware Fisher information already published for differentiable simulators (2411.10935) and of posterior inference over sim parameters (2109.08815); the contact-model-card component is engine-specific and sits on a large classical drop-test calibration literature I could not re-check (search budget exhausted). The proposal characterises EKFPhys, GAUGE, IRIS, DANOs, One-Shot and Bounce-and-Learn accurately but omits SMASH, Vid2Param and Delta-ynamics. What genuinely survives is measurement rigour rather than a new capability: a material x surface x velocity restitution table validated by invariants and by held-out-trial-type prediction of real motion (fit drops, predict slides), plus per-clip identifiability used prescriptively. That is a legitimate but modest contribution, hence refuted as stated and scored 4/10.

evidence: RAN the proposal's own day-1 kill check instead of assuming it (scratchpad apex_grad.py, GPU 1, ~2 min): 7 cm solid cube dropped flat 0.20 m onto the plane at BOUNCE_RIG (pen_frac 5e-3, 1440 Hz, 720 steps), loss = z at t = 0.5 s after a rebound apex of 12.6 / 8.4 / 5.2 cm. d z/d alpha: tape -0.5867 vs central FD -0.5879 (ratio 0.998) at alpha 0.2; +0.1057 vs +0.1055 (1.002) at 0.4; +0.0237 vs +0.0225 (1.053) at 0.8. Tape-variant rollout identical to MeshProbeScene (5.19/4.29/3.05 cm both ways). 0.2-0.3 s forward+backward per clip. The 'biggest risk' (damping gradient through impact unchecked) is retired for one object on a plane; the 20% kill threshold is passed by 20x.

Mass null under alpha holds exactly in the same run: z(T) = 4.291 cm at 0.0318 kg and 4.291 cm at 0.127 kg, confirming p8_alpha.json (e identical for 0.1 and 0.4 kg at every alpha) -- restitution can be fitted without knowing mass, which the uninstrumented protocol requires.

Existing pieces verified on disk: scripts/g0_grad_check.py::DiffMeshScene (CLAUDE.md records d(slide)/d(mu) -0.5448 vs FD -0.5453, 1200 steps, 386 verts); src/sim/mesh_scene.py::set_restitution_alpha (cd = 1.5 alpha k / HC); src/sim/rigs.py BOUNCE_RIG/TILT_RIG; scripts/p3_restitution.py already implements the two routes (velocity parabola extrapolation + sqrt(h_b/h_d)) and the g-in-px/s^2 scale check; src/optimize/lm.py (FD-Jacobian LM, trust region); src/track/cotracker.py. Warp 1.15.0 / Newton 1.4.0 import; DiffMeshScene uses raw Warp kernels, not Newton solvers, so Newton alpha churn is off the critical path.

Hidden dependency 1 -- the velocity exponent p is NOT in the simulator: src/sim/mesh_contact.py line 101/153 is fn = max(k w pen - HC cd w pen vn, 0), i.e. e ~ 1 - alpha v with p fixed at 1 (p8: e 0.70 at 1 m/s -> 0.54 at 2 m/s for alpha 0.4). Fitting (alpha, p) across heights 0.1-0.4 m (v 1.4-2.8 m/s) needs a modified kernel plus rule-5 revalidation of the e(alpha, v) curve. Small change, but it is on the days-15-35 critical path and is not scheduled.

Hidden dependency 2 -- meshes of real asymmetric objects. Days 36-60 run DiffMeshScene on 'the object's own mesh' for a mug, hammer and wrench, but the project has no scanner and no capture rig; only calliper-constructible shapes (spheres, blocks, cylinders) have meshes today. Phone photogrammetry is obtainable but adds a step and ~1-2 mm base-edge error that feeds the topple leverage b/h directly (p9 read CoM to 0.61 mm on the simulator; o11 showed geometric topple estimates can be far off for irregular shapes).

Hidden dependency 3 -- src/track/balls.py is a colour tracker tuned to RENDERED red/blue balls on a wooden table (thresholds r>195 etc., Y_TABLE=120); a real-video ball/blob tracker must be written; p3's CoTracker3 dense-grid path exists but was built for 10-60 px objects at 30 fps and will need online-mode/windowing for 480-frame 1080p clips.

Capture-rate claim is internally inconsistent: 'about 30 objects a day' x 45 clips = 1,350 clips/day vs the resources line 'one day of capture per 10 objects' (= 450/day). The scheduled numbers are nonetheless feasible: 2,500 clips over days 61-80 is 125/day (~3-4 min per drop incl. reset and logging); the 150-clip pilot is one capture day.

Kill criterion misfires on blocks: a hand-released flat-face block (card pull) lands on an edge or corner in a fraction of trials, so IQR(e) > 0.10 is likely for blocks for geometric reasons the proposal itself names, and would kill 'restitution from phone video' while spheres pass. A steel bearing also dents a wooden reference board, drifting e across the 10 repeats (surface damage, not instrument).

Budget and data: 2,500 clips x ~1 min CoTracker3 = ~42 GPU-h, tape fits 0.3 s/clip, FD Jacobians ~10 s/clip -> under the 50 GPU-h stated; GPUs 1-5 were idle at check time. New captures are the researcher's own data (no licence issue); Physics 101 is used only in-house for the days-1-7 tooling check. e is scale-free (a ratio of velocities or sqrt of a height ratio), so metric scale enters only mu (via the inclinometer angle, 1 deg -> 0.02 mu per p1) and the simulator alpha(v) mapping, and the per-clip g check is already designed.
verdicts.surviving_form: Survives with four narrowings. (1) Make the pilot's kill criteria sphere-only (IQR(e) <= 0.05, routes within 0.03, g within 5%) and treat flat-face blocks as a secondary cell whose spread is reported, not used to kill; add a hard reference surface (granite/glass tile) alongside the wooden board so steel bearings do not dent the reference. (2) Move the velocity-exponent kernel change (fn = max(k w pen - HC cd w pen |vn|^p, 0) or equivalent) and its e(alpha, p, v) revalidation into days 1-7, since the stock law forces e to fall ~2x from 1.4 to 2.8 m/s and the height-independence invariant cannot be tested without it. (3) For days 36-60 either state phone photogrammetry as the mesh source and gate it (mesh base-edge error vs CoM resolution), or use calliper-constructible asymmetric objects with KNOWN CoM offsets (a block with an embedded steel nut, a cylinder with an off-axis insert) so the CoM claim has a ground truth; keep mug/hammer/wrench as a demonstration, not a validated cell. (4) Replace '30 objects a day' with the schedule's own 125-200 clips/day and write the real-video ball/blob tracker in week 1 (balls.py does not transfer). Days 1-14 then fit: the day-1 gradient check is already done (this review), and the pilot needs only a phone, a board, 5 objects and one capture day.
verdicts.summary: Not refuted. The plan's single named show-stopper -- whether the Warp tape gives a correct d(apex)/d(alpha) through penalty impact at BOUNCE_RIG -- was run rather than argued and passes at 0.998 / 1.002 / 1.053 of central finite differences, 0.3 s per clip, with restitution exactly mass-independent, so the first experiment can run within two weeks on existing code (DiffMeshScene, set_restitution_alpha, p3's two-route readout, lm.py) plus a phone and one capture day. Nothing in the 90-day plan depends on something unobtainable: no robot, rig, depth or mocap is needed; e is scale-free; GPU cost is ~50 h on idle cards; data are self-captured. What the plan under-states are three real but obtainable dependencies -- the velocity exponent p is not in the contact kernel (fixed p = 1, e ~ 1 - alpha v), real asymmetric objects have no meshes without photogrammetry, and the real-video ball tracker does not exist -- plus an inflated capture-rate claim and a block-based kill criterion that would fail for geometric rather than instrumental reasons. With those narrowed as stated, the 90-day milestone is credible for one researcher.

verdicts.lens: Impact and practicality: who consumes the output, is the effect size actionable, does it answer the user's ask (differentiable physics, practical for robots/sims, scale beyond rooms)
evidence: Restitution has almost no consumer in robot simulation: MuJoCo has no restitution coefficient at all (solref/solimp soft constraints), PhysX/Isaac Sim default restitution to 0 and manipulation sim2real work randomises it without task sensitivity; the pipelines the proposal names as omitting it (PhysXNet, UniPhys-40K, ManiTwin) omit it because their downstream tasks do not use it. A 30-material e table is a number few act on.

The 'contact-model card for Newton/Warp penalty contact' calibrates the project's OWN kernels (src/sim/mesh_contact.py penalty + Hunt-Crossley, src/sim/rigs.py), not Newton's shipped solvers (VBD/XPBD/MuJoCo-Warp). GAUGE scored Newton's stock bouncing ball (nRMSE 22.7); a card about a bespoke contact law nobody else runs tells Newton users nothing about their engine.

Differentiability is not load-bearing. The proposal itself fits with FD Jacobians wherever the tape misses by >20% and states 6-10 parameters per clip at 0.4 s per rollout: a central-FD Jacobian is 12-20 rollouts = 5-8 s per clip, and J^T J from FD gives the identical Fisher matrix. Verified tape gradient exists for ONE parameter on ONE contact type (scripts/g0_grad_check.py: d(slide)/d(mu) -0.5448 vs FD -0.5453, plane slide only); damping through impact is unchecked and docs/results/g0d_verdict_12frame.json / g0_verdict.json are FAIL verdicts on the collision/video side. So the user's ask (a) is satisfied in name only.

The user's ask (c), 'very large scale beyond rooms, interactable worlds at scale', is explicitly rejected by the proposal ('the scene-scale framing is wrong'); 'beyond rooms' is reinterpreted as three outdoor surface tiles. UrbanVerse/URBAN-SIM/Vid2Sim users need terrain friction for wheels/feet and navigable geometry, not the restitution of a mug dropped on a paver.

The novelty hinge 'no public dataset holds restitution beyond three materials' is weak: COR by drop test is a century-old engineering measurement (Goldsmith 'Impact' 1960; Cross's ball studies; handbook tables for steel/brass/glass/wood), and PhysVid/IRIS already ship video-annotated bounce clips. The new part is 'everyday objects on everyday surfaces by phone', which is a dataset-track contribution, not a top-venue method paper.

The practically useful parameters for robots (friction, mass, CoM) are the ones this project ALREADY has from real footage with held-out validation (e1: 2.6 mm median on 70 held-out objects, mass within 25% for 69%); the proposal's genuinely new robot-relevant piece (CoM from a tumble on asymmetric objects, days 36-60) depends on fitting an initial orientation through a hand-dropped tumble, which the proposal itself names as 'the hardest fit in the plan' and which has no validated gradient path.

Real-drop restitution of non-spherical objects is dominated by impact geometry (edge/corner hits); the clean e is for spheres and flat drops, which no asset library needs. docs/results/p3_restitution_summary.json at 30 fps already shows the readout is geometry-noise (h_wood on glass e_h = 0.0, m_coin on table 0.56), and the 240 fps pilot only removes the frame-rate part of that.

Positive side: the capture protocol (phone, inclinometer, object's own edge as scale) and per-clip identifiability report are genuinely low-barrier and falsifiable, with a stated kill test (IQR(e) > 0.10, routes > 0.05 apart, g spread > 10%, e span < 0.15), and the existing track/fit stack (src/track/cotracker.py, src/track/balls.py, src/optimize/lm.py, src/simready/usd_physics.py) exists on disk, so it is actionable within 90 days by one person.
verdicts.surviving_form: Demote restitution from headline to one column. Re-headline as a phone-to-USD physics-material instrument whose output is validated by HELD-OUT REAL MOTION on asymmetric everyday objects (friction + mass by build + CoM + e), delivered as SimReady/USD physics materials and DR ranges, with the consumer named concretely (Isaac Sim / BEHAVIOR-style asset pipelines and SimReady material tables, which today assign these by VLM or bulk table). Make the contact-model card about engines people run: calibrate and score Newton's shipped solvers (MuJoCo-Warp, XPBD/VBD) and PhysX against the measured impacts, not the project's own penalty kernels. Either make differentiability load-bearing (a demonstrated joint fit over hundreds of clips with shared per-material/per-session parameters that FD cannot afford, with FD-verified tape gradients through impact on day 1) or drop the word and sell FD-Jacobian Fisher reporting honestly. Replace 'beyond rooms' with an explicit statement that scale here is materials covered and transfer to authored assets via the LLM-named material table (e1), and do not claim to answer the interactable-worlds ask.
verdicts.summary: The proposal is honest, falsifiable and executable, but its headline product (a 30-material restitution table and a calibration of the project's own penalty contact) has almost no consumer: robot simulators either lack restitution (MuJoCo) or default it to zero (PhysX/Isaac), the contact card describes bespoke kernels nobody else runs, differentiability is admittedly optional (FD at 6-10 parameters costs seconds and yields the same Fisher matrix), and the user's 'interactable worlds at scale' ask is explicitly declined rather than answered. The parts that matter to practitioners (friction, mass, CoM from a phone, validated on held-out real motion, exported as USD materials) are present but buried, so as written it would read as an incremental measurement paper. Score 4/10; survives only if re-headlined around the held-out-validated material instrument with named consumers and an engine-level, not kernel-level, contact calibration.

scouts.angle: Differentiable physics engines and differentiable-simulation system identification: which engines give contact gradients, whether they handle mesh contact, how many environments they batch, and which identification results exist on REAL data (parameters, accuracy, ground truth). Coverage 2024-2026 plus canonical earlier works (gradSim, DiffTaichi, Dojo, Le Lidec RA-L, ContactNets lineage).

works.name: NVIDIA Newton (on Warp)
works.what: GPU physics engine (NVIDIA + DeepMind + Disney, Linux Foundation) built on Warp's tape-based reverse-mode autodiff. Solvers: XPBD, VBD, MuJoCo (MuJoCo Warp backend, the primary one), Featherstone, SemiImplicit, Kamino, ImplicitMPM, Style3D. Collision pipeline: sphere/box/capsule/cylinder/cone/ellipsoid/convex mesh via GJK/MPR; triangle meshes via BVH vertex queries or precomputed SDFs; hydroelastic contacts; contact reduction. Contact gradients: documented as 'limited' -- `eval_rigid_contact_kinematics()` re-reads narrow-phase output with 'the narrow phase frozen' and gives first-order gradients w.r.t. body poses only. The MuJoCo Warp backend has no autodiff (MJX docs: 'no immediate plans'). Project state (not from docs): SolverVBD gradients are exactly 0.0 in 1.4.0, SolverSemiImplicit is differentiable.
works.params_from: n.a. (engine)
works.evaluated_against: none (engine; no sysid benchmark published by the project)
works.scale: Batched worlds via Warp; counts not stated on the pages read. Isaac Lab integration.
works.limitations: Gradients through contact only via the frozen-narrow-phase post-processing step; no gradient through collision detection itself; the primary backend (MuJoCo Warp) is non-differentiable; API churn (1.4 -> 1.7 dev within months).
works.confidence: high for collision/differentiability statements (read from docs page); medium for solver list (secondary summary)

works.name: MuJoCo MJX (JAX) and MuJoCo Warp (MJX-Warp)
works.what: Two GPU MuJoCo ports. MJX-JAX: differentiable 'mostly' (jax.grad; issue #2259), batch dims on mjx.Model/Data, ~950K steps/s at batch 8192 on GPU but ~10x slower than CPU MuJoCo for one scene. Geoms: PLANE, HFIELD, SPHERE, CAPSULE, BOX, MESH fully; convex-convex meshes should have <32 vertices; no SDF. MJX-Warp: 'does not support automatic differentiation and has no immediate plans'; supports mesh, heightfield, SDF; maintained by DeepMind+NVIDIA as part of Newton; batch renderer across many worlds.
works.params_from: n.a. (engine)
works.evaluated_against: none (engine)
works.scale: 8192-world batches documented for MJX-JAX
works.limitations: Mesh contact in the differentiable branch limited to small convex hulls; the fast branch (Warp) is non-differentiable; feature gaps vs CPU MuJoCo (joint types, solvers).

works.name: Hard Contacts with Soft Gradients / DiffMJX + Contacts-From-Distance
works.what: Fixes MJX gradients under stiff (realistic) penalty contact by adaptive time integration, and adds 'Contacts From Distance' -- a backward-pass-only straight-through penalty that yields informative pre-contact gradients while the forward pass stays physical. Demonstrated on sysid, MPC and musculoskeletal (MyoHand 39 MTUs, MyoArm 63 MTUs) control.
works.params_from: fit to real motion (ContactNets cube-toss dataset): cube side length + MuJoCo contact params solimp/solref; ~550 trajectories, MSE on 5-step segments
works.evaluated_against: real motion (ContactNets acrylic-cube tosses, AprilTag-tracked at 148 Hz)
works.scale: vmapped environments ('contacts in one simulation do not slow down other simulations'); ~10 s per gradient step on the cube task
works.limitations: Mesh-mesh collisions explicitly 'not modified' (planned); identified only geometry + contact stiffness, not friction/restitution/mass independently; trajectory error stays >0.25 due to chaotic corner impacts; mass/stiffness compensation acknowledged.

works.name: Dojo
works.what: Julia differentiable engine: variational integrator, hard contact as NCP with second-order friction cones solved by a custom primal-dual interior-point method; smooth gradients by implicit differentiation of the IPM. Demos: planning, policy optimization, sysid, and a hardware push experiment.
works.params_from: fit to real motion: friction coefficient + 8 vertex positions of a box from a real box-toss dataset
works.evaluated_against: real motion (box-toss dataset: learned parameters 'within 5% of the true geometry and friction coefficient'); hardware: xArm6 pushing a 0.5 kg box, final-position error ~0.5 cm (1.25%) and flip outcomes matched
works.scale: single-process Julia; no parallel-environment numbers
works.limitations: Collision support is 'point, sphere, and capsule collisions with flat surfaces' -- no meshes; CPU; Julia with Python bindings.

works.name: Genesis
