works.what: Unified multi-physics engine (rigid, MPM, SPH, FEM, PBD, Stable Fluid) with autodiff through its own compiler ('hand-derived gradients for the hardest kernels'); differentiable mode via requires_grad on SimOptions, PyTorch-style backward through recorded substeps.
works.params_from: n.a. (engine)
works.evaluated_against: none (engine)
works.scale: Claims 10-80x faster than Isaac Gym/Lab and MJX; no environment counts on pages read
works.limitations: Docs: 'Not every operation is differentiable: some contact and collision paths do not provide gradients' (zero or undefined); earlier docs say only MPM and Tool solvers were differentiable with rigid 'to be added'; differentiable mode stores every substep state (memory grows with horizon).
works.confidence: medium (docs read, but rigid-solver gradient status for the current version not confirmed on a primary page)

works.name: Brax
works.source: https://github.com/google/brax ; arXiv:2207.05060 (Zhong et al., gradient-correctness analysis)
works.what: JAX rigid-body engine with four pipelines (MJX, generalized, positional/PBD, spring), 'fully differentiable', ships APG (analytic policy gradient) alongside PPO/SAC/ES.
works.params_from: n.a. (engine)
works.evaluated_against: none (engine); Zhong et al. 2022 found that for LCP, convex, compliant and PBD contact models 'none of the calculated gradients match the analytical gradients'
works.scale: 'millions of physics steps per second on TPU', multi-device
works.limitations: Contact gradients are high-variance / incorrect in contact-rich settings (the reason DiffMJX exists); no mesh-mesh contact beyond MJX's convex limits.
works.confidence: high for README claims; medium for contact-gradient verdict (from search summary of Zhong et al.)

works.name: Ostrich: Taking Large Strides Through Stiff Contact in Differentiable Dynamics
works.what: GPU simulator that solves contact by non-smooth Newton iteration and differentiates the converged residual through the implicit function theorem, reusing the forward Schur complement for an O(1)-memory adjoint per step, allowing ~0.1 s timesteps with accurate gradients through stiff contact. Compared against MJX and Newton SemiImplicit (tape-based).
works.params_from: fit to real motion (robot trajectories over pallet obstacles), details not in abstract
works.evaluated_against: real motion (real-robot trajectories; 'maintained MuJoCo's accuracy at 50x larger timesteps')
works.scale: 8,192 parallel differentiated simulations on one 24 GB GPU; 29x MJX throughput; 211x faster than MJX, 4.7x faster than Newton SemiImplicit; 10 s trajectory optimisation over triangle-mesh terrain
works.limitations: Research prototype (Kucera & Zimmermann); the real-data use is trajectory optimisation/control, not per-object parameter identification with ground truth; mesh handling shown for terrain, not mesh-mesh object contact.
works.confidence: medium (abstract only; numbers from fetched abstract page)

works.name: DiffTaichi
works.what: Canonical: source-code-transformation autodiff for imperative simulation kernels with a lightweight tape; 10 differentiable simulators (MPM, FEM, rigid, fluids); controllers optimised in tens of iterations. Ancestor of the Warp tape design gradSim and PhysTwin build on.
works.params_from: n.a. (framework)
works.evaluated_against: sim-only
works.scale: single GPU; no batched-environment story
works.limitations: No real-data sysid; contact handled by penalty/soft models per example; maintained as Taichi, not a robotics engine.

works.name: gradSim
works.what: Canonical pixels-to-parameters: differentiable multiphysics (DiffTaichi-style kernels; rigid, FEM deformables, cloth) + differentiable rendering, so mass/friction/elasticity are fit from video with no 3D labels.
works.params_from: fit to video, but SIMULATED video only ('10000 simulated videos generated from variations of 14 objects'; 100 deformable instances)
works.evaluated_against: sim-only (mass abs. rel. error 9.01e-5 reported on synthetic)
works.scale: 14 objects x variations, synthetic
works.limitations: No real footage anywhere; ill-posedness acknowledged; project's own successor work (gradSim lineage) still lacks a real validation.

works.name: Le Lidec et al., 'Differentiable simulation for physical system identification' (RA-L 2021)
works.source: https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-03025616 (HAL blocked fetch; details from search summaries)
works.what: Extends staggered projections for frictional contact, derives analytical derivatives of the involved optimisation problems, and estimates friction coefficients and object masses 'in both synthetic and real experiments'.
works.params_from: fit to real motion (friction, mass)
works.evaluated_against: real motion (real experiments reported; accuracy numbers not readable from primary source)
works.scale: a few objects (unconfirmed)
works.limitations: Could not read primary; no mesh-contact or batching information; CPU implementation (Pinocchio lineage).
works.confidence: low-medium (primary page returned Access Denied; facts from abstract snippets)

works.name: ContactNets lineage: Bianchini, Halm, Posa, 'Simultaneous Learning of Contact and Continuous Dynamics' (CoRL 2023) + ContactNets cube-toss dataset
works.what: Learns geometry/contact + continuous dynamics (e.g., joint friction) from real contact-rich trajectories with a complementarity/maximum-dissipation-inspired loss rather than a prediction loss; reports it 'outperforms differentiable simulation and end-to-end alternatives with more data efficiency'. The cube-toss dataset (10 cm acrylic cube on wood, 3 x 148 Hz cameras, 570 clean tosses) is the de-facto real benchmark that Dojo and DiffMJX also fit.
works.params_from: fit to real motion (learned SDF geometry, friction, inertial/joint terms)
works.evaluated_against: real motion (cube toss + new articulated-object dataset)
works.scale: two real datasets, one or few objects each
works.limitations: Ground truth exists only for geometry (cube side) -- friction/restitution are never independently measured; one object per dataset; not a general-purpose engine.
works.confidence: high for dataset facts and abstract claims (read); medium for comparative numbers

works.name: One-Shot Real-to-Sim via End-to-End Differentiable Simulation and Rendering
works.what: From one robot push observed by a single RGB-D camera, jointly optimises geometry (Shape-as-Points), appearance, mass, diagonal inertia, centre of mass and friction through an MLCP rigid-body simulator (Strecke et al.) and PyTorch3D rendering.
works.params_from: fit to real motion (mass, CoM, inertia diag, friction) with TripoSR geometry init
works.evaluated_against: real motion: UR5e + F/T pusher, 3 YCB objects, 1 train / 3 test pushes each; real mass error 0.257 kg, Chamfer 5.66 mm at trajectory end; sim: 9 objects, mass err 0.0728 kg, friction err 0.106, novel-trajectory position err 15.5 mm
works.scale: 3 real objects, 9 simulated; <15 min per object on an RTX 4090
works.limitations: Needs GT segmentation masks, a robot pusher with F/T, flat terrain; cylindrical objects' rotation unidentifiable; no lighting/shadows; real mass error is large relative to YCB masses (~0.3-0.9 kg).

works.name: D-REX: Differentiable Real-to-Sim-to-Real Engine for Learning Dexterous Grasping
works.what: Gaussian-splat reconstruction (300-340 images/object) + a custom semi-implicit differentiable rigid engine assembled from MuJoCo/Brax/gradSim pieces; identifies object MASS from robot-hand interaction and learns grasping policies.
works.params_from: mass: fit to real motion; friction/stiffness: VLM-inferred (explicitly not optimised)
works.evaluated_against: real motion with weighed ground truth: 8 real objects (53-726 g) and three 3D-printed density variants; mass error 4.8-12.0% (ketchup 667 g vs 726 g), density variants within 13 g
works.scale: 8 objects + 3 replicas; 30-35 min reconstruction per object
works.limitations: Only mass; needs a dexterous hand and hundreds of images; rigid only; friction/stiffness come from a VLM, i.e., the same unvalidated source the project found uninformative.
works.confidence: high (read from arXiv HTML, first 100k chars)

works.name: PhysTwin
works.what: Deformable digital twins from 3 RGB-D views: spring-mass physics in a custom Warp simulator, generative shape prior, Gaussian-splat appearance. Stage 1 zero-order (CMA-ES) over global stiffness/damping/collision/topology params; stage 2 gradient descent over dense per-spring stiffness and collision params.
works.params_from: fit to video (spring stiffness, dashpot damping, collision elasticity/friction, topology)
works.evaluated_against: real motion via Chamfer + tracking error against 9 manually annotated points per video (CoTracker3 pseudo-GT), plus PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/IoU; 22 scenarios, 7:3 train/test
works.scale: 22 real scenarios (ropes, plush toys, cloth, packages)
works.limitations: No ground-truth physical parameters -- only trajectory fidelity; needs 3 RGB-D views; single interaction type; parameters are effective spring constants, not material properties.

works.name: RigPI: Dynamic Parameter Identification of Rigid Body via VLM-Seeded Differentiable Simulation
works.what: Identifies mass, moments of inertia, friction and joint parameters of rigid and articulated objects during robot-object interaction by combining VLM semantic priors (initialisation + constrained search space), force-torque measurements and motion in a differentiable-simulation pipeline.
works.params_from: VLM init, then fit to real motion + F/T data
works.evaluated_against: real motion ('extensive real-world experiments on objects with revolute and prismatic joints'; predictive validity on a real robot); accuracy numbers not in abstract
works.scale: not stated in abstract
works.limitations: Requires an F/T-sensed robot interaction; simulator unnamed in abstract; ground-truth source unstated; the project's own result (LLM/VLM numeric priors are generic) bears on the VLM-seeding step.
works.confidence: low-medium (abstract only; the arXiv page lists an unusual venue line, treat venue as unconfirmed)

gaps: No differentiable engine exposes gradients through MESH-MESH narrow-phase contact. Evidence: Newton docs state contact gradients come only from `eval_rigid_contact_kinematics` with 'the narrow phase frozen'; MJX docs limit differentiable convex-convex contact to hulls of <32 vertices and have no SDF; MuJoCo Warp has 'no immediate plans' for autodiff; DiffMJX says mesh-mesh collisions are 'currently not modified'; Dojo supports 'point, sphere, and capsule collisions with flat surfaces'; Genesis docs say 'some contact and collision paths do not provide gradients'. Searches for 'differentiable mesh contact gradients' returned only Ostrich (mesh terrain, research prototype) and the 2020 'Scalable Differentiable Physics' paper.

No differentiable-simulation sysid result is validated on HELD-OUT real objects, i.e., parameters assigned by class/material and checked against the motion of objects never fitted. Every real-data result found fits one object at a time (Dojo and DiffMJX: one cube; One-Shot: 3 YCB objects, 1 train push each; D-REX: 8 objects, mass only; PhysTwin: per-scenario; few-shot neural diff sim 2603.06218: two printed cubes). Search 'differentiable simulation ... sim-ready ... validated against real motion held-out objects material transfer' returned only vendor marketing (artlabs SimReady, Rigyd 'mass within 15-20%') with no held-out protocol.

No real dataset with INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED friction, restitution and mass per object is used for differentiable sysid; ground truth is geometry (cube side length) or weighed mass only. Evidence: ContactNets/Dojo/DiffMJX cube toss has side-length GT and no measured friction; D-REX weighs mass only; One-Shot reports real mass error but friction only in simulation; Guo et al. 'Benchmarking Rigid Body Contact Models' (L4DC 2023) is synthetic and itself 'calls for the collection of more diverse real-world contact datasets'.

No differentiable-sim identification of coefficient of restitution from real high-frame-rate video in 2024-2026. Search 'coefficient of restitution identification differentiable simulation high-speed video' returned SMASH (2016), Bounce Maps (graphics), NJIT sphere measurements, and a 2025 video-foundation-model paper -- no differentiable-engine fit to measured bounces.

No 'interactable world at scale' built on a differentiable engine with identified parameters. Search 'differentiable physics scene-scale thousands of objects large-scale world' returned only Qiao et al. 'Scalable Differentiable Physics for Learning and Control' (ICML 2020, localized collision handling) and parallel-environment throughput claims (Ostrich 8192 differentiated sims, MJX 8192 batch); Vid2Sim (urban navigation, CVPR 2025) builds interactive scenes from video but with a non-differentiable simulator and no object parameter identification.

No rigid-object parameter identification from a single uninstrumented (phone) video without a robot or F/T sensing in the differentiable-sim literature. Every real-data method found depends on a robot pusher + depth (One-Shot), a dexterous hand + 300 images (D-REX), F/T sensing (RigPI), multi-camera AprilTags (ContactNets lineage, 2603.06218) or 3 RGB-D views (PhysTwin). gradSim, the one pixels-only method, is evaluated on simulated video only ('10000 simulated videos').
scouts.relevance_to_our_assets: The project's own Warp mesh-vertex contact kernels with demonstrated density-through-contact gradients sit in a documented hole: no shipped engine (Newton, MJX, MuJoCo Warp, Genesis, Dojo) gives gradients through mesh-mesh narrow phase, and DiffMJX lists it as future work -- so the kernels are an asset, not a reinvention, though they are penalty-based and therefore inherit exactly the stiff-contact gradient problem DiffMJX (adaptive integration + contacts-from-distance) and Ostrich (implicit-function-theorem adjoint) were built to fix; both techniques are directly transferable to the existing Hunt-Crossley/regularised-Coulomb path. The Physics 101 pipeline (CoTracker3 + Newton fits to 0.4-1.0 mm RMS, friction for 11 materials, two-angle and scale invariants) and especially the held-out test (70 objects, 359 trials, material-table transfer at 2.6 mm vs 1.8 mm oracle) are the only results in this landscape that validate assigned parameters on objects never fitted; the differentiable-sim literature fits one object at a time against cube-toss or robot-push data and never asks the transfer question, so this is non-redundant. Redundant or weaker than the field: re-fitting a single cube/box to its own trajectory (Dojo and DiffMJX already reach ~5% on the ContactNets toss; a 240 fps phone capture would merely replicate ContactNets' 148 Hz AprilTag rig with worse pose precision), pixels-to-parameters on synthetic renders (gradSim did it in 2021 on 10,000 synthetic clips), and VLM-seeded friction (RigPI, D-REX) which the project's f14/e1 results already show is a generic prior. The failed 30 fps restitution attempt matches the field's absence of any real restitution fit; nothing on disk fills it. The Blender/probe harness and sensitivity matrix have no counterpart in the engine papers but are not what they evaluate on; the engines' batching (8192 worlds) exceeds what the project's single-GPU, credit-metered setup has used, and the project's 'rule 1' sweep-before-trust protocol has no analogue in any engine paper read.
scouts.caveats: Le Lidec et al. (RA-L 2021) could not be read from the primary source (HAL returned Access Denied twice); its 'real experiments' claim and parameter list come from abstract snippets only. RigPI was read from the abstract page only, which carries an implausible venue line; treat its numbers and venue as unconfirmed. Genesis rigid-solver gradient status was taken from v1.2.2 and v0.4.7 docs plus a search snippet, not from the current differentiable-simulation guide (404 on two URL guesses). Newton docs read are 1.7.0.dev0 while the project runs 1.4.0; the SolverVBD-zero-gradient fact is the project's own measurement, not documentation. DiffMJX, Dojo and D-REX HTML pages were read only to the first ~100k characters; the ContactNets cube numbers (side length ~100 mm vs 10 cm GT, trajectory error 0.32 -> 0.26) come from that partial read. Ostrich facts are from its abstract page; its engine internals and real-data protocol are not verified. Dates: several arXiv ids in the 26xx range (2603.01151, 2603.06218, 2606.03479, 2606.25212, 2609.08800) are 2026 preprints; venue claims for those ('ICLR 2026 poster') are as printed on the arXiv page. Zhong et al. 2022 gradient-correctness verdict and DiffTaichi details were taken from search summaries rather than the papers. Splatting Physical Scenes (2506.04120), PersistGS (2606.03479), few-shot neural differentiable simulator (2603.06218), Vid2Sim x2 (2501.06693, 2506.06440), Scalable Differentiable Physics (2007.02168) and Guo et al. L4DC 2023 were read but kept out of the 15-work list to respect the cap; they are cited only as gap evidence.

scouts.angle: Sim-ready asset and scene generation with physical properties: for each pipeline, where mass / friction / restitution / centre of mass come from and what the assigned values are evaluated against. Covered 2024-2026 (PhysX family, UniPhysGen, VoMP/AdaVoMP, PhysGS, Sim Anything, HoloScene, CoDimRecon, EmbodiedGen V2, ManiTwin, SimReady, BEHAVIOR-1K) plus the canonical earlier NeRF2Physics / DANOs, and the two works that actually touch real motion (Scalable Real2Sim, GAUGE). The specific question asked -- does anyone validate assigned parameters against the real motion of held-out objects -- is answered in the gaps.

works.name: PhysX-3D (PhysXNet dataset + PhysXGen generator)
works.what: Image-to-3D generation that also emits per-part physical annotations in five dimensions: absolute scale, material (material name, Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, density), affordance rank, kinematics, function description. PhysXNet = 26K+ annotated objects; PhysXNet-XL = 6M+ procedurally generated.
works.params_from: VLM (GPT-4o) proposes material name + E, nu, rho per part from rendered part images, then human expert verification. Values are the VLM's handbook-style numbers, not measurements. No friction, restitution or centre of mass are annotated; mass is implied by density x volume.
works.evaluated_against: Annotation agreement only: Euclidean distance for scale, PSNR of predicted vs annotated material/affordance maps, instantiation distance for kinematics, on a 1K held-out PhysXNet split. No physics simulation and no real motion in the evaluation.
works.scale: 26K objects (PhysXNet), 6M procedural (PhysXNet-XL); object-level, single assets.
works.limitations: Ground truth is itself VLM+human opinion, so the metric measures agreement with a prior, not physical correctness. Authors state limits in fine-grained properties, artefacts, long-tailed scale (three orders of magnitude), spatial inconsistency in material/affordance maps.

works.name: PhysX-Anything (PhysX-Mobility dataset)
works.what: Single in-the-wild image -> VLM-based generative model producing geometry (193x token-compressed representation), articulation and physical attributes, exported as URDF/MJCF XML for direct use in MuJoCo-style simulators. PhysX-Mobility: 2K+ objects, 47 categories.
works.params_from: VLM prediction (the generative model is itself a VLM) trained on PhysX-Mobility annotations, which were produced by GPT-5 from part-segmentation images and then verified by human volunteers. Explicitly named attributes: absolute dimension, density, material. The paper does not state that friction, restitution, centre of mass or inertia are predicted; what populates the URDF beyond scale/density is not specified.
works.evaluated_against: Scale error vs PhysXGen (43.44 -> 0.30), material score (17.52 vs 6.29), affordance (14.28 vs 9.75), kinematics VLM score 0.83 -- all against the dataset's own VLM/human annotations; plus a 14-volunteer user study and GPT-4 judgements. 'Sim-ready' is demonstrated by training a contact-rich policy in simulation, not by comparing motion to reality.
works.scale: 2K+ real-world objects; single-object assets.
works.limitations: Contact parameters not documented; ground truth is VLM+human; no real-motion check. Evaluation of 'physical plausibility' is a user study and a VLM judge -- exactly the class of signal the project has measured as uninformative for parameter values.
works.confidence: high for scale/density/material and the evaluation; medium for the absence of friction/restitution (I searched the HTML for those terms and found no prediction of them, but could not read the exported file schema)

works.name: PhysX-Omni (PhysXVerse dataset + PhysX-Bench)
works.what: Unified single-image generator for rigid, deformable and articulated sim-ready assets with an uncompressed high-resolution geometry representation for VLMs. PhysXVerse: 8.7K+ assets over 2.9K categories, 1-65 parts each, built on PartVerse segmentation. PhysX-Bench scores six attributes: geometry, absolute scale, material, affordance, kinematics, description.
works.params_from: GPT-family VLM preliminary annotation of scale, material, affordance, kinematics, function; human-in-the-loop refinement. Material carries E, nu, rho (as in PhysXNet). No friction/restitution/CoM listed.
works.evaluated_against: PhysX-Bench: scale = symmetric percentage error vs a VLM-estimated reference dimension; material = render the asset in free-fall and water-drop simulation videos and have a VLM (Qwen3.5-122B) judge the behaviour for plausibility of E/nu/rho; affordance and kinematics also VLM-judged; descriptions vs human references. Spearman of VLM judge vs human ranking reported ~1.0 for several attributes, 0.8 for geometry. Downstream robotic policy learning in simulation. No real motion.
works.scale: 8.7K assets, 2.9K categories; object-level, including vehicles/robots/scene components.
works.limitations: The first sim-ready pipeline to put a physics engine in the evaluation loop, but the simulated behaviour is still scored by a VLM judge, not by a real trajectory; the 'ground truth' scale is a VLM estimate. Authors note geometry quality on complex structures and under-performance on appearance metrics.

works.name: UniPhysGen (UniPhys-40K / UniPhys-Bench)
works.what: Maps an input 3D geometry (optionally with image) to structured physical semantics: part-level material class, density, friction coefficient, Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio, affordance; object-level mass, scale, category; articulation type/axis/pivot/limits. Assets deployed in Isaac Sim for drawer/faucet/laptop tasks.
works.params_from: Automated pipeline: perceptual part decomposition, GPT-5 reasoning for the physical values, geometry-constrained candidate generation, and simulation-driven consistency verification (the simulator is used to filter inconsistent articulation, not to fit the numbers), then human verification for the 1,927-object benchmark subset. Friction is a VLM number; mass is VLM-derived. Restitution and CoM not listed.
works.evaluated_against: UniPhys-Bench (1,927 manually verified objects): joint-type accuracy, axis angle error, pivot distance, structure mIoU, material classification accuracy, mass and scale ALDE/MnRE -- all vs the pipeline's own human-verified labels. Isaac Sim used to show stable interaction. No real motion.
works.scale: 40K+ assets, 84 categories; object-level.
works.limitations: Friction/mass ground truth is GPT-5 + human plausibility, so a correct-looking metric says the model reproduces the prior. Image modality ablations show geometry dominates the reasoning. No real-world calibration of any value.
works.confidence: high (read from arXiv HTML, first 100K chars)

works.name: VoMP / AdaVoMP (NVIDIA Spatial Intelligence Lab)
works.what: Feed-forward prediction of dense volumetric Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio and density for any 3D representation that can be rendered and voxelised (mesh, SDF, 3DGS, NeRF). AdaVoMP replaces fixed voxels with a sparse adaptive voxel structure generated autoregressively, 16^3x the resolution. Integrated with Isaac Sim ('RoboLab') for building interactive environments.
works.params_from: VLM annotation (Qwen2.5-VL 72B) of segmented 3D datasets, combined with material databases, projected onto a learned manifold of 100K physically-valid (E, nu, rho) triplets (MatVAE). AdaVoMP reuses VoMP's VLM labels (GVT dataset = GVM + 61 objects). No friction, restitution or CoM -- these are mechanical (deformation) properties only.
works.evaluated_against: Voxel-level ALDE/ARE/ADE/MnRE against the VLM-labelled 'material trees' on GVT-Test and GVT-Hard (50 hard objects); a check that predictions fall within physically measured material ranges; qualitative deformable FEM / Isaac Sim simulations compared to NeRF2Physics, PUGS, Phys4DGen, PIXIE. No real motion.
works.scale: Object-level, thousands of assets; the stated purpose is 'interactive physically realistic worlds' through Isaac Sim.
works.limitations: Ground truth is VLM opinion; validity is checked against handbook ranges (the project's rule 2 says this proves little). Authors: no directional/anisotropic materials; static assets only (no video cues); possible overfitting under distribution shift. Not a rigid-contact pipeline at all -- no mu, no e.
works.confidence: high for AdaVoMP (arXiv HTML read); medium for VoMP details (project page only)

works.name: NeRF2Physics
works.what: Posed images -> NeRF point cloud with fused CLIP features; BLIP-2 caption -> GPT-3.5/4 proposes K candidate materials with property values (density, friction, hardness); zero-shot kernel regression assigns per-point values; mass = integrated density with LLM-estimated wall thickness.
works.params_from: LLM-proposed material names and numeric values (the LLM is the table), CLIP for spatial assignment.
works.evaluated_against: Mass: ABO-500 (500 Amazon products with product-metadata mass), metrics ADE/ALDE/APE/MnRE. Friction and hardness: an in-house dataset of real objects with kinetic friction measured on 6 surfaces using an iOLab with fabric pads (10 trials averaged) and Shore hardness at 31 points with durometers -- i.e. per-point static measurements, not motion. The 'digital twin' ball-collision demo is qualitative only.
works.scale: 500 objects (mass), ~6 surfaces / 31 points (friction/hardness); object-level.
works.limitations: Documented failures: caption errors (brick -> sand/concrete), black painted steel vs plastic indistinguishable to CLIP; interiors unobservable so thickness is an LLM guess. Mass ground truth is listed product weight.

works.name: PhysGS (Bayesian-inferred Gaussian splatting)
works.what: Extends 3DGS with per-splat Bayesian beliefs over material class (Dirichlet-Categorical) and continuous properties (Normal-Inverse-Gamma), updated from SAM part masks and GPT-5 answers across views; outputs per-point friction, hardness, stiffness, density, object mass, with aleatoric/epistemic uncertainty.
works.params_from: VLM (GPT-5) priors per part, fused across views; the numeric values are the VLM's.
works.evaluated_against: Mass: ABO-500 product masses (APE improves 22.8% over NeRF2Physics). Friction and Shore hardness: real per-point measurements on 15 household objects in 13 scenes (kinetic friction ALDE -18.1%, hardness ADE -61.2%). Stiffness: MIT fabric dataset (30 fabrics). All static measurements of the property, no motion.
works.scale: 500 + 15 objects + 30 fabrics; object and small-scene (indoor/outdoor captures).
works.limitations: Authors: estimates inherit mask ambiguity when parts merge visually similar materials. Friction ground truth is a pad-on-surface meter reading, not the object sliding; no restitution; no CoM.

works.name: Sim Anything (MLLM-guided Gaussian-splat physics)
works.what: Static 3DGS scene -> open-vocab object segmentation and in-painting -> MLLM-P3 (GPT-4V) predicts mean density, Young's modulus, Poisson's ratio per object -> MPDP network predicts a geometry-aware distribution of those values -> MLS-MPM simulation on a 64^3 grid; ~2 min per scene on an RTX 3090.
works.params_from: GPT-4V zero-shot for the means; MPDP trained on synthetic BlenderNeRF scenes labelled with Physics3D values.
works.evaluated_against: 42-participant user study on motion realism and a LAION aesthetic score; compared on PhysDreamer's 4 real scenes (which have real videos of the objects moving) and 9 synthetic scenes. No parameter ground truth, no trajectory error.
works.scale: A handful of scenes (LERF, Instruct-NeRF2NeRF, PhysDreamer); object-in-scene level.
works.limitations: Authors: cannot segment partially occluded objects. Deformable only (E, nu, rho); no rigid contact parameters; evaluation is human preference.

works.name: HoloScene
works.what: Single video of a static indoor scene -> interactive scene graph with complete object geometry, appearance (3DGS) and physical parameters p_i = (mass, friction, damping, restitution); reconstruction as energy minimisation combining observation, physical-stability (Isaac Sim) and generative-prior terms, optimised by sampling plus gradient refinement.
works.params_from: The per-object (m, kappa, zeta, r) are variables of the optimisation whose physics term is static stability under gravity; the paper does not state an external source (VLM/table) for them. In practice the stability objective constrains geometry/pose far more than it constrains mass or friction values.
works.evaluated_against: Stable% (fraction of objects that stay put in Isaac Sim), object reconstruction ratio, penetration and geometry failure counts, rendering metrics; on Replica (3 synthetic scenes, 81.7% stable), ScanNet++ (3 real), iGibson (2), one self-captured scene. No real motion, no parameter ground truth.
works.scale: Room-scale indoor scenes, ~10 scenes.
works.limitations: Authors: static indoor videos only; dynamic scenes and large outdoor environments remain challenging. Static stability does not identify mass, friction or restitution (any sufficiently grippy, any mass is stable), so the physical parameters are effectively unconstrained.

works.name: CoDimRecon
works.what: Agentic multi-view RGB reconstruction of sim-ready scenes with rigid, articulated and deformable objects, the deformables typed by codimension (curves with radii, shells with thickness, watertight volumes for tet meshing); an agent initialises compatible physical models/parameters via simulator 'skills', runs behavioural tests, and revises material modelling where tests expose mismatches.
works.params_from: Simulator skills initialise parameters (prior/defaults chosen by the agent); the abstract does not distinguish recovered from assumed values and the project's prior reading of it records the authors' own statement that accepted values are effective properties under the assumed model.
works.evaluated_against: Compositional reconstruction accuracy on Replica and ScanNet++; demonstrated robot interactions with rod/shell/solid assets. No real motion comparison reported in the abstract.
works.scale: Room-scale indoor scenes.
works.limitations: Parameters are effective, model-dependent quantities; evaluation is geometric plus qualitative interaction.
works.confidence: medium (abstract only; the 'effective parameters' quote is from the project's own earlier reading and I could not re-verify it in the abstract)

works.name: NVIDIA SimReady specification / Isaac Sim asset conventions
works.what: A USD-based asset contract: a Rigid Body capability requires a UsdPhysics collider, a mass (kg) per geometry prim, and a bound PhysicsMaterialAPI with physics:density, physics:staticFriction, physics:dynamicFriction, physics:restitution.
works.params_from: Not prescribed. The spec defines the fields and their schema; it says nothing about whether the values are measured, looked up or guessed, and defines no tolerance.
works.evaluated_against: None. Conformance is schema validation.
works.scale: Catalogue-level (NVIDIA SimReady asset packs, third-party vendors).
works.limitations: A container format, not a measurement. Note it uses the PhysX contact model (static+dynamic friction, restitution scalar), which differs from the project's Hunt-Crossley/alpha formulation -- a value in one is not directly a value in the other.
works.confidence: high for the field list; medium for the absence of any value-provenance guidance (the requirements page I read was partly placeholder)

works.name: BEHAVIOR-1K / OmniGibson object annotation
works.what: 9,000+ object instances over 1,900+ categories with 'rich physical (friction, mass, articulation) and semantic properties', simulated in OmniGibson on PhysX 5.
works.params_from: Per the paper and docs: Weight is a human-annotated property; CenterOfMass, MomentOfInertia, StableOrientations and collision meshes are computed programmatically from the mesh; friction comes from a curated mapping from visual material to friction coefficient; mass/density 'assigned realistic' values. Restitution not mentioned.
works.evaluated_against: No validation of the physical values is reported; annotation QA (>96.8% approval) covers extraction and semantic properties. No real motion.
works.scale: 50 scenes, 9K objects -- the largest annotated interactive household set.
works.limitations: Provenance of the mass numbers (lookup vs estimate) is not documented in the paper; friction is a material-name lookup table with unstated source; CoM assumes a uniform-density mesh convention.
works.confidence: medium (paper read in part via HTML; docs sentences from search snippets, not a primary page I could open)

works.name: EmbodiedGen V2 (and ManiTwin-100K as the scale datapoint)
works.what: Agentic text/image -> sim-ready multi-room worlds: visual mesh + collision mesh + 3DGS per object, grasps validated in SAPIEN, exported as URDF, MJCF (MuJoCo/Genesis), USD (Isaac Sim), deployed in Genesis, Isaac Gym/Sim, MuJoCo, PyBullet, SAPIEN3. 150 task-driven worlds, 778 asset instances in 128 categories. ManiTwin: 100K image-derived twins with 5M simulation-verified grasps.
works.params_from: GPT-5.4 infers real-world scale, mass and a friction RANGE from multi-view renderings plus category; stored as metadata 'for downstream sampling or calibration'. ManiTwin likewise: VLM mass from apparent material and volume, friction by material cue (e.g. 0.3 plastic, 0.5 rubber); its authors state 'physical property estimates are VLM-inferred rather than ground-truth calibrated'.
works.evaluated_against: Indirect only: 96.5% human acceptance, 98.6% collision success in simulated grasp-and-lift, 83.3% of worlds usable without manual fixes; real-robot task success 21.7% -> 75.0% from training in the generated worlds. ManiTwin: 92.2% human-judged plausibility on 500 sampled objects plus grasp-stability simulation. No comparison of mass/friction with measured values.
works.scale: Multi-room scenes (the only entry here that goes beyond a single room); 100K assets for ManiTwin.
works.limitations: Physical values are a VLM prior wrapped as a range for domain randomisation; the real-robot gain shows the geometry/affordance pipeline works, not that the parameters are right. ManiTwin excludes articulated and deformable objects.
works.confidence: high for EmbodiedGen V2 and ManiTwin (arXiv HTML read)

works.name: Scalable Real2Sim (robotic pick-and-place asset generation)
works.what: Fully automated pipeline: a robot grasps a real object, reconstructs visual + collision geometry from an external camera, and identifies mass, centre of mass and the full inertia tensor from joint-torque sensing on one excitation trajectory (robot parameters identified first from 10 trajectories), solved as an SDP with physical-feasibility constraints; assets exported for Drake.
works.params_from: Measured by robot interaction (torque sensing); contact parameters (friction, restitution) explicitly left as future work.
works.evaluated_against: Known-inertia reconfigurable test object (8 configs): mass 1.34% +/- 0.21%, CoM 2.15% +/- 1.20%, inertia 42.35% +/- 15.64%; one 3D-printed mustard bottle of known mass 427.1 g: 1.23% mass error, 358.6% inertia error. Sim vs real rollouts shown only qualitatively side by side because 'individual simulation rollouts are highly sensitive to initial conditions'. 20 benchmark assets.
works.scale: 20 YCB-like objects; tabletop.
works.limitations: Needs a torque-sensing arm; no friction/restitution; inertia poorly identified; no quantitative trajectory validation.

works.name: GAUGE: measurement-grounded physical-fidelity benchmark
works.what: 22 task families (rigid collision/friction/momentum transfer, cables, textiles, volumetric soft bodies) each with 20 real trials captured by 16 NOKOV infrared cameras at 180 Hz in a 2 m cube (~1,560 trials), downsampled to 30 fps, paired with independently measured parameters: friction by inclined-plane method with velocity measurement, restitution on an air-bearing rail (e = v_out/v_in), textile stretch/bending on Style3D instruments, E and nu by compression + DIC. Physics engines (Isaac Sim 6.0 PhysX, Genesis 1.12, Newton 1.3 with MuJoCo rigid / VBD soft) are run with parameters SET from the measurements, defaults otherwise; six image-to-video models tested on 5 rigid tasks for law consistency and parameter stability.
works.params_from: Measured, with mean +/- sd over 20 trials.
works.evaluated_against: Real trajectories: RMSE and DTW normalised by the real-world trial-to-trial variability. Slope slider: Genesis 0.58/0.69, Isaac 0.61/0.71 normalised RMSE/DTW; turntable Isaac 0.17/0.61; bouncing ball best result still 15.63x baseline RMSE; Newton's cradle momentum-transfer efficiency 0.20 (Isaac) / 0.26 (Newton). No engine uniformly faithful; worst on impulsive contact, fast textiles, volumetric deformation. Video models: right equation form, wrong accelerations/momentum/oscillation timing.
works.scale: Lab bench, 2 m cube; three rigid materials (wood, plastic, metal), six fabrics, two foams.
works.limitations: Tests engines given measured parameters, not any pipeline that assigns parameters; the materials are nominal categories (authors note surface treatment/wear vary); world-model track is rigid-only because 3D coordinates cannot be extracted from video for deformables. Newton was evaluated at v1.3.0 with MuJoCo/VBD solvers, not with custom contact kernels.

works.name: DANOs: Differentiable physics simulation of dynamics-augmented neural objects (canonical earlier work)
works.what: NeRF object + Dojo differentiable contact simulator; learns sliding/rolling/torsional friction, mass scale, CoM and inertia by gradient descent through contact, from a real video of a soap bar sliding and from synthetic Panda pushes of a Stanford bunny.
works.params_from: Fit to observed motion (real video for the soap, simulated pushes for the bunny).
works.evaluated_against: Soap sliding friction learned 0.61 vs 0.75 measured experimentally; bunny parameters <1.5% relative error from 10 pushes; qualitative trajectory overlays.
works.scale: 2 objects.
works.limitations: Single contact point; no articulated/soft bodies; pose extraction from RGB sensitive to initialisation; no renderer-in-the-loop. n = 1 real object.
works.confidence: medium (ar5iv render read; venue not confirmed)

gaps: No sim-ready asset/scene pipeline validates its assigned mass, friction, restitution or CoM against the REAL motion of held-out objects. Searched: 'validate estimated physical parameters against real-world object motion held-out', 'sim-ready asset generation physical parameters evaluated against real object motion video', 'simulation-ready assets held-out real trajectories friction restitution digital twin', and read the evaluation sections of PhysX-3D, PhysX-Anything, PhysX-Omni, UniPhysGen, AdaVoMP, PhysGS, NeRF2Physics, Sim Anything, HoloScene, EmbodiedGen V2, ManiTwin. Every one evaluates against (a) its own VLM+human annotations, (b) static per-point meter readings (PhysGS/NeRF2Physics friction pads, durometers), (c) product-listing mass (ABO-500), (d) simulator stability or VLM-judged simulation videos (PhysX-Bench, HoloScene, 2602.12633), or (e) downstream policy success. The closest: Scalable Real2Sim (mass/CoM from torque sensing, no friction, qualitative rollouts), DANOs (one soap bar, 0.61 vs 0.75), and the project's own Physics 101 held-out test (70 objects, 359 trials).

No work combines a physical-parameter ASSIGNMENT pipeline with a measurement-grounded trajectory benchmark. GAUGE (2608.05948) measures friction/restitution and real trajectories but feeds the measured values straight into engines; it never tests a VLM/table/material-transfer assignment. Searched 'GAUGE benchmark' details and 'measurement-grounded benchmark sim-ready asset parameters' -- no paper reports normalised trajectory error for assets whose parameters were assigned rather than measured.

Restitution is almost entirely absent from asset pipelines. Of the generation/annotation works, only HoloScene lists a restitution variable (unconstrained by its static-stability objective) and the SimReady schema has a field for it; PhysXNet/PhysXVerse/UniPhys-40K/PhysDB/ManiTwin annotate none. The only real restitution measurements found are GAUGE's air-bearing rail (3 rigid materials) and Bounce-and-Learn (one ball, many surfaces, already known to the project). Searched 'restitution annotation 3D asset dataset', found nothing object-level.

Centre of mass is never assigned from evidence: every pipeline that outputs a CoM computes it from the mesh under a uniform-density (or vertex) convention (BEHAVIOR-1K programmatic CoM, HoloScene, 2602.12633 optimises CoM only toward static stability). No dataset annotates a hollow-vs-solid build or a measured CoM; searched 'center of mass annotation object dataset shell solid' and found only Scalable Real2Sim (robot torque sensing, 2.15% error on a test object).

No published check that a material-name -> friction lookup (the mechanism in BEHAVIOR-1K, ManiTwin, EmbodiedGen V2, NeRF2Physics, PhysGS) predicts how an unseen object of that material actually slides. The project's e1 result (material table 2.6 mm vs LLM number 7.5 mm vs oracle 1.8 mm) has no published counterpart; searched 'material friction table transfer held-out objects slide prediction error' and found only the robot-interaction papers (PhyPush 2605.26284, Real2Sim via active perception 2601.08454), which identify per-object values with a robot rather than transfer by material.

The engine itself is unvalidated in the sim-ready pipelines: PhysX-Bench's free-fall/water-drop test and HoloScene's stability test treat the simulator as truth, while GAUGE shows Isaac/Genesis/Newton (default solvers, measured parameters) at 0.6-15x the real trial-to-trial variability on friction and bounce tasks. No sim-ready pipeline paper reports the contact-model error of its target engine on the probe it uses; searched 'simulation-ready asset validation physics engine fidelity contact' -- only GAUGE.

Beyond-room scale with physical parameters does not exist in a validated form: EmbodiedGen V2 reaches multi-room worlds but with VLM mass/friction ranges meant for randomisation; HoloScene and CoDimRecon are single-room and state outdoor/large scenes as open; PhysXVerse includes outdoor categories as isolated objects. Searched 'large-scale interactive world physical properties outdoor simulation-ready' and found no scene-scale work whose parameters are anything but a VLM prior or defaults.
scouts.relevance_to_our_assets: The landscape splits into three layers and the project's validated assets sit in the one that is empty. Layer 1, assignment (PhysX family, UniPhysGen, VoMP/AdaVoMP, PhysGS, NeRF2Physics, EmbodiedGen V2, ManiTwin, BEHAVIOR-1K, SimReady): every one gets mass/friction from a VLM or a material table and scores against annotations, meters or simulator stability -- this is exactly what the project has measured (f14, e1): LLMs name materials well and give numbers that are a generic ~0.4 prior, while a measured per-material table transfers to held-out real objects at 2.6 mm. So the project's Physics 101-derived table plus LLM material naming is not redundant with these pipelines; it is the missing calibration step that any of them could plug in (PhysXNet/UniPhys-40K/ManiTwin material labels are the natural interface, and the areal-vs-solid build rule for mass is something none of them has). Layer 2, measurement-grounded evaluation (GAUGE; Scalable Real2Sim; DANOs; the project's p1-p5/e1): GAUGE is the only external benchmark with real trajectories and measured friction/restitution, and it evaluated Newton 1.3 with stock MuJoCo/VBD solvers -- the project's exact-mesh contact kernels, alpha-restitution and the Physics 101 fit (0.4-1.0 mm RMS) are directly comparable to GAUGE's slope-slider and bouncing-ball tasks, and its mocap trials would give the project the 180 Hz restitution data that the 30 fps p3 attempt could not. Layer 3, differentiable fitting (DANOs, 2602.12633, gradSim/PhysTwin already known): small, per-object, and never run at dataset scale; the project's differentiable Warp contact path is the same tool but has only been exercised for density recovery. Redundancies to note: the rendering/probe/judge machinery overlaps with PhysX-Bench's VLM-judged free-fall test, which the project has already shown to be uninformative for parameter values, and the CoM-from-build code duplicates what BEHAVIOR-1K/HoloScene compute programmatically, except that the project's is checked against textbook invariants and theirs is a uniform-density convention.
scouts.caveats: (1) Five sources (PhysX-Omni, UniPhysGen, AdaVoMP, HoloScene, GAUGE, EmbodiedGen V2) were read only up to the first 100K characters of their arXiv HTML; appendix-level details such as GAUGE's per-task tables and UniPhysGen's exact label provenance may contain more. (2) CoDimRecon was read from its abstract only; the 'effective parameters' statement is carried over from the project's own prior note and was not re-verified here. (3) BEHAVIOR-1K's friction-lookup and 'assigned realistic mass' statements come from search snippets of the Stanford docs that I could not open as primary pages, hence medium confidence. (4) PhysX-Anything: I found no prediction of friction/restitution/CoM in its HTML, but I could not inspect the exported URDF schema, so 'absent' is inferred. (5) Articulate-Anything (ICLR 2025, arXiv 2410.13882) and URDF-Anything+ (2603.14010) were checked and omitted from the list because they assign no physical parameters (physics is domain-randomised at policy-training time); PhysForge/PhysDB (2605.05163, 150K Objaverse assets with VLM+human part-level material and mass) and SiPhy (2607.22355, single-image density/mass on PhysXNet-100, ABO-500) were omitted as further instances of layer 1 with the same evaluation pattern. (6) Some arXiv ids are from mid-2026 (2605-2609) and may still revise; venues are stated only where a conference page confirmed them.

scouts.angle: Interactive neural world models and "interactable worlds at scale": Genie 3 / Project Genie, Matrix-Game 2.0 and the game-world-model class (Hunyuan-GameCraft, Oasis, Mirage, Yan), Cosmos-Predict2.5 to Cosmos 3, V-JEPA 2-AC as a planning world model; their physics-consistency and persistence evaluations (Physics-IQ, IntPhys 2, Principia, WRBench, WBench/WorldMark, PhyWorldBench); the 2026 literature on what latent world models can and cannot identify (PokeWorld, ACWM-Phys); hybrid physics-engine + neural-renderer systems (PhysGen, Force Prompting, WonderPlay/PhysDreamer/PhysCtrl, PhysWorld, PIN-WM/OrbiSim, MOSIV); and the one city-scale sim-ready pipeline found (UrbanVerse). Coverage 2024-2026 (to 2026-10) with canonical earlier anchors.

works.name: Genie 3 / Project Genie (Google DeepMind)
works.what: Autoregressive video world model that generates navigable environments from text at 720p/24 fps, with navigation actions and 'promptable world events' (text edits to the world mid-run). Consistency 'for several minutes', visual memory reaching back ~1 minute. Physics is entirely learned; no simulator, no object state. 2026 Project Genie exposes it to Ultra subscribers; secondary reports say it can be seeded from Street View imagery.
works.params_from: none (no explicit physical parameters or object state exist; all behaviour is emergent in pixels)
works.evaluated_against: none published (no quantitative physics or persistence evaluation; only demos and a stated limitations list)
works.scale: single-user, minutes of interaction, room-to-landscape scenes rendered as video; no persistent 3D representation
works.limitations: Stated by DeepMind: 'limited action space', no simulation of other agents, no geographic accuracy, 'a few minutes of continuous interaction'. Secondary 2026 commentary reports collision failures (figures walk through cacti) - unconfirmed from a primary source. No way to query or set a parameter; cannot be made to answer 'how heavy'.
works.confidence: high for capabilities/limitations (DeepMind blog); low for the collision-failure claim (newsletters only)

works.name: Matrix-Game 2.0 (Skywork) and the game-world-model class: Hunyuan-GameCraft / -2 (Tencent), Oasis (Decart/Etched), Mirage 2 (Dynamics Lab), Yan (Tencent)
works.year: 2025 (Matrix-Game 2.0 Aug; GameCraft Jun, GameCraft-2 Nov; Oasis Oct 2024; Mirage 2 Aug; Yan Aug)
works.source: arXiv 2508.13009 (Matrix-Game 2.0); arXiv 2506.17201 and 2511.23429 (GameCraft, GameCraft-2); https://github.com/etched-ai/open-oasis (Oasis 500M, MIT); arXiv 2508.08601 (Yan); Mirage 2 secondary only
works.what: Real-time streaming interactive video generation conditioned on keyboard/mouse. Matrix-Game 2.0: 1.8B, few-step causal autoregressive diffusion, 25 fps, minute-long rollouts, trained on ~1200 h of Unreal Engine and GTA5 footage with action labels. GameCraft-2: 14B I2V MoE adding text-driven interactions ('open the door', 'trigger an explosion') with its own InterBench. Oasis: ViT-VAE + DiT with diffusion forcing on Minecraft, ~20 fps. Yan: 3D-VAE for 1080p/60 fps simulation plus multimodal generation and mechanics/visual disentangled editing. All of them: no engine, no object state.
works.params_from: none (no physical parameters; dynamics come from game-engine footage, i.e. whatever UE/GTA5/Minecraft physics did in the training data)
works.evaluated_against: visual quality, action-following and temporal-consistency metrics on generated clips (GameWorld-style scores, InterBench, human preference); no comparison to real motion
works.scale: game worlds; real-time at 720p-1080p; minute-scale memory; single agent
works.limitations: Interaction = camera/avatar control (plus semantic events in GameCraft-2); physics is whatever the source engine did and is unqueryable; drift and forgetting when looking away (documented for Oasis); 'interactable' means the avatar moves, not that objects carry properties. Matrix-Game 2.0 abstract gives no physics metric at all.
works.confidence: high for Matrix-Game 2.0/GameCraft/Yan/Oasis (arXiv + GitHub); medium for Mirage 2 (press only)

works.name: Cosmos-Predict2.5 / Cosmos-Transfer2.5 (NVIDIA), succeeded by Cosmos 3 (June 2026)
works.what: Predict2.5: flow-based world foundation model (2B/14B) unifying text/image/video-to-world, Cosmos-Reason1 as text encoder, 200M clips, RL post-training; Transfer2.5 is a ControlNet-style sim2real/real2real translator (3.5x smaller than Transfer1). Cosmos 3: mixture-of-transformers 'omnimodel' (Super ~32B, Nano ~8B per press; Edge coming) that understands/generates text, image, video, audio and robot actions ('world-action model'). NVIDIA claims first place on Physics-IQ, PAI-Bench, R-Bench, RoboLab, RoboArena without numbers in the release.
works.params_from: none (learned video prior; physics only via data and RL preference post-training)
works.evaluated_against: Physics-IQ (real-video benchmark) and others per NVIDIA's claim; Predict2.5 paper reports video-quality / instruction-alignment gains over Predict1; secondary sources cite Cosmos3-Super i2v at 39.5 on Physics-IQ with Magi-1 24B at 58.2 and Sora 2 at 26.5 (unverified)
works.scale: foundation-model scale; robotics/AV/warehouse scenes; not real-time except Nano ('fractions of a second')
works.limitations: No object-level state or parameter interface; physics correctness is a dataset-and-preference property; the project already measured Cosmos-3-Nano as a judge at chance (rho ~0 with density/damping/friction), consistent with Physics-IQ-class findings that visual realism and physical understanding are unrelated.
works.confidence: high for Predict2.5 (arXiv); medium for Cosmos 3 details (press release, no numbers); low for the 39.5 Physics-IQ figure (Chinese secondary article)

works.name: V-JEPA 2 / V-JEPA 2-AC as a planning world model (Meta)
works.what: Frozen V-JEPA 2 video encoder plus a ~300M block-causal predictor trained on <62 h of unlabeled Droid robot video with 7-D end-effector delta actions (teacher-forcing + 2-step rollout loss). Planning = CEM over action sequences minimising L1 between predicted latent and an image-goal latent. Zero-shot on Franka arms in two labs: reach 100%, grasp 65% avg (cup 65 / box 25), pick-and-place 72.5% avg (cup 80 / box 65); ~16 s per action vs ~4 min for a Cosmos video-generation baseline (which got 0% pick-and-place).
works.params_from: none (latent dynamics; no explicit physics quantities)
works.evaluated_against: real robot success rates; latent planning is scored by task outcome, not by physical fidelity
works.scale: tabletop, single arm, short horizons with subgoals
works.limitations: Stated: implicit camera-frame inference requires manual camera placement; error accumulation over long horizons; goals must be images. What the latent encodes about mass/friction is not tested here (see PokeWorld entry); the project already measured V-JEPA 2 surprise at chance on impossible motion in its renders.
works.confidence: high (arXiv HTML read; intuitive-physics tables not read)

works.name: Principia: Relational Physics Tests for Video Models
works.what: Benchmark of eight laws (gravity, restitution, friction, rotational inertia, projectile, momentum, pendulum, mass-spring) tested relationally: paired objects obeying the same law must be consistent, scored in image space with a calibration-independent consistency score, on real recorded scenes under controlled protocols. Six video generators evaluated; VLMs also tested as violation detectors.
works.params_from: n.a. (benchmark; ground truth is real recorded motion of paired objects)
works.evaluated_against: real motion (recorded pairs); result: no generator exceeds 0.42 while all score ~0.8 on VBench; best VLM 67% at detecting relational violations, most near chance
works.scale: tabletop lab scenes
works.limitations: Relational only, so absolute parameters (a specific mu or e) are not recovered or tested; generative models only, not interactive/action-conditioned ones.

works.name: WRBench / 'Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core' (plus WBench and WorldMark as the other 2026 interactive-WM benchmarks)
works.source: arXiv 2606.20545 (WRBench); arXiv 2605.25874 (WBench, 289 cases / 1,058 turns, 20 models, 22 automatic sub-metrics mixing specialist vision models and LMMs); arXiv 2604.21686 (WorldMark, 10 models, 500 cases, per-axis control-systems metrics)
works.what: WRBench treats camera motion as an observability intervention: start an event, look away, look back, and check whether the returning target advanced while unseen. 9,600 videos over 23 models in four control paradigms. Finding: every model keeps 'the observed world as a tracking shot', resuming the target in the state it was abandoned; this holds across families, scales and architectures.
works.params_from: n.a. (benchmarks); physics compliance in WBench is judged by vision models + LMMs validated against human ratings; WorldMark does not score physics at all
works.evaluated_against: VLM/LMM judges and human ratings on generated video; no real-motion ground truth in any of the three
works.scale: generated clips, multi-turn interaction
works.limitations: The physics dimension in all three is a model-judged proxy (the same class of judge the project found at chance). WRBench's result is the strongest evidence that no interactive video world model carries a persistent physical state.

works.name: 'From Generation to Simulation: How Far Are World Models from Being True Simulators?' (survey of 200 works, 2018-Jun 2026)
works.what: Scores world-model literature against eight simulator capabilities (asset construction, physics engine, interaction, controllability, stability, state feedback, diversity, evaluation). Defines three physics-integration levels: hard physics (the model is a differentiable physics engine, e.g. OrbiSim, PIN-WM), soft constraints (physics as guidance), physical evaluation (post-hoc benchmarks only).
works.params_from: n.a. (survey)
works.evaluated_against: n.a.; key statistic: 'only 6 of 163 implementation papers expose a runtime interface for queryable entity states or physical parameters'; also notes the literature gives 'little comparable evidence on seed control, deterministic execution, tolerance bands, or repeat-run variance'
works.scale: n.a.
works.limitations: Does not name the six compliant papers in the portion read; a capability map, not a measurement.
works.confidence: high for the quoted statements (HTML read); the six papers not identified

works.name: PokeWorld: 'What can latent world models know? Physical parameter identifiability' (plus ACWM-Phys, arXiv 2605.08567)
works.what: 2-D force-controlled finger pushes visually identical objects whose mass [0.5,3] log-uniform, drag [0.5,4], contact stiffness [500,6000] log-uniform are hidden; ~5M-parameter JEPA-style latent world models with multi-horizon heads; ridge-probe R^2 on the latents. ACWM-Phys does the analogous test for action-conditioned video DiTs over rigid/deformable/particle regimes with in- and out-of-distribution shifts.
works.params_from: simulator ground truth (the point is to test whether latents recover them)
works.evaluated_against: simulator parameters (R^2) and a real-robot replication on RH20T (4,258 episodes): contact force readable only when touch is both input and prediction target (R^2 0.88 vs -0.16 vision-only)
works.scale: toy 2-D (PokeWorld); tabletop video (ACWM-Phys)
works.limitations: Latent readout of log-mass R^2 0.21-0.25 vs 0.71 supervised reference; drag 0.12-0.14 vs 0.41; stiffness goes from -0.01 to 0.43 only when touch is a prediction target. I.e. a vision-only predictive world model barely encodes mass or friction-like quantities; ACWM-Phys finds video world models 'depend heavily on visual appearance patterns'. Both are small-scale and synthetic.
works.confidence: high (HTML read for PokeWorld); medium for ACWM-Phys (abstract)

works.name: Force Prompting (NeurIPS 2025) and Goal Force (2026)
works.what: Fine-tunes CogVideoX-5B-I2V with a ControlNet so a video model follows force prompts: global wind (magnitude, angle) and local point forces (a Gaussian blob moving distance proportional to F). Trained on ~15k Blender flag videos plus ~23k ball-rolling/plant videos (the plants via PhysDreamer), ~1 day on 4 A100s. Goal Force extends to specifying goals as force vectors trained on synthetic causal primitives (collisions, dominos).
works.params_from: none at inference (no simulator); training videos carry simulator forces but the model is conditioned on force only, never on mass/friction
works.evaluated_against: human studies (N=10) on force adherence/physics/quality vs text-only and Motion Prompting; a qualitative mass test (soccer ball moves farther than bowling ball under equal force)
works.scale: single clips, single image, 49 frames
works.limitations: The 'mass awareness' is a one-pair qualitative observation, not a sweep; response cannot be inverted for a parameter; inherits the base video prior's failures off-domain. Same architecture family the project found yields seed-set speeds (Wan) and no object dependence.

works.name: PhysGen (ECCV 2024) and PhysMotion (2024)
works.what: Training-free image-to-video: GPT-4V estimates each segmented object's mass (g), Coulomb friction and elasticity (0-1); a 2-D rigid-body engine (Pymunk, 1 px = 1 cm, 120 steps) simulates under a user force/torque; a diffusion model refines the rendered motion. PhysMotion lifts the same idea to 3-D Gaussians with MPM.
works.params_from: VLM (GPT-4V) commonsense per object
works.evaluated_against: user study (14 raters, physical realism 4.14/5) and Image-/Motion-FID against 50 real reference videos; no per-object parameter check
works.scale: single image, in-plane rigid motion
works.limitations: Authors: rigid only, 2-D image-space, no out-of-plane motion. Parameters are never validated; the project's e1 result (LLM numbers 3x worse than a material table) applies directly to this parameter source.

works.name: WonderPlay (ICCV 2025), with PhysDreamer (2024), DreamPhysics (2024), PhysGaussian (CVPR 2024), PhysCtrl (NeurIPS 2025) as the same lane
works.what: WonderPlay: single image -> 3-D scene -> Genesis solvers (shape-matching rigid, MPM for elastic/liquid/granular, PBD for cloth/smoke) -> coarse dynamics condition a video generator -> generated video updates the 3-D scene via photometric L1. PhysDreamer/DreamPhysics: differentiable MPM on 3-D Gaussians with Young's modulus fields distilled from video-diffusion priors. PhysGaussian: MPM directly on Gaussian kernels. PhysCtrl: a diffusion model over 3-D point trajectories trained on 550K simulator animations (elastic, sand, plasticine, rigid), conditioned on physics parameters and forces.
works.params_from: VLM 6-way material class and VLM-estimated parameter values 'with optional manual adjustment' (WonderPlay); video-diffusion SDS (PhysDreamer/DreamPhysics); user-set (PhysGaussian); given as conditioning, not estimated (PhysCtrl)
works.evaluated_against: 2AFC user studies (WonderPlay: 200 raters, 70-80% preference), VBench, GPT-4o physical-realism scores; PhysDreamer user study on realism; PhysCtrl visual quality/plausibility; none against measured real motion of the same object
works.scale: 15 scenes (WonderPlay); single objects; demonstration scale
works.limitations: All demo-scale, parameter sources are VLM/diffusion priors/manual, and the evaluation is preference or VLM-judged. This lane is crowded (dozens of Gaussian+MPM papers) and none closes the loop on real motion.
works.confidence: high for WonderPlay/PhysGen (HTML read); medium for the others (abstracts/secondary)

works.name: PhysWorld: Robot Learning from a Physical World Model (DeepMind/USC/Stanford/TRI)
works.what: Generate a task video (Veo 3), reconstruct a metric digital twin (MegaSaM depth, image-to-3D meshes, RANSAC gravity alignment, SDF-based penetration removal), then learn an object-centric residual RL policy in simulation that tracks the generated video's object poses (FoundationPose). 82% average real-world success over 10 tasks vs 67% for RIGVid; grasp failures 18% -> 3%; usable-video ratio Veo 3 70% vs CogVideoX 4%.
works.params_from: VLM 'typical physical parameters' per object category (mass, friction)
works.evaluated_against: real robot task success; the physics parameters themselves are never checked against motion
works.scale: tabletop, single-view, 10 tasks
works.limitations: Authors: bounded by simulator fidelity and extra sim-to-real gaps; ~7% of failures from occluded-geometry reconstruction. Physics parameters are a VLM prior, exactly the source the project measured as generic (~0.4 for everything).

works.name: PIN-WM (RSS 2025) and OrbiSim (hard-physics world models)
works.source: arXiv 2504.16693 (PIN-WM); OrbiSim is described in arXiv 2608.23070's physics-engine section (own arXiv id not located)
works.what: PIN-WM: identify a 3-D rigid-body dynamical system end-to-end from images using differentiable physics simulation and a Gaussian-splatting observation loss, from few-shot task-agnostic interaction trajectories; the identified model is then perturbed into 'digital cousins' for sim-to-real non-prehensile manipulation. OrbiSim (per the survey): an object-centric differentiable physics core computing position/velocity/configuration in explicit, queryable state, with a state-guided diffusion model used purely as a neural renderer; claims parameter inference (mass, friction, elasticity) and better prediction/control than video world models.
works.params_from: fit by gradients through a differentiable simulator from the robot's own interaction video (PIN-WM); inferred from observations (OrbiSim)
works.evaluated_against: PIN-WM: simulation and real-robot pushing tasks vs Real2Sim2Real baselines; OrbiSim: prediction fidelity and control (details unread)
works.scale: tabletop rigid bodies; few objects
works.limitations: Both are the structurally closest existing designs to 'differentiable engine + neural view'. Neither reports held-out real-object parameter validation against measured motion, neither goes beyond a table, and OrbiSim's primary text could not be located.
works.confidence: high for PIN-WM existence/claims (arXiv abstract); low for OrbiSim (survey description only)

works.name: MOSIV: Multi-Object System Identification from Videos (ICLR 2026)
works.what: Multi-view video of two contact-rich interacting objects -> object-aware 4-D Gaussians -> Gaussian-to-continuum particle lifting -> custom differentiable MPM (dt 1/4800, 200 substeps per 24 fps frame) optimising per-object constitutive parameters (E, nu; yield stress; viscosity, bulk modulus; sand friction angle) against geometry-aligned objectives.
works.params_from: fit by gradients through differentiable MPM to video
works.evaluated_against: synthetic only: 45 Genesis-rendered sequences (10 geometries, 5 materials, 11 views, 30 frames); PSNR 30.51 vs 25.93 (OmniPhysGS), Chamfer 1.256 vs 11.79 mm^2; future prediction PSNR 28.26 vs 19.00
works.scale: two objects on a table; 5,021 s per sequence on one A6000 (29.8 GB)
works.limitations: Authors: relies on predefined constitutive models, computationally intensive, sensitive to initial geometry, and 'extending ... to real-world videos with complex lighting and noise also remains challenging'. No real footage at all.

works.name: UrbanVerse: Scaling Urban Simulation by Watching City-Tour Videos (ICLR 2026); related: PhysEditWorld (2606.26694), SimWorld (2512.01078)
works.what: Real-to-sim at city scale: crowd-sourced city-tour videos -> layout extraction -> retrieval from UrbanVerse-100K (100k+ urban assets) -> metric-scale IsaacSim scenes with rigid-body dynamics; 160 scenes from 24 countries plus 10 artist test scenes. Each asset carries 36 attributes (semantic, affordance, physical incl. mass and friction). PhysEditWorld: UE5 replay dataset (12 scenes, 100+ h, 60M frames) varying gravity with engine states exposed. SimWorld: UE5 open-ended simulator for LLM/VLM agents.
works.params_from: GPT-4.1 from a thumbnail and four yaw snapshots ('we leverage the world knowledge of GPT-4.1 ... to annotate each asset with semantic, affordance, and physical attributes'; ~$1,334 API cost)
works.evaluated_against: human realism ratings 'comparable to manually crafted scenes'; navigation policy zero-shot sim-to-real +30.1%, a 300 m real mission with two interventions. No validation of any physical attribute against real motion.
works.scale: city blocks; 100k assets; PhysX (IsaacSim), not differentiable
works.limitations: The only beyond-room sim-ready pipeline found, and its physics numbers are LLM guesses, unvalidated; the downstream test (navigation) barely exercises contact physics. PhysEditWorld edits only gravity.
works.confidence: high (HTML read for the annotation section)

gaps: No interactive neural world model (Genie 3, Matrix-Game 2.0, GameCraft-2, Oasis, Mirage 2, Yan, Cosmos 3) exposes per-object physical state or parameters, or lets a user set one. Evidence: the 2026 survey (arXiv 2608.23070) counts 6 of 163 implementation papers with any runtime state/parameter interface; the Genie 3 blog lists only navigation and text events; Matrix-Game 2.0 / GameCraft abstracts describe keyboard/mouse/text conditioning only. Searches for 'interactive world model object physical properties' returned only toy identifiability studies (PokeWorld) and tabletop system-ID (PIN-WM, OrbiSim, MOSIV).

No beyond-room 'physics-ready' world pipeline validates its assigned parameters against real motion. Evidence: UrbanVerse (ICLR 2026) assigns mass/friction to 100k assets with GPT-4.1 and evaluates only human realism and navigation transfer; PhysWorld uses VLM 'typical' values; WonderPlay uses VLM + manual; PhysGen uses GPT-4V. Searched 'city-scale ... physics parameters per object friction mass validated real motion' and 'sim-ready ... held-out real object' and found nothing with a held-out real-motion check. Combined with the project's own e1 result (LLM numbers 3x worse than a material table), this is the same gap already observed for PhysX-3D/VoMP et al., now confirmed at city scale.

No differentiable-physics world model exists beyond tabletop scale. Evidence: the survey's 'hard physics' exemplars (OrbiSim, PIN-WM) are rigid-body tabletop systems; MOSIV is two objects on a table, synthetic only, 84 minutes per sequence; UrbanVerse and SimWorld run non-differentiable engines (PhysX/UE5). Searched '"world model" "differentiable physics" ... interactive' (extended) and found no outdoor- or building-scale differentiable physics core.

No benchmark scores an interactive (action-conditioned) world model against real recorded outcomes of a controlled applied action. Evidence: Physics-IQ and Principia use real video but evaluate generative models with fixed conditioning; WBench scores physics with 22 sub-metrics built from specialist vision models and LMMs, WorldMark scores no physics, WRBench and PhyWorldBench use VLM/human judgment of generated clips. Searched 'interactive world model benchmark real recorded interaction ground truth' and found none.

No persistent physical state in any interactive video world model: WRBench (arXiv 2606.20545, 9,600 videos, 23 models, four control paradigms) finds every model resumes a looked-away object in the state it was left, independent of family, scale or architecture. Nobody has shown a persistent physics-state kernel driving a neural renderer at scene scale; the closest (OrbiSim) is tabletop and its primary text was not found.

No force-conditioned or physics-controllable video model has been subjected to a rule-1 style parameter sweep. Evidence: Force Prompting's mass evidence is one qualitative soccer-vs-bowling-ball pair; PhysCtrl conditions on parameters but reports visual quality/plausibility; PhysEditWorld varies only gravity; ACWM-Phys and PokeWorld show latents encode mass with R^2 0.21-0.25 and drag 0.12-0.14 in a 2-D toy. Searched 'force prompting mass friction sweep correlation' variants; no monotonicity/range test against a simulator or real motion was found.

Restitution is unmeasured everywhere in this landscape: Principia tests restitution only relationally; no world model or sim-ready pipeline reports recovering per-object restitution from video, and no public >=240 fps real-object bounce dataset beyond Bounce-and-Learn (one ball, many surfaces) was found. Searched 'restitution from video high frame rate dataset world model' and related terms.

Determinism is unreported: the survey notes the world-model literature gives 'little comparable evidence on seed control, deterministic execution, tolerance bands, or repeat-run variance'; none of the interactive world models above reports repeat-run variance of an outcome under identical actions.
scouts.relevance_to_our_assets: The project's validated assets sit almost exactly in the hole this landscape leaves open. The exact-mesh, differentiable Newton/Warp contact stack, fitted to real Physics 101 slides at 0.4-1.0 mm RMS and with per-body queryable mass/friction/restitution/CoM, is the 'state feedback' and 'hard physics' capability the 2026 survey finds in 6 of 163 world-model papers and that OrbiSim/PIN-WM claim only on a tabletop without held-out real-object validation; nothing in the interactive-world-model class (Genie 3, Matrix-Game 2.0, Cosmos 3) has a state to query at all, and WRBench shows they do not keep one. The real-footage pipeline (CoTracker3 + simulator fits, invariant checks, 11 of 15 materials, the 70-object held-out test) is the piece every scale pipeline lacks: UrbanVerse assigns mass and friction to 100k city assets with GPT-4.1 and never checks them, PhysWorld and WonderPlay use VLM typical values, PhysGen uses GPT-4V, and e1 already shows that route is 3x worse than a measured material table while an LLM naming the material costs only 0.1 mm, so the project's 'name with an LLM, number from a measured table, verify with an invariant' recipe is a direct, tested replacement for the parameter-assignment stage of those pipelines, at any scale, since the per-material table is what scales rather than per-object fitting. Three of the project's assets are redundant with or superseded by this landscape and should not be re-run: the render-and-judge probes (Cosmos judge, V-JEPA surprise, FPT/MYRIAD/Wan readouts) replicate what Physics-IQ, Principia (VLM violation detection 67%), PhyWorldBench and PokeWorld (mass R^2 ~0.2 in latents) now report, so the negative results are confirmation rather than a lead; the soft-body/MPM material-inference lane (PhysDreamer, DreamPhysics, PhysGaussian, MOSIV, GausSim) is crowded, differentiable-MPM-based, and ahead of the project's diverging soft-press probe; and VLM-estimated per-object parameters are what the project measured as a generic ~0.4 prior. What the assets could feed is therefore the physics-core side of a hybrid (OrbiSim/PIN-WM shape) or the parameter-validation side of a UrbanVerse-shape pipeline; the restitution gap (>=240 fps phone capture is within the project's constraints) is open across the whole landscape; and the determinism/seeded-repeatability discipline the project already enforces is a reportable property no interactive world model documents.
scouts.caveats: Several 2026 entries (Principia, WRBench, WBench, WorldMark, ACWM-Phys, Goal Force, GigaWorld-0, 'Physically Viable World Models', Hunyuan-GameCraft-2, Cosmos-Predict2.5) were read from arXiv abstract pages only; numbers quoted from them are as stated in the abstracts. OrbiSim's own arXiv id was not located; its description comes entirely from the survey arXiv 2608.23070 and is low confidence. Cosmos 3's Physics-IQ figure (39.5 Super i2v; Magi-1 58.2; Sora 2 26.5) comes from a Chinese secondary article and NVIDIA's release gives rankings without numbers; the project's own cited Wan 2.2 Physics-IQ Verified 32.2 and Sora 2 26.5 were not re-verified here, and no Veo 3 figure was confirmed. The claim that Genie 3 lets figures pass through objects is from newsletters, not DeepMind. V-JEPA 2's intuitive-physics tables (IntPhys/GRASP/InfLevel) were in the unread half of the paper. Decart's Oasis article returned 404; the GitHub README (open-oasis, MIT) was used. Mirage 2 and Yan were covered as a class; Yan's arXiv (2508.08601) abstract was seen via search only. IntPhys 2, Physics-IQ, PhysTwin, gradSim, CoDimRecon and the other works the task listed as already known were deliberately not re-entered; Physics-IQ numbers (396 videos / 66 scenarios, VideoPoet 29.5%, Sora 10.0%, r = -0.46 with visual realism) were read from the HTML and are available if needed. The gap claims rest on targeted searches that returned nothing matching; absence from search is weaker evidence than a published negative.

scouts.angle: Real-to-sim beyond single rooms: street/city/driving-scale reconstructions and simulators, building/campus-scale embodied-AI environments, and "digital twin at scale" efforts. Question asked of each: where contact physics (mass, friction, restitution) lives, whether it is measured or validated against real motion, and what "interaction" means at that scale.

works.name: Driving-scene neural reconstruction family: OmniRe (ICLR 2025), with UniSim (CVPR 2023), NeuRAD (CVPR 2024), Street Gaussians (ECCV 2024) and MatrixCity (ICCV 2023) as the canonical lineage
works.source: OmniRe arXiv 2408.16760 / ziyc.github.io/omnire; UniSim arXiv 2308.01898; NeuRAD arXiv 2311.15260; Street Gaussians arXiv 2401.01339; MatrixCity arXiv 2309.16553
works.what: Reconstruct a driving log as an editable scene graph of neural fields / 3D Gaussians (background + per-actor nodes: rigid vehicles, SMPL pedestrians, deformation fields for far actors) and re-render novel trajectories; 'simulation' = replaying or editing node poses and SMPL joints (OmniRe), or re-synthesising sensor data for new ego/actor trajectories (UniSim). MatrixCity is the synthetic counterpart: 28 km2 of UE5 City Sample, 67k aerial + 452k street images, for city-scale NVS only.
works.params_from: none. OmniRe paper: 'reconstructed assets that can be flexibly edited in terms of position and rotation'; interaction scenarios are 'reenacted', no physics engine, collision or contact is mentioned. MatrixCity abstract: no physics or interaction.
works.evaluated_against: Rendering metrics only: PSNR/SSIM on full image and on human/vehicle regions, depth RMSE / Chamfer vs LiDAR (OmniRe on 32 Waymo dynamic scenes, ~150 frames each; extended to nuScenes, Argoverse2, PandaSet, KITTI, nuPlan). UniSim additionally reports small sim-to-real domain gap on downstream autonomy tasks.
works.scale: Per-log street segments (hundreds of metres, ~15 s); city map scale only in MatrixCity (28 km2, synthetic, static).
works.limitations: No dynamics of any kind: actors are kinematic pose sequences; no lighting model; novel views degrade away from the captured trajectory. Mass/friction/restitution do not exist in these representations.
works.confidence: high for OmniRe and MatrixCity (read from arXiv HTML/abs); medium for UniSim/NeuRAD/Street Gaussians actor-control details (abstract-level only)

works.name: HUGSIM: real-time, photo-realistic, closed-loop AD simulator
works.what: Lifts KITTI-360 / Waymo / nuScenes / PandaSet logs into 3DGS and closes the loop: ego state updated from control commands, actors from behaviour models, observations re-rendered. 70+ sequences, 400+ scenarios at 4 difficulty levels; evaluates UniAD, VAD, Latent-Transfuser with an HD-Score (route completion x safety x comfort).
works.params_from: none. Ego = discrete kinematic bicycle model with LQR; actors = unicycle model with IDM (normal) or adversarial optimisation (aggressive). Collision = BEV bounding-box overlap for actors and, for background, 'counting the number of background Gaussians inside the ego vehicle's 3D bounding box' (ground Gaussians excluded). No contact forces, friction or mass.
works.evaluated_against: Closed-loop driving metrics (NC, DAC, TTC, comfort, route completion) and NVS quality; no real-motion validation of any dynamics.
works.scale: Per-sequence urban street segments; 4 datasets, 70+ sequences.
works.limitations: Authors note the absence of a physics engine (kinematic models only), RGB-only algorithms, missing HD maps for aggressive actors on some datasets.

works.name: Generative driving world models: Cosmos-Drive-Dreams (NVIDIA) and NVIDIA OmniDreams
works.source: Cosmos-Drive-Dreams arXiv 2506.09042, github nv-tlabs/Cosmos-Drive-Dreams; OmniDreams arXiv 2606.03159 (research.nvidia.com/labs/sil)
