works.what: Cosmos-Drive specialises the Cosmos WFM to generate controllable multi-view driving video conditioned on HD maps / LiDAR; the released dataset is 81,802 clips with paired HDMap and LiDAR, used to improve 3D lane / object detection and policy training. OmniDreams runs the same idea closed-loop: sensor frames generated autoregressively from past frames, simulator state and the policy's actions.
works.params_from: none / n.a. The scene has no explicit physical state; dynamics are whatever the video model emits.
works.evaluated_against: Downstream perception / policy metrics on generated data; NVIDIA's own framing says current WFMs 'fall short as reliable simulators of the physical world'.
works.scale: Street scenes, per clip; dataset of 81.8k clips.
works.limitations: No object-level physical parameters; closed-loop dynamics are generative, not simulated. Same model class the project already measured as carrying no theta (Cosmos-3, Wan 2.2).
works.confidence: medium (abstracts, project pages and NVIDIA press; full OmniDreams paper not read)

works.name: Waymo Open Sim Agents Challenge (WOSAC)
works.what: Benchmark for 'sim agents': given 1 s of history, emit 32 futures of 8 s of x/y/z boxes + heading for every agent; realism scored by likelihood of the logged future under histogram/KDE approximations of kinematic (speed, acceleration), interactive (collision, TTC, distance) and map (off-road, traffic-light) features.
works.params_from: none. The challenge page states 'We do not enforce any motion model'; agents report coordinates directly.
works.evaluated_against: Distributional realism vs logged Waymo Open Motion trajectories; 2025 adds traffic-light violation and a TTC vehicle filter.
works.scale: Full WOMD (tens of thousands of 9 s scenarios); city-wide coverage but trajectory-level only.
works.limitations: No vehicle dynamics, contact or mass; 'interaction' means avoiding bounding-box overlap. This is the de-facto standard for what 'interactive' means in driving simulation.

works.name: Vid2Sim: Realistic and Interactive Simulation from Video for Urban Navigation
works.what: Monocular web video of a sidewalk -> geometry-regularised 3DGS -> TSDF mesh for collision -> Unity scene (GS for visuals, mesh for physics) with obstacle/scene augmentation -> RL navigation policy -> real four-wheeled delivery robot.
works.params_from: none stated. Unity 'real-time physics'; robot is a bicycle model (0.8 m wheelbase, 30 deg max steer). No mass, friction or restitution for environment or robot is documented.
works.evaluated_against: Real-world zero-shot deployment: 85% / 65% / 55% success on go-straight / static-obstacle / dynamic-obstacle, 20 trials each; sim success +31.2%, real +68.3% vs prior sim training.
works.scale: 30 reconstructed urban scenes from web videos, each >= 3 m wide x 20 m long.
works.limitations: Authors: GLOMAP initialisation is slow, so only 30 environments. Interaction = collision with a static mesh; nothing in the scene is movable; no contact parameter is identified or validated.

works.name: URBAN-SIM / MetaUrban: scalable urban simulation for micromobility
works.year: 2024 (MetaUrban, arXiv Jul 2024; ICLR 2025) and 2025 (URBAN-SIM, CVPR 2025 highlight)
works.what: Procedural urban street generation with static obstacles, pedestrians (ORCA), terrain (flat/slope/stairs/rough) and 4 robot morphologies (wheeled, quadruped, wheeled-legged, humanoid). MetaUrban: Panda3D rendering on MetaDrive's architecture, 12,800 train + 1,000 test scenes, 10k obstacle assets, ~20,000 m2 per scene, 410 m episodes. URBAN-SIM: 'built on top of Nvidia's Omniverse and PhysX 5', 15k static + 1,620 dynamic assets, scenes from 25 m2 to 200,000+ m2 (Urban-Tra-City 1.44 million m2), 1,800-2,600 fps over 256 parallel envs on one L40S.
works.params_from: table / designer-set. URBAN-SIM: terrain 'friction coefficients varied across 8 texture types'; MetaUrban: 'texture-based friction coefficients' per ground material; objects are collision boxes; robots from URDF. No per-object mass/friction provenance; nothing measured.
works.evaluated_against: sim-only (URBAN-BENCH: 8 tasks across locomotion / navigation / traverse). URBAN-SIM: 'None reported' for real-world; sim-to-real pipeline listed as future work. MetaUrban: no real-world deployment.
works.scale: Street block to 1.44 km2 (synthetic).
works.limitations: Interaction = collision avoidance and terrain traversal; no pushable / graspable objects; friction is a per-texture label, never identified or checked against motion.

works.name: UrbanVerse: Scaling Urban Simulation by Watching City-Tour Videos
works.what: Crowdsourced city-tour videos -> scene distillation (YOLO-World, SAM2, MASt3R) -> retrieve matching assets from UrbanVerse-100K (102,444 objects, 659 categories, 306 sky HDRIs, 288 ground materials) by CLIP/DINOv2 -> instantiate 'physics-ready' Isaac Sim / URBAN-SIM scenes with ORCA pedestrians; 160 auto-generated scenes from 24 countries + 10 artist test scenes (CraftBench), ~200 m routes.
works.params_from: VLM. Each asset annotated by GPT-4.1 from thumbnails/multi-view snapshots with mass, friction and 31 other attributes. Appendix C.4 checks 1,335 objects in 17 categories with public specifications: geometric attributes 1-8% MAPE, mass ~19.6% MAPE 'attributed to material uncertainty'. Friction is not validated anywhere; no motion-based check.
works.evaluated_against: Navigation policy: 41.9% vs 35.6% (MBRA) on CraftBench; real zero-shot 77.1% (wheeled) and 89.7% (quadruped) vs 47.9/58.6 (S2E); 337 m mission with 2 interventions. Scene fidelity on KITTI-360: 93.1% category recovery, 1.4 m position / 19.8 deg orientation error, 75.1% retrieval accuracy; human realism 3.58/5 vs artist 4.08/5.
works.scale: Street-level, ~200 m per scene, 160 scenes; 100k-asset library.
works.limitations: Street-level only (parks, campuses, indoor-outdoor transitions excluded); depth/pose drift in low light / fast motion; no evidence objects are movable by the robot (navigation = avoidance). The GPT mass check is against spec sheets, not motion, and friction is unchecked.

works.name: GRUtopia: Dream General Robots in a City at Scale
works.what: Isaac Sim platform with GRScenes (100k interactive annotated scenes in 89 categories; 100 released across 7 building types with 2,956 interactive and 22,001 non-interactive objects), NPC social system, and GRBench (object loco-navigation, social loco-navigation, loco-manipulation). Scenes can be composed into city-level environments.
works.params_from: artist / undisclosed. 'Professional teams modify these assets and create complete objects to make them interactable in a physically plausible manner'; no statement of how mass, friction or joint parameters are set.
works.evaluated_against: sim-only benchmarks; humanoid loco-nav 58% / quadruped 14% in clutter; mobile manipulation 0% success 'due to collision handling and planning challenges'.
works.scale: Building to city-level composition (synthetic).
works.limitations: Physical parameter provenance undisclosed; manipulation does not work yet at this scale; no real-world validation.

works.name: Infinigen Indoors (CVPR 2024) and Infinigen-Sim (articulated sim-ready assets)
works.source: Infinigen Indoors arXiv 2406.11824; Infinigen-Sim arXiv 2505.10755 (v3 Oct 2025)
works.what: Blender procedural generators: Indoors = 79 generators (641 parameters), constraint DSL + simulated-annealing solver with a 'StableAgainst' relation (no gravity settling), export to Isaac Sim and UE5 with URDF collision/articulation. Infinigen-Sim = 18 articulated categories with joints, exported to URDF/USD/MJCF with joint stiffness/damping and material 'friction and density'.
works.params_from: table / sampled distributions. Infinigen-Sim includes 'distributions for joint dynamics parameters' and material friction and density; the paper does not say whether these are measured or chosen ranges (GitHub doc page returned 404).
works.evaluated_against: Downstream only: part segmentation (+1.3 mAP on handles), RL generalisation (2.86x success over PartNet-Mobility), sim-to-real imitation on a Franka (door 18/30 vs 3/30). No comparison of simulated vs real object dynamics.
works.scale: Multi-room, multi-floor buildings; ~29 objects per scene.
works.limitations: Joints modelled independently; CoACD collision meshes slow simulation; physical values are generator ranges, never validated.
works.confidence: high for structure (arXiv HTML read); medium for the provenance of friction/density values

works.name: AI2-THOR lineage at scale: ProcTHOR (NeurIPS 2022) -> Holodeck (CVPR 2024) -> MolmoSpaces (2026)
works.source: AI2-THOR docs ai2thor.allenai.org/ithor/documentation/environment-state; Holodeck arXiv 2312.09067; MolmoSpaces arXiv 2602.11337
works.what: Unity-physics houses: ProcTHOR procedurally generates 10k+ houses; Holodeck has GPT-4 lay out Objaverse assets (50k) by constraints; MolmoSpaces scales to 230k indoor environments, 130k annotated assets, 48k manipulable objects with 42M grasps, simulator-agnostic (MuJoCo, Isaac, ManiSkill) with MolmoSpaces-Bench (8 tasks).
works.params_from: artist for THOR assets (metadata has 'mass of a Pickupable or Moveable sim object in Kilograms' and salientMaterials; method unstated), VLM for the Objaverse expansion: MolmoSpaces uses 'mass estimates, canonical poses, pickable and receptacle properties ... generated by GPT-4o'; colliders by CoACD or human-annotated primitives.
works.evaluated_against: MolmoSpaces: sim-to-real correlation of policy rankings on 752 RoboArena pick tasks, Pearson 0.96 / Spearman 0.98 (Franka FR3, DROID config; RB-Y1 for navigation); scene QA pass rates >95% in MuJoCo (stability, liftability, articulation). Parameter values themselves are not validated against motion.
works.scale: Houses (multi-room), 230k of them.
works.limitations: Validation is at the policy-ranking level, which is insensitive to whether individual mass/friction values are right; parameter provenance is GPT-4o or unstated artist choice.
works.confidence: high (MolmoSpaces HTML and AI2-THOR docs read); medium for ProcTHOR/Holodeck specifics

works.name: Habitat 2.0/3.0 with ReplicaCAD and HSSD; RoboCasa
works.source: Habitat 2.0 arXiv 2106.14405 / aihabitat.org/datasets/replica_cad; Habitat 3.0 arXiv 2310.13724; RoboCasa arXiv 2406.02523 (RSS 2024)
works.what: Habitat: Bullet-based home rearrangement with ReplicaCAD (90+ artist-rebuilt objects with convex collision and mass/friction/restitution) and HSSD (37/12/10 scenes for social nav); Habitat 3.0 adds humanoid avatars driven by pre-computed motion clips (kinematic) alongside a dynamic Spot. RoboCasa: 120 MuJoCo kitchens (10 floor plans x 12 styles), 2,509 objects in 153 categories, 1,592 of them from Luma text-to-3D.
works.params_from: artist (ReplicaCAD: 3D artists reproduced Replica with 'size and friction' attention); RoboCasa: unspecified -- assets converted to MJCF, no statement on mass/friction assignment.
works.evaluated_against: Policy success in sim; RoboCasa real Franka kitchen: 24.4% with sim co-training vs 13.6% real-only (seen objects), 9.3 vs 2.6% unseen. No object-dynamics validation.
works.scale: Apartment / kitchen; Habitat up to ~60 HSSD scenes, RoboCasa 120 kitchens.
works.limitations: Humanoids are kinematic; RoboCasa authors cite camera calibration, lighting and controller mismatch; physical values are artist or default.
works.confidence: medium (ReplicaCAD assignment from aihabitat.org and secondary pages; Habitat 3.0 humanoid mechanism inferred from HTML; RoboCasa HTML read)

works.name: LLM-assigned physics for reconstructed worlds: Video2Game (CVPR 2024) and RobotArena-infinity (2025)
works.what: Video2Game: NeRF -> mesh -> cannon.js physics in a browser game; colliders from boxes, spheres, V-HACD or simplified trimesh; demonstrated on Mip-NeRF-360 Garden, VR-NeRF apartment and a 16-block KITTI-360 loop. RobotArena-infinity: real demo videos (Bridge, DROID, RH20T) -> Gemini segmentation, Hunyuan-3D meshes, MoGe depth -> Genesis simulator; ~100 nominal environments with hundreds of perturbations, 7,000+ human preference judgements over 4 VLA policies.
works.params_from: VLM. Video2Game: 'query GPT-4 with box highlights' for a mass/friction/restitution range, then 'selecting a value within this range provides reasonable results'; static objects use defaults. RobotArena: mass, friction and surface type by 'prompting Gemini' with segmented objects; the paper states no validation of these.
works.evaluated_against: Video2Game: PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS and depth error only, 'no formal physics accuracy evaluation'. RobotArena: policy ranking vs human preference; one real-vs-sim task ('put carrot in plate') with consistent ranking.
works.scale: Street block (KITTI-360, 16 blocks) to tabletop.
works.limitations: Both acknowledge the parameter path is unvalidated; RobotArena notes simulators 'struggle with fine-grained contact dynamics'. This is the pattern the project measured as a generic prior (~0.4) for every object.

works.name: NVIDIA SimReady specification, Isaac Sim 5 / NuRec and the PhysicalAI SimReady warehouse assets
works.source: docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/simready/latest/simready-asset-creation/physics-best-practices.html; Isaac Sim arXiv 2606.03551; developer.nvidia.com NuRec blog
works.what: The asset-side 'digital twin at scale' stack: SimReady requires a USDPhysics Collider, a Mass in kg on each geometry prim, and a Physical Material 'that describes the static and dynamic friction of an asset along with its density and restitution values', all at metre scale. Isaac Sim ships warehouse layout builders / conveyor tools and (5.0) NuRec 3DGS neural rendering for real-to-sim; NVIDIA's own description: 'a particle cloud captures appearance only, and physical interaction requires separate collision geometry'.
works.params_from: artist. The best-practices page offers no material library, reference table or measurement protocol -- creators 'dial in these parameters to simulate specific material types' in the Physics Material panel.
works.evaluated_against: none at the parameter level. The Isaac Sim paper reports zero-shot RL navigation transfers and ORBIT-Surgical tasks but 'no systematic benchmarking of physics accuracy against measured real-world contact dynamics'.
works.scale: Warehouse / factory; 1,000 OpenUSD assets in the PhysicalAI dataset release.
works.limitations: Provenance of every mass/friction/restitution value is left to the artist; NuRec reconstructions carry no physics until a mesh is attached by hand.
works.confidence: high (spec page and arXiv read); medium for Isaac Sim 5 / NuRec details (NVIDIA blogs)

works.name: Identifying Terrain Physical Parameters from Vision (ETH RSL)
works.what: A physical decoder trained in simulation (legged_gym with procedural terrain) predicts per-foot terrain friction and stiffness from ANYmal proprioception; a vision network is then self-supervised from those labels to predict friction/stiffness densely in images, indoors and outdoors.
works.params_from: fit to real motion (robot-in-the-loop). Digital-twin check: real ANYmal D on a wet whiteboard vs high-friction ground, simulated twin initialised from the real state, 400 ms rollouts over 10 friction values 0.0-0.9; the decoder's estimate (~0.1 whiteboard, >0.4 ground) matches the best-fitting range (0.0-0.2 / 0.3-1.0); mean error 0.02+-0.08 vs baseline 0.33+-0.11. Dense vision prediction error 0.03+-0.05 (whiteboard), 0.00+-0.01 (ground), confidence-mask IoU 0.82.
works.evaluated_against: real motion (joint position, base orientation, foot-slip errors) on manually reconstructed flat rigid surfaces.
works.scale: Outdoor terrain patches traversed by one quadruped; no object parameters.
works.limitations: Only the robot's footing friction/stiffness, only on flat rigid twins; labels require the robot to walk on the surface, so it does not scale to objects or to scenes the robot has not touched.
works.confidence: high (arXiv HTML read; venue from university repository)

works.name: GAUGE: a measurement-grounded benchmark for physical fidelity in simulation engines and video world models
works.what: ~1,560 motion-capture trials (16 NOKOV cameras, 180 Hz, 2 x 2 x 2 m volume on a 0.9 m breadboard) over 22 task families (rigid bodies, cables, textiles, volumetric deformables) with instrument-measured metadata: friction and restitution by inclined plane and air-bearing rail collisions, textile stretch/bending by Style3D instruments, Young's modulus / Poisson ratio by compression + DIC. Evaluates Isaac Sim, Genesis and Newton on 14 task families, and Cosmos3-Nano, Cosmos3-Super-I2V, Wan-2.2, Wan-2.7, Seedance 2.0, Genie 3 on 5 rigid tasks.
works.params_from: measured.
works.evaluated_against: real motion. Headline: no engine dominates; largest failures in impulsive contact, rapid textile motion, volumetric deformation; video models give visually plausible trajectories with wrong accelerations, momentum transfer and oscillation timing.
works.scale: Tabletop (2 m3). Included because it is the only measurement-grounded physics benchmark found that scores Newton, and because nothing comparable exists at room scale or beyond.
works.limitations: Restricted material ranges, no fluids, deformables not assessable from 2D video alone; corresponding author at Shanghai AI Lab (pjlab), full affiliation list not extracted.
works.confidence: high for content (arXiv HTML read); medium on exact engine-level numbers (second half of page not read)

gaps: No street-, campus- or city-scale simulator identifies or validates per-object contact parameters against real motion. Searched 'large-scale real-to-sim physical parameters city/building/warehouse digital twin friction validated real robot 2025 2026' (extended) and 'city-scale Gaussian splatting physics-enabled interactive simulation digital twin contact': hits were tabletop (PhysTwin-style soft-body, Real-is-Sim PushT, RobotArena-infinity with unvalidated Gemini parameters), the RA-L terrain paper (robot footing only), or Siemens' material-informed GS (reflectivity for LiDAR, not contact). UrbanVerse, the most complete urban real-to-sim pipeline, validates GPT-4.1 mass only against spec sheets (19.6% MAPE) and never validates friction.

Every driving-scale neural simulator has zero contact physics. HUGSIM detects background collision by counting Gaussians in the ego box; OmniRe edits node poses; WOSAC states 'We do not enforce any motion model'; Cosmos-Drive/OmniDreams generate frames. Searched 'driving simulator measured tire-road friction real-to-sim validation neural rendering closed-loop vehicle dynamics 2025 arXiv': only classical tyre-model / CarSim / racing system-ID results, no neural-reconstruction simulator with road friction.

'Interaction' at scale means collision avoidance and terrain traversal, never moving an object. URBAN-SIM, MetaUrban, UrbanVerse and Vid2Sim evaluate navigation success; GRUtopia reports 0% on mobile manipulation; Infinigen Indoors places objects by a stability relation rather than physics. No outdoor-scale benchmark was found in which a robot pushes, lifts or topples a scene object, so mass, restitution and centre of mass are never exercised at that scale.

Sim-ready asset pipelines at 100k-object scale state no provenance for friction/mass. UrbanVerse-100K (GPT-4.1), MolmoSpaces 130k (GPT-4o), GRUtopia ('professional teams'), SimReady spec (artist 'dials in'), RoboCasa (unstated), Infinigen-Sim (generator distributions). Searched the SimReady physics best-practices page and 'NVIDIA PhysicalAI SimReady warehouse dataset physics attributes mass friction': the spec names the attributes and gives no material library, table or measurement protocol.

No measurement-grounded physics benchmark exists beyond tabletop. Searched 'benchmark dataset real scene measured object mass friction restitution ground truth many objects rooms 2025 2026' (extended): GAUGE (2 m mocap volume), Physics 101 (tabletop), and the rest simulator-generated (PhyParam, ExPhy). Nothing with measured parameters over a room, building or street.

No large-scale environment runs on a differentiable engine. All surveyed platforms use PhysX 5 (URBAN-SIM, Isaac, GRUtopia), Unity (Vid2Sim, AI2-THOR), Bullet/Panda3D (Habitat, MetaUrban), MuJoCo (RoboCasa, MolmoSpaces), Genesis (RobotArena), cannon.js (Video2Game). Searched 'Newton physics engine OR MuJoCo Warp large-scale scene thousands of objects GPU differentiable benchmark 2025 2026': results are about thousands of parallel small environments, not one large scene; GAUGE evaluates Newton only at tabletop.

Vision-to-friction identification exists only where the robot itself supplies the label (RA-L terrain paper: labels from proprioception, flat rigid twins). No work found that transfers a measured material table to scene objects at scale and checks held-out real motion -- the e1-style test -- outside the project's own Physics 101 result.
scouts.relevance_to_our_assets: The landscape splits into (i) reconstruction/generation stacks that produce geometry and appearance at street-to-city scale with no contact physics at all (OmniRe/HUGSIM/Cosmos-Drive/WOSAC/MatrixCity), (ii) procedural or retrieval-based embodied platforms that do have a rigid-body engine (PhysX 5, Unity, MuJoCo, Bullet) but fill mass/friction/restitution by artist choice, per-texture labels, or a VLM prompt (URBAN-SIM, UrbanVerse, GRUtopia, MolmoSpaces, Video2Game, RobotArena, SimReady), and (iii) two measurement-grounded islands, both tabletop or robot-footing only (GAUGE, ETH terrain RA-L). The project's validated assets map onto the hole between (ii) and (iii): the held-out real-object test (material table + LLM naming -> 2.6 mm median on 359 real trials, vs 7.5 mm for an LLM number) is exactly the parameter-level validation that none of the 100k-asset pipelines perform, and it directly measures the cost of the GPT-4.1/GPT-4o route they all take; the Newton kernels with exact mesh contact, build-aware CoM and alpha-restitution are the only differentiable contact path in this list and could be scored on GAUGE's measured rigid trials (rule 2 applies: that is a check against instrumented motion, not a handbook); the CoTracker + simulator-fit pipeline and the Physics 101 density/friction tables are a material-provenance layer that UrbanVerse-100K, MolmoSpaces and SimReady currently lack. Redundant with the field: scene reconstruction and asset retrieval at urban scale (Vid2Sim, UrbanVerse already deliver GS->mesh->Isaac plumbing and real-robot navigation), LLM-based material naming as a scaling trick (UrbanVerse and MolmoSpaces already do it for 100k+ assets, only without the number validation), policy-level sim-to-real correlation (MolmoSpaces R=0.96), and the project's own negative results on video models, which GAUGE now independently reproduces (plausible video, wrong accelerations and momentum transfer). Not covered by anything found: any demonstration that a differentiable engine with measured parameters survives a scene larger than a table, and any outdoor benchmark where objects, not just the robot, move.
scouts.caveats: Most primary pages were read through WebFetch summaries limited to the first ~100k characters, so appendix-level details (e.g. GAUGE's per-engine numbers, URBAN-SIM's limitations appendix, MolmoSpaces' second half) may be incomplete. UniSim, NeuRAD and Street Gaussians were taken from abstracts and the project page of OmniRe; their actor control being kinematic is inferred from the model class and from OmniRe's explicit statement, not quoted from each paper. Habitat 3.0's kinematic humanoids and physics engine (Bullet) are inferred from the HTML and from Habitat 2.0; ReplicaCAD's artist assignment of mass/friction/restitution comes from aihabitat.org and secondary pages. GRUtopia was read via ar5iv. The provenance of Infinigen-Sim's friction/density values could not be confirmed (GitHub doc 404). Cosmos-Drive-Dreams / OmniDreams physics absence is inferred from the generative model class and NVIDIA's own framing, not from a statement in the paper. Several 2026 items (GAUGE 2608.05948, Isaac Sim 2606.03551, ArtiTwinSplat 2606.24628, MolmoSpaces 2602.11337) are recent arXiv postings whose venues are unconfirmed except where stated (UrbanVerse ICLR 2026; terrain paper RA-L 2024). No code was run and no numbers were recomputed.

scouts.angle: Learning physical properties (friction, restitution, mass/density, stiffness) from video at scale: what datasets exist with MEASURED ground truth, how parameters are supervised, and how estimators/engines are scored against real motion.

works.name: Physics 101 + Galileo (canonical)
works.source: Galileo: NeurIPS 2015 (proceedings.neurips.cc hash d09bf41544a3365a46c9077ebb5e35c3); Physics 101: BMVC 2016 paper039
works.what: Galileo fits an object-centric physics engine (mass, friction, 3D shape, position) to real ramp/collision videos by MCMC and distils to a CNN; Physics 101 is the dataset: 101 objects, 15 materials, ramp at two angles, drops on 5 surfaces, springs, liquids, side/top DSLR + Kinect at ~30 fps, with measured mass and volume.
works.params_from: measured (mass, volume) + fit to video (friction via physics-engine MCMC)
works.evaluated_against: real motion (outcome prediction on held-out clips) and human judgements; accuracy 'comparable to human subjects', no per-parameter error vs an independent instrument
works.scale: 101 objects / 15 materials / ~17k video clips (dataset); Galileo fitted per clip
works.limitations: 30 fps DSLR: restitution unrecoverable (project confirmed); friction ground truth never independently measured; evaluation is outcome/human-agreement rather than parameter error; 2015-era engine (Bullet) with no contact fidelity check.

works.name: Bounce and Learn (Bounce Dataset)
works.what: 5K RGB-D videos of one foam ball bounced off surfaces in homes/offices; a Physics Inference Module predicts post-bounce trajectory from pre-bounce trajectory and per-location restitution + effective collision normal predicted by a Visual Inference Module from a still image.
works.params_from: fit to video (restitution and normal are latent, learned end-to-end from trajectories; no instrument measurement)
works.evaluated_against: real motion (post-bounce trajectory prediction vs Newtonian trajectory-fitting baseline); no measured restitution
works.scale: 5K bounces, one probe object, many surfaces
works.limitations: One ball of one material — it maps SURFACES, not object materials; restitution is an effective fitted quantity; abstract gives no numeric accuracy (full PDF not parsed).

works.name: Physion++
works.what: Simulated benchmark (TDW) with 9 scenarios where outcome prediction requires online inference of latent mass, friction, elasticity, deformability from how objects move; compares models to humans.
works.params_from: table (simulator-assigned, hidden from the model)
works.evaluated_against: sim-only outcome prediction + human judgements
works.scale: thousands of synthetic clips across 9 scenarios (count not in abstract)
works.limitations: Entirely simulated; measures binary outcome accuracy, not parameter error; all models far below humans and poorly correlated with them. Useful as a protocol template (property only observable through interaction), not as ground truth.

works.name: PhysVid — Inferring Dynamic Physical Properties from Video Foundation Models (Oxford VGG)
works.what: Regresses elasticity (bouncing balls), viscosity (pouring) and dynamic friction (sliding) from video with (a) a classical-CV oracle, (b) probes on DynamiCrafter and V-JEPA-2 with visual prompts, (c) MLLM prompting. Per property: 10,000 synthetic train, 1,000 test-1, 1,000 test-2, 100 REAL test-3 videos.
works.params_from: measured for the real split: friction via spring dynamometer at constant drag speed (mu_k = F/G) over 5 objects x 6 surfaces, mu 0.105-0.544; elasticity from manually annotated fronto-parallel bounce heights; viscosity from reference tables for 12 liquids
works.evaluated_against: real motion with measured GT (Pearson on test-3): friction — oracle 0.83, DynamiCrafter 0.21, V-JEPA-2 0.28, Qwen2.5-VL 0.06, GPT-4o 0.38, Gemini 0.12; with real-domain adaptation DynamiCrafter 0.82 / V-JEPA-2 0.71. Elasticity: oracle 0.87, V-JEPA-2 0.47, DynamiCrafter 0.07. Viscosity: oracle 0.80, V-JEPA-2 0.79.
works.scale: 30k synthetic + 300 real videos; 5 real objects, 6 surfaces
works.limitations: Only 30 real object-surface pairs; synthetic-to-real friction transfer fails without adaptation; 'all models fall short of the oracle, particularly in absolute value prediction'; no simulation closed loop — parameters never re-simulated against the real trajectory.

works.name: EKFPhys — Physics-Based Rigid Body Tracking and Friction Filtering from RGB-D Video
works.what: Extended Kalman filter whose state-transition model is a custom end-to-end differentiable 3D rigid-body engine (LCP contact, mesh shapes); jointly estimates pose, velocity and coefficient of friction from RGB-D.
works.params_from: fit to video (online filtering); ground truth measured by tilting the table and recording 10 mocap slides, mu = tan(alpha) - a/g
works.evaluated_against: real motion with measured GT: 4 YCB objects x 5 sequences, RealSense D455 at 60 Hz, mocap at 240 Hz; median friction error 0.0246 (zero-baseline 0.03), mean 0.082 vs 0.164
works.scale: 4 objects, 20 real sequences + synthetic
works.limitations: Needs several frames of clearly observable sliding to converge; unmodeled damping biases real results; tiny object set; requires depth + known mesh.

works.name: IRIS — Real-World Benchmark for Inverse Recovery of Physical Dynamic Systems from Monocular Video
works.what: 240 lab videos (4K, 60 fps) of 8 phenomena (dropping/falling ball, sliding cone, pendulum, rotating cone, colliding cones, coupled pendulums), 3 settings x 10 repeats each, paired with governing equations; evaluates parameter estimation, identifiability, extrapolation and equation identification (VLM prompting, CNN classifier, path labelling, multi-step physics loss).
works.params_from: measured (lengths +/-2 mm, angles +/-0.5 deg, radii by calipers) for geometric parameters; fit to video for damping/friction (mu = tan a - a/(g cos a), damping by nonlinear least squares) with uncertainty from 10 trials
works.evaluated_against: real motion with measured GT; multi-step physics loss helps single-body gravity (MAE -0.90) but diverges on multi-body (errors >10^2 m); CNN equation ID 99.3%, VLMs 65-73%
works.scale: 240 videos, 8 systems
works.limitations: Authors admit damping/friction GT are trajectory fits, not independent measurements; multi-body contact modelled as a continuous coupling, not impact mechanics; textbook objects (cones, balls), not everyday objects.

works.name: WorldBench — physical-parameter-estimation subset
works.what: Isolates physics concepts for video world models; a parameter subset has 234 real videos (51 gravity, 80 viscosity, 103 friction) plus synthetic; SAM2 tracking + checkerboard calibration + quadratic/linear fits extract g, mu, terminal velocity from generated continuations.
works.params_from: table (GT ranges from material references, e.g. wood 0.2-0.5, plastic 0.05-0.2; viscosity 1.2-14.1 Pa·s); estimates fit to video
works.evaluated_against: real-video-conditioned generations from Cosmos, Wan 2.2, HunyuanWorld, CogVideoX, Runway, Kling, LTX-2.0; all fail — gravity from -0.039 to 10.8 m/s^2, viscosity often >50 vs 14.1, friction 0.3-1.5 vs 0.2-2.0
works.scale: 234 real + 45 synthetic videos
works.limitations: Ground truth is a material-table RANGE, not a per-object measurement; evaluates generators, not estimators; authors note each concept 'requires careful experimental design and extensive validation'.

works.name: GAUGE — Measurement-Grounded Benchmark for Physical Fidelity in Simulation Engines and Video World Models (InternRobotics)
works.what: ~1,560 motion-capture trials (16 NOKOV cameras, 180 Hz, sub-mm) over 22 task families (rigid: wood/plastic/metal slope slider, turntable, bouncing ball, Newton's cradle, pendulum; textiles: 6 fabrics; foams). Measured parameters are injected into Isaac Sim, Genesis and NEWTON, and simulated trajectories are scored against the real mean trajectory by RMSE and DTW; 6 image-to-video models scored on 5 rigid tasks by law-consistency and parameter stability.
works.params_from: measured: friction by inclined plane mu = (g sin th - a)/(g cos th); restitution by inclined air-bearing rail e = v_out/v_in; textile stretch/bend on Style3D instruments; foam E and nu by compression + DIC
works.evaluated_against: real motion (mocap) for engines; Newton: slope slider normalized RMSE 1.71/0.51/1.15 (wood/plastic/metal), turntable 2.88/1.92/1.97, bouncing ball 22.71 (best engine still 15.63x baseline), pendulum period 1.09 s vs 1.06 measured; Newton's cradle momentum-transfer efficiency 0.26 (Isaac 0.20). Video models: Cosmos3-Super-I2V infers 0.088 m/s^2 for g; Wan 2.2 / Genie3 pendulum period 1.93/1.90 s vs 1.06 s
works.scale: 22 task families, 3 rigid materials + 6 fabrics + foams, 20 trials/task
works.limitations: 'materials and calibrated parameter ranges remain limited'; three rigid materials only; engines run with defaults except the measured parameters, so contact model mismatch (bouncing ball) dominates; release status of raw trajectories not confirmed from the excerpt.

works.name: XDen-1K — density fields of 1,000 real objects from biplanar X-ray
works.what: 1,000 real objects / 137 categories with part-annotated 3D models, biplanar X-rays, and volumetric density fields reconstructed by differentiable optimisation (Beer-Lambert, rho = mu/0.17); benchmarks image-based density estimation and X-ray-conditioned segmentation; CoM prior raises grasp success 27.5% -> 77.75%.
works.params_from: measured-ish: X-ray attenuation converted to density, validated by reprojection MAE 0.778 and a small CT subset (no reported weighing)
works.evaluated_against: none (no motion); static density/CoM GT: NeRF2Physics density MAE 1.157 and CoM error 0.523 cm, GaussianProperty 1.295/0.632, Pixie 1.228/0.547
works.scale: 1,000 objects
works.limitations: Density is inferred from attenuation with a single mass-attenuation constant, not weighed; interior modelling is manual for hard cases; no friction/restitution/dynamics.

works.name: EgoPhys — physics models of deformables from egocentric video
works.what: Builds deformable digital twins from RGB-only egocentric video: 4D point clouds -> spring-mass simulator fitted by CMA-ES on geometry + track losses, then distils per-object solutions into a stiffness codebook for zero-shot prediction on unseen objects; validated on an xArm6.
works.params_from: fit to video (CMA-ES on spring stiffness), then predicted from a learned codebook
works.evaluated_against: real motion but only as video/geometry consistency (Chamfer 0.015 vs PhysTwin 0.024; zero-shot CD 0.0319 vs 0.0457); robot pulling error reduced up to 77.6%; NO measured physical ground truth
works.scale: 19 sequences, ~2.2 h, plush/towel/cloth/bags
works.limitations: Authors: 'modest-scale', 'initial reusable physics prior rather than a universal material model'; effective spring stiffness, not material constants; deformables only.

works.name: VideoPhysEdit — rigid-body physical scene reconstruction from monocular video
works.what: From a single monocular video, recovers meshes, collision proxies, camera and physical parameters Theta (mass, friction, restitution, initial states) using SAM2 + CoTracker3 + VGGT; stable intervals constrain force balance/friction/rolling, contact events constrain momentum/restitution; outputs an executable scene for counterfactual video editing.
works.params_from: fit to video, with explicit priors 'only for quantities the observations do not determine'
works.evaluated_against: sim-only quantitative GT (PCVE-RigidBench: 20 PyBullet/Blender scenes, 129 tasks; trajectory error -54% vs strongest baseline, Physical Edit Score 0.376); real videos qualitative only
works.scale: 20 synthetic scenes; handful of real clips
works.limitations: No measured ground truth on real video; static camera; identifiability of mass/friction from passive video is not separately tested; closest existing pipeline to 'CoTracker + physics' on rigid bodies.

works.name: ExPhy — explicit physical property learning in multi-object trajectory forecasting
works.what: 24,000 simulated scenes with explicit per-object mass, friction and restitution labels; ID and two OOD splits (parameters, initial states); PhyODE baseline cuts ADE/FDE by 33.1%/31.0%. Headline finding: 'accurate trajectory forecasting does not necessarily imply accurate recovery of the underlying physical properties'.
works.params_from: table (simulator-assigned labels)
works.evaluated_against: sim-only
works.scale: 24k scenes
works.limitations: Synthetic only; exists mainly as evidence that forecasting objectives do not identify parameters.

works.name: PhysInOne — visual physics learning and reasoning in one suite
works.what: 2M synthetic videos over 153,810 dynamic 3D scenes and 71 phenomena (mechanics, optics, fluids, magnetism) with geometry, motion, physical-property and text labels; tasks include physical property estimation, future prediction, physics-aware generation; fine-tuning foundation models improves plausibility but 'critical gaps' remain in estimating intrinsic properties.
works.params_from: table (simulator-assigned)
works.evaluated_against: sim-only
works.scale: 2M videos (largest synthetic physics-property corpus found)
works.limitations: No real split with measured parameters; property labels are simulator inputs, so the sim-to-real transfer question that PhysVid shows failing for friction is untouched.

works.name: Deformable system-ID cluster: PAC-NeRF / Spring-Gaus / Vid2Sim / MASIV / MonoPhysics
works.source: Spring-Gaus arXiv 2403.09434 (ECCV 2024); Vid2Sim arXiv 2506.06440 (CVPR 2025); MASIV arXiv 2508.01112 (ICCV 2025); MonoPhysics arXiv 2605.30320 (NeurIPS 2026)
works.what: Differentiable simulator + differentiable rendering (NeRF/3DGS/LBS) to recover Young's modulus, Poisson ratio, viscosity or neural constitutive laws from multi-view (now monocular, MonoPhysics) video of deformables; Vid2Sim adds a feed-forward prior and a 12-object elastic dataset; MASIV uses learned constitutive models with particle-trajectory guidance.
works.params_from: fit to video (gradient through simulation); synthetic GT from the simulator
works.evaluated_against: sim-only parameter error plus real video reconstruction/future-frame metrics (Chamfer, PSNR); MonoPhysics reports Young's modulus 'comparable to a multi-view baseline' on Vid2Sim
works.scale: tens of objects (Vid2Sim 12 elastic objects; Spring-Gaus real subset a few objects)
works.limitations: Real-world material constants never measured independently (effective parameters); mostly elastic/plasticine; multi-view capture until 2026; rigid contact (friction, restitution) is not the target.

works.name: Mass from human-interaction video: CORSMAL / VisPhysQuant (PhysQuantAgent) / Patchwork Physics
works.source: CORSMAL: arXiv 2012.01311, 2203.01207; PhysQuantAgent: arXiv 2603.16958; Patchwork Physics: VSS 2026 poster (visionsciences.org id 3927), supporting arXiv 2508.19852
works.what: CORSMAL: 15 containers x 3 fillings x 3 levels recorded with 4 cameras + 8-mic array; estimate container mass/capacity/filling from handover video (vision-only ~65% weighted score). PhysQuantAgent: RGB-D multi-view videos of real objects with weighed masses; VLM + visual prompts (detection, scale, cross-sections). Patchwork Physics: Ego4D hand-object pipeline (segmentation, tracking, monocular depth) extracting 3D trajectories, velocities, contact onset and volume to reproduce human mass-speed biases.
works.params_from: measured (weighed masses) for CORSMAL / VisPhysQuant; none for Patchwork (kinematic statistics only)
works.evaluated_against: measured mass (CORSMAL, VisPhysQuant); human psychophysics (Patchwork); no simulation
works.scale: 15 containers; VisPhysQuant count not in abstract; Ego4D-scale video for Patchwork
works.limitations: Mass only; VLM numbers not given in abstract; Ego4D pipeline yields no object-level physical parameters with GT — it extracts kinematics, which is exactly the project's finding that internet video carries motion statistics, not material constants.

gaps: Nobody validates ASSIGNED (transferred) parameters on the real motion of HELD-OUT objects. Searched 'held-out object material transfer friction real video', 'sim-ready parameters validated against real motion', 'material table friction transfer unseen objects': PhysVid, EKFPhys, IRIS and GAUGE score estimators or engines on the SAME objects they measured; GAUGE injects measured parameters into engines but never transfers them to a new object; XDen-1K transfers nothing. The project's e1 (70 objects, 359 trials, 2.6 mm median) has no published counterpart.

No multi-material restitution dataset with adequate frame rate. Searched 'restitution dataset many materials high-speed video', 'coefficient of restitution benchmark objects': Bounce and Learn is one foam ball vs many surfaces; GAUGE measures e for wood/plastic/metal only via an air-bearing rail; PhysVid elasticity is 100 real bounce clips with manually annotated heights; Physics 101 drops are 30 fps (project confirmed unrecoverable). Nothing covers tens of object materials.

No open 'physics atlas' (material -> measured mu, e, rho) derived from real motion. Searched 'physics atlas material properties from motion', 'material property table from video crowdsourced', 'large-scale dataset real objects measured friction restitution density sim-ready': GAUGE (3 rigid materials), PhysVid (5 objects x 6 surfaces), NeRF2Physics' small hand-measured set and XDen-1K (density only, X-ray derived) are the closest; none is a queryable table spanning common materials with uncertainty from repeated real trials.

No rigid-body parameter recovery from monocular internet/egocentric video with MEASURED ground truth. Searched 'Ego4D mass estimation physical properties', 'Something-Something HowTo100M physical property', 'friction restitution from monocular internet video 2026': EgoPhys (19 sequences, deformables, no GT), Patchwork Physics (kinematics only), VideoPhysEdit (real clips qualitative only), CORSMAL/VisPhysQuant (mass only, lab capture). Internet-scale extraction of mu/e with instrument GT does not exist.

No closed-loop benchmark for ESTIMATORS (parameter -> re-simulate -> compare to real trajectory) beyond EKFPhys (4 YCB objects). Searched 'differentiable simulation friction estimation real-world benchmark': IRIS and PhysVid report parameter error only; GAUGE closes the loop only for engines fed measured parameters, not for video-derived estimates; WorldBench closes it for generators, which fail.

Newton/Warp contact fidelity on real impacts is only sampled by GAUGE (bouncing ball RMSE 22.71, Newton's cradle efficiency 0.26) with default contact settings; no study calibrates a penalty/Hunt-Crossley contact model against measured restitution across masses and speeds. Searched 'Newton physics engine real-world validation contact restitution': only GAUGE and GPUSimBench (arXiv 2607.13059, scalability not fidelity) appeared.

No large real dataset couples geometry-aware mass models (shell vs solid, areal density for hollow builds) with measured mass across object categories. XDen-1K gives density fields for 1,000 objects but validates by X-ray reprojection rather than weighing and offers no 'build type'; Google Scanned Objects estimates mass from volume. Searched 'mass from volume hollow objects dataset measured mass category'.
scouts.relevance_to_our_assets: The landscape confirms that the project's validated pieces sit at an empty intersection: measured-GT datasets exist (PhysVid's 30 dynamometer-measured object-surface pairs, IRIS's 240 4K/60 fps lab videos, GAUGE's ~1,560 180 Hz mocap trials with inclined-plane mu and air-bearing e, XDen-1K's 1,000 density/CoM fields), and all of them are external ground truth the project could consume without a capture rig — PhysVid real friction and GAUGE slope-slider/turntable trajectories are drop-in tests for the Newton+exact-mesh-contact pipeline and the CoTracker3+simulator fit, while GAUGE's measured restitution and IRIS's bounces are the first high-rate real impacts available to check the Hunt-Crossley alpha calibration, which currently rests on an assumed 0.4. The project's negative results on video models are independently replicated (PhysVid friction Pearson 0.21-0.28 for V-JEPA-2/DynamiCrafter and 0.06-0.38 for MLLMs; WorldBench and GAUGE world-model parameter failures; ExPhy's forecasting-without-identification finding), so those experiments need no repetition and can be cited as corroboration rather than re-run. Redundant parts: fitting Physics 101 ramps is Galileo's 2015 experiment with a better engine; mass-from-density transfer overlaps XDen-1K's CoM prior and PhysQuantAgent's weighed benchmark; deformable system-ID (Vid2Sim/MonoPhysics/EgoPhys) already covers stiffness from video with differentiable simulators, so the project's cloth/soft probes add little. Non-redundant and unmatched: the held-out-object transfer test (e1), the build-aware (shell/solid/areal) mass model checked to 1% against textbook values, and the rule-1 sensitivity-matrix discipline — GAUGE is the only work that even injects measured parameters into Newton, and it reports contact failures (bouncing ball 15.6x baseline) that the project's exact-vertex contact and alpha-restitution kernels are positioned to diagnose on GAUGE's own trajectories.
scouts.caveats: Numbers for GAUGE, IRIS, WorldBench, XDen-1K, VideoPhysEdit and EgoPhys were read from arXiv HTML via fetch summaries that covered only the first ~100k characters of each paper; GAUGE's 'normalized RMSE' units and its data-release status were not confirmed, and its Newton numbers come from Table 5 as summarised, not re-read. Venues for GAUGE, IRIS, WorldBench, XDen-1K, ExPhy and VideoPhysEdit are unstated on arXiv (2026 preprints). Bounce and Learn details beyond the abstract (frame rate, how restitution is 'inferred') could not be parsed from the PDF; it is ICLR 2019, not CVPR as the task text says. PhysInOne, ExPhy, MASIV, MonoPhysics and PhysQuantAgent are summarised from abstracts only (medium confidence). XDen-1K's density is X-ray-attenuation-derived with a single mass-attenuation constant and validated by reprojection and a CT subset, not by weighing — treat as semi-measured. IRIS's friction/damping ground truth is itself a trajectory fit, as its authors state. No work matching 'ContactNet dataset' as a video dataset was found; ContactNets (arXiv 2009.11193) is a learned contact-dynamics model trained on ~60 s of real tosses and its BundleSDF integration (arXiv 2309.05832, IROS 2023 workshop) reports no parameter accuracy, so it was not listed as a dataset. Audio-visual material estimation (Visual Vibrometry CVPR 2015, Visual Vibration Tomography CVPR 2022, ObjectFolder Real CVPR 2023 with 100 objects and contact-force-annotated impact sounds) targets stiffness/density of rods, fabrics and shells via modal analysis rather than contact parameters and was left out of the 15 for scope; it remains the only video route to stiffness with physical units.

scouts.angle: What robot-learning practitioners actually do with physical parameters: system identification vs domain randomisation, real-to-sim digital twins for policy evaluation, differentiable-simulator sysid, contact-rich datasets, SimReady/asset-level parameter assignment, and the evidence on whether better object parameters change policy transfer.

works.name: ASID: Active Exploration for System Identification in Robotic Manipulation (Memmel, Wagenmaker, Zhu, Yin, Fox, Gupta)
works.what: Uses an initial inaccurate MuJoCo model to synthesise a Fisher-information-maximising exploration policy, runs it for a single real episode, then fits simulator parameters by CEM on ||tau_real - tau_sim||^2 and retrains the task policy in the refined sim. Tasks: rod balancing (mass distribution along the rod), sphere striking (rolling/tangential friction, stiffness), laptop articulation (joint presence/position), shuffleboard (sliding + torsional friction of the puck).
works.params_from: fit to real robot interaction trajectories (one episode), parametric family known a priori; black-box CEM/REPS, no gradients needed
works.evaluated_against: real robot task success after transfer: rod balancing 6/9 vs domain randomisation 0/9; shuffleboard 7/10 vs DR 3/10; in sim, rod tilt 0.0 deg vs DR 26.7 deg
works.scale: 4 tasks, one Franka, one real episode per identification; a handful of objects
works.limitations: Needs a robot to excite the object; parameter space must be pre-defined; authors note a CoM near the rod centre makes identification ambiguous; validated per-object on the same object, no transfer of identified values to other objects.

works.name: SIMPLER: Evaluating Real-World Robot Manipulation Policies in Simulation (Li et al.)
works.what: Real-to-sim policy EVALUATION: SAPIEN (validated also in Isaac Sim) scenes for RT-1 / BridgeData setups. Closes the 'control gap' by offline sysid of the arm's PD stiffness/damping against recorded real end-effector trajectories (simulated annealing, 3 rounds), and the 'visual gap' by green-screening real backgrounds and projecting real textures onto meshes.
works.params_from: robot controller: fit to real trajectories. OBJECT physics: set manually -- density from 'GPT-4 or Google search' of material properties, or mass/volume for hollow items; friction 'based on common material properties'
works.evaluated_against: ~1500 paired sim/real policy evaluations; MMRV 0.056 and Pearson r 0.924 (Google Robot, visual matching). Perturbing controller params raises MMRV 0.031 -> 0.412. Ablation: varying object physics within plausible ranges changes success <= 15%.
works.scale: 2 embodiments, 8 task families, tens of assets, fixed cameras
works.limitations: Rigid objects only; manual asset curation; cannot scale to thousands of environments; the object-physics ablation is the only evidence about object parameters and it says the evaluation is insensitive to them, i.e. it never tests whether they are right.

works.name: Real-is-Sim: Bridging the Sim-to-Real Gap with a Dynamic Digital Twin (Abou-Chakra et al.)
works.what: A particle-based 'Embodied Gaussians' twin (rigid bodies as spherical collision primitives bound to 3D Gaussians) runs at 60 Hz alongside the real robot; photometric-loss 'visual forces' from posed cameras continuously pull particle poses onto the observed scene, so the simulator state tracks reality without ever identifying physical parameters.
works.params_from: none identified -- object physics are nominal and errors are corrected online by visual forces at 30 Hz
works.evaluated_against: PushT on a real robot: sim and real success curves correlate; 30 real + 30 sim demos reach 80% vs 72% for 60 real; 60 measurements per success-rate point
works.scale: one task (PushT), one robot, tabletop
works.limitations: Authors: constrained by the underlying simulator; only PushT; extending to multi-object, cloth or non-prehensile pushing 'will require tailoring the simulator's dynamics model'; explicit visual correction limits complex physics. It substitutes state correction for parameter correctness, so it cannot predict motion it does not observe.

works.name: TwinAligner: Real2Sim2Real with visual and dynamic alignment
works.what: Builds an editable 3DGS + SDF twin of a tabletop scene, then identifies rigid physics in the Genesis engine from a scripted 'Control-Hit-Slide' robot-object interaction: theta = {friction, mass, centre of mass, robot controller params}, by particle-swarm optimisation (gradient-free, chosen for compatibility with non-differentiable simulators). Trains Diffusion Policy / RISE in the aligned sim.
works.params_from: fit to robot-object interaction trajectories (20 clips over 4 test objects)
works.evaluated_against: real object trajectory error: ADD 1.39 cm / ADD-S 0.78 cm (vs PIN-WM 2.37 / 1.28); zero-shot real success 10/15, 14/15, 9/15, 10/15 on push, stack, pick-place, close-laptop (real-data baselines 11-13/15)
works.scale: 4 objects, 4 tasks, one arm, tabletop
works.limitations: Authors: human effort for multi-view capture and trajectory collection remains; accuracy/speed bounded by the engine; no deformables. Each object is identified individually; nothing transfers to an object the robot has not hit.

works.name: PIN-WM: Physics-INformed World Models for Non-Prehensile Manipulation (Li et al.)
works.what: End-to-end identification of a 3D rigid-body system from visual observations only: a differentiable velocity-based LCP contact solver (primal-dual interior point) coupled to Gaussian-splat rendering, so mass/inertia, restitution and friction are optimised through a rendering loss with no state estimation. Identified model used for model-based RL ('physics-aware digital cousins').
works.params_from: fit to ONE task-agnostic real push (robot pushes object straight for a fixed distance), gradients through differentiable physics + rendering
works.evaluated_against: one-step prediction error (translation/rotation) and real-robot task success: push 75%, flip 65% vs ASID 40% / 10%
works.scale: few objects, two tasks, one arm
works.limitations: Authors: rendering alignment is critical, robot shadows corrupt the loss; rigid bodies only. Restitution and friction are identified from a single push that barely excites restitution; parameter values themselves are not reported against measured ground truth (only trajectory/task metrics, per the sections read).

works.name: Vid2Sid: Videos Can Help Close the Sim2Real Gap
works.what: Video-driven sysid: SAM3 extracts trajectories from paired sim/real videos; a VLM in the optimiser loop diagnoses mismatches in words ('the simulated tentacle oscillates too fast') and proposes parameter updates. Platforms: tendon finger in MuJoCo (joint friction, viscous damping, rotor inertia, link density) and silicone tentacle in PyElastica (Young's modulus, density, Poisson ratio, damping; fluid density/drag underwater).
works.params_from: fit to real actuated videos (sinusoidal actuation), VLM-proposed updates scored by pixel trajectory error
works.evaluated_against: held-out control profiles: tip error 10.9 px vs 12.1 px (best baseline) on the finger; 53.0 px vs CMA-ES 52.1 px on the tentacle; in sim2sim with ground truth 7.13 mm vs BO 9.70 mm and 8.7% parameter error vs 28-98% for baselines
works.scale: 2 platforms, actuated by the robot itself, single fixed camera
works.limitations: Authors: needs clean perception and expressive simulators; 3-5 px segmentation jitter degrades results; model misspecification dominates underwater (all methods converge alike); 11 s VLM latency per iteration; static background. Note the VLM proposes updates but the acceptance signal is tracked-trajectory error, not VLM judgement.

works.name: SPI-Active: Sampling-Based System Identification with Active Exploration for Legged Robot Sim2Real
works.what: Two-stage CMA-ES identification in Isaac Gym of base-link mass, CoM and inertia plus per-joint motor gain (tanh torque-saturation model) by minimising sim/real trajectory prediction error over massively parallel rollouts; stage 2 adds Fisher-information-maximising exploration trajectories.
works.params_from: fit to real robot trajectories (~60 s teleoperated validation data plus a small set of active-exploration trajectories); no torque sensing, no gradients
works.evaluated_against: prediction error -33% position / -28% joint angle vs vanilla; task performance +42-63% vs domain randomisation; forward jump error 3.6 cm
works.scale: quadruped(s), locomotion tasks
works.limitations: Authors: active exploration limited to quadrupeds (humanoid safety); offline only; parameter coupling (pitch/roll inertia overfit) when excitation is insufficient. Robot-body parameters only; no object parameters.

works.name: ASAP: Aligning Simulation and Real-World Physics for Agile Humanoid Whole-Body Skills (He et al.)
works.what: Instead of identifying parameters, learns a residual 'delta action' model from real rollouts and inserts it into the simulator, then fine-tunes the policy. Explicitly compared against a SysID baseline that identifies base CoM shift (cx,cy,cz), base mass ratio and PD-gain ratios on 23 joints.
works.params_from: SysID baseline: fit to real motion-capture rollouts; ASAP itself: residual network, no parameters
works.evaluated_against: real Unitree G1 motion tracking: kick error 43.5 -> 40.1 mm, out-of-distribution motion 55.3 -> 47.5 mm; in sim-to-sim ASAP beats SysID and delta-dynamics baselines across difficulty levels; reported up to 52.7% tracking-error reduction
works.scale: one humanoid, 100 real motion clips (4-DoF ankle delta model; full 23-DoF needs >400 episodes)
works.limitations: Authors: two robots damaged during data collection; needs mocap; sample-hungry. Their stated reason for abandoning SysID: pre-defined parameter spaces 'may not fully capture the sim-to-real gap' and SysID 'often relies on ground truth torque measurements'.

works.name: Achieving Precise and Reliable Locomotion with Differentiable Simulation-Based System Identification
works.what: Gradient-based sysid in MuJoCo-XLA (MJX) of actuator armature, frictionloss and damping from an isolated motor (HTDW-5047) driven by sum-of-Fourier velocity profiles, minimising L2 state error over trajectory segments; identified model used inside RL training.
works.params_from: fit to real actuator trajectories via differentiable simulation gradients
works.evaluated_against: motor trajectory MSE ~8x smaller; sim-to-real position drift 1.13 m -> 0.16 m; RL policy rotational deviation -75%, travel +46% on the Mini pi robot
works.scale: one small legged robot, three actuator parameters
works.limitations: Authors: assumes the whole gap is captured by the parameter vector; exact sim/real equality 'impractical'. Representative of how differentiable engines are used in practice: for robot/actuator parameters, not object properties.

works.name: Real-World Deployment of Massively Parallel Sampling-Based MPC for Contact-Rich Manipulation
works.what: Sampling MPC (Hydrax / MJX, 1024 samples, 8-10 Hz) on a Franka Research 3 Push-T task, with online domain adaptation: per-domain weights w_d proportional to exp(-d_SE(3)(T_hat(d), T_obs)/sigma^2) over randomised physics domains.
works.params_from: randomised domains re-weighted online from observed object pose; no offline identification
works.evaluated_against: real Push-T final pose error over 6 seeds (lowest mean and variance vs MPPI/PS/CEM); Bugtrap in sim
works.scale: one task, one arm, one object
works.limitations: Key practitioner finding: 'Mass and friction yield no stable adaptation signal. Physics is dominated by contact timing and constraint resolution forces rather than by smooth variation in the randomized parameter'; low-mass/friction domains overshoot while heavy domains look 'spuriously consistent', so they adapt contact margins (collision buffers) instead. Authors: global physics parameters are 'effectively non-identifiable within a single replanning interval'; timestep/horizon trade-off.

works.name: DROPO: Sim-to-Real Transfer with Offline Domain Randomization (Tiboni, Arndt, Kyrki) -- with BayesSim (Ramos et al. 2019) as the canonical predecessor
works.what: Estimates a domain-randomisation DISTRIBUTION over dynamics parameters (mean and variance) by maximum likelihood against a small pre-collected offline dataset of real trajectories, no knowledge of the data-collection policy; BayesSim instead trains an amortised posterior network on simulated rollouts. Both are the standard 'identify the DR range, not a point' recipe.
works.params_from: fit to offline real trajectories (DROPO) / amortised posterior from simulated rollouts (BayesSim)
works.evaluated_against: zero-shot sim-to-real on robot tasks; shown to recover parameter distributions and to compensate an unmodelled phenomenon by widening variance (per abstract)
works.scale: single-robot tasks (Panda pushing in follow-ups), few parameters
works.limitations: Read from abstract/secondary only. Parameter distribution absorbs model error as variance, i.e. the identified values are effective, not physical; needs robot-collected trajectories.

works.name: TacSL: A Library for Visuotactile Sensor Simulation and Learning (Akinola, Xu, Carius, Fox, Narang)
works.what: GPU visuotactile sensor (GelSight-type) simulation inside Isaac Gym, >200x faster than prior methods; sensor models, contact-rich environments, and an asymmetric actor-critic distillation algorithm for tactile policies with sim-to-real transfer.
works.params_from: sensor/contact models calibrated by the authors (details not in the abstract read); object physics nominal
works.evaluated_against: sim-to-real transfer on contact-rich insertion-type tasks (numbers not in the abstract read)
works.scale: Isaac Gym parallel environments, one sensor family
works.limitations: Abstract only. It is the practitioners' tool for contact SENSING simulation; it does not identify object parameters and the value of object-parameter accuracy for the tactile policies is not reported in what was read.

works.name: Isaac Lab: A GPU-Accelerated Simulation Framework for Multi-Modal Robot Learning (NVIDIA)
works.what: The de facto practitioner stack: PhysX GPU physics, actuator models, domain-randomisation 'events' (asset swapping within a class, visual/material/texture randomisation, physics randomisation), USD/SimReady assets with converters from URDF/MJCF/meshes; case studies of sim-to-real on ANYmal/Spot locomotion, quadruped door opening, humanoid pick-and-place in procedural kitchens.
works.params_from: nominal asset values (SimReady USD: physics:density, static/dynamicFriction, restitution, mass, CoM, inertia) plus randomisation ranges set by the user; the SimReady spec page read gives no guidance on how values are obtained or validated
works.evaluated_against: qualitative sim-to-real demonstrations; no quantitative parameter-accuracy validation in the sections read
works.scale: thousands of parallel environments; SimReady library ~1000 assets (vendor figure, low confidence)
works.limitations: Paper states 'simulation parameters, such as friction coefficients, rigid-body masses, and joint properties, must still be set via the PhysX CPU APIs due to current design constraints' -- a bottleneck for parameter sweeps/learning; Newton (differentiable) integration is future work (Sec. 7.1). Common DR practice in the locomotion papers surfaced: friction 0.1-1.0 or 0.3-1.5, restitution 0-0.1, mass +/-15-50% (secondary summary, low confidence).

works.name: Measured object-property databases: 'Interactive Learning of Physical Object Properties Through Robot Manipulation and Database of Object Measurements' (2404.07344) and ViTacPhys (2608.21355)
works.what: 2404.07344: a robot squeezes/lifts objects, a Bayesian network over material, mass, volume, stiffness picks actions by expected information gain; releases >24,000 measurements of 63 objects with different grippers. ViTacPhys: 60 rigid and deformable objects with mass class, silicone-contact friction class and continuous stiffness labels, learned from human visual-tactile demonstrations and used for grasping.
works.params_from: measured by robot interaction (2404.07344) / measured labels then predicted by a visual-tactile model with a VLM semantic prior (ViTacPhys)
works.evaluated_against: 2404.07344: action selection vs baseline, trick objects whose appearance conflicts with material. ViTacPhys: 97.2% mass / 98.8% friction class accuracy on familiar objects, 87.5% / 97.5% on novel; grasp success 95.0% in-distribution, 83.4% OOD
works.scale: 63 and 60 objects
works.limitations: Both abstract-only. Neither feeds the measurements into a simulator or checks that a simulator with those values reproduces real motion; friction is a discrete class in ViTacPhys and absent in 2404.07344; both need contact hardware (gripper, tactile glove).

works.name: The Reality Gap in Robotics: Challenges, Solutions, and Best Practices (Aljalbout, Xing, Romero, Akinola, Garrett, Heiden, Gupta, Hermans, Narang, Fox, Scaramuzza, Ramos)
works.year: 2025 (Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems 2026)
works.what: Survey by the Isaac/NVIDIA-adjacent community. Taxonomy: causes (parameterisation -- 'friction, aerodynamics, mass, inertia... assigning accurate values to these parameters can be challenging'; contact modelling -- point contacts, linearised cones, spring-dampers give 'spurious internal forces, unstable grasps'), solutions (sysid 'repeatedly shown to be crucial', DR, real-to-sim, abstractions, co-training), and metrics.
works.params_from: n.a. (survey)
works.evaluated_against: n.a.; it DEFINES the metrics practitioners use: Sim-to-Real Correlation Coefficient (Pearson between sim and real policy performance), Offline Replay Error (open-loop replay of real actions, summed squared state difference), and visual FID/KID/SSIM
works.scale: n.a.
works.limitations: On real-to-sim physical properties it says methods exist 'to take constructed geometries and imbue them with physical properties' but 'still provide a considerable gap with respect to the real world'. Open question it poses: whether 'accurate physics modeling is needed to perform reliable model-based control' at all, vs learning a dynamics model that merely improves control. Only the first ~100k characters were read.

gaps: No sim-ready asset pipeline or asset library validates its assigned object parameters against the real motion of held-out objects. Evidence: the SimReady physics-material requirements page (nvidia.github.io/simready-foundation) lists density/static friction/dynamic friction/restitution attributes and says nothing about how values are obtained or validated; SIMPLER sets density from 'GPT-4 or Google search' and friction from 'common material properties' and only ablates that evaluation is insensitive to them; EmbodiedGen (2506.10600) assigns mass and friction from a VLM over four orthographic renders with, per the full text, no comparison to real measurements; searches for 'SimReady validation measured friction', 'object property dataset measured friction simulator held-out' returned measured databases (2404.07344, ViTacPhys) that never enter a simulator.

No per-object system-identification work transfers what it identified to an object the robot has not touched. Evidence: ASID, TwinAligner, PIN-WM, D-REX (2603.01151), Learning-to-Slide (2005.05456) each identify one object from that object's own interaction and report trajectory/task metrics on that object; none reports a material-level table or a held-out-object prediction. Searched 'material transfer identified friction unseen objects robot sysid' and 'held-out object real motion validation physical parameters' -- only the project's own e1 design matches that description.

No robot-free, video-only identification of rigid-object friction/mass/restitution exists in the robot-learning literature at more than a few objects. Evidence: Vid2Sid actuates the system itself and uses a fixed camera; PIN-WM needs one scripted robot push; TwinAligner needs Control-Hit-Slide; Real-is-Sim needs posed cameras plus a live robot. Searched 'video-only sysid rigid objects friction robot 2025 2026' -- hits were all robot-actuated.

Restitution is almost never identified or measured by practitioners. Evidence: of the works above only PIN-WM includes restitution (from one straight push, which barely excites it); SPI-Active, ASID, TwinAligner, MJX-sysid, DROPO identify mass/CoM/inertia/friction/actuator terms only; Isaac Lab DR practice randomises restitution in [0, 0.1] (secondary). Searched 'restitution identification real robot drop high-speed sim-to-real' -- nothing beyond Bounce-and-Learn (already known) surfaced.

No controlled study isolates whether OBJECT (not robot/actuator) parameter accuracy changes manipulation policy transfer. Evidence: positive evidence is task-specific (ASID rod balancing 6/9 vs DR 0/9); negative/indifferent evidence is SIMPLER's <= 15% sensitivity and 2606.20712's 'mass and friction yield no stable adaptation signal'; SPI-Active's +42-63% and MJX-sysid's 86% drift reduction concern the robot body. The Reality Gap survey lists sysid as 'crucial' without separating object from robot parameters. Searched 'ablation object friction mass accuracy policy transfer manipulation real robot' -- no dedicated study found.

Large contact datasets carry no object-physics labels. Evidence: DROID (76k trajectories, 564 scenes) and Open X-Embodiment (1M+ episodes) are vision + proprioception; a vendor summary claims <5% of Open-X contributors include force/torque (claru.ai, low confidence); searched 'DROID Open-X object mass friction annotation' -- nothing. Measured-property datasets exist only at 60-63 objects (2404.07344, ViTacPhys) and YCB's original physical-property table.

Differentiable engines are used in practice for actuator/robot parameters, not object properties, and not yet in the Isaac stack. Evidence: 2508.04696 (MJX, armature/frictionloss/damping), 2604.10351 (MJX actuator + payload mass), DiffMJX (2506.14186) on contact gradients; Isaac Lab paper says friction/mass must be set through PhysX CPU APIs and Newton integration is future work. Searched 'Warp Newton differentiable sysid object friction real video' -- only D-REX (mass via Gaussian-splat engine) and PIN-WM (own LCP solver).

'Interactable worlds beyond rooms' with validated physics do not exist. Evidence: scene generators found (EmbodiedGen, SAGE 2602.10116, ProcTHOR, Infinigen Indoors, survey 2604.26509) assign physics by VLM or defaults at room scale; the Isaac Sim survey (2606.03551) itself says generative world models 'lack physically consistent interaction'; searched 'city scale digital twin robot learning physics interactable 2025 2026' and got only Isaac Sim/Lab framework papers. Note: this absence is also consistent with no one needing it yet; it is an observed gap, not a demonstrated demand.
scouts.relevance_to_our_assets: The landscape splits into (i) per-object sysid from robot interaction (ASID, TwinAligner, PIN-WM, SPI-Active, DROPO/BayesSim), (ii) real-to-sim twins that sidestep parameters by visual correction or green-screening (Real-is-Sim, SIMPLER), (iii) differentiable-engine sysid of actuators (MJX works), and (iv) asset-level parameter assignment by VLM or material lookup with no validation (SimReady spec, EmbodiedGen, SIMPLER's object physics). The project's validated material table with a held-out real-object test (2.6 mm median vs 1.8 mm oracle, 70 objects) is exactly the missing validation layer under (iv): it is what SimReady/EmbodiedGen/SIMPLER would need to justify their numbers, and the finding that an LLM should name the material but not supply the number is directly usable by every pipeline that currently asks GPT for density. The real-footage Newton fit (0.4-1.0 mm RMS replay error) is the survey's 'offline replay error' metric computed without a robot, so it is the no-robot analogue of (i) and redundant with (i) only where a robot is available. The exact-mesh, differentiable Warp contact kernels are redundant with MJX/DiffMJX for actuator ID but are not duplicated for object-level ID from video (only PIN-WM's LCP solver and D-REX's splat engine do that, both robot-driven, both few objects); Isaac Lab's pending Newton integration is the delivery path practitioners will use, and SimReady USD (density, static/dynamic friction, restitution, mass, CoM, inertia) is the container the project's theta already maps onto. The negative results on Cosmos/V-JEPA/FPT/MYRIAD/Wan match practice: no practitioner work uses generative or predictive video models to obtain parameters, and the one place a VLM sits in a sysid loop (Vid2Sid) it proposes updates that are accepted by tracked-trajectory error, which is what the project's CoTracker3 pipeline already computes. Restitution measurement (240 fps phone drops into the p3 pipeline) would fill a hole nobody in the list fills. The sensitivity matrix and probe design map onto ASID/SPI-Active's Fisher-information exploration, but those need a robot; the project's probes are the authored-asset substitute. Finally, the evidence that object-parameter accuracy matters for policy transfer is thin and task-dependent (ASID positive; SIMPLER and 2606.20712 indifferent or negative), so any claim the project makes for robots must be made through the survey's SRCC / replay-error metrics rather than assumed.
scouts.caveats: Read in full (HTML, first ~100k chars): ASID, SIMPLER, Real-is-Sim, TwinAligner, PIN-WM, Vid2Sid, SPI-Active, ASAP, 2508.04696, 2606.20712, Isaac Lab, Reality Gap survey, EmbodiedGen. Abstract-only: TacSL, DROPO, 2404.07344, ViTacPhys, D-REX, Learning-to-Slide, Isaac Sim survey. Numbers were extracted by a fetch-summariser from the HTML and were not cross-checked against the PDFs; treat second-decimal figures as approximate. The '<5% of Open-X datasets have force/torque' figure and the '~1000 SimReady assets' figure come from vendor blogs (claru.ai, simready.artlabs.ai) and are low confidence. The Isaac Lab DR ranges (friction 0.1-1.0 / 0.3-1.5, restitution 0-0.1, mass +/-15-50%) are a search-engine synthesis across several locomotion papers, not a single primary source. Venues: ASID ICLR 2024 oral, SIMPLER CoRL 2024 (PMLR v270), PIN-WM and ASAP RSS 2025, Reality Gap survey ARCRAS 2026 are confirmed from listings; Vid2Sid appears in an ICLR 2026 virtual listing but its acceptance status was not verified further. arXiv ids dated 2602-2608 are 2026 papers and may still be under revision. Works the task listed as already identified (PhysX-*, VoMP, PhysTwin, gradSim, Galileo, SimReady, BEHAVIOR-1K, etc.) were deliberately not re-listed.

gap_scouts.angle: GAP SCOUT 1 — scoop sweep Jul–Oct 2026 (plus seeds and canonical works): does anything already deliver a measured multi-material, multi-surface (mu, e, CoM) table for everyday objects from consumer video with weighed/dynamometer truth and held-out-motion validation, or an assignment-route benchmark (VLM / LLM / handbook / generator) scored against held-out real motion?

works.name: GAUGE: A Measurement-Grounded Benchmark for Physical Fidelity in Simulation Engines and Video World Models (InternRobotics)
works.source: arXiv 2608.05948; code github.com/InternRobotics/GAUGE (MIT); HF dataset (gated, 401 on fetch)
works.what: 22 controlled task families (rigid bodies, cables, textiles, volumetric deformables) with real trajectories from 16 NOKOV infrared mocap cameras at 180 Hz on a 0.9 m x 0.9 m optical breadboard; 20 trials per task (~1,560 trials). Benchmarks Isaac Sim, Genesis and Newton on 14 families with parameters SET from the measured calibrations (no per-task tuning), errors reported as multiples of measurement repeat error; also 6 image-to-video models on 5 rigid tasks (Cosmos3, Genie3 named in README).
works.params_from: measured: friction by inclined-plane velocity tracking mu=(g sin t - a)/(g cos t); restitution on an inclined air-bearing rail e=v_out/v_in; mass and dimensions measured. Inertia/CoM: not stated as measured. Materials: wood, plastic, metal (rubber ball for bounce), apparently on one board/breadboard substrate (pairs wood-on-wood 0.39, plastic-on-wood, metal-on-wood listed).
works.evaluated_against: real motion (mocap) vs engine rollouts; no held-out-object protocol (it is an engine benchmark, not an assignment benchmark)
works.scale: 8 rigid task families x 3 materials, few physical specimens; 20 trials each; 22 families overall
works.limitations: Few objects and essentially one substrate; CoM/inertia not measured; no consumer video (mocap only); no assignment-route comparison. Directly relevant: with calibrated inputs, Newton's stock contact under-predicts slope-slider acceleration (wood 2.06 vs 2.58 m/s^2 real) and fails the bouncing ball (22.7x repeat error; negative acceleration trend), turntable 20x — i.e. the same contact regime the project's own kernels were built to fix. HF data card could not be read (gated).
works.confidence: high for abstract/method (arXiv HTML read); medium for per-engine numbers (part from pebblous.ai secondary report)

works.name: PhysVid — Inferring Dynamic Physical Properties from Video Foundation Models (Zhan, Ma, Xie, Zisserman, VGG Oxford)
works.source: arXiv 2510.02311 (CC BY 4.0); project page robots.ox.ac.uk/~vgg/research/physvid/ (404 on fetch)
works.what: Dataset + benchmark for elasticity (bouncing), viscosity (pouring) and dynamic friction (sliding) with synthetic train/test splits and a REAL split per property. Friction real split: 5 objects (plastic disk, LEGO brick, paper box, metal pencil box, wooden box) x 6 surfaces (gray towel, kitchen paper, tablecloth, red towel, wooden table, cardboard), 100 iPhone slow-motion videos, objects launched off a slope onto the flat surface, bird's-eye homography. Elasticity real split: 100 YouTube ball videos; viscosity: 12 liquids.
works.params_from: friction MEASURED with a spring dynamometer (drag at constant speed, mu_k = F/G), range 0.105–0.544; elasticity truth = manually annotated bounce-height ratios (no instrument); viscosity from reference tables
works.evaluated_against: real motion with instrument truth, object-surface pairs held out (train: 3 objects x 3 surfaces; test: 2 objects x 3 other surfaces). Real friction split: oracle Pearson 0.83 / AUC 0.87; DynamiCrafter 0.25 (0.80 with real-domain adaptation); V-JEPA-2 0.21 (0.73 with DA); GPT-4o 0.38, Gemini-2.5-pro 0.12, Qwen2.5VL 0.06
works.scale: 30 object-surface pairs, 100 real friction clips; 300 real clips overall
works.limitations: Scores video models as regressors, not assignment routes; no restitution with measured truth (ball videos annotated by hand), no CoM, no mass; objects are small flat sliders so shape/CoM effects absent; single phone, fps not stated in the read portion. Closest existing thing to a multi-surface measured mu table on phone video — but 5 objects.

works.name: Measuring Asset and Scene Reconstruction Effects in Real-to-Sim Robot Evaluation (Kaedim; 'yam-sim-harness')
works.source: arXiv 2610.00731 (CC BY 4.0); github.com/Kaedim/yam-sim-harness-oss (Apache 2.0; assets CC BY 4.0)
works.what: Compares an 'authored' real2sim reconstruction (metric scale from ChArUco board, authored physics, scene splats) against a generative-mesh + PhysX-default baseline for evaluating robot policies on a bimanual I2RT YAM cell in Isaac Sim 6.0.1. 5 tasks x 2 policies x 20 trials, real reference trials scored by a third party (Robocurve).
works.params_from: VLM assigns each object a material class and estimates mass and restitution from renders of the reconstructed mesh; friction from a per-class lookup table (source unstated). No measurement.
works.evaluated_against: real robot task scores: authored r = 0.90 vs default r = 0.51 with real trials; mean score error −10.56 pp. No comparison of any parameter to a scale, dynamometer or object motion.
works.scale: 21 objects (bottles, bin, bowls, blocks, cup, can, spray bottle, cutting board, cube, baseball, grapes, mug, plate)
works.limitations: Authors state geometry, scale, physics and scene change together so the physics contribution cannot be isolated; two policies, five tasks; automatic grading. Confirms the gap: sim-ready pipelines validate by policy success, not by held-out object motion.
