works.name: Δynamics: Language-Based Representation for Inferring Rigid-Body Dynamics From Videos (Kao et al., Cornell/Amazon)
works.what: VLM emits a structured text scene description (primitive shapes: sphere/cylinder/box) with mass, sliding and rolling friction and damping, which MuJoCo simulates; test-time sampling and evolutionary search refine it. Evaluated on CLEVRER and 235 real videos of everyday items (shoebox, Pringles can, baseball, tennis ball, tissue box, soccer ball, …) on indoor floors, running tracks, basketball courts.
works.params_from: VLM (fit to video by re-simulation search); 'ground truth' parameters are human annotations from a two-annotator pilot (~25 min per video)
works.evaluated_against: re-rendered simulation vs the input video (segmentation IoU, flow EPE; L1 parameter error only against human-annotated values). No instrument truth, no held-out protocol on measured parameters.
works.scale: 235 real videos, many everyday objects, several surfaces
works.limitations: Parameter truth is human-guessed, so it cannot say whether the recovered mu/mass is right; primitive-shape geometry; non-commercial licence. Nearest 'many objects, multiple surfaces, consumer video' work — but without measured truth.

works.name: EmbodiedGen V2: An Agentic, Simulation-Ready 3D World Engine for Embodied AI
works.what: Generative pipeline producing sim-ready assets (visual + collision geometry, physical parameters, affordances) and task-driven interactive worlds; 4K+ assets with affordances, 150 generated worlds.
works.params_from: VLM infers real-world scale, mass and friction RANGES from multi-view renders + category; stored in metadata 'for downstream sampling or calibration'
works.evaluated_against: sim task success (98.6% collision success in grasp-lift, 79.8% RL success) and 75% real-robot transfer; 200 held-out assets evaluated for geometry/scale, not for physics
works.scale: 4K+ assets, 150 worlds
works.limitations: No validation of mass/friction against measured values or real object motion; no restitution/CoM stated. Same construction as PhysX-Anything / ManiTwin.

works.name: ManiTwin: Scaling Data-Generation-Ready Digital Object Dataset to 100K
works.what: Image-to-sim-ready-asset pipeline producing 100K rigid graspable objects with physical properties, functional points, grasps and language, 'validated through physics-based simulation'.
works.params_from: VLM-inferred (search snippet quotes the paper's limitation: 'physical property estimates are VLM-inferred rather than ground-truth calibrated')
works.evaluated_against: sim stability / downstream data generation; no real motion
works.scale: 100K objects
works.limitations: No measured parameters, no held-out real-motion test; rigid graspables only. Confirms the gap at the largest scale.
works.confidence: medium (abstract read; VLM-inferred statement from a search snippet, not read in the PDF)

works.name: MolmoSpaces (Ai2) — physics-grounded scenes and 130K object assets
works.what: 230K+ scenes and 130K+ USD/MJCF objects (Objaverse + THOR) with mass, scale, metadata and 42M grasps for MuJoCo / ManiSkill / Isaac; stability tests remove jittering objects.
works.params_from: LLM: GPT-4.1 estimated mass and canonical pose for Objaverse objects; density adjusted so simulated mass matches LLM estimates; robot (Franka FR3) system-identified against real pick/push trajectories of cubes of known weight; articulated joints hand-tuned by teleoperation
works.evaluated_against: sim-to-real policy correlation with RoboArena (Pearson 0.96 / Spearman 0.98 on pick); no per-object parameter validation
works.scale: 130K objects, 230K scenes
works.limitations: Object mass/friction are LLM values checked for plausibility, not measured; the only real-motion calibration is of the robot plus known-weight cubes. Outside the Jul–Oct window (seed).

works.name: Agentic Real2Sim: Physics-based World Modeling with Vision-Language Agents
works.what: VLM agents convert real recordings of robot-object interaction (e.g. 25 DROID episodes) into simulatable scenes: geometry, object states, physical parameters; used for policy fine-tuning and as a surrogate evaluator; rigid, deformable and humanoid scenes.
works.params_from: VLM agent proposes parameters; for deformables, simulator rollouts are checked against observed deformation
works.evaluated_against: 8 real-sim episode pairs shown; policy-level evaluation; no parameter error against measured truth, no held-out-object protocol stated
works.scale: tens of episodes
works.limitations: Which parameters (mass/friction/restitution) and their accuracy are not quantified on the pages read.

works.name: ExPhy: A Benchmark for Explicit Physical Property Learning in Multi-Object Trajectory Forecasting
works.what: 24k PyBullet scenes (3–8 primitives each) with per-object mass, friction and restitution labels; ID, OOD-parameter and OOD-initial-state splits for trajectory forecasting that must expose physical properties.
works.params_from: simulator ground truth (synthetic)
works.evaluated_against: sim-only
works.scale: 24k scenes
works.limitations: No real data at all; primitives only. Listed because it is the in-window benchmark closest in parameter set (mu, e, mass).

works.name: PhyParam: Learning Explicit Physical Parameter Control and Benchmarking for Video Generation
works.what: 130K physically simulated videos across 5 rigid-body motion types with dense annotations (forces, mass, friction, restitution, gravity); a video generator conditioned on explicit parameters plus a benchmark checking force-balance/smooth-trajectory consistency.
works.params_from: simulator (synthetic)
works.evaluated_against: sim-only consistency checks
works.scale: 130K synthetic videos
works.limitations: No real objects, no measured parameters. Relevant only as evidence that 'parameter-conditioned video generation' is being pursued without any real-motion grounding.

works.name: DiagGen: Agentic Generation of Deformable Assets with Sim-based Diagnostics
works.what: Single image -> sim-ready deformable asset via a generate–simulate–diagnose–refine loop in which a VLM agent probes material parameters in simulation and refines them.
works.params_from: VLM diagnosis of simulated behaviour (no measurement)
works.evaluated_against: sim pick-and-place; no real motion
works.scale: not stated on pages read
works.limitations: Deformable, not rigid; the 'diagnostic' is a VLM judging simulator output — the same construction the project measured as uninformative for rigid parameters.

works.name: Vid2Sid: Videos Can Help Close the Sim2Real Gap (Qiu, Zhang, Cygan, Hughes)
works.what: VLM-in-the-loop system identification: foundation-model perception on paired sim/real videos, VLM diagnoses mismatches and proposes updates to friction, damping and stiffness with rationales; tendon finger in MuJoCo and continuum tentacle in PyElastica.
works.params_from: fit to video (VLM-proposed updates, optimiser-accepted)
works.evaluated_against: sim-sim validation (<13% mean relative error vs 28–98% baselines) and sim2real controls
works.scale: 2 systems, no object sets
works.limitations: Robot/mechanism parameters, not object tables; no held-out objects. Shows the field's current answer to 'VLM for parameters' is VLM as proposer with a simulator fit as the measurement — consistent with the project's finding that LLMs name but do not measure.

works.name: D-REX: Differentiable Real-to-Sim-to-Real Engine for Learning Dexterous Grasping
works.what: Gaussian-splat-based differentiable engine that identifies object MASS from real visual observations plus robot control signals, builds digital twins and trains force-aware grasping policies.
works.params_from: fit (gradient) to real observations + robot commands
works.evaluated_against: accuracy of mass identification 'across geometries and mass values' (numbers vs weighed truth not on the page read); grasp success
works.scale: not stated on the page read
works.limitations: Mass only (no friction/restitution/CoM); needs a robot and its control signals, which the project does not have.

works.name: Acoustic coefficient of restitution via smartphone (phyphox '(In)elastic collision'; Heckel, Glielmo, Gunkelmann, Pöschel, PRE 93, 032901, 2016; education replications)
works.source: Phys. Rev. E 93, 032901 (2016); phyphox.org/experiment/inelastic-collision/; JPPI 2022 (jurnal.untirta.ac.id 13400, DOAJ d8a930d7…) — both 403 on fetch
works.what: COR from the timing of successive bounce sounds, assuming equal fractional energy loss per bounce; phyphox implements it on any phone.
works.params_from: measured (acoustic timing)
works.evaluated_against: n.a. (instrument); the education paper reports 0.889±0.006 to 0.893±0.003 across temperatures and 0.848 / 0.716 / 0.836 for small basketball / tennis / ping-pong (secondary snippet)
works.scale: balls only in published uses
works.limitations: Requires audible, repeated bounces on a hard surface, so it does not cover soft objects or soft surfaces; no multi-object household table found; repeatability numbers come from a search snippet of an education journal, not read from the paper. OSP Tracker publications could not be checked (search budget exhausted).

works.name: Physics-Based Rigid Body Object Tracking and Friction Filtering From RGB-D Videos (Kandukuri-line, 3DV 2024)
works.what: Differentiable physics simulation as the transition model of an EKF to track mesh-shaped rigid objects in RGB-D and filter their friction coefficient; synthetic sliding/colliding sequences plus a real-world dataset; benchmark released.
works.params_from: fit to video (EKF through differentiable sim)
works.evaluated_against: real RGB-D sequences (object count, surfaces and friction truth not stated on the abstract page)
works.scale: small
works.limitations: RGB-D, few objects; canonical precedent for 'differentiable sim + filtering' friction from video, not a many-object table.

gaps: No measured multi-material x multi-surface (mu, e, CoM) table for everyday objects from consumer video with held-out-motion validation exists. Evidence: searches 'coefficient of restitution video dataset everyday objects 2026', 'friction from monocular video household objects real2sim 2026', 'physical parameter benchmark real trajectories rigid body friction restitution dataset 2026 weighed objects', 'real2sim rigid digital twin phone video physical parameters identification 2026 CoRL' returned only PhysVid (mu for 5 objects x 6 surfaces, dynamometer; no e/CoM/mass), GAUGE (mu and e for 3 materials on one breadboard, mocap, no CoM, no held-out object) and Δynamics (235 videos, human-annotated 'truth'). Nothing covers all three parameters, and nothing beyond PhysVid uses phone video with instrument truth.

No restitution dataset for many household objects on multiple surfaces at any frame rate. Evidence: the restitution searches above surfaced PhysVid's elasticity split (YouTube balls, bounce heights annotated by hand), GAUGE (air-bearing rail, a few balls) and acoustic phyphox education papers (balls only); the search 'high-speed video drop test restitution dataset household objects multiple surfaces 2025 2026' could not be run (budget), so this gap is asserted on the first set of queries only.

No assignment-route benchmark (VLM vs LLM vs handbook/material table vs generator) scored against held-out REAL object motion. Evidence: the search 'sim-ready asset physics validation real motion held-out VLM material assignment 2026' and the primary pages of Kaedim YAM (2610.00731), EmbodiedGen V2 (2607.07459), ManiTwin (2603.16866), MolmoSpaces (2602.11337), DiagGen (2609.23103) and Agentic Real2Sim (2607.19190) all show VLM/LLM-assigned parameters validated only by sim stability, downstream policy success or sim-to-real policy correlation; PhysVid compares video models and MLLMs as regressors on measured mu (GPT-4o Pearson 0.38, Gemini 0.12) but does not score a material-table or handbook route; none compares routes on held-out objects.

No work measures or validates centre of mass of everyday objects from video. Evidence: none of the 15 hits reports CoM/inertia measurement (GAUGE lists mass and dimensions only; Δynamics uses primitives; PhysVid sliders are flat); the query terms 'centre of mass' did not surface anything beyond the project's own topple probe literature.

No Newton/Warp-specific real-motion calibration of mesh contact exists outside GAUGE's engine comparison, which reports stock Newton as the worst of three engines on slope-slider, bouncing-ball and turntable tasks when fed measured parameters — i.e. the project's p4 result (Newton fitted to Physics 101 slides at 0.4–1.0 mm RMS) and its own contact kernels have no published counterpart. Evidence: GAUGE HTML (Table 3, Appendix) and the pebblous summary; no other hit evaluates Newton.

Scoop check for the exact seeds: 'Kaedim YAM' (2610.00731) is a policy-evaluation harness with VLM mass/restitution and a per-class friction table, not a measurement; UrbanVerse validates asset DIMENSIONS against published specs (1,335 objects, 17 categories), not physics; MolmoSpaces validates LLM mass only for plausibility. No follow-ups to GAUGE, PhysVid or Scalable Real2Sim adding held-out real-motion validation were found (the Scalable Real2Sim follow-up search returned only policy-evaluation real2sim systems: RobotArena-inf, PolaRiS, ComSim, Real2Render2Real, World Labs R2S2R blog, none describing parameter validation).
gap_scouts.relevance_to_our_assets: On this evidence the project's e1 held-out test (70 Physics 101 objects, 359 real trials; material-table 2.6 mm vs LLM-number 7.5 mm vs oracle 1.8 mm) is the only assignment-route comparison scored on held-out real motion in the literature, and its Physics 101 friction/density tables remain the only measured multi-material table — PhysVid (CC BY 4.0, iPhone slow-mo, dynamometer mu for 5 objects x 6 surfaces, pairs held out) is the one dataset that could extend that test to the MULTI-SURFACE axis Physics 101 lacks and would plug straight into the existing CoTracker3 + Newton fitting pipeline, while also giving a direct check of the project's geometric-mean pair rule across six substrates. GAUGE is complementary rather than redundant: its calibrated mu/e plus 180 Hz mocap trials (MIT code; data card gated) are an independent invariant check for the project's exact-mesh contact and Hunt-Crossley alpha, and its headline that stock Newton under-predicts slope sliding and fails bouncing with measured inputs is a published baseline the project's p4/p7/p8 results already improve on but have never been compared against. The VLM/LLM-assignment pipelines (Kaedim YAM, EmbodiedGen V2, ManiTwin, MolmoSpaces, PhysX-*) are what the project's 'LLM names material, table supplies number' finding benchmarks; none of them has a real-motion number, so the project's existing results are the only ones that can be cited as such. Restitution is the shared hole: no hit supplies a measured household-object e table, the project's own 30 fps attempt failed, and the acoustic phyphox route (phone microphone, reported ~±0.006 repeatability on balls, secondary source) is the cheapest instrument found that fits the no-rig constraint. The project's generative/predictive-model negatives (Cosmos, V-JEPA 2, FPT, MYRIAD, Wan) are consistent with PhysVid's real-split numbers (V-JEPA-2 Pearson 0.21 on mu without domain adaptation; MLLMs 0.06–0.38), which is independent corroboration rather than redundancy. Differentiable-engine parameter identification from real observation exists (D-REX mass via Gaussian splats + robot signals; the 3DV 2024 EKF friction filter on RGB-D) but each needs a robot or depth sensor and recovers one parameter; the project's Warp kernels with demonstrated density gradients through contact have no published many-object, video-only counterpart.
gap_scouts.caveats: The shared WebSearch budget ran out after ~20 queries, so the proceedings-level sweep requested (CoRL 2026 camera-ready list, RSS/ICRA/IROS 2026 proceedings, SIGGRAPH Asia 2026, NeurIPS 2026 D&B, CoRL sim-to-real / physical-world-model workshops) was NOT performed; coverage rests on keyword searches plus direct fetches of arXiv abstracts/HTML, GitHub READMEs and project pages. Not checked at all: OSP Tracker publications, Bounce-and-Learn follow-ups, Scalable Real2Sim's own follow-ups beyond the search snippet, PhysX-Omni's PhysXVerse material provenance, and any CoRL 2026 paper not already on arXiv under these keywords. ICCV runs in odd years, so there is no ICCV 2026 cycle (ECCV 2026 is the 2026 vision venue) — from background knowledge, not verified online. GAUGE's HF dataset card returned 401 and its project page was empty, so dataset licence (as opposed to the MIT code licence) and the per-pair coefficient values are unconfirmed; per-engine GAUGE numbers partly come from a secondary blog. PhysVid's project page 404'd; all PhysVid numbers are from the arXiv HTML. ManiTwin's 'VLM-inferred, not ground-truth calibrated' statement and the phyphox repeatability figures come from search snippets of secondary pages (the education-journal pages returned 403). Δynamics, MolmoSpaces, ManiTwin, Vid2Sid and D-REX fall outside the Jul–Oct 2026 window and are included only as seeds/closest neighbours. Nothing was fabricated; where a page did not state a quantity it is recorded as not stated.

gap_scouts.angle: GAP SCOUT 2 — consumer/impact brief: is there published evidence that per-object friction / restitution / centre-of-mass accuracy changes a downstream outcome (policy transfer, task success, sim-real correlation, outcome class), and can any delivery target (SimReady/UsdPhysics, PhysX/Isaac Lab, MuJoCo, Genesis, UrbanVerse) ingest a per-material (mu, e(v), density, provenance) row rather than a scalar?

works.name: SIMPLER — Evaluating Real-World Robot Manipulation Policies in Simulation (Li et al., CoRL 2024)
works.source: arXiv 2405.05941 (HTML v1, Appendix F, Table X)
works.what: Sim replicas of real robot setups for policy evaluation; the only paper found that explicitly sweeps object physics and reports the downstream effect on sim-real agreement. Table X-a sweeps coke-can mass 10/20/40/80 g x gripper static friction 0.25/0.5/1.0/2.0: Pearson r stays 0.957-0.990, MMRV 0.031 in every cell. Table X-b sweeps cabinet joint friction 0.0125-0.20: r 0.903-0.941, MMRV 0.055 (0.105 at 0.15). Authors: 'altering these parameters has a moderate (<=15%) impact on the success rates of different policies' and SIMPLER 'is robust to imprecisely estimated physical simulation parameters.' By contrast, robot-controller sysID matters: perturbing PD gains raised control loss 0.131 -> 0.432 and MMRV 0.031 -> 0.100 (Table II).
works.params_from: table / LLM: uniform density 'by querying their common material density in GPT-4 or Google search', friction 'based on their common material properties'; CoM and static/dynamic friction explicitly simplified.
works.evaluated_against: real robot policy success (paired sim/real evaluation; Pearson r and MMRV)
works.scale: 2 robot setups (Google Robot, WidowX), a handful of objects, 4x4 and 6-point physics sweeps
works.limitations: Measures ranking robustness of closed-loop policy evaluation, not physical accuracy: a <=15% success shift that preserves ranking is reported as a non-effect. Only one object (coke can) and one articulation swept; no restitution or CoM sweep; no held-out real object.

works.name: ASID: Active Exploration for System Identification in Robotic Manipulation (Memmel et al., ICLR 2024)
works.what: Fisher-information-driven real exploration, then sim parameter refinement, then policy training. Real results: rod balancing with unknown mass distribution 6/9 (ASID) vs 0/9 (domain randomisation); shuffleboard (puck sliding on unknown-friction surface) 7/10 vs 3/10. Sim: rod tilt error 0.00 deg vs 26.69 deg (DR). 'Typically a single episode of data suffices.'
works.params_from: fit to real robot interaction (mass/inertia distribution, surface/rolling/torsional friction, articulation)
works.evaluated_against: real robot task success with vs without identification
works.scale: 3-4 tasks, 1 robot, ~10 real trials per task
works.limitations: Needs a robot to excite the object; outcome deltas are for open-loop/feed-forward tasks where the parameter directly sets the outcome; no per-object library or transfer to unseen objects.

works.name: DROPO: Sim-to-Real Transfer with Offline Domain Randomization (Tiboni, Arndt, Kyrki)
works.what: Likelihood-based fit of mean and covariance of a Gaussian over sim parameters from offline real trajectories. Real posteriors are extremely narrow: hockey puck mass 0.111 (sigma 2.2e-4), friction x 0.349 (3.4e-5), friction y 0.231 (4.7e-4), contact time constant 0.019 (6.7e-5); Panda box push mass 1.065 kg (1.3e-4), friction x 0.387 (3.0e-3), friction y 0.921 (5.3e-4), plus CoM offset. Real transfer: puck — DROPO and DROID 'significantly outperformed UDR', no meaningful DROPO-vs-DROID difference; box push — DROPO reached 'as close as 2 cm' to target, beating DROID and BayesSim.
works.params_from: fit to real robot trajectories (offline, gradient-free optimiser)
works.evaluated_against: real robot distance-to-target / success
works.scale: 2 real tasks (hockey puck, offset-CoM box push), 18 and 5 parameters
works.limitations: Posterior widths are optimiser outputs, not calibrated uncertainty (sigmas of 1e-5 on friction are not physical). Anisotropic friction x/y absorbs unmodelled effects ('effective' parameters). Robot required.

works.name: BayesSim: adaptive domain randomization via probabilistic inference (Ramos, Possas, Fox; RSS 2019)
works.what: Likelihood-free posterior over sim parameters. The outcome-level finding: on Fetch Slide (open-loop puck slide, friction unknown) 'using a wide uniform prior has led the robot to achieve a very poor performance' while posterior-trained policies peak 'around the true friction value'; posterior log-prob at truth -2.39+/-0.06 (BayesSim RFF) vs 1.01+/-0.38 for uniform prior.
works.params_from: fit to (mostly simulated, some real) trajectories
works.evaluated_against: sim-only for the friction result; policy reward vs true parameter
works.scale: CartPole, Fetch push/slide; single-parameter posteriors
works.limitations: The friction-sensitivity evidence is sim-only; shows that open-loop tasks are friction-sensitive and closed-loop ones are not, which is the same split SIMPLER's robustness finding sits on.

works.name: Real-World Deployment of Massively Parallel Sampling-Based MPC for Contact-Rich Manipulation (Dierking, Carvalho, Le, Chalvatzaki, Peters)
works.what: JAX+MuJoCo sampling MPC on a Franka Research 3 for Push-T, with online domain randomisation over 8 domains. Verified quote: 'Mass and friction yield no stable adaptation signal. Physics is dominated by contact timing and constraint resolution forces rather than by smooth variation in the randomized parameter.' Also: error signal is asymmetric — 'low-mass/friction domains overshoot and accumulate large pose errors, while high-mass domains move less and can appear spuriously consistent.' Contact-initiation margins (+/-1 cm) do give interpretable signals. On hardware both uniform and adaptive DR improve pose quality; adaptive-vs-uniform advantage 'small and not yet statistically conclusive.'
works.params_from: randomised ranges (per-body/per-geom MuJoCo models), adapted online from pose error
works.evaluated_against: real robot Push-T final pose
works.scale: 1 task, 1 robot, 6 seeds, 8 domains x 160 samples at 5 Hz
works.limitations: Negative result specific to MPC replanning at 5 Hz with pose-error feedback; does not say friction is irrelevant to the outcome, only that it is not identifiable from that feedback (the 'high-mass appears consistent' asymmetry is the same motion-magnitude confound this project measured).

works.name: Measuring Asset and Scene Reconstruction Effects in Real-to-Sim Robot Evaluation (Verma et al.; code github.com/Kaedim/yam-sim-harness-oss)
works.what: Bimanual cell, 5 tasks x 2 policies (pi0.5, MolmoAct2), 20 sim trials per cell per reconstruction vs 200 real trials. Authored reconstruction: Pearson r = 0.90 between sim and real cell means, mean score error 6.97 pp; default (TRELLIS mesh, hand-typed scale, convex decomposition, PhysX defaults density 1000, friction 0.5, restitution 0): r = 0.51, error 17.54 pp; reduction 10.56 pp.
works.params_from: VLM (mass and restitution 'estimated by a vision-language model per object'), friction 'from a per-class table'
works.evaluated_against: real robot policy success correlation
works.scale: 10 cells, 400 sim / 200 real trials
works.limitations: Verified confound, in the authors' words: the two conditions 'differ in object geometry, texture, metric scale, collision geometry, mass, friction, restitution and scene at once, so the current design ... cannot say how much comes from the objects, how much from the scene, or which object property matters most.' The 0.51 -> 0.90 is therefore not evidence about physics parameters.

works.name: Validating Robotics Simulators on Real-World Impacts (Acosta, Yang, Posa; RA-L/IROS 2022)
works.what: Identifies contact parameters of Drake, MuJoCo, Bullet from real cube tosses and a Cassie landing. Identified: Drake stiffness 10,800 N/m, dissipation 0.4 s/m, mu 0.10; MuJoCo stiffness 3,300, damping 45, mu 0.22; Bullet 1,800, 27, mu 0.36 — three different 'frictions' for one cube. Cube-toss errors: position 13.5/25.1/14.9 % of cube width, rotation 16.5/21.7/16.5 deg. 'Simulators capture inelastic impacts surprisingly well, though generally fail to reproduce elasticity.' Sensitivity: good fits exist over 'a wide range of contact parameters, which suggests that extensive identification of the contact parameters is not necessary.'
works.params_from: fit to real motion-capture trajectories per simulator
works.evaluated_against: real cube toss and biped landing trajectories
works.scale: 1 cube, 1 biped; 3 simulators
works.limitations: Parameters are simulator-specific effective values (mu 0.10-0.36 for the same cube); restitution is the part none reproduces; a flat objective means the outcome is insensitive to parameters in the inelastic regime tested.

works.name: More than a Million Ways to Be Pushed / Friction Variability in Auto-collected Planar Pushing (Yu, Bauza, Fazeli, Rodriguez; MIT)
works.what: Real pushing dataset on 4 surfaces. Dynamic-friction std per surface: Delrin 0.016, ABS 0.017, plywood 0.024, PU 0.064. Break-in drift after 100 scans: Delrin 0.16 -> 0.12 (-22%), ABS -13.6%, plywood -11.3%. PU friction is velocity-dependent (rises up to 1.0 at high speed) and anisotropic (max/min ~3/2). Repeatability of 2,000 identical pushes: final-pose std 3.4 mm/1.3 deg (Delrin) to 11.7 mm/4.5 deg (PU).
works.params_from: measured (force/torque + motion capture)
works.evaluated_against: real motion (repeat trials)
works.scale: 11 shapes, 4 surfaces, >1M samples
works.limitations: Pushing only, no restitution; defines the noise floor any per-object friction claim must beat (a 5-10% friction uncertainty is within surface drift).

works.name: Omnipush: accurate, diverse, real-world dataset of pushing dynamics (Bauza et al., IROS 2019)
works.what: 250 objects x 250 pushes with modular mass distribution (60-150 g side weights, ~5x range). Meta-learned dynamics: RMSE 4.9 mm vs 7.2 mm pooled baseline vs Bayes-error bound <3.6 mm; noise baseline from 5 shapes x 2.5k repeated pushes. Mass distribution demonstrably changes outcome: weight nearer the pusher -> more rotation.
works.params_from: measured (known added masses, shapes)
works.evaluated_against: real motion (held-out objects)
works.scale: >60k pushes, 250 objects
works.limitations: Learned model, not simulator parameters; CoM effect shown qualitatively plus prediction error, not as an outcome-class flip rate.

works.name: UrbanVerse: Scaling Urban Simulation by Watching City-Tour Videos (ICLR 2026)
works.what: 100k+ urban assets with 33-36 attributes incl. mass and friction, 288 PBR ground materials (98 road, 190 sidewalk) selected by pixel MSE; policies: +6.3% sim, +30.1% zero-shot real success, 300 m mission with 2 interventions.
works.params_from: VLM: 'we leverage the world knowledge of GPT-4.1 to annotate each asset with semantic, affordance, and physical attributes'. Ground materials come from free PBR repositories with no friction table found in paper, appendix, project page.
works.evaluated_against: real robot navigation success; attribute check: mass MAPE 19.58% vs references, geometry 1-8%
works.scale: 100k assets, city scale
works.limitations: No ablation isolating physical attributes; friction never validated; ground-material friction assignment not documented (the 'ground-material table' in the brief could not be confirmed as a physics table).

works.name: MetaUrban: An Embodied AI Simulation Platform for Urban Micromobility
works.what: Compositional urban scenes; ground 'textures with different friction coefficients' and procedural terrain (slopes, steps, stairs, ramps, rough). Section 4.2 varies agent mechanical parameters (max speed, steering, wheel friction, engine/brake force) across wheelchair/scooter/delivery robot and finds cost/mobility trade-offs.
works.params_from: authored/assigned per texture and per vehicle (no measurement reported)
works.evaluated_against: sim-only agent cost/success
works.scale: infinite procedural scenes
works.limitations: Friction-label effect on policy is not isolated; the mechanical-structure ablation varies five vehicle parameters together.

works.name: BEHAVIOR-1K / RoboCasa / RoboVerse (benchmark asset suites)
works.source: arXiv 2403.09227; arXiv 2406.02523; arXiv 2504.18904; roboverse.wiki randomization page
works.what: BEHAVIOR-1K: 9,000+ objects 'annotate rich physical (e.g., friction, mass, articulation)' — some properties 'programmatically generated from the 3D assets', others 'need to be annotated ... such as Weight'; annotation verified by human approval (>96.8%), never against real motion; only ablation is on grasping/motion-execution assumptions. RoboCasa: Objaverse/Luma assets, physics assignment not discussed, DR is visual only (100 textures per surface class). RoboVerse/MetaSim: PhysicsRandomCfg exposes mass_range, friction_range (example 0.3-0.8), restitution_range (0.1-0.3) with no cited evaluation of ranges.
works.params_from: manual annotation / unspecified / randomised ranges
works.evaluated_against: none for physics parameters
works.scale: 1k activities / 120 tasks / unified multi-sim
works.limitations: No DR-range ablation on physics parameters found in any of the three; physics values carry no provenance.

works.name: Delivery path A: SimReady / UsdPhysicsMaterialAPI + PhysX combine modes + Isaac Lab RigidBodyMaterialCfg
works.source: nvidia.github.io/simready-foundation (physics_materials/requirements), docs.omniverse.nvidia.com simready physics-best-practices, archive.docs.nvidia.com PxCombineMode, github isaac-sim/IsaacLab physics_materials_cfg.py and envs/mdp/events.py
works.what: Per-material row IS the schema: physics:density, physics:staticFriction, physics:dynamicFriction, physics:restitution on a Material prim bound via material:binding:physics; SimReady additionally requires a UsdPhysics Mass per geometry prim (kg). Pair combination (PhysxMaterialAPI frictionCombineMode / restitutionCombineMode): average (a+b)/2, min, multiply a*b, max; precedence 'maximum(material0.combineMode, material1.combineMode)' with enum order AVERAGE<MIN<MULTIPLY<MAX. Isaac Lab RigidBodyMaterialCfg: static_friction 0.5, dynamic_friction 0.5, restitution 0.0, combine modes default 'average', compliant_contact_stiffness/damping 0.0; no density, no velocity field. Isaac Lab DR samples num_buckets materials uniformly from ranges (PhysX limit 64,000 materials), optional make_consistent (dynamic <= static).
works.params_from: n.a. (schema)
works.evaluated_against: none
works.scale: industry standard
works.limitations: Restitution is a scalar; no e(v) law, no provenance/metadata field (measured vs estimated) found on any requirements page; SimReady spec pages reached were overview-level, so a hidden provenance field is possible but was not found.

works.name: Delivery path B: MuJoCo contact model (solref/solimp, friction max rule, <pair>)
works.what: Pair friction: 'the element-wise maximum of each friction coefficient over the two geoms is used' unless geom priority differs; solref/solimp mixed by solmix-weighted average. Restitution is not a material scalar: controlled indirectly through solref (negative 'direct' format allows damping = 0 for elastic). <contact><pair> lets an explicit geom pair override condim, friction, solref, solreffriction, solimp, margin, gap.
works.params_from: n.a. (schema)
works.evaluated_against: none
works.scale: industry standard
works.limitations: No velocity-dependent restitution mechanism documented; no density-free per-material restitution row; a material table must be expanded into per-pair <pair> elements to express anything but max-rule friction.

works.name: Delivery path C: Genesis gs.materials.Rigid
works.what: Rigid material fields: rho (density), friction, friction_torsional, friction_rolling, coup_friction 0.1, coup_softness 0.002, coup_restitution 0.0 ('Non-zero coup_restitution could lead to instability'), SDF settings. DR guidance: per-link friction ratio 0.5-1.5x, mass 0.75-1.25x, CoM shift up to 5 cm, actuator gains.
works.params_from: n.a. (schema); DR ranges are unexplained recommendations
works.evaluated_against: none
works.scale: library
works.limitations: Restitution exists only for solver coupling, not rigid-rigid contact; no e(v); per-material friction is a single scalar with no documented pair-combine rule found.

gaps: No published outcome-flip number for per-object physics. Searched: SIMPLER (Table X), the Kaedim/Verma harness (2610.00731), Acosta-Yang-Posa, Dierking 2606.20712, UrbanVerse, MetaUrban, BEHAVIOR-1K, RoboCasa, RoboVerse. Every paper that varies friction/mass either (a) reports the downstream metric as robust (SIMPLER: r 0.957-0.990 across a 8x mass x 8x friction grid, <=15% success shift; Acosta: 'extensive identification ... is not necessary'), (b) finds no adaptation signal (2606.20712), or (c) changes everything at once (2610.00731's own confound statement). Nobody reports P(outcome class flips | parameter error) for stays/slides/topples/bounces on a held-out real object.

No consumer ingests a velocity-dependent restitution e(v). Checked UsdPhysicsMaterialAPI/SimReady (physics:restitution scalar), PhysxMaterialAPI/Isaac Lab (restitution float, compliant stiffness/damping only), MuJoCo (restitution via solref damping, no velocity term documented), Genesis (coup_restitution scalar, rigid-rigid none). Acosta et al. independently report that none of Drake/MuJoCo/Bullet reproduce elastic impacts.

No provenance field (measured / table / VLM / fit-to-video) in any physics-material schema or asset suite. SimReady requirement pages, Isaac Lab cfg, MuJoCo XML, Genesis material: none. UrbanVerse (GPT-4.1), BEHAVIOR-1K (manual 'Weight'), SIMPLER (GPT-4/Google lookup), Verma (VLM mass/restitution + per-class friction table) all store values without origin.

No published ablation of domain-randomisation RANGES for object friction/mass/restitution in the large asset suites. RoboCasa DR is visual only; BEHAVIOR-1K's only ablation is on grasp/motion assumptions; RoboVerse and Genesis docs give example ranges (0.3-0.8; 0.5-1.5x) with no cited effect; Isaac Lab's randomize_rigid_body_material documents the bucket mechanism, not an evaluation. (Search budget expired before 2025-2026 DR-range ablation queries could run; see caveats.)

No sim-ready suite validates annotated friction against real motion. UrbanVerse validates mass (MAPE 19.58%) and geometry (1-8%) against reference values, never friction, and never against motion; BEHAVIOR-1K validates by human approval (>96.8%); SIMPLER and Verma assign and move on. The only real-motion validations found are robot-in-the-loop sysID (ASID, DROPO, BayesSim, SPI-Active 2505.14266) and the MIT push / Omnipush datasets, none of which produce a reusable per-material library.

Pair-friction combine rules are engine-specific and none is a geometric mean: PhysX offers average/min/multiply/max with max-wins precedence, MuJoCo uses element-wise max (or priority), Genesis undocumented. A material table whose rows were fitted under a product rule (as this project's p5 ratio test supports) has no direct slot; expressing sqrt(mu_a*mu_b) requires authoring sqrt(mu) per material under 'multiply' or expanding to explicit pairs (MuJoCo <pair>). No paper found that states or tests which combine rule matches real pair data.
gap_scouts.relevance_to_our_assets: The landscape says the project's validated assets sit in a slot nobody occupies but few consumers currently reward. What they could feed: (1) a per-material row (mu_pair, density by build, e via alpha, provenance) maps directly onto UsdPhysicsMaterialAPI / Isaac Lab RigidBodyMaterialCfg and MuJoCo <pair> overrides, but e(v)=1-alpha*v must be collapsed to a scalar at a stated reference speed and the geometric-mean pair rule must be re-expressed as sqrt(mu) under PhysX 'multiply' or as explicit MuJoCo pairs, since no engine combines by geometric mean; (2) the held-out real-motion test (2.6 mm median on 70 unseen objects; LLM-named material costs 0.1 mm, LLM number 3x worse) is exactly the validation that UrbanVerse, BEHAVIOR-1K, SIMPLER and the Kaedim harness lack, and the MIT-push repeatability floor (3.4-11.7 mm final-pose std) shows that resolution is at the noise floor of real pushing; (3) the project's own motion-magnitude confound and 'no static friction creep' findings are the same mechanism Dierking et al. report as 'high-mass domains ... appear spuriously consistent', so the probe-sensitivity matrix is a ready instrument for the outcome-class sensitivity number that does not exist in print. Where it is redundant: robot-in-the-loop sysID (ASID, DROPO, BayesSim) already recovers mass/friction/CoM posteriors from one real episode with downstream success deltas (0/9 -> 6/9; 3/10 -> 7/10), so a per-object fit from real footage competes with them only where no robot exists (authored assets, city-scale suites); the Physics-101/Galileo line already fit physics to the same footage, and SIMPLER's Table X is direct evidence that closed-loop policy-evaluation consumers are nearly insensitive to the parameters this project measures, so any impact claim has to be made on open-loop or outcome-class tasks (Fetch Slide, hockey puck, stays/slides/topples), which is where BayesSim and DROPO show the parameter actually sets the result.
gap_scouts.caveats: The shared WebSearch budget ran out after ~15 queries; everything after that was direct WebFetch of known primary URLs. Not covered as a result: PolaRiS (named in 2610.00731 as the default-scene recipe), a targeted 2025-2026 scan for DR-range ablations on object physics, and a deeper MetaUrban friction-label check (only its HTML first 100k chars were read). SimReady requirement pages fetched were overview-level (the 'collider-material-binding' and FET_006/007 subsections were not reachable), so absence of a provenance field there is medium confidence; the PhysX combine-precedence rule was read from the archived PhysX 3.3.4 API page and confirmed in spirit by Isaac Lab docs. Isaac Lab cfg was read from the GitHub main file (docs pages 404'd). The UrbanVerse 'ground-material table' named in the brief could not be found as a physics table in the paper, appendix, or project page; the GitHub repo URL guessed returned 404. BEHAVIOR-1K's appendix was read only through character 200k of the HTML. DROPO sigmas are quoted as printed; their physical meaning is doubtful. SPI-Active (2505.14266) was fetched but identifies mass/inertia/actuator parameters, not friction, so it is not listed as a work. All numbers are quoted from arXiv HTML/abs pages or official docs; none were inferred.

gap_scouts.angle: GAP SCOUT 3 — engine / contact-law brief: (a) which shipped differentiable simulators give validated gradients through mesh–mesh narrow-phase contact; (b) velocity-dependent restitution laws and DEM calibration / substep-convergence practice.

works.name: Nimble (DART fork): Fast and Feature-Complete Differentiable Physics for Articulated Rigid Bodies with Contact
works.what: Analytical gradients through an LCP contact solver (Dantzig-style, Baumgarte-stabilised), exploiting LCP sparsity. Appendix C enumerates supported pairs: sphere-sphere, sphere-mesh, capsule-capsule/sphere/mesh, and mesh-mesh via 'witness hull' construction from approximate separating planes, splitting into vertex-face and edge-edge contacts. For mesh/polygonal geometry the contact-normal derivative dn/dq is set to ZERO (normals treated as locally constant); analytic only for curved primitives. Elastic collision handled by a continuous-time approximation: dp_{t+1}/dp_t ~ -sigma (restitution), dp_{t+1}/dv_t ~ -sigma*dt, combined by least squares into a global Jacobian. 'Complementarity-aware' gradient heuristic to escape saddles.
works.params_from: n.a. (engine); the paper states it 'doesn't yet differentiate through geometric properties ... or friction coefficients'
works.evaluated_against: sim-only trajectory optimisation (catapult, jump-worm, Atlas jump). Finite differences are used as a TIMING baseline (87.8x speedup vs central differences on Atlas, 21.9x on Half Cheetah); no gradient-error metric vs FD is reported.
works.scale: single robots, tens of contacts, CPU
works.limitations: no friction-coefficient gradient; mesh normals frozen; 'computing dJ^T f/dq takes a large portion of total computation'; complementarity-aware gradient 'does not guarantee' global convergence; no real-data system ID; sustained vs glancing regimes not separately validated.

works.name: Dojo: A Differentiable Physics Engine for Robotics
works.what: Variational integrator + hard contact as a nonlinear complementarity problem with second-order (exact Coulomb) cone constraints, solved by a custom primal-dual interior-point method; gradients by the implicit function theorem at the solver's central path (smooth by construction). Stable at 20–500 Hz.
works.params_from: system ID on REAL data: friction coefficient and the 8 vertex positions of a box tossed on a table, recovered 'within 5% of the true geometry and friction'
works.evaluated_against: real box-toss trajectories (one object); qualitative comparison of IFT gradients vs randomized smoothing and point-wise gradients (Fig. 4) — no numeric FD error reported
works.scale: single objects / humanoid, Julia + Python bindings
works.limitations: collision geometry 'limited to simple shape primitives': point, sphere, capsule vs flat surfaces (humanoid foot = 4 points); no meshes; no restitution (inelastic impacts); per-step NCP cost and interior-point warm-start difficulty; nonconvex solves can fail.

works.name: DiffMJX / Contacts-from-Distance (CFD): Differentiable Simulation of Hard Contacts with Soft Gradients
works.what: Extends MuJoCo-XLA: adaptive (5th-order RK, PID tolerance 1e-5) time integration of MuJoCo's soft-constraint/penalty contact (solref/solimp impedance) so stiff contacts stop corrupting gradients, plus CFD — penalty + straight-through estimation used only in the backward pass so pre-contact gradients do not vanish when bodies separate.
works.params_from: system ID on REAL data: ContactNet acrylic-cube tosses (550 trajectories, 1480 Hz; GT 0.37 kg, mu 0.18, e 0.125). Fitted side length, mass, solref (time constant, damping ratio), solimp and friction jointly; restitution/friction not fitted directly but via solver parameters.
works.evaluated_against: central finite differences on toss distance (Fig. 3: MJX deviates for stiff contact, DiffMJX agrees — plotted, no error number); real cube-toss trajectory MSE 0.32 -> 0.25 with pre-tuned init; MPC tasks (dexterous hand, tennis, cube reorientation with muscle models).
works.scale: single objects / hands, GPU via JAX
works.limitations: collision smoothing modified only for plane-cylinder, sphere-capsule, capsule-capsule, plane-capsule, plane-box; mesh-mesh explicitly 'not relevant in our experiments'; authors note cube dynamics after a CORNER hits the table are chaotic, so trajectory error stays ~0.25; adaptive stepping needs tolerance loosened to 1e-4 for cost; glancing impacts not addressed.

works.name: Ostrich: Taking Large Strides Through Stiff Contact in Differentiable Dynamics
works.what: GPU rigid-body simulator with hard contact via Fischer–Burmeister NCP + Coulomb friction (maximal dissipation), resolved by non-smooth Newton at ~0.1 s steps; adjoint via implicit function theorem reusing the forward Schur complement at O(1) memory per step. 8,192 parallel worlds; 50x larger steps than MuJoCo, 211x faster iterations than MJX.
works.params_from: system ID of friction coefficients and servo stiffness on real-robot training runs
works.evaluated_against: FD gradient checks run in CI: max relative error 0.02% on an impulsive contact-boundary test, <=0.4% across all wheel DOFs, <=1.6% on cart-pole losses over 50-step horizons; real three-wheeled 106 kg robot, 14 pallet traversals (0.12–2.05 m/s), ten held-out runs, 0.208 m combined error vs lidar-inertial odometry (matches reference MuJoCo).
works.scale: 8,192 worlds on one GPU; triangle-mesh terrain with ~12,500 faces
works.limitations: geometry: primitives vs plane/triangle-mesh terrain (mesh-wheel); mesh–mesh not demonstrated; 'impacts are resolved inelastically (e=0); restitution is left to future work'; long-horizon mesh contact requires truncating position pull-back gradients; single robot platform; code 'will be released' (not available at time of reading).

works.name: Jade: Differentiable Physics Engine for Articulated Rigid Bodies with Intersection-Free Frictional Contact
works.what: Standalone engine (explicit Euler + LCP, modified Dantzig for multiple frictional contacts). Continuous collision detection for two triangle MESHES — edge-edge and vertex-face pairs checked recursively each step — with backtracking to the time of impact; gradient derived through the backtracking/TOI step by implicit differentiation.
works.params_from: n.a. (no parameter identification experiments)
works.evaluated_against: sim-only: gripper-plate picking (intersection-free), ball-collision optimisation (position error 0.00156, reported as ~20x smaller than Nimble), sliding-object friction robustness. No FD error table.
works.scale: few articulated bodies, CPU
works.limitations: authors note 'rounding approximation of gradient calculation caused by coarse detection in CCD'; no deformables; code promised ('will be released at our project website'), repository not linked in paper; no real data; sustained-contact gradient accuracy not quantified.

works.name: DiffSDFSim: Differentiable Rigid-Body Dynamics with Implicit Shapes
works.what: Objects as signed distance fields; meshes extracted by marching cubes, contact points localised by Frank–Wolfe on triangles; LCP time-stepping (de Avila Belbute-Peres et al. 2018 primal-dual, differentiable at solution); novel implicit differentiation of the time of impact w.r.t. shape via D(h,theta)=0 and a pseudo-inverse. Non-convex shapes supported.
works.params_from: gradient-based fits of friction, mass, applied force, shape (radius / latent code), restitution, pose from trajectories or depth images
works.evaluated_against: synthetic: 50-run batteries (friction error 1e-4, mass 0.002, force 0.01; shape Chamfer 0.010–0.021; depth-image radius 3.68 -> 3.13 cm vs GT 3.24); REAL: one RealSense D455 RGB-D sequence of a tennis ball (radius, restitution, friction, init state). No finite-difference gradient validation reported.
works.scale: single objects, PyTorch, 'several seconds of computation per simulated second'
works.limitations: 'sharp-edged shapes exhibit unstable contact geometry'; shape-from-inertia hits local minima; one real object; mesh–mesh via SDF-extracted meshes, not raw triangle meshes.

works.name: NVIDIA Newton 1.4.0 collision pipeline + 'differentiable contacts' (installed source and docs)
works.what: Full shape-pair coverage (plane, heightfield, sphere, capsule, box, cylinder, cone, ellipsoid, convex hull, mesh, SDF, particle) via MPR/GJK for convex pairs, Warp BVH for raw triangle meshes, precomputed SDFs, and SDF-hydroelastic area contacts. Differentiability: the narrow phase is FROZEN (kernels use enable_backward=False / record_tape=False); a post-processing kernel re-reads frozen body-local contact points, world normal and margins and reconstructs world points and signed distance through the differentiable body_q — 'gradients flow through the contact points and distance but not through the normal direction' ('first-order tangent-plane approximation'). Docs mark it Experimental: 'may change without prior notice'. Warp itself ships native adjoints adj_mesh_query_point_sign_normal / adj_mesh_query_point / adj_mesh_eval_position (warp/native/mesh.h).
works.params_from: n.a. (engine)
works.evaluated_against: unit tests only: FD agreement of distance gradient w.r.t. z for sphere-on-plane and for two overlapping BOXES across translation DOFs; multi-step sphere position loss vs FD. No mesh or SDF shape appears in the differentiable-contact tests; no published gradient-accuracy numbers.
works.scale: GPU, many worlds
works.limitations: frozen normals and frozen contact assignment (no gradient through which pair/face is in contact); tested on sphere/box only; SolverVBD gradients exactly 0 (project measurement); SolverSemiImplicit differentiable; alpha-stage API.

works.name: MuJoCo XLA (MJX) / Brax generalized pipeline
works.what: JAX reimplementation of MuJoCo (successor of Brax's generalized pipeline). Convex-mesh collisions by branchless Separating Axis Test; non-convex meshes only via convex decomposition (maxhullvert). Autodiff via jax.grad.
works.params_from: n.a. (engine)
works.evaluated_against: none published for contact gradients; docs: 'Differentiability is mostly supported in MJX-JAX but is not currently available in MJX-Warp' (with a linked open issue).
works.scale: thousands of parallel envs on GPU/TPU
works.limitations: mesh-primitive ~200 vertices, convex-convex 'fewer than 32 vertices'; CYLINDER/ELLIPSOID do not collide with box/mesh/hfield; no gradient validation statement; MJX-Warp non-differentiable.

works.name: Genesis (rigid solver differentiability status)
works.what: General-purpose multi-solver engine (rigid, MPM, SPH, FEM, PBD). Claims 'differentiable by design' with 'hand-derived gradients for the hardest kernels'.
works.params_from: n.a.
works.evaluated_against: no gradient validation found in the docs
works.scale: GPU, many envs
works.limitations: docs state 'some contact and collision paths do not provide gradients. Gradients through those paths may be zero or undefined'; earlier docs listed only MPM and Tool solvers as differentiable with rigid 'planned'; the current page does not say which solvers are differentiable. Could not confirm rigid mesh-contact gradients from a primary source.

works.name: Randomized-smoothing / bundled gradients through contact (Suh, Pang, Tedrake RA-L 2022; Suh, Simchowitz, Zhang, Tedrake ICML 2022) and the 2026 re-examination
works.what: Replaces the exact contact gradient by the gradient of a Gaussian-convolved objective (bundled gradient, Monte-Carlo with N=100 samples, first- or zero-order), analysed for penalty and implicit-time-stepping (LCP/QP) contact; ICML paper gives bias/variance analysis and an alpha-order estimator interpolating first- and zero-order. The 2026 follow-up (Onoda, Parmas, Yaguchi, Matsuo) argues variance control, not discontinuity bias, dominates in practice and proposes DDCG / IVW-H estimators.
works.params_from: n.a. (gradient estimator; applied to planning/MPC)
works.evaluated_against: sim-only: pendulum, Dubins car, quadrotor, planar two-finger hand, planar pushing, box pivoting; policy-gradient benchmarks
works.scale: low-DOF manipulation, N*T gradient evaluations per step
works.limitations: converges to the smoothed objective's optimum (biased); Monte-Carlo first-order gradient fails at jump discontinuities (zero-order variant needed); analysis 'focuses on sustained contact modes (sticking/sliding), not impact dynamics'; no mesh geometry.

works.name: Hunt–Crossley (1975) and the hysteresis-damping family: Lankarani–Nikravesh (1990), Flores et al. (2011), Gonthier, Zhang et al. (2020) comparison
works.source: arXiv:2001.01344 (Zhang, Li, Zhao, He, comparative study of five models); Hunt & Crossley, J. Appl. Mech. 42 (1975); secondary: Alves et al. Multibody Syst. Dyn. 2015 (abstract only)
works.what: Continuous contact force F = K delta^n (1 + chi * ddelta/ddelta0) with a hysteresis damping factor chi set from a target restitution e at the initial impact speed ddelta0. Hunt–Crossley: chi = 3(1-e)/2 (derived assuming e ~ 1 - alpha v, i.e. LINEAR velocity dependence, valid near e=1); Lankarani–Nikravesh: chi = 3(1-e^2)/4 (near e=1); Flores et al.: chi = 8(1-e)/(5e) (claimed usable down to low e). In all of them e is velocity-DEPENDENT once chi is fixed: the stated e holds only at the calibration speed.
works.params_from: restitution e supplied externally (table or drop test) at a stated impact speed; stiffness K from Hertz
works.evaluated_against: analytic/numeric impact cases only; the 2020 comparison reports all five models agree at e=0.9 but HC and LN deviate 25–45% in indentation, peak force and duration from the others at e=0.2 (search-snippet figure, secondary)
works.scale: single impact pair
works.limitations: the exponent of e(v) is a consequence of the chosen damping kernel (delta^{3/2} ddelta -> linear in v), not a measured material law; models are valid near e~1 unless specifically re-derived (Flores); no corner/polyhedral impacts.

works.name: Kuwabara–Kono (1987) / Brilliantov–Spahn–Hertzsch–Pöschel (1996) / Schwager–Pöschel compact expressions (2008)
works.source: arXiv:cond-mat/9711313 ; arXiv:1102.5247 ; Kuwabara & Kono, Jpn. J. Appl. Phys. 26 (1987) (cited via arXiv:2509.07461 which quotes '(1-e_n) ∝ v^{1/5}')
works.what: Viscoelastic sphere contact: F = min(0, -rho xi^{3/2} - (3/2) A rho xi^{1/2} xi_dot) (Hertz elastic + dissipative term with xi^{1/2} xi_dot kernel, 'first motivated in Kuwabara 1987 and rigorously derived in Brilliantov 1996'). Restitution e(v) = 1 + sum_k h_k (beta^{1/2} v^{1/10})^k, leading term 1 - C1 A kappa^{2/5} v^{1/5}: (1-e) ∝ v^{1/5}. The series converges extremely slowly and diverges when truncated; Schwager–Pöschel give Padé [3/6] (near-exact) and [1/4] approximants for practical use. Delayed shape recovery after separation raises e vs earlier estimates.
works.params_from: material constants (Young's modulus, Poisson ratio, viscosity A) — measured or fitted
works.evaluated_against: Bridges et al. 1984 ice-ball restitution data at low temperature ('remarkable' agreement; residual deviations attributed to surface forces, plasticity, adhesion)
works.scale: single sphere pair
works.limitations: valid for smooth viscoelastic spheres at low speed, no plastic deformation; exponent 1/5 is specific to the xi^{1/2} xi_dot kernel; nothing on polyhedral corner contact.
works.confidence: high (1102.5247 read); medium for the 1987/1996 originals

works.name: Müller, Heckel, Sack, Pöschel — Complex velocity dependence of the coefficient of restitution of a bouncing ball
works.source: doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.110.254301 (FAU CRIS record; full PDF server certificate expired)
works.what: Automated high-count bouncing-ball experiment; finds an OSCILLATION in e(v) superimposed on the known monotone decay, previously hidden by statistical scatter; explained quantitatively (wavelength and amplitude) as interplay of translational and vibrational degrees of freedom of the colliders.
works.params_from: measured directly (drop/bounce)
works.evaluated_against: large-N real measurements vs an analytic vibrational model
works.scale: one ball/plate system
works.limitations: only abstract confirmed; material, speed range and amplitude numbers not read from the primary text; shows that no single smooth e(v) law is exact even for a sphere.

works.name: DEM calibration & timestep practice: Itasca PFC 'Calibrating the Normal Critical Damping Ratio' and LIGGGHTS fix check/timestep/gran
works.what: PFC: for the linear spring-dashpot model the critical damping ratio is set from the target restitution analytically, zeta = ln(e)/sqrt(ln^2(e)+pi^2) (so e is velocity-INDEPENDENT by construction); verified by a drop test (32 balls, 50 mm, 2650 kg/m^3, kn 5e4 N/m, 1 m drop). LIGGGHTS: two timestep criteria — Rayleigh time dt_r = pi r sqrt(rho/G)/(0.1631 nu + 0.8766) and Hertz collision time dt_h = 2.87 (m_eff^2/(r_eff Y_eff^2 v_max))^0.2 — with a warning when dt exceeds a user fraction of either (0.1 in the example; 0.1–0.2 is common practice).
works.params_from: restitution from a physical drop test at the impact speed of interest; stiffness from material table or calibrated
works.evaluated_against: PFC: simulated vs analytic e within 3% with automatic timestep, within 1% at a fixed dt = 1e-5 s; the cfdem forum guidance quoted is that simulated e 'should not deviate more than a couple %' for e > 0.2
works.scale: sphere particles only
works.limitations: all criteria are for SPHERES (Rayleigh wave on a sphere, Hertz sphere contact duration); neither document states a steps-per-collision count for corner/edge impacts of polyhedra; velocity dependence of e must be added by choosing a different kernel (Kuwabara–Kono, Tsuji) or a parameter-dependent COR table (MFiX-style drop-test COR functions).

gaps: No shipped differentiable engine reports finite-difference-validated gradients through sustained, frictional MESH–MESH (triangle mesh vs triangle mesh) contact. Evidence: Nimble supports mesh-mesh but freezes mesh normals, uses FD only as a timing baseline and does not differentiate friction (arXiv:2103.16021 App. C/D, Conclusions); Jade does mesh-mesh CCD but validates only by an optimisation task and had no released code (arXiv:2309.04710); Ostrich has the only FD-in-CI numbers (0.02%/0.4%/1.6%) but only body-vs-mesh terrain, e=0, code unreleased (arXiv:2609.08800); DiffMJX modifies five primitive pairs and states mesh-mesh was 'not relevant' (arXiv:2506.14186); Dojo is point/sphere/capsule vs flat (arXiv:2203.00806); Newton 1.4.0 freezes the narrow phase and normal and tests only sphere-plane and box-box (installed test_differentiable_contacts.py, docs 'Experimental'); MJX is convex-only (<=32 verts convex-convex) with differentiability 'mostly supported' (docs); Genesis docs say some collision paths give zero/undefined gradients. The statement 'no shipped engine gives validated gradients through mesh–mesh narrow phase' survives.

No engine separately validates the GLANCING-strike regime or the SUSTAINED-pushing regime of contact gradients. Evidence: Suh et al. restrict analysis to sustained sticking/sliding modes 'not impact dynamics' (arXiv:2109.05143); DiffMJX focuses on transient hard impacts and notes post-corner-impact chaos (arXiv:2506.14186); Ostrich's FD tests are an impulsive boundary test, wheel DOFs and cart-pole, with mesh-contact position gradients 'truncated' on long horizons; Dojo/Nimble report no regime-resolved checks. Nobody reports gradient error as a function of contact duration or approach angle.

No differentiable rigid-body engine ships a velocity-dependent restitution law with a published exponent as an identifiable parameter. Evidence: Ostrich 'impacts resolved inelastically (e=0); restitution left to future work'; Dojo inelastic NCP; Nimble constant per-contact sigma; MuJoCo/MJX/DiffMJX encode contact softness via solref/solimp with no restitution parameter (DiffMJX had to fit solref/solimp instead of the known e=0.125); DiffSDFSim fits a constant restitution. Drake's hydroelastic model uses a Hunt–Crossley dissipation parameter but its user guide says nothing about AutoDiff through it. Searched for 'Kuwabara-Kono' / 'Hunt-Crossley' together with 'differentiable simulator' — only the project's own alpha law and Drake's dissipation parameter surfaced.

No published convergence criterion exists for CORNER/EDGE impacts of polyhedral bodies under penalty contact. Evidence: LIGGGHTS fix check/timestep/gran defines Rayleigh and Hertz timesteps for spheres and 'does not explicitly state how many timesteps per collision are needed'; Itasca PFC's restitution verification uses 50 mm spheres and reports <3% / <1% agreement without a steps-per-contact rule; the arXiv:2509.07461 DEM review is restricted to tangential Mindlin models and contains no timestep fractions; DiffMJX explicitly reports chaos after corner impacts and loosened its tolerance for cost. Searched 'penalty contact corner impact timestep convergence' (search budget exhausted before results); nothing found in the fetched primary sources.

No real-data system identification of restitution through a differentiable mesh-contact engine on MORE THAN ONE object. Evidence: DiffMJX — one acrylic cube (550 tosses); Dojo — one box; DiffSDFSim — one tennis ball; Ostrich — one wheeled robot (friction and servo stiffness, not restitution); Jade and Nimble — no real data. Combined with Physics 101's 30 fps drops failing (project), there is no multi-object real restitution-vs-velocity dataset tied to a differentiable engine.

No shipped engine exposes gradients through the CONTACT ASSIGNMENT (which face/edge pair, or the contact normal) for meshes. Evidence: Nimble sets dn/dq = 0 for meshes; Newton's augment kernel passes the normal 'frozen, no orientation gradients' and the narrow phase is enable_backward=False; Jade's CCD gradient is described as having 'rounding approximation ... caused by coarse detection'. The project's own measurement (tape picks one face at a corner where FD averages three) is the same non-differentiability, unaddressed anywhere.
gap_scouts.relevance_to_our_assets: The project's exact-mesh vertex-vs-plane contact with an FD-validated d(slide)/dmu (−0.5448 vs −0.5453) already sits where the best shipped engines are validated — Ostrich (body-vs-terrain, FD 0.02–1.6%) and Nimble (mesh-mesh but frozen normals, no friction gradient) — and its measured defect (sustained pushing: total −0.70 right, split between bodies wrong, −0.032 vs −0.385; one adjoint component exploding at the stiff setting) is precisely the regime no engine validates, so a fixed and FD-characterised pair adjoint through sustained frictional mesh–mesh contact would not be reinventing anything that ships; Newton 1.4.0's own 'differentiable contacts' are not a substitute (narrow phase frozen, normals frozen, tested on sphere/box only, marked experimental), though Warp's native adj_mesh_query_point_sign_normal is the same primitive the project already uses. DiffMJX's Contacts-from-Distance (straight-through pre-contact gradients) and Ostrich's implicit-function-theorem adjoint with FD checks in CI are the two published templates for the vanishing-gradient and memory problems the project's tape rollout will hit on longer horizons; Suh et al.'s bundled gradients are the fallback when exact gradients are too rough, at N≈100 rollouts per step. On restitution, the project's law is ALREADY a named one — Hunt–Crossley 1975, whose e ≈ 1 − alpha·v is the linear small-dissipation expansion of the delta^{3/2}·delta_dot kernel — and the literature does not offer a single exponent to adopt instead: Kuwabara–Kono/Brilliantov give (1−e) ∝ v^{1/5} only for the delta^{1/2}·delta_dot kernel of smooth viscoelastic spheres, the linear spring-dashpot (PFC) gives constant e by construction, and Müller–Heckel show real balls superimpose oscillations on the decay; so 'fitting p' is a model-selection question between kernels, and DEM practice sidesteps it by calibrating damping from a drop test at the impact speed of use (PFC accepts <3% error on e) — which the project's 240 fps phone option could supply where Physics 101's 30 fps could not. The project's stability rule dt·sqrt(k/m) < 0.3 is equivalent to ~10 substeps per half contact period, the same order as the DEM 0.1–0.2 × Hertz/Rayleigh-time convention, but every published criterion assumes spheres; the measured non-determinism and FD step-size dependence at the stiff tilt rig is the corner-impact case nobody has a criterion for, and DiffMJX reports the same corner chaos on real cube tosses. Redundant with existing assets: DiffSDFSim's and Dojo's friction/mass/vertex identification from a single real sequence is what the project's Physics 101 + Newton loop already does at 70-object held-out scale; the sim-ready pipelines in the parent's list remain the ones that never validate against held-out real motion, and none of the engines here changes that.
gap_scouts.caveats: The session's shared WebSearch budget ran out after the first round; all later confirmation came from direct WebFetch of known primary URLs and from reading the installed Newton 1.4.0 / Warp 1.15 source and tests, so coverage of 2025–2026 engines beyond Ostrich, DiffMJX and the Suh follow-up may be incomplete (e.g. no check of DiffTaichi-derived rigid engines, Brax-positional, or MJX-Warp roadmap updates). Müller–Heckel PRL 2013 and the Alves et al. 2015 comparative study were read only as abstracts (certificate / paywall), so their numbers are not reported. The Hunt–Crossley / Lankarani–Nikravesh / Flores damping-factor formulas are quoted from standard knowledge and secondary snippets, not from the fetched primary text (medium confidence). The initial small-model summary of arXiv:2509.07461's normal-law content was contradicted by the paper's own HTML (it is a tangential-model review) and was discarded; only its Kuwabara–Kono quotation is used. Ostrich and Jade code releases could not be verified as available. Genesis's rigid-contact differentiability status could not be pinned from its docs.
